We study the registration of images acquired with different signal intensity distributions, focusing on the separation of intensity and warping effects.

We formalize the problem within the framework of registration and describe different methods to estimate the intensity modulation factor (IMF) - a parameter that quantifies the intensity difference between images.

We perform a theoretical analysis of the behavior of the common registration energy function with intensity differences, and we derive a continuous version of the IMF by considering the gradient of the registration energy.
We propose a simple yet effective algorithm to estimate the IMF, and we show that our method is very robust and efficient, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques.
Finally, we discuss the physical meaning of the IMF and show that it can be interpreted as a dimensionless contrast factor that quantifies the departure from linear intensity scaling.

Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionize medical imaging, but its adoption and implementation must be guided by principles that prioritize patient safety, privacy, and ethical considerations.
This paper presents the FUTURE-AI initiative, which aims to establish guiding principles and consensus recommendations for trustworthy AI in future medical imaging.

The initiative brings together experts from various disciplines, including radiology, computer science, ethics, and law, to develop a framework that addresses the technical, ethical, and legal challenges associated with AI in medical imaging.
The resulting principles and recommendations cover areas such as data privacy, algorithm transparency, bias mitigation, and accountability.
By adhering to these principles, stakeholders can ensure the responsible and ethical deployment of AI in medical imaging, ultimately benefiting patients and healthcare providers.
EdgeFlow is a novel approach to interactive image segmentation that combines edge detection and flow-based methods to achieve practical and efficient results.
The proposed method utilizes an edge-guided flow algorithm to guide the segmentation process, allowing users to interactively refine the segmentation boundaries.
The algorithm incorporates both local and global information to accurately capture object boundaries and handle complex image structures.

Experimental results demonstrate that EdgeFlow outperforms existing interactive segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising tool for various applications such as image editing and object recognition.
Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable segmentation labels for medical images is often challenging due to the high cost and time required for manual annotation.
In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised contrastive learning approach for label-efficient medical image segmentation.
Our method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to learn a representation space where similar instances are brought closer and dissimilar instances are pushed apart.
We introduce a novel contrastive loss function that encourages the model to learn discriminative features for segmentation.

We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy while requiring fewer labeled samples.
Our results suggest that semi-supervised contrastive learning can significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of medical image segmentation tasks.
Multi-organ segmentation is a challenging task in medical image analysis due to the imbalance between the number of organs and the amount of available training data.
In this paper, we propose a novel loss function called Combo Loss to address the input and output imbalance in multi-organ segmentation.
The Combo Loss combines the Dice loss and the Tversky loss, which are widely used in segmentation tasks, to achieve a balanced optimization between sensitivity and specificity.
We evaluate the performance of the Combo Loss on two publicly available datasets and compare it with other state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the Combo Loss outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in the Combo Loss.
Overall, our proposed Combo Loss provides a promising solution for handling input and output imbalance in multi-organ segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for training a 3D seismic fault segmentation model using only a few 2D slice labels.
The proposed method leverages attention mechanisms to guide the model's focus on relevant regions in the seismic data.
By incorporating attention-based mechanisms, the model is able to effectively learn from limited labeled data and generalize to unseen 3D volumes.

Experimental results on a real-world seismic dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods while requiring significantly fewer labeled samples.
This work has implications for reducing the annotation burden in seismic fault segmentation tasks and improving the efficiency of seismic data analysis.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image.
In recent years, deep learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in semantic segmentation.
However, CNNs have limitations in capturing long-range dependencies and modeling global context.
In this paper, we propose a new model called Segmenter, which is based on the Transformer architecture.
The Transformer has shown great success in natural language processing tasks, but its application to computer vision tasks, especially semantic segmentation, is relatively unexplored.
We adapt the Transformer to the semantic segmentation task by introducing a novel self-attention mechanism that operates on the spatial dimensions of the feature maps.
Our experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Segmenter outperforms state-of-the-art CNN-based models in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components of Segmenter and provide insights into its working mechanism.
Overall, our work highlights the potential of the Transformer architecture for semantic segmentation and opens up new avenues for research in this field.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.

While recent advances in deep learning have led to significant improvements in semantic segmentation accuracy, these methods often rely solely on image-based features and do not take into account contextual information.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for mining contextual information beyond the image to improve semantic segmentation performance.
Our method leverages both image-based features and contextual cues, such as object relationships and scene context, to enhance the accuracy of semantic segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Our findings highlight the importance of considering contextual information in semantic segmentation tasks and provide insights into how it can be effectively incorporated into deep learning models.
This paper presents a comprehensive approach for referring image segmentation using multi-modal interactions.
The proposed method combines natural language instructions with visual cues to accurately segment objects in images.
The authors introduce a novel dataset for referring image segmentation and develop a deep learning model that leverages both textual and visual information.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming existing methods on the new dataset.
The paper contributes to the field of computer vision by providing a robust and versatile framework for referring image segmentation.
Few-shot segmentation is a challenging task that requires the model to accurately segment objects with only a few annotated examples.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for few-shot segmentation using global and local contrastive learning.
Our method leverages both global and local information to learn discriminative representations for the few-shot segmentation task.
We introduce a global contrastive loss that encourages the model to learn global features that are invariant to object appearance variations.
Additionally, we propose a local contrastive loss that encourages the model to learn local features that capture fine-grained details of the objects.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing few-shot segmentation methods.
Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization to unseen classes.
Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of few-shot segmentation techniques and provides insights into the importance of global and local contrastive learning for this task.
This paper presents an efficient and generic interactive segmentation framework that aims to correct mispredictions during the clinical evaluation of medical images.
The proposed framework utilizes a combination of deep learning models and user interaction to improve the accuracy of segmentation results.
The framework incorporates a novel interactive segmentation algorithm that allows users to correct mispredictions by providing feedback on the segmentation results.
The algorithm then updates the segmentation model based on this feedback, resulting in improved segmentation accuracy.
The framework is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and compared to existing interactive segmentation methods.
The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves higher accuracy and efficiency in correcting mispredictions, making it a valuable tool for clinical evaluation of medical images.
This paper introduces a new method for constructing prediction sets that are both distribution-free and capable of controlling the risk of incorrect predictions.
Traditional prediction sets often rely on assumptions about the underlying distribution of the data, which can limit their applicability in real-world scenarios.
The proposed method, called Distribution-Free, Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets (DF-RCP), overcomes this limitation by leveraging the concept of conformal prediction.
DF-RCP constructs prediction sets that are guaranteed to contain the true value with a specified probability, regardless of the underlying distribution.
The method is demonstrated through extensive simulations and real-world examples, showing its effectiveness in various settings.
The results highlight the advantages of DF-RCP over existing methods, making it a valuable tool for prediction tasks in diverse domains.
This paper presents a novel approach for synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) image segmentation using an iterative, deep, and unsupervised method.
The proposed method combines the power of deep learning techniques with an iterative refinement process to achieve accurate and robust segmentation results.
The deep learning model is trained on a large dataset of labeled SAS images, and then used to generate initial segmentation masks.
These masks are then iteratively refined using a combination of region growing and graph-cut algorithms.
The unsupervised nature of the method allows for the segmentation of SAS images without the need for manual annotation, making it applicable to a wide range of applications.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting SAS images, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.
This paper presents a novel approach to unsupervised semantic image segmentation using a combination of StyleGAN and CLIP.
StyleGAN is a state-of-the-art generative model that can generate high-quality images, while CLIP is a powerful image-text embedding model that can understand the content of images.
By combining these two models, we propose a method that can segment images into semantically meaningful regions without the need for any labeled training data.
Our approach leverages the style information learned by StyleGAN to guide the segmentation process, while CLIP provides the semantic understanding necessary for accurate segmentation.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in producing high-quality segmentations.

Our results show that our approach outperforms existing unsupervised segmentation methods and achieves comparable performance to supervised methods, highlighting the potential of combining generative and embedding models for unsupervised semantic image segmentation.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Existing methods often rely on deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn discriminative features for accurate segmentation.
However, these methods often suffer from high computational costs and limited generalization ability.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Double Similarity Distillation (DSD) for semantic image segmentation.
DSD leverages the concept of similarity distillation to transfer knowledge from a teacher network to a student network.
Specifically, DSD consists of two stages: feature similarity distillation and spatial similarity distillation.
In the feature similarity distillation stage, the teacher network and student network are trained to minimize the feature-level similarity loss.
This encourages the student network to learn similar feature representations as the teacher network.
In the spatial similarity distillation stage, the teacher network and student network are trained to minimize the spatial-level similarity loss.
This encourages the student network to produce similar segmentation maps as the teacher network.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DSD achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, ablation studies and visualization analysis are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
Overall, DSD provides a promising solution for semantic image segmentation with improved performance and reduced computational costs.

The proposed SGSCN has the potential to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of medical image segmentation, thereby facilitating more accurate diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.

This paper presents a semi-supervised approach for left atrium segmentation in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using mutual consistency training.

Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy.

The semi-supervised approach presented in this paper has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of left atrium segmentation, leading to better diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation.
This paper presents a novel approach for robust visual tracking using a cell-level differentiable neural architecture search (CHASE).

The proposed method leverages the advantages of both neural architecture search and differentiable architecture search to automatically discover the optimal cell-level architecture for visual tracking.

This paper proposes a novel method for weakly supervised segmentation using inter extreme points geodesics.
The method leverages the extreme points of objects in an image to generate geodesic paths that accurately segment the objects.
The proposed method is able to achieve state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for practical applications.
The paper also provides a detailed analysis of the proposed method and compares it with existing approaches, highlighting its advantages and limitations.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for weakly supervised segmentation that can contribute to advancements in computer vision and image analysis.
K-Net: Towards Unified Image Segmentation is an academic paper that proposes a novel approach for unified image segmentation.
The paper introduces a new deep learning architecture called K-Net, which combines the strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs).
The K-Net architecture consists of a CNN module for feature extraction and an RNN module for capturing spatial dependencies.

ComBiNet is a compact convolutional Bayesian neural network designed for image segmentation tasks.

The proposed architecture achieves a balance between model complexity and performance by employing a compact network design.

The network's ability to provide uncertainty estimates makes it suitable for applications where reliable segmentation results and uncertainty quantification are crucial, such as medical imaging and autonomous driving.
Semantic segmentation of urban scene images is a challenging task due to the presence of very fine details and complex structures.

This paper presents a large-scale image segmentation approach based on distributed clustering algorithms.

This paper presents RLCorrector, a novel approach for proofreading errors in connectomics image segmentation.

Points2Polygons: Context-Based Segmentation from Weak Labels Using Adversarial Networks

Abstract:

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a class label to each pixel in an image.
Traditional approaches rely on pixel-level annotations, which are expensive and time-consuming to obtain.
In this paper, we propose a novel method called Points2Polygons that leverages weak labels in the form of point annotations to perform context-based segmentation.
Our approach combines a generative adversarial network (GAN) with a polygon generation module to generate accurate polygon masks from the given point annotations.
The GAN is trained in a two-step process, where the generator learns to generate realistic polygons, and the discriminator learns to distinguish between real and generated polygons.
We also introduce a context module that captures the contextual information of the image and incorporates it into the segmentation process.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing weakly supervised segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we show that our approach can handle complex scenes with multiple objects and achieve competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods.

Overall, our Points2Polygons method provides a promising solution for context-based segmentation from weak labels, opening up new possibilities for efficient and accurate semantic segmentation in various applications.
This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of exact inference in graphs using the degree-4 sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy.
The SOS hierarchy is a powerful tool for solving optimization problems, and has been successfully applied to various problems in computer science and mathematics.
In this paper, we focus on the problem of exact inference in graphs, which involves computing the partition function of a graphical model.
We present a detailed overview of the SOS hierarchy and its application to exact inference in graphs.
We discuss the theoretical foundations of the SOS hierarchy and its relationship to other optimization techniques.
We also provide a thorough analysis of the computational complexity of exact inference in graphs using the SOS hierarchy.
Our analysis includes a comparison with other state-of-the-art algorithms for exact inference in graphs, and we demonstrate the effectiveness of the SOS hierarchy in solving this problem.
Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive view of exact inference in graphs using the degree-4 SOS hierarchy, and offers insights into the theoretical and practical aspects of this approach.
This paper presents a high-resolution segmentation method for tooth root fuzzy edges based on polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection.
The proposed method aims to accurately segment tooth root fuzzy edges, which are challenging due to their irregular shapes and low contrast.
The method first detects landmarks on the tooth root fuzzy edge using a landmark detection algorithm.
Then, a polynomial curve fitting algorithm is applied to fit a smooth curve to the detected landmarks.
Experimental results on a dataset of dental images demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in segmenting tooth root fuzzy edges, outperforming existing methods.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the accuracy of dental image analysis and assist in dental diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper presents a novel approach for deep active contours using locally controlled distance vector flow.
Active contours, also known as snakes, are widely used in image segmentation tasks.
However, traditional active contour models suffer from limitations such as sensitivity to initialization and inability to handle complex image structures.
To address these issues, the proposed method incorporates deep learning techniques into the active contour framework.
Specifically, a convolutional neural network is trained to predict the local control parameters for the distance vector flow, which guides the contour evolution.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing active contour models in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The combination of deep learning and active contours opens up new possibilities for image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for referring segmentation, a task that involves segmenting an object in an image based on a natural language description.
The proposed method, called Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension (CMPC), leverages both visual and textual information to improve the accuracy of segmentation.

CMPC consists of two stages: a pre-training stage where a visual-semantic embedding model is trained, and a fine-tuning stage where the model is further optimized using a cross-modal progressive comprehension framework.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CMPC outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.

This paper presents a Bayesian logistic shape model inference approach for the segmentation of cochlea images.

This paper presents a generalized asymmetric dual-front model for active contours and image segmentation.

Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model compared to existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.

The BiSeNet architecture has shown promising results in real-time semantic segmentation, but it has limitations in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Our method builds upon the original GENESIS framework, which uses a generative model to learn object representations from unlabelled data.

We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that GENESIS-V2 outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the learned representations and show that they capture meaningful semantic information about the objects.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of unsupervised learning by providing a more effective and efficient method for inferring unordered object representations.
This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using generative models.
The proposed method leverages the power of generative models to improve the performance of semantic segmentation tasks, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data.
The authors introduce a semi-supervised learning framework that combines labeled and unlabeled data to train the generative model, which is then used for segmentation.
Additionally, the paper demonstrates the strong out-of-domain generalization capabilities of the proposed method, showing its effectiveness in segmenting images from unseen domains.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets validate the superiority of the proposed approach compared to existing methods, highlighting its potential for practical applications in computer vision.
This paper proposes a novel ensemble learning approach for polyp localisation using classifier prediction confidence and comprehensive learning particle swarm optimisation (CLPSO).
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of polyp localisation by combining multiple classifiers and optimising their performance.
The ensemble learning approach considers the prediction confidence of each classifier and assigns weights accordingly to make more accurate predictions.
Additionally, CLPSO is used to optimise the weights and parameters of the ensemble learning model.
Experimental results on a polyp localisation dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The findings of this study have implications for improving the effectiveness of polyp detection and localisation in medical imaging applications.
Pneumothorax is a potentially life-threatening condition that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment.
In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach for pneumothorax segmentation in chest X-ray images.
We utilize a convolutional neural network architecture to automatically identify and segment regions of pneumothorax in the images.
Our model is trained on a large dataset of annotated chest X-ray images and achieves high accuracy in pneumothorax segmentation.
We evaluate the performance of our model on a separate test dataset and compare it with other state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately predicting pneumothorax regions, which can aid radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.
Our proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of pneumothorax detection in clinical practice.
Biomedical image segmentation plays a crucial role in medical diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, accurate and efficient segmentation of biomedical images remains a challenging task due to the complexity and variability of the images.
In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning architecture called FANet (Feedback Attention Network) for improved biomedical image segmentation.
FANet incorporates a feedback mechanism that allows the network to iteratively refine its predictions based on the feedback from previous iterations.
Additionally, FANet utilizes an attention mechanism to selectively focus on informative regions of the image, improving the segmentation accuracy.
We evaluate FANet on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that FANet achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
Our proposed FANet has the potential to significantly improve biomedical image segmentation, leading to more accurate and reliable medical diagnoses.
Few-shot segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision, where the goal is to segment objects in an image given only a few annotated examples.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Self-Guided and Cross-Guided Learning (SGCL) for few-shot segmentation.
SGCL leverages both self-guided and cross-guided learning to improve the segmentation performance.

Self-guided learning uses the available annotated examples to guide the segmentation process, while cross-guided learning utilizes information from other images to further refine the segmentation results.
We evaluate SGCL on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that SGCL achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.
Our approach shows promise for addressing the challenges of few-shot segmentation and has the potential to advance the field of computer vision.
This paper proposes a novel method for learning to segment objects from scribbles using multi-scale adversarial attention gates.
The method leverages the power of adversarial training to generate realistic segmentations from rough scribbles.
The proposed approach incorporates multi-scale attention gates to capture both local and global contextual information, improving the accuracy of the segmentation.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of this research.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting fluorescence microscopy images using deep neural networks.

The authors propose a method that leverages the ability of deep neural networks to learn meta-structures, which are higher-level structures that capture the relationships between different objects in the image.
The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on a benchmark dataset and demonstrates the effectiveness of using meta-structures for image segmentation tasks.
The results suggest that deep neural networks can learn to extract meaningful information from fluorescence microscopy images and improve the accuracy of segmentation algorithms.
This research has implications for the field of biomedical imaging and can potentially contribute to advancements in automated image analysis and understanding.
This paper proposes a contrastive registration method for unsupervised medical image segmentation.
The method leverages a contrastive loss function to learn a registration network that aligns images from different modalities.
The aligned images are then used to train a segmentation network.

Experimental results on a dataset of brain MRI scans demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive segmentation performance compared to supervised methods, even without any manual annotations.
The proposed contrastive registration method shows promise for unsupervised medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper proposes a method for learning food portion estimation from monocular images using cross-domain feature adaptation.
The authors address the challenge of limited labeled data by leveraging a large-scale dataset with food portion annotations and a larger dataset without portion annotations.

They propose a two-step approach that first learns a feature adaptation model to align the feature distributions of the two datasets, and then trains a portion estimation model using the adapted features.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately estimating food portions from monocular images, outperforming existing methods.
The proposed method has potential applications in dietary assessment and portion control.
This paper proposes a novel federated domain generalization framework, called FedDG, for medical image segmentation.
FedDG leverages episodic learning in continuous frequency space to address the challenges of domain shift and data heterogeneity in federated learning.
The proposed framework consists of three key components: a frequency-based data augmentation module, a frequency-based episodic training module, and a frequency-based model aggregation module.

Experimental results on two benchmark medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that FedDG outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization capability.
The proposed framework has the potential to improve the performance of medical image segmentation models in real-world scenarios where data is distributed across multiple institutions.
Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable segmentation masks for medical images is challenging due to the limited availability of annotated data.
In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised approach for medical image segmentation that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data.
Our method incorporates a dual-task consistency framework, where the segmentation task is coupled with a self-supervised pretext task.
By jointly training these two tasks, our model learns to generate consistent predictions across different views of the same image, thereby improving the segmentation performance.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image datasets and demonstrate its superiority over state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
Our findings suggest that semi-supervised learning with dual-task consistency can effectively enhance medical image segmentation, even with limited labeled data.
This paper proposes an unsupervised domain adaptation network with a category-centric prototype aligner for biomedical image segmentation.
The goal is to address the challenge of limited labeled data in the biomedical domain by leveraging unlabeled data from a different domain.
The proposed network consists of two main components: a feature extractor and a category-centric prototype aligner.
The feature extractor is responsible for extracting discriminative features from both the source and target domains.
The category-centric prototype aligner aligns the prototypes of different categories between the source and target domains to reduce the domain gap.

Experimental results on two publicly available biomedical image segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving segmentation performance compared to existing methods.
Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring.
Deep learning-based methods have shown promising results in medical image segmentation tasks.
However, these methods often require a large amount of annotated data for training, which is time-consuming and costly to obtain.
In this paper, we review recent advancements in deep network models for medical image segmentation with limited supervision.
We discuss various approaches, including semi-supervised learning, weakly supervised learning, and transfer learning, that aim to alleviate the need for fully annotated data.
We also analyze the strengths and limitations of these approaches and provide insights into future research directions.

Overall, this review provides a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art deep network models for medical image segmentation with limited supervision, highlighting their potential for improving clinical practice.
The paper presents the fifth version of the Environmental Microorganism Image Dataset (EMDS-5), which is a comprehensive collection of images of microorganisms found in various environmental samples.
The dataset is designed to facilitate research in multiple image analysis tasks related to environmental microbiology.
The paper describes the dataset creation process, including sample collection, image acquisition, and annotation.
It also provides an overview of the dataset statistics and discusses its potential applications in tasks such as classification, segmentation, and detection of microorganisms.
The EMDS-5 dataset is expected to serve as a valuable resource for researchers working in the field of environmental microbiology and related areas.
Food image segmentation is an important task in computer vision, as it enables various applications such as food recognition and dietary analysis.
However, existing methods often struggle with class-agnostic segmentation, where the goal is to segment food regions without prior knowledge of specific food classes.
In this paper, we propose a saliency-aware class-agnostic food image segmentation method.
Our approach leverages saliency maps to guide the segmentation process, allowing for more accurate and robust segmentation results.
We evaluate our method on a large-scale food image dataset and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving high-quality class-agnostic food image segmentation.
In this paper, we propose a novel image segmentation framework called Co-Seg that aims to address the issue of label corruption in training data.
Label corruption can significantly degrade the performance of image segmentation models, leading to inaccurate and unreliable results.
Co-Seg leverages the idea of co-training, where two models are trained simultaneously on different subsets of the training data.
One model focuses on learning from clean labels, while the other model learns from corrupted labels.
The two models then collaborate to generate more accurate segmentation predictions.
We evaluate Co-Seg on several benchmark datasets and compare its performance against state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that Co-Seg effectively mitigates the impact of label corruption and achieves superior segmentation accuracy.
Additionally, we conduct an ablation study to analyze the contribution of different components in Co-Seg and provide insights into its working mechanism.
Overall, Co-Seg presents a promising solution to the problem of label corruption in image segmentation, with potential applications in various domains such as medical imaging and autonomous driving.
This paper presents a network-agnostic knowledge transfer method for medical image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages pre-trained models from different domains to improve the performance of segmentation models on medical images.
The method involves transferring knowledge from a source domain to a target domain by aligning the feature distributions using adversarial learning.

Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art transfer learning methods and achieves competitive segmentation performance across different medical imaging modalities.
The network-agnostic nature of the method makes it applicable to a wide range of medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a nonparametric clustering approach for image segmentation.
Traditional image segmentation methods often rely on assumptions about the underlying data distribution, which may not hold in practice.
In contrast, nonparametric clustering methods do not make any assumptions about the data distribution and can therefore be more flexible and robust.
The proposed method utilizes a density-based clustering algorithm to identify regions of similar pixel values in an image.
Experimental results on various image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting images.
The nonparametric clustering method shows promising potential for image segmentation tasks and can be a valuable tool in computer vision and image processing applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for semantic segmentation of point clouds using a boundary-aware geometric encoding.
Point clouds are a popular representation for 3D data, but their irregular and unordered nature makes semantic segmentation challenging.
The proposed method addresses this challenge by encoding geometric information about the boundaries of objects in the point cloud.
This encoding is then used as input to a deep neural network for semantic segmentation.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

The boundary-aware geometric encoding provides a valuable representation for point cloud segmentation tasks and has the potential to improve performance in various applications such as autonomous driving and robotics.
Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is a challenging task in medical image analysis, particularly in the context of hip joint bone segmentation.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Intra- and Cross-modality Semantic Consistency (ICMSC) for UDA on hip joint bone segmentation.
Our method leverages the semantic consistency between intra-modality and cross-modality images to improve the segmentation performance.
Specifically, we introduce a dual-branch network architecture that consists of an intra-modality branch and a cross-modality branch.

The intra-modality branch is responsible for learning the segmentation task on the source domain, while the cross-modality branch learns to transfer the knowledge from the source domain to the target domain.
We also propose a semantic consistency loss that encourages the predicted segmentation maps from both branches to be consistent.

Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in unsupervised domain adaptation for hip joint bone segmentation.
In recent years, 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks.
However, the large number of parameters and computational cost of 3D CNNs pose challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices.
In this paper, we propose a novel method called Channel-wise Automatic KErnel Shrinking (CAKES) to address this issue.
CAKES dynamically adjusts the kernel size of each channel in a 3D CNN based on its importance, thereby reducing the number of parameters and computational cost without sacrificing performance.

Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that CAKES achieves significant parameter reduction and computational cost reduction while maintaining competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Our method provides a promising solution for efficient deployment of 3D CNNs on resource-constrained devices.
Few-shot medical image segmentation is a challenging task due to the limited availability of annotated data.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called the Global Correlation Network with Discriminative Embedding (GCN-DE) for few-shot medical image segmentation.
The GCN-DE leverages a global correlation module to capture long-range dependencies and a discriminative embedding module to learn discriminative features.
We also introduce a novel few-shot learning strategy that utilizes a meta-learner to adapt the model to new classes with limited annotated data.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.
Our approach shows promise for improving medical image segmentation in scenarios with limited annotated data.
Infrared imaging is widely used in various fields such as medical diagnosis, surveillance, and target recognition.
However, the presence of intensity inhomogeneity in infrared images poses a challenge for accurate segmentation.
In this paper, we propose a multi-feature driven active contour segmentation model for infrared images with intensity inhomogeneity.
The model incorporates multiple features, including intensity, gradient, and local variance, to capture the characteristics of different regions in the image.
A region-based energy function is formulated to drive the contour evolution, which is optimized using the level set method.
Experimental results on a dataset of infrared images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in accurately segmenting objects in the presence of intensity inhomogeneity.
The proposed model outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
This research contributes to the development of advanced segmentation techniques for infrared imaging applications.
This paper proposes a bidirectional recurrent neural network (RNN)-based approach for few-shot learning in the context of 3D medical image segmentation.
Few-shot learning is a challenging task in medical imaging due to the limited availability of annotated data.
The proposed approach leverages the bidirectional nature of RNNs to capture both forward and backward dependencies in the input data.
The model is trained on a small number of labeled samples and then fine-tuned on a larger unlabeled dataset using a self-training strategy.

Experimental results on a publicly available 3D medical image segmentation dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The bidirectional RNN-based few-shot learning approach shows promise for improving the segmentation accuracy of 3D medical images with limited labeled data.
This paper presents a novel medical image segmentation model called w-Net, which incorporates multi-dimensional attention and cascade multi-scale convolution.
The proposed model is trained using dual supervision, combining both pixel-level and region-level annotations.
The multi-dimensional attention mechanism allows the model to focus on relevant features in different dimensions, improving segmentation accuracy.
The cascade multi-scale convolution further enhances the model's ability to capture fine details and handle scale variations.
Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that the w-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art segmentation models in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The proposed model has the potential to improve medical image analysis and assist in clinical decision-making.
This paper proposes a novel approach for multimodal and semi-supervised image segmentation.
The proposed method disentangles the different modalities of the input data, aligns them to a common feature space, and fuses them to generate accurate segmentation results.
The disentanglement step involves learning separate representations for each modality, while the alignment step utilizes a shared feature space to ensure consistency across modalities.
The fusion step combines the aligned representations to produce the final segmentation output.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has potential applications in medical imaging, remote sensing, and other domains where multimodal and semi-supervised image segmentation is required.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable annotations for training deep learning models is challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a teacher-student framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation that leverages both fully annotated and weakly annotated data.
The teacher network is trained on fully annotated data to provide pseudo-labels for weakly annotated data.
The student network is then trained on a combination of fully annotated and pseudo-labeled data.

Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods while requiring fewer expert annotations.
Our framework has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks in clinical practice.
This paper proposes a novel architecture for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) called HS-ResNet, which incorporates a hierarchical-split block to improve the performance of CNNs.
The hierarchical-split block splits the input feature maps into multiple branches, each with its own convolutional layers, and then combines the outputs of these branches.
This allows the network to capture both local and global information, leading to better feature representation and improved performance.
The proposed HS-ResNet architecture is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate its superiority over existing CNN architectures in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach to enhance the performance of CNNs by incorporating hierarchical-split blocks.
This paper presents a new region-based active learning method called MetaBox+ for semantic segmentation tasks.
The proposed method utilizes priority maps to select informative regions for annotation, aiming to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the active learning process.
The priority maps are generated by combining multiple uncertainty measures, including entropy and margin, to identify regions with high uncertainty.
The MetaBox+ method then selects regions within these high uncertainty areas based on their saliency scores.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that MetaBox+ outperforms existing active learning methods in terms of both annotation efficiency and segmentation accuracy.
The proposed method has the potential to enhance the performance of semantic segmentation models in real-world applications.
This paper presents a content-based propagation method for interactive segmentation of patterned images.
The proposed method utilizes user markings to guide the segmentation process and improve the accuracy of the results.
The method incorporates a content-based propagation algorithm that considers both the local and global features of the image to propagate the user markings.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
The method is applicable to a wide range of patterned images and can be used in various applications such as image editing and object recognition.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting microscopy images using lazy labels.
Traditional methods for image segmentation require pixel-level annotations, which can be time-consuming and expensive to obtain.
In this work, we propose a lazy labeling strategy where only a small subset of pixels are annotated, and the remaining pixels are labeled based on their similarity to the annotated pixels.
We introduce a deep learning framework that leverages this lazy labeling strategy to learn the segmentation task.
Our experiments on a dataset of microscopy images demonstrate that our approach achieves comparable performance to fully annotated methods while significantly reducing the annotation effort.
This work has the potential to accelerate the development of image segmentation algorithms for microscopy applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for semi-supervised instance segmentation using a mask-guided sample selection method.
The goal is to improve the performance of instance segmentation models by leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data.
The proposed method utilizes a mask-guided sampling strategy to select informative samples from the unlabeled data, which are then used to train the instance segmentation model.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing semi-supervised instance segmentation approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The findings of this study contribute to the development of more effective and efficient methods for instance segmentation in the field of computer vision.
This paper presents a novel deep learning framework called PC-U Net for jointly reconstructing and segmenting the cardiac walls in 3D from CT data.
The proposed framework utilizes a U-Net architecture with a novel point cloud representation to effectively capture the spatial information of the cardiac walls.
The network is trained using a combination of reconstruction and segmentation loss functions to ensure accurate and consistent results.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the PC-U Net outperforms existing methods in terms of both reconstruction and segmentation accuracy.
The proposed framework has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment planning of cardiac diseases.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation using Cellular Automata (CA).
CA is a computational model that consists of a grid of cells, each of which can be in one of several states.
We adapt the CA model to perform image segmentation by assigning each pixel in the image to a cell in the CA grid.
The state of each cell is then updated based on the states of its neighboring cells, resulting in the segmentation of the image into distinct regions.
We evaluate our approach on a variety of benchmark datasets and compare it to existing segmentation methods.
Our results demonstrate that the proposed CA-based approach achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper presents a promising alternative to traditional image segmentation techniques, highlighting the potential of CA models in computer vision applications.

This paper presents a novel approach for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image semantic segmentation using a combination of 3D discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and Markov random field (MRF) techniques.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional SAR image segmentation methods by incorporating both spatial and spectral information.
The 3D DWT is used to decompose the polarimetric SAR image into different frequency subbands, which are then used to extract relevant features for segmentation.
The MRF model is employed to capture the spatial dependencies between neighboring pixels and enforce smoothness in the segmentation results.
Experimental results on real-world polarimetric SAR images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting different land cover classes.

The proposed approach offers a promising solution for polarimetric SAR image segmentation, with potential applications in various fields such as agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.
This paper examines the current state of deep learning techniques for image segmentation and evaluates their effectiveness and potential limitations.
The abstract discusses the growing popularity of deep learning in the field of computer vision and its application to image segmentation tasks.
The authors highlight the advantages of deep learning algorithms, such as their ability to learn complex features and their potential for high accuracy.
However, they also address the challenges and limitations of deep learning, including the need for large amounts of labeled data, computational requirements, and potential overfitting.
The abstract concludes by emphasizing the need for further research and evaluation to determine the true potential and limitations of deep learning for image segmentation.
This paper presents a shape-aware semi-supervised approach for 3D semantic segmentation of medical images.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The shape information is incorporated into the segmentation process through a shape-aware regularization term, which encourages the segmentation to adhere to the underlying anatomical structures.

The semi-supervised learning framework is formulated as a graph-based optimization problem, where the labeled and unlabeled data are represented as nodes in a graph and the segmentation labels are propagated through the graph using a diffusion process.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The shape-aware regularization term effectively improves the segmentation quality by preserving the anatomical structures.
The semi-supervised learning framework allows for better utilization of unlabeled data, leading to improved segmentation performance.
Overall, the proposed method shows promise for accurate and efficient 3D semantic segmentation of medical images.
Automatic image labelling at pixel level is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning semantic labels to individual pixels in an image.
This paper proposes a novel approach for automatic image labelling at pixel level using deep learning techniques.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to learn the features of the input image and predict the labels for each pixel.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of labelled images, and the learned features are used to classify the pixels in unseen images.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed approach has potential applications in various domains, such as object recognition, scene understanding, and image segmentation.
This paper presents an uncertainty-based human-in-the-loop system for industrial tool wear analysis.
The system utilizes machine learning algorithms to predict tool wear based on sensor data collected from the manufacturing process.
However, due to the inherent uncertainty in the prediction models, human intervention is required to validate and refine the predictions.
The system incorporates a user interface that allows operators to review and provide feedback on the predicted tool wear levels.
This feedback is then used to update the prediction models and improve their accuracy.
The effectiveness of the system is demonstrated through experiments conducted on real-world manufacturing data.
The results show that the uncertainty-based human-in-the-loop system significantly improves the accuracy of tool wear prediction compared to traditional machine learning approaches.
This research contributes to the field of industrial tool wear analysis by providing a practical and effective solution that combines the strengths of machine learning algorithms and human expertise.
Cardiac segmentation is a crucial step in medical image analysis, but it often requires a large amount of annotated data, which can be time-consuming and expensive to obtain.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Dual-Teacher, which integrates intra-domain and inter-domain teachers to improve the efficiency of cardiac segmentation annotation.
The intra-domain teacher is trained on a small amount of annotated data from the same domain, while the inter-domain teacher is trained on a large amount of annotated data from a different domain.
The two teachers collaborate to generate pseudo-labels for the unlabeled data, which are then used to train a segmentation model.

Experimental results on a cardiac MRI dataset demonstrate that our Dual-Teacher approach achieves comparable segmentation performance to the fully supervised method, while significantly reducing the amount of annotated data required.
This approach has the potential to greatly improve the efficiency of cardiac segmentation annotation and facilitate the development of accurate and reliable cardiac image analysis algorithms.
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks.
However, they are limited in their ability to capture long-range dependencies due to their local receptive fields.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Fully Hyperbolic Convolutional Neural Networks (FHCNNs) that addresses this limitation.
FHCNNs leverage the hyperbolic space to model long-range dependencies by mapping the input data onto a hyperbolic manifold.
We introduce a hyperbolic convolution operation and a hyperbolic pooling operation to perform computations in the hyperbolic space.
We also propose a hyperbolic activation function that preserves the hyperbolic geometry.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that FHCNNs outperform traditional CNNs in terms of capturing long-range dependencies and achieving higher accuracy in various computer vision tasks.
Our findings suggest that leveraging the hyperbolic space can be a promising direction for improving the performance of CNNs.
This paper presents a method for robust semantic segmentation in adverse weather conditions using fast video-sequence segmentation.
Adverse weather conditions such as rain, snow, and fog can significantly degrade the performance of semantic segmentation algorithms.
The proposed method leverages the temporal information in video sequences to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The method consists of two main steps: motion estimation and segmentation refinement.
In the motion estimation step, optical flow is computed between consecutive frames to estimate the motion of objects.
In the segmentation refinement step, the estimated motion is used to refine the initial segmentation masks.

Experimental results on a dataset of videos captured in adverse weather conditions demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art semantic segmentation algorithms in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The method is computationally efficient and can be easily integrated into existing computer vision systems for various applications such as autonomous driving and surveillance.
This paper proposes a novel method for self-supervised learning using region-of-interest guided supervoxel inpainting.
The method leverages the concept of supervoxels to divide an image into coherent regions, and then inpaints missing regions within these supervoxels.
The proposed approach utilizes a region-of-interest guidance mechanism to prioritize the inpainting process, focusing on important regions of the image.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing self-supervised learning techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The findings suggest that region-of-interest guided supervoxel inpainting can be a valuable tool for self-supervised learning tasks.
In medical image segmentation tasks, the presence of corrupted labels and domain shift can significantly degrade the performance of deep learning models.
This paper proposes a novel Cross-denoising Network (CDN) to address these challenges.
CDN consists of two denoising modules: a label denoising module and a feature denoising module.
The label denoising module utilizes a self-supervised learning strategy to estimate the true labels from the corrupted labels.
The feature denoising module employs a domain adaptation technique to align the feature distributions between the source and target domains.

Experimental results on a medical image segmentation dataset demonstrate that CDN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness against corrupted labels and domain shift.
This paper presents a novel approach for 3D medical image segmentation using elastic boundary projection.
The proposed method leverages the concept of elastic deformation to accurately delineate boundaries in medical images.
The algorithm starts by initializing a boundary surface and iteratively deforms it based on the image intensity gradients.
The deformation is guided by a set of elastic forces that ensure smooth and accurate boundary projection.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting various anatomical structures.
The proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of medical image segmentation and has the potential to improve clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper presents a novel approach for fast image segmentation called Super-BPD (Super Boundary-to-Pixel Direction).
The proposed method leverages the boundary-to-pixel direction information to improve the efficiency and accuracy of image segmentation.
The authors introduce a new boundary-to-pixel direction estimation algorithm that is able to accurately estimate the direction of each pixel in an image.
They then use this information to guide the segmentation process, resulting in faster and more accurate segmentation results.
The experimental results demonstrate that the Super-BPD method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both speed and accuracy.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation and offers a promising approach for fast and accurate segmentation.
Edge detection is a fundamental task in computer vision and image processing, with applications in various fields such as object recognition and scene understanding.
Traditional edge detection methods, such as the Canny edge detector, have been widely used due to their effectiveness and simplicity.
However, these methods often rely on handcrafted features and may not perform well on complex images with noise and texture.
In this paper, we propose a deep neural network architecture inspired by traditional edge detection methods.
Our network combines the strengths of both traditional methods and deep learning, leveraging the power of convolutional neural networks to learn features from raw image data.
We evaluate our proposed method on benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art edge detection algorithms.
The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance and outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Overall, our work bridges the gap between traditional edge detection methods and deep learning, providing a promising approach for edge detection in complex images.
This paper proposes a novel approach for segmenting eye fundus images using a deep neural convolution network (DNCN) with a convex shape prior.
The proposed method leverages the power of DNCN to extract high-level features from the images and incorporates a convex shape prior to improve the accuracy of the segmentation.
The convex shape prior is learned from a large dataset of annotated eye fundus images and is used to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment of various eye diseases by providing accurate and reliable segmentation of eye fundus images.
This paper proposes a novel approach for initializing the weights of a deep neural network for image segmentation tasks using meta-learning.

The authors argue that the choice of initial weights can greatly impact the performance of the network, and traditional random or pre-trained initializations may not be optimal for segmentation tasks.
They introduce a meta-learning framework that learns to initialize the weights of the network based on the characteristics of the specific segmentation task.
The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared against traditional initialization methods.
The results show that the meta-learned initializations consistently outperform the other methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the segmentation tasks.
The authors conclude that meta-learning can be a powerful tool for improving the initialization of deep neural networks for image segmentation.
This paper proposes a novel approach for segmentation across domains using importance-driven continual learning.
The authors argue that existing methods for domain adaptation in segmentation tasks often fail to generalize well to new domains due to the lack of importance weighting.
To address this issue, they introduce a framework that leverages importance-driven continual learning to adapt the segmentation model to new domains.
The proposed method incorporates a dynamic importance weighting mechanism that assigns higher weights to more important samples during training.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving state-of-the-art performance in segmentation across domains.
The authors conclude that importance-driven continual learning is a promising direction for improving the generalization capability of segmentation models in diverse domains.
Color image segmentation is an important task in computer vision and image processing.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for color image segmentation using adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) and fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering.
APSO is used to optimize the parameters of FCM, which helps in achieving better segmentation results.
The proposed method adaptively adjusts the inertia weight and acceleration coefficients of APSO based on the fitness values of the particles.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms and shows promising results for color image segmentation.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining large amounts of annotated medical images for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised few-shot learning approach for medical image segmentation.
Our method leverages a small amount of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data to improve the performance of the segmentation model.
We introduce a novel few-shot learning framework that combines a pre-trained segmentation network with a few-shot learning module.
The few-shot learning module is trained on a small labeled dataset and then fine-tuned on a large unlabeled dataset using a self-training strategy.
Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior segmentation performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Our approach shows promise for improving medical image segmentation in scenarios where labeled data is limited.
This paper presents a fast and fully octave convolutional neural network (CNN) for document image segmentation.
Document image segmentation is a crucial step in many document analysis tasks, such as optical character recognition and document understanding.
However, existing CNN-based methods for document image segmentation are often computationally expensive and require a large amount of memory.
To address these issues, we propose a fully octave CNN architecture that leverages octave convolutional layers to capture multi-scale information efficiently.
Our network achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets while being significantly faster and more memory-efficient than existing methods.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed approach for document image segmentation.

This paper presents a deep grouping model for unified perceptual parsing, which aims to simultaneously perform multiple visual tasks such as object detection, semantic segmentation, and instance segmentation.

The proposed model leverages the power of deep convolutional neural networks to learn hierarchical representations of visual data and uses a grouping mechanism to integrate information from different tasks.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance on various visual tasks, highlighting its effectiveness and versatility in unified perceptual parsing.
This paper presents a deep learning approach for automatic tracking of the tongue surface in real-time ultrasound videos.
Traditional methods for tongue tracking rely on contour-based techniques, which can be computationally expensive and prone to errors.
In this study, we propose a landmark-based approach that utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to detect and track specific landmarks on the tongue surface.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of ultrasound videos with manually annotated landmarks.
Experimental results show that our proposed method achieves high accuracy and real-time performance, outperforming traditional contour-based methods.
This landmark-based approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of tongue tracking in various applications, such as speech therapy and pronunciation training.
In many real-world applications, training data is often labeled with noise, which can significantly degrade the performance of machine learning models.
This paper proposes a novel approach to improve training on noisy structured labels.
The proposed method leverages the inherent structure in the labels to identify and correct noisy instances during training.
Specifically, a graph-based model is used to represent the label structure, and a noise detection algorithm is applied to identify noisy instances.
These noisy instances are then corrected using a label correction algorithm that takes into account the label structure.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the accuracy of machine learning models trained on noisy structured labels.
The proposed method provides a promising solution for training on noisy data in real-world applications.
This paper presents a variational image segmentation model based on normalized cut with adaptive similarity and spatial regularization.
The proposed model aims to accurately segment images by considering both the similarity between pixels and their spatial relationships.
The model incorporates an adaptive similarity measure that dynamically adjusts the weights of the similarity term based on the local image characteristics.
Additionally, a spatial regularization term is introduced to encourage smoothness in the segmentation results.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in achieving accurate and visually pleasing image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for performing arbitrary style transfer on portrait images using a neural network with an attention mechanism.
Style transfer is the process of applying the style of one image onto the content of another image.
Previous methods for style transfer have focused on general images, but this paper specifically addresses the challenges of applying style transfer to portrait images.

The proposed method utilizes an attention mechanism to selectively transfer the style to different regions of the portrait image, ensuring that the style is applied in a visually pleasing and coherent manner.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both visual quality and computational efficiency.

This work contributes to the field of computer vision by providing a new technique for performing style transfer on portrait images, which has potential applications in various domains such as art, photography, and entertainment.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, it remains challenging due to the complex and diverse nature of medical images.
In this paper, we propose a novel multi-scale self-guided attention mechanism for medical image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages the inherent hierarchical structure of medical images and incorporates self-guided attention to capture both local and global contextual information.
Experimental results on two publicly available medical image datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.

The proposed multi-scale self-guided attention mechanism has the potential to improve the performance of medical image segmentation and facilitate more accurate diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with spatial regularization, volume, and star-shape priori.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by incorporating spatial information, volume constraints, and star-shape priori into the CNN architecture.
The spatial regularization helps to preserve the spatial coherence of the segmented regions, while the volume constraint ensures that the segmented regions have a consistent volume.
The star-shape priori is used to guide the segmentation process by enforcing a star-shaped boundary for each segmented region.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various applications such as medical image analysis, object recognition, and scene understanding.
This paper proposes a novel approach for referring image segmentation using a dual convolutional LSTM network.
Referring image segmentation is the task of segmenting an object in an image based on a natural language expression that refers to the object.
The proposed network consists of two parallel convolutional LSTM networks, one for processing the image and the other for processing the language expression.
The two networks are then fused together to generate the final segmentation mask.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed network can be applied to various applications such as image understanding, object recognition, and scene understanding.
This paper presents a novel approach for volume preserving image segmentation using entropic regularization optimal transport (EROT) and its applications in deep learning.
The proposed method aims to preserve the volume of segmented regions while achieving accurate segmentation results.
EROT is utilized to measure the similarity between image regions and guide the segmentation process.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method through experiments on various datasets and compare it with existing segmentation techniques.
Additionally, the paper explores the application of volume preserving image segmentation in deep learning tasks, such as object detection and image synthesis.

The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and volume preservation, highlighting its potential for improving deep learning applications.
This paper presents a self-learning artificial intelligence (AI) framework for the segmentation and classification of skin lesion images.
The proposed framework utilizes a deep learning approach to automatically segment the skin lesions from the background.
The segmented images are then fed into a convolutional neural network (CNN) for classification into different categories of skin lesions.
