The framework incorporates a self-learning mechanism, where the AI system continuously learns from its own mistakes and improves its performance over time.

Experimental results on a large dataset of skin lesion images demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework, achieving high accuracy in both segmentation and classification tasks.
The self-learning AI framework has the potential to assist dermatologists in the diagnosis and treatment of skin lesions, leading to improved patient care and outcomes.
Deepfake technology has become increasingly sophisticated, making it difficult to detect manipulated content.
In this paper, we propose a method for detecting deepfake-forged contents using a separable convolutional neural network (CNN) and image segmentation.
The separable CNN is designed to capture both global and local features of the image, while the image segmentation technique helps to identify regions that have been manipulated.
We evaluate our method on a large dataset of deepfake images and compare it with existing detection methods.
The results show that our approach achieves high accuracy in detecting deepfake-forged contents, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods.
This research contributes to the development of effective techniques for combating the spread of deepfake content.
This paper presents a method for computing valid p-values for image segmentation using selective inference.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for computing p-values in this context often suffer from multiple testing issues, leading to inflated false positive rates.
The proposed method addresses this problem by leveraging selective inference, which allows for valid inference while controlling the false discovery rate.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various image segmentation datasets, showing improved accuracy compared to existing methods.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation by offering a reliable and statistically sound method for computing p-values.
This paper presents a novel approach for generating image collages using memory attention mechanisms.
The proposed method leverages a memory module to store and retrieve relevant image patches, which are then used to guide the generation of collages.
The memory module is trained to attend to specific image patches based on their relevance to the current collage generation task.
The generated collages can be either guided, where a target image is provided as input, or unguided, where the collage is generated without any specific target.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of collage quality and diversity.
Additionally, the memory attention mechanism allows for fine-grained control over the collage generation process, enabling users to specify desired visual attributes.
Overall, this work contributes to the field of image generation by introducing a memory attentive approach for generating guided and unguided image collages.
This paper presents a deep learning neural network approach for identifying cells' nuclei.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to accurately detect and classify nuclei in microscopic images.
The network is trained on a large dataset of annotated images and achieves high accuracy in identifying nuclei.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the deep learning approach in automating the identification of cells' nuclei, which can have significant applications in various fields such as medical diagnosis and biological research.
This paper proposes a method for utilizing clinically available delineations in radiotherapy treatment planning to improve the accuracy of CNN-based segmentation.
The authors demonstrate that by incorporating these delineations as additional input channels in the CNN architecture, the segmentation performance can be significantly enhanced.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of 100 patients and compared against traditional CNN-based segmentation methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves higher segmentation accuracy and outperforms the traditional methods in terms of Dice similarity coefficient and Hausdorff distance.

The findings of this study suggest that leveraging clinically available delineations can be a valuable strategy for improving the accuracy of CNN-based segmentation in radiotherapy treatment planning.
This paper presents a comprehensive study on optimizing the Dice score and Jaccard index for medical image segmentation.
The Dice score and Jaccard index are widely used evaluation metrics for measuring the accuracy of segmentation algorithms.
However, they have limitations in certain scenarios, such as imbalanced class distributions and partial overlap between the ground truth and predicted masks.
In this study, we propose novel modifications to the Dice score and Jaccard index to address these limitations.
We also provide theoretical explanations for the proposed modifications and demonstrate their effectiveness through extensive experiments on various medical image datasets.
Our results show that the optimized metrics outperform the traditional ones in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy.
These findings have significant implications for improving the performance of medical image segmentation algorithms and can potentially enhance the diagnosis and treatment of various diseases.
This paper presents U-Time, a fully convolutional network (FCN) designed for time series segmentation, specifically applied to sleep staging.
Sleep staging is the process of classifying different stages of sleep based on physiological signals.
U-Time utilizes a modified version of the U-Net architecture, which has been successful in image segmentation tasks.
The network is trained on a large dataset of polysomnography recordings and achieves state-of-the-art performance in sleep staging.
The authors also propose a novel loss function that incorporates both pixel-wise and sequence-wise information, improving the segmentation accuracy.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of U-Time in accurately segmenting sleep stages, making it a valuable tool for sleep research and clinical applications.
Scene parsing, the task of assigning semantic labels to each pixel in an image, is a challenging problem in computer vision.
In this paper, we propose a deep multiphase level set method for scene parsing.
Our method combines the advantages of deep learning and level set methods to achieve accurate and efficient scene parsing.
We first train a deep convolutional neural network to predict the initial level set function for each semantic class.
We then use the level set method to evolve the level set functions and refine the segmentation results.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
This paper presents NeurReg, a novel neural registration framework that combines deep learning and image registration techniques for accurate and efficient image segmentation.
NeurReg utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the spatial transformations between two images, enabling the alignment of anatomical structures for segmentation.

The proposed framework is trained on a large dataset of paired images and achieves state-of-the-art performance on various medical imaging tasks, including brain tumor segmentation and cardiac image analysis.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of NeurReg in improving the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation compared to traditional registration methods.
The proposed framework has the potential to significantly advance the field of medical image analysis and facilitate clinical decision-making.
Synthetic data has been widely used in medical image segmentation tasks to overcome the limitations of limited annotated data.
However, most existing methods require ground truth segmentation masks for the synthetic data, which can be time-consuming and expensive to obtain.
In this paper, we propose a novel method called SynSeg-Net that can perform synthetic segmentation without the need for target modality ground truth.

Our method leverages a cycle-consistent generative adversarial network (CycleGAN) to learn the mapping between synthetic and real images, and a segmentation network to perform segmentation on the synthetic images.
We evaluate our method on two different medical imaging datasets and compare it with existing methods that require ground truth segmentation masks.

The results show that our method achieves comparable segmentation performance to the existing methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in synthetic segmentation without target modality ground truth.
This paper proposes a novel approach for semantic segmentation using extremely weak supervision in the form of image-to-image translation.
The authors introduce a framework that leverages unpaired images from different domains to generate synthetic training data for semantic segmentation.

The proposed method utilizes a cycle-consistent adversarial network to learn the mapping between the source and target domains, while also ensuring that the generated images are consistent with the original input.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods, highlighting the potential of weakly supervised image-to-image translation for semantic segmentation tasks.
This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using deep learning by incorporating the Mumford-Shah loss functional.
The Mumford-Shah loss functional is a well-established method in image processing that aims to balance the fidelity to the input image and the smoothness of the segmentation.
By integrating this loss functional into the deep learning framework, the proposed method achieves more accurate and visually appealing image segmentation results.

The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, where it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and visual quality.
The paper also provides insights into the underlying mechanisms of the Mumford-Shah loss functional and its impact on the deep learning process.
Overall, this work contributes to the field of image segmentation by bridging the gap between traditional image processing techniques and deep learning methods.
Video segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves partitioning a video into different regions based on their visual characteristics.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semi-supervised video segmentation that exploits the temporal information present in videos.
We introduce a new temporal consistency loss function that encourages consistency between neighboring frames in the segmentation results.
We also propose a new training strategy that combines both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation performance.
Our experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Furthermore, our approach is computationally efficient and can be easily integrated into existing video segmentation pipelines.
Overall, our work highlights the importance of considering temporal information for video segmentation and provides a practical solution for semi-supervised video segmentation tasks.
This paper presents ACE-Net, a novel deep learning architecture for biomedical image segmentation.
ACE-Net combines contracting and expansive paths with augmented features to improve the accuracy and efficiency of segmentation tasks.
The contracting path captures high-level features through convolutional and pooling layers, while the expansive path reconstructs the segmented image using deconvolutional layers.
Augmented features are incorporated to enhance the representation of the image and improve segmentation performance.
Experimental results on various biomedical datasets demonstrate that ACE-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed architecture has the potential to advance biomedical image analysis and facilitate medical diagnosis and treatment.
This paper presents a novel approach for improving long-term visual localization by leveraging fine-grained segmentation networks.
The proposed method utilizes self-supervised segmentation to generate high-quality semantic segmentation maps, which are then used to enhance the localization accuracy of visual odometry systems.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various datasets, showing significant improvements in localization performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The results highlight the potential of fine-grained segmentation networks for advancing long-term visual localization capabilities.
Conv-MCD is a multi-task module designed for medical image segmentation tasks.
It is a plug-and-play module that can be easily integrated into existing convolutional neural network architectures.
The module utilizes a multi-channel decoder (MCD) to extract features from multiple scales and channels, improving the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation results.
Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that Conv-MCD outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.
The module can be easily adapted to different medical image segmentation tasks, making it a valuable tool for medical image analysis.
This paper presents AttentionBoost, a novel approach for learning what to attend in fully convolutional networks.
The proposed method leverages the concept of boosting to enhance the attention mechanism in these networks.
AttentionBoost introduces a new loss function that encourages the network to focus on informative regions of the input data.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that AttentionBoost significantly improves the performance of fully convolutional networks in tasks such as image classification and object detection.
The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results and outperforms existing attention mechanisms in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, AttentionBoost provides a promising approach for improving the attention mechanism in fully convolutional networks.
This paper presents a method called Pick-and-Learn for automatic quality evaluation of noisy-labeled image segmentation.
The proposed method aims to address the challenge of noisy labels in image segmentation datasets, which can significantly affect the performance of segmentation models.
The Pick-and-Learn method leverages a two-step process, where it first selects high-quality samples from the dataset using a novel uncertainty-based sampling strategy.
These selected samples are then used to train a quality evaluation model that can automatically assess the quality of segmentation labels.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the Pick-and-Learn method in improving the performance of image segmentation models by filtering out noisy labels.
The proposed method shows promising potential for practical applications in the field of image segmentation.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, accurately segmenting medical images is challenging due to the complex and diverse nature of the images.
In this paper, we propose a novel network architecture called ET-Net, which stands for Edge-aTtention guidance Network.
ET-Net utilizes an attention mechanism to guide the segmentation process by focusing on the edges of the objects in the image.
This attention mechanism helps the network to better capture the boundaries and details of the objects, leading to improved segmentation accuracy.
We evaluate the performance of ET-Net on several medical image segmentation tasks, including brain tumor segmentation and lung nodule segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that ET-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of the different components of ET-Net.
Overall, our proposed ET-Net provides a generic and effective solution for medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents an efficient 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) for action/object segmentation in videos.
The proposed network architecture leverages the temporal information in videos by incorporating 3D convolutions, which capture both spatial and temporal features.
To improve efficiency, the network utilizes a lightweight backbone network and employs dilated convolutions in the decoder module.
The proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets for action/object segmentation in videos, while maintaining a low computational cost.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed network for action/object segmentation in videos.
This paper presents a stereo-based terrain traversability analysis method using normal-based segmentation and superpixel surface analysis.
The proposed method aims to accurately classify terrain regions into traversable and non-traversable areas.
The normal-based segmentation technique is used to segment the terrain into homogeneous regions based on the surface normals.
Superpixel surface analysis is then performed to extract features from the segmented regions.
These features are used to train a support vector machine classifier to classify the terrain regions.
Experimental results on real-world stereo images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately analyzing terrain traversability.
The proposed method can be applied in various applications such as autonomous navigation and robotic exploration.
This paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of deep learning techniques for image segmentation.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Deep learning has emerged as a powerful approach for image segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art results in various applications.

This paper reviews the key concepts and methodologies of deep learning for image segmentation, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), fully convolutional networks (FCNs), and U-Net architectures.
It also discusses popular loss functions, data augmentation techniques, and evaluation metrics used in deep learning-based image segmentation.
Furthermore, the paper explores recent advancements and challenges in the field, such as weakly supervised and semi-supervised learning, domain adaptation, and multi-modal segmentation.
Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of deep learning techniques for image segmentation, serving as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field.
This paper presents a general framework for complex network-based image segmentation.
The proposed framework leverages the power of complex networks to model the relationships between image pixels and their neighboring pixels.
The framework consists of three main steps: network construction, feature extraction, and segmentation.
In the network construction step, a graph is constructed where each pixel represents a node and the edges represent the relationships between neighboring pixels.
In the feature extraction step, various features are extracted from the network to capture the local and global characteristics of the image.
Finally, in the segmentation step, a clustering algorithm is applied to the extracted features to partition the image into different regions.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework compared to existing methods.
The proposed framework provides a flexible and powerful tool for image segmentation tasks in various domains.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning image dehazing models specifically for segmentation tasks.
The proposed method leverages a deep learning framework to train a dehazing model that can effectively enhance hazy images while preserving important details for subsequent segmentation tasks.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, showing significant improvements in segmentation performance compared to existing dehazing methods.
The results highlight the potential of incorporating image dehazing models into segmentation pipelines to enhance the accuracy and robustness of segmentation algorithms.
This paper presents a method for segmenting retinal images using fully convolutional networks (FCNs).
The proposed approach involves training FCNs on patches extracted from retinal images and then using these trained networks to segment the entire retinal image.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their method by comparing it to other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques on a publicly available dataset of retinal images.
The results show that the proposed method achieves superior segmentation accuracy and outperforms other methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
The authors conclude that FCNs can be successfully applied to retinal image segmentation and offer a promising approach for this task.
Automated skin lesion segmentation is an important task in computer-aided diagnosis systems for skin cancer.
However, the lack of a gold standard and the subjective nature of lesion delineation make it challenging to evaluate the performance of segmentation algorithms.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to handle inter-annotator agreement in automated skin lesion segmentation.
Our method utilizes a consensus-based approach, where multiple annotators independently segment the same set of skin lesion images.
We then calculate the inter-annotator agreement using various metrics, such as Dice coefficient and Jaccard index.
Based on the agreement scores, we develop a weighting scheme to assign higher weights to more reliable annotators.
Finally, we use these weighted annotations to train a deep learning model for automated skin lesion segmentation.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that our approach improves the segmentation accuracy compared to using annotations from all annotators equally.

Our method provides a practical solution to handle inter-annotator agreement in automated skin lesion segmentation, which can contribute to the development of more accurate computer-aided diagnosis systems for skin cancer.
Semantic segmentation is an important task in remote sensing imagery analysis, as it allows for the identification and classification of different objects and regions within an image.
However, existing methods often struggle with accurately segmenting boundaries between different classes.
In this paper, we propose a novel boundary loss function that addresses this issue by penalizing errors in boundary prediction.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art approaches.
Our results demonstrate that the proposed boundary loss significantly improves the accuracy of semantic segmentation, particularly in challenging scenarios with complex boundaries.
Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of remote sensing imagery analysis and has potential applications in various fields such as urban planning and environmental monitoring.
This paper explores the concept of diversity in machine learning and its implications for the field.
It discusses the importance of diversity in training data, algorithms, and models, and how it can lead to more robust and fair machine learning systems.
The paper also examines the challenges and limitations of achieving diversity in machine learning, such as biases in data collection and algorithmic decision-making.
It concludes with recommendations for researchers and practitioners to promote diversity in machine learning and mitigate its potential negative effects.

Overall, this paper contributes to the growing body of literature on the ethical and social implications of machine learning and highlights the need for diversity as a fundamental principle in the development and deployment of these systems.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image or video sequence.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic segmentation of video sequences using Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) networks.
We leverage the spatio-temporal information present in video sequences by extending the ConvLSTM architecture to incorporate both convolutional and recurrent layers.
Our model is trained on a large dataset of annotated video sequences and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets.
We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in real-world scenarios by applying it to a video surveillance task.
Our results show that the proposed ConvLSTM-based approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of semantic segmentation by introducing a new and effective method for analyzing video sequences.
This paper proposes a novel approach for cardiac cine magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation using a distance map regularized convolutional neural network (CNN).

The proposed method incorporates a distance map regularization term into the loss function of the CNN, which encourages the network to learn the spatial relationships between different regions in the image.
Experimental results on a large dataset of cardiac cine MR images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the clinical diagnosis and treatment planning for cardiovascular diseases.
Semantic segmentation plays a crucial role in pathology image analysis, enabling accurate identification and classification of different tissue structures.
However, the inherent complexity and variability of pathology images pose significant challenges for existing segmentation methods.
In this paper, we propose an Adaptive Weighting Multi-Field-of-View Convolutional Neural Network (AW-MF-CNN) for semantic segmentation in pathology.
The AW-MF-CNN leverages multiple field-of-view scales to capture both local and global contextual information, while adaptively weighting the contributions of each scale based on the image content.
We evaluate the proposed method on a large dataset of pathology images and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation approaches.

The experimental results demonstrate that the AW-MF-CNN achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness, highlighting its potential for improving pathology image analysis and diagnosis.
This paper presents a novel approach for efficient transmission and accurate segmentation of 3D medical images in cloud-based systems.
The proposed method utilizes machine vision techniques to guide the compression process, resulting in reduced data size while preserving important image features.
The compressed images are then transmitted to the cloud for storage and further analysis.
Additionally, the paper introduces a segmentation algorithm that leverages the compressed images to accurately identify and delineate anatomical structures.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in terms of compression ratio, transmission time, and segmentation accuracy, making it a promising solution for cloud-based medical image analysis.
Auto-DeepLab is a hierarchical neural architecture search (NAS) method for semantic image segmentation.
It aims to automatically discover the optimal neural network architecture for this task.
The proposed method consists of two stages: a coarse-grained search and a fine-grained search.
In the coarse-grained search, a search space is defined by stacking multiple cells, each containing a set of candidate operations.
A reinforcement learning algorithm is then used to search for the best cell architecture.
In the fine-grained search, the best cell architecture is used as a building block to construct the final network architecture.

The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in automatically designing neural network architectures for semantic image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for generating realistic vehicle images that blend seamlessly with their surroundings.
The proposed method leverages deep learning techniques to learn the contextual information of the environment and incorporate it into the generated vehicle images.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments and comparisons with existing methods.
The results show that the generated vehicle images exhibit a high level of realism and coherence with the surrounding environment.
This research has significant implications for various applications, such as virtual reality, autonomous driving, and computer graphics.
This paper presents a novel approach for brain segmentation on dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion magnetic resonance (MR) head scans with abnormal brain anatomy.
The proposed method utilizes a cumulative sum (CUSUM) filter to enhance the accuracy of brain segmentation in cases where the brain anatomy deviates from the normal structure.
The CUSUM filter is applied to the perfusion MR images to detect and correct for artifacts and noise, improving the quality of the segmentation results.
Experimental results on a dataset of abnormal brain anatomy cases demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting the brain regions.

The CUSUM filter for brain segmentation on DSC perfusion MR head scans with abnormal brain anatomy has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment planning for patients with brain abnormalities.
This paper presents a method for interactive segmentation of medical images using fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs).
The proposed approach allows users to interactively refine the segmentation results by providing feedback during the segmentation process.
The FCN model is trained on a large dataset of annotated medical images and is able to accurately segment various anatomical structures.
The interactive segmentation is achieved by incorporating user feedback into the FCN model through a novel feedback mechanism.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and efficient segmentation.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, which is crucial for various medical applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting multiple surfaces and objects in knee MRI scans using learning-based cost functions.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of 3D and 4D techniques to accurately identify and segment different structures in the knee joint.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach by applying it to data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, a large-scale study on knee osteoarthritis.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
This research has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment of knee osteoarthritis by providing more accurate and detailed information about the joint structures.
This paper presents a novel approach for left atrium segmentation in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using a combination of global shape priors and local intensity priors.
The proposed method utilizes a mixture modeling framework to integrate both types of priors, allowing for accurate and robust segmentation of the left atrium.
The global shape priors are learned from a training dataset using a shape model, while the local intensity priors are learned using an autoencoder.
The mixture model is then trained using a combination of the shape and intensity priors, and is used to segment the left atrium in new MRI images.
Experimental results on a dataset of cardiac MRI images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve clinical diagnosis and treatment planning for patients with left atrium abnormalities.
This paper presents a novel approach for multi-modal image segmentation using a hyper-densely connected convolutional neural network (CNN) called HyperDense-Net.
The proposed network architecture incorporates dense connections at multiple levels to enhance information flow and improve segmentation accuracy.
The HyperDense-Net is trained and evaluated on a dataset consisting of multi-modal medical images, achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting multi-modal images, highlighting its potential for various medical imaging applications.
This paper presents a method for dense 3D visual mapping using semantic simplification.
The proposed method leverages semantic information to simplify the dense 3D map representation, reducing the computational complexity and memory requirements.
The method utilizes a deep neural network to extract semantic information from the input images and incorporates it into the mapping process.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the computational and memory costs.
The method has potential applications in various fields such as robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous navigation.
This paper presents a rule-based hybrid approach for segmenting brain MRI images.
The proposed method combines both rule-based and machine learning techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of brain MRI segmentation.
The rule-based approach uses a set of predefined rules to identify and classify different brain structures, while the machine learning approach is used to refine the segmentation results.
The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and efficiency compared to existing segmentation methods.
The proposed method can be used in various applications, such as brain tumor detection and neuroimaging analysis.
This paper presents a novel approach for neuron segmentation in electron microscopy (EM) images using learning metric graphs.
Neuron segmentation is a crucial step in understanding the structure and connectivity of neural circuits.
Traditional methods for neuron segmentation rely on manual annotation or thresholding techniques, which are time-consuming and prone to errors.
In this work, we propose a learning-based approach that leverages the power of metric graphs to accurately segment neurons in EM images.
We first construct a graph representation of the image, where each node corresponds to a pixel and edges represent the similarity between pixels.
We then learn a metric on this graph using a deep neural network, which captures the underlying structure of the neurons.
Finally, we use this learned metric to perform graph-based segmentation, where nodes are grouped into connected components corresponding to individual neurons.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Our method has the potential to significantly advance the field of connectomics by enabling automated and accurate segmentation of neurons in large-scale EM images.
This paper presents a novel approach for joint shape learning and segmentation of medical images using a minimalistic deep network.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to simultaneously learn the shape and segment the objects of interest in medical images.
The network architecture is designed to be lightweight and efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image analysis tasks, leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
This paper presents a novel decoding method called Cascade Decoder for biomedical image segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a cascade structure to iteratively refine the segmentation results.
It incorporates both local and global information to improve the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation.
The Cascade Decoder is designed to be universal, meaning it can be applied to various biomedical image segmentation tasks without the need for task-specific modifications.
Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that the Cascade Decoder outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to significantly advance biomedical image segmentation research and contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable medical imaging systems.
This paper presents a novel approach to iris recognition using image segmentation and retrained off-the-shelf deep neural networks.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of iris recognition systems by leveraging the power of deep learning techniques.
The authors first perform image segmentation to isolate the iris region from the rest of the image.
They then employ pre-trained deep neural networks, which have been retrained on a large dataset of iris images, to extract features from the segmented iris region.
The extracted features are then used for iris recognition.
Experimental results on a benchmark iris dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high recognition accuracy and outperforming existing methods.
The proposed method shows promise for real-world applications of iris recognition, such as biometric authentication and surveillance systems.
This paper presents a novel approach for semantic segmentation of 3D magnetic resonance (MR) images using a holistic decomposition convolution (HDC) method.

The proposed method aims to address the challenges of accurately segmenting complex anatomical structures in MR images by decomposing the input image into multiple scales and capturing both local and global contextual information.
The HDC method combines a multi-scale feature extraction module with a holistic decomposition module, which effectively captures the hierarchical structure of the input image.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed HDC method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

The findings of this study suggest that the HDC method has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of semantic segmentation in 3D MR images, which can have significant implications for clinical applications such as tumor detection and treatment planning.
SwipeCut is a novel interactive segmentation method that aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method utilizes diversified seed proposals generated through a swipe-based user interaction, allowing users to quickly and easily provide initial segmentation guidance.
These seed proposals are then used to generate a diverse set of candidate segmentations, which are refined through an iterative optimization process.
Experimental results demonstrate that SwipeCut outperforms existing interactive segmentation methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and user efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to significantly enhance the performance of various computer vision applications that rely on accurate image segmentation.

The paper presents a novel approach for efficiently computing matrix-vector products for the graph Laplacian of fully connected networks using the Non-uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NFFT) and Krylov methods.
The proposed method leverages the inherent structure of fully connected networks to reduce the computational complexity of the matrix-vector product.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy.
The findings of this study have implications for various applications in graph analysis and network science.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting infant brain MRI scans using deep 3D fully convolutional DenseNets.
The proposed method utilizes exclusive independent probability estimation to improve the accuracy of segmentation.
The DenseNets architecture is employed to capture both local and global features of the MRI scans.
The method is evaluated on a dataset of iso-intense infant brain MRI scans and achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of segmentation accuracy.

The proposed approach shows promise for improving the segmentation of infant brain MRI scans, which can have significant implications for early diagnosis and treatment of neurological disorders in infants.
This paper presents a novel approach for brain tumor segmentation using an ensemble of 3D U-Nets and overall survival prediction using radiomic features.
The proposed method combines the strengths of multiple 3D U-Nets to improve the accuracy of tumor segmentation.
Additionally, radiomic features extracted from the segmented tumor regions are used to predict the overall survival of patients.
The experimental results demonstrate that the ensemble of 3D U-Nets achieves superior segmentation performance compared to individual U-Nets.
Furthermore, the radiomic features show promising predictive power for overall survival.
This research contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing an effective and accurate method for brain tumor segmentation and survival prediction.
This paper presents a novel approach for joint segmentation and localization of foreground objects in videos and images.
The proposed method utilizes a clustering algorithm to group pixels or regions that belong to the foreground object, thereby enabling accurate segmentation and localization.
The algorithm takes into account both spatial and temporal information to effectively handle the challenges posed by dynamic scenes and object motion.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach compared to existing methods.
The proposed method has potential applications in various domains such as video surveillance, object tracking, and image analysis.
This paper presents a novel hybrid deep attention-aware network called RA-UNet for the extraction of liver and tumor regions in CT scans.
The proposed network combines the strengths of both U-Net and attention mechanisms to improve the accuracy and efficiency of liver and tumor segmentation.
The attention mechanism is used to highlight important features and suppress irrelevant information, while the U-Net architecture enables effective feature extraction and segmentation.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed RA-UNet outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed network has the potential to assist radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment planning of liver diseases.
This paper presents a fast graph-cut based optimization method for dense deformable registration of volume images.
The proposed method aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of existing registration algorithms by incorporating a graph-cut optimization framework.
The method utilizes a graph representation of the registration problem and formulates it as a minimum cut problem.
By solving this problem using a graph-cut algorithm, the proposed method is able to find an optimal deformation field that aligns the input images.
Experimental results on a variety of medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing registration algorithms.
The proposed method shows promise for practical applications in medical image analysis and computer-aided diagnosis.
This paper presents a novel domain adaptation framework for medical image segmentation.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in various clinical applications, but it often suffers from the lack of labeled data in the target domain.
To address this issue, we propose a domain adaptation framework that leverages labeled data from a source domain and unlabeled data from the target domain.
Our framework consists of two main components: a feature extractor and a domain classifier.
The feature extractor is trained to learn domain-invariant representations by minimizing the discrepancy between the source and target domains.
The domain classifier is then trained to distinguish between the source and target domains based on the learned representations.
By iteratively updating the feature extractor and domain classifier, our framework effectively adapts the segmentation model to the target domain.
We evaluate our framework on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods.

The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in improving the segmentation performance on the target domain, even when there is a significant domain shift between the source and target domains.
Overall, our proposed framework provides a promising solution for medical image segmentation in scenarios where labeled data in the target domain is limited.
Interactive image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurately segmenting objects of interest from an image with user interaction.
In this paper, we propose a fully convolutional two-stream fusion network for interactive image segmentation.
The network consists of two streams: a segmentation stream and an interaction stream.
The segmentation stream is responsible for generating initial segmentation masks, while the interaction stream is used to refine the segmentation masks based on user input.
We introduce a novel fusion module that combines the outputs of the two streams to produce the final segmentation result.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance in interactive image segmentation.
Cloud detection and segmentation in satellite imagery is a crucial task for various applications, including weather forecasting and climate studies.
In this paper, we propose an effective cloud detection and segmentation algorithm based on gradient analysis.
The algorithm utilizes the gradient information of the satellite imagery to identify cloud regions accurately.

We apply this algorithm to improve the performance of the PERSIANN-CCS (Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using Artificial Neural Networks-Cloud Classification System) for cloud detection and segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The improved PERSIANN-CCS with our algorithm achieves higher accuracy in cloud detection and segmentation, leading to more accurate precipitation estimation.
This research contributes to the advancement of cloud detection and segmentation techniques in satellite imagery and enhances the performance of the PERSIANN-CCS system.
This paper presents a novel approach for 3D segmentation using the exponential logarithmic loss function.
The proposed method addresses the challenge of highly unbalanced object sizes in 3D segmentation tasks.
The exponential logarithmic loss function is designed to penalize false positives and false negatives differently based on the size of the objects.

Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to object size variations.
The findings of this study have implications for improving the performance of 3D segmentation algorithms in various applications, such as medical imaging and autonomous driving.
This paper presents a novel time series graph cut image segmentation scheme for liver tumors.
The proposed method utilizes the temporal information of the tumor region in a series of images to improve the accuracy of segmentation.
The scheme consists of three main steps: pre-processing, graph construction, and graph cut optimization.
In the pre-processing step, the images are enhanced and normalized to improve the contrast and remove noise.
Then, a graph is constructed using the normalized images, where each pixel is represented as a node and the edges represent the similarity between pixels.
Finally, the graph cut optimization is performed to segment the liver tumors from the background.
Experimental results on a dataset of liver tumor images demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves higher accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment planning of liver tumors.
YouTube-VOS is a large-scale video object segmentation benchmark that aims to advance the state-of-the-art in this field.
The benchmark consists of a diverse set of 4,453 YouTube videos, each containing multiple annotated object masks.
The dataset is carefully curated to cover a wide range of object categories, motion patterns, and video quality.
The paper presents the details of the dataset, including the annotation process and evaluation metrics.
Additionally, the authors provide an analysis of the current state-of-the-art methods on the benchmark and highlight the challenges and opportunities for future research in video object segmentation.
The YouTube-VOS benchmark is expected to facilitate the development of more accurate and robust algorithms for video object segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach to iris recognition using a database of iris images obtained in visible light using a smartphone camera.
The proposed method leverages the advancements in smartphone camera technology to capture high-quality iris images in visible light, eliminating the need for specialized iris recognition hardware.
The paper describes the image acquisition process and the preprocessing steps applied to enhance the quality of the iris images.
The iris recognition algorithm is based on a combination of feature extraction and matching techniques, which are optimized for visible light iris images.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high recognition accuracy on a dataset of iris images captured using a smartphone camera.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the development of iris recognition systems that can be easily deployed using widely available smartphone technology.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting microscopy data to identify nuclei in divergent images.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of image processing techniques and machine learning algorithms to accurately detect and segment nuclei in various types of microscopy images.
The approach involves pre-processing the images to enhance contrast and remove noise, followed by feature extraction and selection.
A support vector machine classifier is then trained on a labeled dataset to classify pixels as either nucleus or non-nucleus.
The segmented nuclei are further refined using morphological operations and post-processing techniques.
The proposed method is evaluated on a diverse set of microscopy images and compared with existing segmentation techniques.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting nuclei in divergent microscopy images.
This paper presents a novel approach called Concept Mask for large-scale segmentation from semantic concepts.
The proposed method leverages the power of semantic concepts to generate accurate and detailed segmentation masks.
The authors introduce a concept embedding network that learns to encode semantic concepts into a continuous vector space.
This embedding is then used to guide the segmentation network to produce high-quality masks.
The authors evaluate their approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing methods.
The Concept Mask approach shows promise for advancing the field of large-scale segmentation and has potential applications in various domains such as computer vision and image analysis.
This paper presents a 3D coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation.
The proposed framework utilizes a deep learning approach to segment medical images into different anatomical structures.
The framework consists of two stages: a coarse segmentation stage and a fine segmentation stage.
In the coarse segmentation stage, a 3D convolutional neural network is used to generate an initial segmentation map.
This map is then refined in the fine segmentation stage using a 3D conditional random field model.
The proposed framework is evaluated on a dataset of volumetric medical images and compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The results show that the proposed framework achieves superior segmentation accuracy and outperforms other methods in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper presents a novel approach for volumetric medical image segmentation that can potentially improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis.
Thalamus segmentation is an important task in neuroimaging research, as it allows for the identification and analysis of specific thalamic nuclei.
In this paper, we propose a novel multi-contrast MRI approach to thalamus segmentation.
Our method combines T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted images to improve the accuracy and robustness of thalamus segmentation.
We first preprocess the images to enhance the contrast and remove noise.
Then, we use a combination of intensity-based and atlas-based segmentation techniques to delineate the thalamus boundaries.
We evaluate our method on a dataset of 50 subjects and compare the results with manual segmentations performed by experts.
Our results show that the proposed multi-contrast MRI approach achieves high accuracy and outperforms existing methods in thalamus segmentation.
This approach has the potential to improve our understanding of thalamic nuclei and their role in various neurological disorders.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in various clinical applications.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called UNet++, which is a nested U-Net architecture for medical image segmentation.
The UNet++ architecture consists of multiple U-Net modules that are connected in a nested manner, allowing for better feature extraction and representation.
We evaluate the performance of UNet++ on three different medical image segmentation tasks and compare it with other state-of-the-art architectures.
The experimental results demonstrate that UNet++ outperforms other architectures in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct an ablation study to analyze the impact of different components in the UNet++ architecture.
Overall, our findings suggest that UNet++ is a promising architecture for medical image segmentation and can potentially improve the accuracy and efficiency of clinical applications.
This paper presents a data-driven approach for segmenting post-mortem iris images.

The segmentation of iris images is a crucial step in iris recognition systems, but it becomes challenging when dealing with post-mortem images due to the presence of various artifacts and degradation.
The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework to learn the features of post-mortem iris images and accurately segment the iris region.
The framework is trained on a large dataset of post-mortem iris images, which are manually annotated for segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The findings of this study contribute to the development of more reliable and efficient iris recognition systems for forensic applications.
This paper explores the role of function norms and regularization techniques in deep neural networks.
The authors investigate the impact of different function norms, such as L1 and L2 norms, on the performance and generalization of deep networks.
They also analyze the effect of regularization techniques, such as dropout and weight decay, on the function norms and the overall performance of the networks.

The experiments conducted on various datasets demonstrate that the choice of function norm and regularization technique significantly affects the network's performance and generalization capabilities.
The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the design and optimization of deep networks for various applications.
This paper presents a fully automatic method for segmenting the myocardium in contrast echocardiography sequences.
The method utilizes a combination of random forests and shape models to accurately and efficiently segment the myocardium.
The proposed method is able to handle variations in image quality and contrast enhancement, and achieves high segmentation accuracy compared to manual segmentation.
The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method for clinical applications such as assessing myocardial function and diagnosing cardiac diseases.
This paper presents a real-time prediction model for segmentation quality in image processing tasks.
The proposed model utilizes a deep learning approach to predict the quality of image segmentation results without the need for ground truth labels.
The model is trained on a large dataset of segmented images and their corresponding quality scores.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high accuracy in predicting segmentation quality in real-time.

The model can be integrated into existing image processing systems to provide real-time feedback on the quality of segmentation results, enabling users to make informed decisions and improve the overall performance of image processing tasks.
This paper proposes a novel approach called Concurrent Spatial and Channel Squeeze & Excitation (CSCSE) for improving the performance of fully convolutional networks (FCNs).
The CSCSE method combines the spatial and channel squeeze & excitation operations, which are commonly used in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to enhance the representation power of FCNs.
The spatial squeeze & excitation operation captures the spatial dependencies within feature maps, while the channel squeeze & excitation operation captures the channel-wise dependencies.

By concurrently applying both operations, the CSCSE method effectively captures both spatial and channel-wise dependencies, leading to improved feature representation and better performance in various computer vision tasks.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed CSCSE method in improving the performance of FCNs compared to existing methods.
This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation called Coarse to Fine Context Memory (CFCM).
The CFCM method leverages the coarse-to-fine strategy to capture both global and local context information for accurate segmentation.
It consists of two main components: a coarse context memory module and a fine context memory module.

The coarse context memory module captures global context information by aggregating features from multiple scales, while the fine context memory module focuses on local context information by incorporating features from neighboring pixels.
The proposed CFCM method achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for 3D shape segmentation using Shape Fully Convolutional Networks (SFCNs).
The proposed method leverages the advantages of both volumetric and surface-based representations of 3D shapes to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation.
The SFCN architecture is designed to capture both local and global shape features by combining volumetric and surface convolutional layers.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed SFCN framework shows great potential for various applications in 3D shape analysis and understanding.
The paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture called Attention U-Net for automatic pancreas segmentation in abdominal CT scans.
The proposed architecture incorporates an attention mechanism that allows the network to focus on relevant regions of the input image, improving the accuracy of pancreas segmentation.
The attention mechanism is integrated into the U-Net architecture by introducing a gating mechanism that learns to assign importance weights to different spatial locations.
The proposed Attention U-Net is trained and evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans, achieving state-of-the-art performance in pancreas segmentation.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the attention mechanism in guiding the network to focus on the pancreas region, leading to improved segmentation accuracy.

The proposed architecture has the potential to enhance the performance of automated pancreas segmentation algorithms, which can have significant implications for clinical applications such as surgical planning and disease diagnosis.
This paper presents a novel approach for interactive medical image segmentation using point-based interaction and sequential patch learning.
The proposed method allows users to provide input in the form of points on the image, which are then used to guide the segmentation process.
The system learns from these user interactions by sequentially selecting patches from the image and updating the segmentation model.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The approach has the potential to improve the usability and performance of medical image segmentation systems, making them more accessible and effective for clinical applications.
This paper presents a Matlab implementation of a machine vision algorithm for evaluating ballast degradation.
The algorithm utilizes image processing techniques to analyze images of ballast samples and determine the level of degradation.
The implementation includes preprocessing steps such as image enhancement and noise reduction, as well as feature extraction and classification steps.
The algorithm is tested on a dataset of ballast images and the results are compared to manual evaluations.
The results show that the algorithm is able to accurately evaluate ballast degradation, with a high level of agreement with manual evaluations.
The Matlab implementation provides a user-friendly interface for researchers and practitioners to easily apply the algorithm to their own ballast samples.
Overall, this paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the machine vision algorithm for ballast degradation evaluation and provides a valuable tool for the railway industry.
This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised pathology image segmentation using representation learning with spherical K-means.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning and unsupervised clustering to automatically segment pathology images without the need for manual annotations.
The key idea is to learn a compact and discriminative representation of the image patches using a deep convolutional neural network.
The learned representations are then clustered using spherical K-means, which takes into account the spherical nature of the data.
Experimental results on a large dataset of pathology images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art segmentation performance.
The proposed approach has the potential to greatly simplify the process of pathology image analysis and improve the efficiency and accuracy of diagnosis.
This paper proposes a novel approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks using sample selection by relaxed upper confident bound.
The authors argue that current methods for training such networks often suffer from the problem of imbalanced training data, leading to poor performance on underrepresented organs.

To address this issue, they introduce a sample selection strategy based on the relaxed upper confident bound, which aims to select informative samples that can improve the network's performance on underrepresented organs.
The proposed method is evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and compared with several state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the segmentation accuracy for underrepresented organs, outperforming existing methods.
The authors conclude that the sample selection strategy based on relaxed upper confident bound is an effective approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on complex algorithms and large computational resources.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Compassionately Conservative Balanced Cuts (CCBC) for image segmentation.
The CCBC method combines the principles of compassion and conservatism to achieve a balanced and accurate segmentation.
We introduce a new objective function that takes into account both the similarity between pixels and the smoothness of the segmentation boundaries.
We also propose a new optimization algorithm that efficiently solves the CCBC objective function.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the CCBC method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Furthermore, we show that the CCBC method is robust to noise and can handle images with complex structures.
Overall, our work provides a new perspective on image segmentation and offers a promising solution for practical applications in computer vision.
This paper presents an adaptive strategy for superpixel-based region-growing image segmentation.

The proposed strategy aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process by dynamically adjusting the parameters of the region-growing algorithm based on the characteristics of the input image.
The strategy utilizes a set of image features, such as color and texture, to estimate the optimal parameters for each region-growing iteration.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the adaptive strategy outperforms traditional fixed-parameter approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed strategy has the potential to enhance the performance of region-growing image segmentation algorithms in various applications, such as object recognition and image analysis.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has various applications in fields such as medical imaging and object recognition.
In this paper, we propose a new active contour model called IEOPF (Inhomogeneities Estimated by Orthogonal Primary Functions) for image segmentation.
The model incorporates the estimation of inhomogeneities in the image using orthogonal primary functions.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model through experiments on synthetic and real-world images.
The results show that the IEOPF model outperforms existing active contour models in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially in the presence of inhomogeneities.
The proposed model has the potential to improve the performance of image segmentation algorithms in various applications.
This paper presents a survey of computer-aided knee joint magnetic resonance image (MRI) segmentation techniques.
MRI segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of knee joint diseases.
The survey provides an overview of the different approaches and algorithms used for knee joint MRI segmentation, including both traditional and deep learning-based methods.
The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of existing techniques and identifies potential areas for future research.

Overall, this survey aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the current state-of-the-art in computer-aided knee joint MRI segmentation and serve as a valuable resource for researchers and clinicians in the field.
Superpixel segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to group pixels into coherent regions.
In this paper, we propose an iterative spanning forest framework for superpixel segmentation.
The framework utilizes a graph-based representation of the image and iteratively constructs a spanning forest by merging adjacent regions.
We introduce a novel merging criterion based on the similarity between regions, which allows for the creation of compact and homogeneous superpixels.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed framework compared to state-of-the-art methods.
TernausNet is a deep learning model for image segmentation that combines the U-Net architecture with a VGG11 encoder pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset.
The U-Net architecture is known for its effectiveness in image segmentation tasks, while the VGG11 encoder provides a powerful feature extraction capability.
The pre-training on ImageNet allows the model to learn rich and generalizable representations of visual features.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that TernausNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in image segmentation tasks, outperforming other popular models.
The proposed model is computationally efficient and can be easily trained and deployed for a wide range of image segmentation applications.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.

In this paper, we propose a highly fused convolutional network (HFCN) for semantic segmentation, which combines the strengths of multiple convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to achieve improved performance.
We also introduce multiple soft cost functions to guide the training process and enhance the accuracy of the segmentation.
Our experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed HFCN with multiple soft cost functions outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
This approach has the potential to advance the field of semantic segmentation and contribute to various applications such as autonomous driving and medical imaging.
Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
While recent deep learning approaches have achieved impressive results in this task, they often struggle with accurately segmenting object boundaries.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to improve semantic image segmentation by incorporating boundary detection.
We introduce a new loss function that combines both semantic segmentation and boundary detection objectives, and train a deep neural network using this loss function.
Our experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the accuracy of semantic image segmentation, particularly in regions with complex boundaries.
Furthermore, we show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both boundary detection and semantic segmentation metrics.
Overall, our work highlights the importance of incorporating boundary information in semantic image segmentation and provides a promising direction for future research in this field.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields.
This paper presents an efficient evolutionary-based method for image segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a genetic algorithm to optimize the segmentation process.
The algorithm starts with an initial population of candidate solutions and iteratively evolves them using genetic operators such as selection, crossover, and mutation.
The fitness of each candidate solution is evaluated based on a fitness function that measures the quality of the segmentation.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method provides a promising approach for image segmentation and can be applied to various real-world applications.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting splenomegaly, a condition characterized by an enlarged spleen, using global convolutional kernels and conditional generative adversarial networks (GANs).
The proposed method leverages the power of global convolutional kernels to capture long-range dependencies in the input data, allowing for more accurate segmentation of splenomegaly.
Additionally, conditional GANs are employed to generate realistic and high-quality segmentation masks.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

This work contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing an effective and efficient solution for splenomegaly segmentation, which can aid in the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.
This paper presents a novel method for automatic color image segmentation using a square elemental region-based seeded region growing and merging approach.

The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of existing segmentation techniques by utilizing a square elemental region-based approach, which allows for more accurate and efficient segmentation.
The method starts by dividing the image into square elemental regions and then applies a seeded region growing algorithm to each region.
The regions are then merged based on a set of merging criteria to obtain the final segmentation result.
Experimental results on various color images demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing segmentation techniques.
The proposed method can be applied to various applications such as object recognition, image retrieval, and image editing.
This paper presents a novel approach called WAYLA (Wearable Eye-trAcked Lightfield Augmentation) for generating images based on eye movements.
The proposed system utilizes a wearable eye-tracking device to capture the user's eye movements and then generates images in real-time based on the captured data.
The generated images are displayed on a head-mounted display, providing an augmented reality experience for the user.
The authors conducted a user study to evaluate the effectiveness of WAYLA and found that it significantly improved the user's visual experience compared to traditional static images.
The results suggest that WAYLA has the potential to enhance various applications such as gaming, virtual reality, and visual communication.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical image analysis, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
In this paper, we propose a multi-modal convolutional neural network (CNN) for medical image segmentation, specifically focusing on image fusion schemes.
We compare three different fusion schemes: early fusion, late fusion, and hybrid fusion.
The proposed CNN architecture consists of two parallel pathways, one for each modality, followed by a fusion layer.
We evaluate the performance of the proposed method on two publicly available medical image datasets: the BraTS dataset for brain tumor segmentation and the ISIC dataset for skin lesion segmentation.
Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multi-modal CNN with hybrid fusion achieves superior segmentation performance compared to the other fusion schemes.
The proposed method shows promising potential for accurate and efficient medical image segmentation, which can aid in improving diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting historical document images using a combination of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and deep neural networks.
The proposed method leverages the topic modeling capabilities of LDA to initialize the deep neural network, which then learns to segment the document images into different regions of interest.
Experimental results on a dataset of historical documents demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of historical document analysis tasks such as text extraction and document understanding.
This paper presents a novel FPGA-based parallelized architecture for an efficient graph-based image segmentation algorithm.
The proposed architecture leverages the parallel processing capabilities of FPGAs to accelerate the segmentation process.
The algorithm is based on the graph-cut technique, which has been widely used in image segmentation tasks.
The parallelized architecture is designed to exploit the inherent parallelism in the algorithm, resulting in significant speedup compared to traditional sequential implementations.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed architecture, showing a substantial reduction in processing time while maintaining high segmentation accuracy.
The FPGA-based parallelized architecture presented in this paper provides a promising solution for real-time image segmentation applications.
DeepIGeoS is a deep interactive geodesic framework proposed for medical image segmentation.
The framework combines the advantages of deep learning and geodesic distance-based methods to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
