It incorporates a deep neural network architecture that is trained on a large dataset of annotated medical images.
The geodesic distance-based method is used to refine the segmentation results by incorporating spatial information and enforcing smoothness constraints.
The proposed framework is evaluated on various medical image datasets and compared with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The results demonstrate that DeepIGeoS achieves superior segmentation accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising tool for medical image analysis and clinical applications.
This paper presents a novel method for 4D multi-atlas label fusion using longitudinal images.
The proposed method utilizes the temporal information from longitudinal images to improve the accuracy of label fusion.
The method first aligns the longitudinal images using a non-rigid registration algorithm.
Then, a multi-atlas label fusion algorithm is applied to fuse the labels from multiple atlases onto the aligned images.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of brain MRI scans and compared with existing methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy in label fusion compared to existing methods.
This suggests that incorporating temporal information from longitudinal images can improve the accuracy of label fusion in medical imaging applications.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation based on iterative inference from conditional score estimation.
Our method leverages the power of deep neural networks to estimate the conditional score of each pixel given its context.
We then iteratively update the segmentation mask by maximizing the conditional score of each pixel.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the proposed method, shedding light on its strengths and limitations.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of image segmentation by introducing a new approach that combines the strengths of deep learning and iterative inference.
This paper presents a method for automatically generating datasets for crop and weeds detection using a model-based approach.
The proposed method leverages computer vision techniques and machine learning algorithms to generate synthetic images of crops and weeds in various environmental conditions.
The generated datasets are then used to train and evaluate deep learning models for crop and weeds detection.
The results show that the proposed method can generate datasets that are both fast and accurate, leading to improved performance in crop and weeds detection tasks.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of automated agricultural systems and can contribute to the improvement of crop yield and weed control.
This paper presents a locally adapting technique for boundary detection using image segmentation.
The proposed technique aims to improve the accuracy of boundary detection by considering local information in the image.
The technique utilizes image segmentation algorithms to divide the image into regions and then adapts the boundary detection process based on the characteristics of each region.
Experimental results show that the proposed technique outperforms existing methods in terms of boundary detection accuracy.
The locally adapting technique has the potential to be applied in various applications such as object recognition and scene understanding.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning aerial image segmentation from online maps.
The proposed method leverages the availability of high-resolution satellite imagery and the abundance of online maps to train a deep neural network for accurate segmentation of aerial images.
The authors introduce a new dataset consisting of aerial images and corresponding online maps, and use it to train a convolutional neural network.
The network is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting aerial images, and highlight the potential of online maps as a valuable resource for training deep learning models in the field of aerial image analysis.
This paper investigates the compactness, efficiency, and representation of 3D convolutional networks (ConvNets) in the context of brain parcellation as a pretext task.
Brain parcellation is a fundamental task in neuroimaging that involves dividing the brain into distinct regions based on anatomical or functional characteristics.
The authors propose a novel framework that leverages 3D ConvNets to perform brain parcellation and evaluate its performance on a large dataset of brain MRI scans.
The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high accuracy and efficiency in brain parcellation, while also providing meaningful representations of the brain regions.
The findings suggest that 3D ConvNets can be effectively utilized for brain parcellation tasks, offering a promising approach for neuroimaging research and clinical applications.
This paper proposes a novel loss function, called the Tversky loss function, for image segmentation using 3D fully convolutional deep networks.
The Tversky loss function is designed to address the class imbalance problem commonly encountered in medical image segmentation tasks.
The proposed loss function combines the Tversky index, which measures the similarity between two sets, with a weighting factor to account for the imbalance between foreground and background classes.

Experimental results on a dataset of brain MRI scans demonstrate that the Tversky loss function outperforms other commonly used loss functions in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to class imbalance.
The proposed approach shows promise for improving the performance of 3D fully convolutional deep networks in medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a dynamic graph-cuts method with integrated multiple feature maps for segmenting kidneys in ultrasound images.
The proposed method combines multiple feature maps, including intensity, texture, and shape features, to improve the accuracy and robustness of kidney segmentation.
The dynamic graph-cuts algorithm is used to iteratively refine the segmentation results by incorporating the feature maps.
Experimental results on a dataset of ultrasound images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to be used in clinical applications for kidney segmentation in ultrasound images.
DeepLab is a semantic image segmentation method that combines deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), atrous convolution, and fully connected conditional random fields (CRFs).
This paper presents the architecture and implementation details of DeepLab, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on the PASCAL VOC 2012 semantic image segmentation benchmark.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of atrous convolution in capturing multi-scale contextual information and propose a novel atrous spatial pyramid pooling module to further improve the performance.
They also introduce a fully connected CRF as a post-processing step to refine the segmentation results.
Experimental results show that DeepLab outperforms previous methods and achieves competitive performance with much faster inference time.
This paper presents a novel approach for object discovery in images based on cohesion measurement.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of color and texture features to calculate the cohesion of image regions.
The cohesion measurement is then used to identify cohesive regions, which are likely to correspond to objects in the image.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in discovering objects in images.
The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art object discovery methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of object discovery and offers a promising solution for automated object detection in images.
This paper presents a deep learning approach for multi-task medical image segmentation in multiple modalities.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture that is capable of simultaneously segmenting multiple anatomical structures in different imaging modalities.
The network is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, allowing it to learn from both labeled and unlabeled data.

Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in multi-task medical image segmentation across multiple modalities.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis, leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
This paper presents a method for structured learning of tree potentials in Conditional Random Fields (CRF) for image segmentation.
The authors propose a novel approach that combines the advantages of both discriminative and generative models.
The proposed method utilizes a tree-structured CRF model to capture the spatial dependencies between image pixels.
The authors also introduce a structured learning algorithm that optimizes the tree potentials based on a structured loss function.
Experimental results on various image segmentation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust segmentation results.
The proposed method shows promising potential for improving the performance of image segmentation algorithms in various applications.
This paper presents a novel algorithm for the ISIC 2017 Skin Lesion Segmentation Challenge, which aims to accurately segment skin lesions from dermoscopic images.
The proposed algorithm combines k-means clustering and an ensemble of regressions to achieve accurate and robust segmentation results.
The k-means clustering is used to initialize the ensemble of regressions, which then iteratively refines the segmentation boundaries.
Experimental results on the ISIC 2017 dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The algorithm also achieves competitive results in terms of computational efficiency.
Overall, the proposed algorithm provides a promising approach for skin lesion segmentation in clinical practice.
This paper proposes a novel approach for improving the accuracy of iterative estimation in medical image segmentation by learning normalized inputs.
The authors argue that traditional iterative estimation methods often suffer from the problem of input data heterogeneity, which can lead to suboptimal segmentation results.

To address this issue, the authors propose a two-step process: first, they learn a normalization function that maps input data to a normalized space, and then they perform iterative estimation in this normalized space.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on a dataset of medical images, showing that their method outperforms traditional iterative estimation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for improving the accuracy of medical image segmentation through the use of learned normalized inputs.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for image segmentation using overlapping group sparsity.
We formulate the problem as a sparse optimization problem and introduce a new regularization term that encourages group sparsity.
We also propose an efficient algorithm to solve the optimization problem.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving accurate and robust image segmentation.
Our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of image segmentation by introducing a new approach that leverages overlapping group sparsity for improved segmentation results.
This paper presents a novel approach for automatic prostate segmentation in ultrasound images using fine-grained recurrent neural networks (RNNs).
The proposed method leverages the temporal dependencies in ultrasound image sequences to improve the accuracy of prostate segmentation.
The RNNs are trained to learn the spatial and temporal features of the ultrasound images, and a fine-grained segmentation network is used to generate pixel-wise prostate segmentation masks.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The fine-grained RNNs provide a promising solution for automatic prostate segmentation in ultrasound images, which can potentially improve the diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer.
This paper presents a novel method for image segmentation using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) shape sampling with nonparametric shape priors.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques by incorporating shape information into the segmentation process.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various datasets, showing improved segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods.
The results suggest that MCMC shape sampling with nonparametric shape priors can be a valuable tool for image segmentation tasks.
Active contours, also known as snakes, are widely used in image processing and computer vision for object segmentation.
In this paper, we present a theoretical analysis of active contours on graphs.
We first introduce the concept of graphs and their representation in image processing.
We then discuss the mathematical formulation of active contours on graphs and their relationship with traditional active contours.
We analyze the properties of active contours on graphs, including their convergence, stability, and sensitivity to initialization.
We also propose a novel energy functional for active contours on graphs, which incorporates both local and global information.
Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on various image datasets.
Our theoretical analysis provides insights into the behavior of active contours on graphs and paves the way for further research in this area.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using combinatorial energy learning.
The proposed method leverages the power of combinatorial optimization techniques to efficiently solve the energy minimization problem in image segmentation.
The approach combines the strengths of both graph cuts and Markov random fields to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.
The combinatorial energy learning approach shows promise for advancing the field of image segmentation and has potential applications in various domains such as computer vision and medical imaging.
This paper presents a novel 4D light-field dataset and convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for material recognition.
The dataset consists of a large collection of light-field images captured from different viewpoints, allowing for the capture of both spatial and angular information.
The CNN architectures are designed to effectively exploit the 4D nature of the dataset, enabling accurate material recognition.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dataset and CNN architectures, achieving state-of-the-art performance on material recognition tasks.

The 4D light-field dataset and CNN architectures presented in this paper provide valuable resources for advancing the field of material recognition and can be used for various applications such as object recognition, scene understanding, and augmented reality.
This paper presents a novel approach for electron microscopy image segmentation using a semi-supervised hierarchical merge tree (SSHMT) algorithm.
The proposed method combines the advantages of both supervised and unsupervised learning techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation.
The SSHMT algorithm utilizes a hierarchical merge tree structure to represent the image and performs a series of merging operations based on both labeled and unlabeled data.
Experimental results on a dataset of electron microscopy images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation algorithms in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The SSHMT algorithm has the potential to significantly advance the field of electron microscopy image segmentation and facilitate further research in this area.
Superpixel Convolutional Networks (SPCNs) have been proposed as an effective approach for image segmentation tasks.
However, existing SPCNs suffer from limitations such as high computational complexity and limited receptive field.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Bilateral Inceptions for SPCNs, which addresses these limitations.
The Bilateral Inceptions architecture incorporates bilateral filtering and inception modules into the SPCN framework, enabling efficient and effective feature extraction.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the contributions of different components in our architecture.
Overall, our work provides a valuable contribution to the field of SPCNs and paves the way for further advancements in image segmentation.
This paper proposes a novel method for screen content image segmentation using sparse decomposition and total variation minimization.

The method aims to accurately separate the foreground and background regions in screen content images, which are commonly encountered in various applications such as video surveillance and image editing.
The proposed method first decomposes the input image into a sparse representation using a dictionary learning algorithm.
Then, a total variation minimization algorithm is applied to refine the segmentation result by promoting piecewise smoothness in the image.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in real-world applications that require accurate and efficient screen content image segmentation.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical image analysis, as it plays a vital role in various clinical applications.
Incorporating prior knowledge into the segmentation process can improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation results.
In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the existing methods that incorporate prior knowledge in medical image segmentation.
We categorize these methods into three main groups: statistical methods, shape-based methods, and deep learning-based methods.
We discuss the advantages and limitations of each approach and provide insights into future research directions.

This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of medical image segmentation, providing a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art techniques and highlighting the potential for further advancements in this area.
Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
Deep structured models have shown promising results in this task, but training them can be computationally expensive.
In this paper, we propose an efficient piecewise training approach for deep structured models for semantic segmentation.
Our method divides the training process into multiple stages, where each stage focuses on a specific region of the image.
We also introduce a novel loss function that encourages the model to learn both local and global context information.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance while significantly reducing training time and computational resources.
Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.

Existing methods typically focus on either category-level segmentation, which assigns a single label to each object category, or instance-level segmentation, which assigns a unique label to each individual object instance.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that bridges the gap between these two levels of segmentation.
Our method leverages both category-level and instance-level information to improve the accuracy and robustness of semantic image segmentation.
We achieve this by incorporating a category-level segmentation network and an instance-level segmentation network into a unified framework.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Our work provides a valuable contribution to the field of semantic image segmentation and opens up new possibilities for future research in this area.
This paper presents a fast semantic image segmentation method that incorporates high order context and guided filtering.
The proposed method utilizes high order contextual information to improve the accuracy of segmentation results.
Additionally, guided filtering is employed to refine the segmentation boundaries and enhance the overall quality of the segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The method is particularly effective in handling complex scenes with intricate object boundaries.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of semantic image segmentation by introducing a fast and accurate approach that leverages high order context and guided filtering.
This paper proposes a classifier-guided approach for top-down salient object detection.
The approach combines the strengths of both bottom-up and top-down methods to improve the accuracy and efficiency of salient object detection.
The classifier is trained to distinguish between salient and non-salient regions, and is used to guide the top-down process by providing saliency scores for each region.
Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The approach is also robust to various challenging scenarios, such as cluttered backgrounds and complex object shapes.
Overall, the classifier-guided approach offers a promising solution for top-down salient object detection.
This paper presents a fully-automatic method for synapse prediction and validation on a large data set.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of machine learning techniques and image processing algorithms to accurately identify and validate synapses in a high-throughput manner.
The method is applied to a large data set consisting of electron microscopy images, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately predicting and validating synapses.
The proposed method has the potential to significantly accelerate the process of synapse identification and validation, thereby facilitating the study of synaptic connectivity in the brain.
This paper proposes a novel approach for noisy image segmentation using a combination of kernelized weighted SUSAN (Smallest Univalue Segment Assimilating Nucleus) and fuzzy C-means clustering.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques in the presence of noise.

The kernelized weighted SUSAN algorithm is used to detect image regions with similar intensity values, while the fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm is employed to assign pixels to different clusters based on their similarity.

Experimental results on various noisy images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting noisy images and outperforming existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise.
This paper presents a novel approach for integrating inference and learning of neural factors in structural support vector machines (SVMs).
The proposed method combines the strengths of both neural networks and SVMs to improve the performance of structured prediction tasks.
The authors introduce a new neural factorization model that allows for efficient inference and learning of neural factors in SVMs.
They demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it to existing methods.
The results show that the integrated inference and learning of neural factors in SVMs outperforms other approaches in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of structured prediction and highlights the potential of combining neural networks and SVMs for improved performance.
This paper explores the use of graph entropies in the task of texture segmentation of images.
Texture segmentation is an important step in image analysis and understanding, as it allows for the identification and separation of different regions based on their texture properties.
The authors propose a novel approach that leverages graph entropies to capture the complexity and randomness of texture patterns in an image.
The proposed method is compared against existing state-of-the-art techniques on various benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately segmenting textures.
The findings of this study contribute to the field of image analysis and provide a new perspective on texture segmentation using graph entropies.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using regional active contours based on variational level sets and machine learning.
The proposed method combines the advantages of both variational level sets and machine learning techniques to achieve accurate and efficient image segmentation.
The variational level sets are used to model the contour evolution process, while the machine learning algorithm is employed to learn the regional information and guide the contour evolution.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method compared to existing approaches.
The proposed method has potential applications in medical imaging, computer vision, and other fields that require accurate and efficient image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach to message passing inference in deep learning models.
The authors propose a method called "Deeply Learning the Messages" (DLM) that aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of message passing algorithms.
The DLM method leverages the power of deep learning techniques to learn the messages exchanged between nodes in a graph-based model.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of DLM on various benchmark datasets and compare it with existing message passing algorithms.
The results show that DLM outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of DLM in the field of deep learning and graph-based models.
This paper presents a novel approach towards image segmentation using clustering techniques.
The proposed method combines the advantages of both k-means clustering and fuzzy c-means clustering algorithms to achieve improved segmentation results.
The algorithm starts by initializing the cluster centers using k-means clustering and then applies fuzzy c-means clustering to refine the segmentation.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting images.
The proposed method outperforms existing clustering-based image segmentation techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation and offers a promising approach for future research in this area.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical imaging analysis, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of various diseases.
Deep learning techniques have shown promising results in medical image segmentation due to their ability to learn complex patterns and features from large amounts of data.

This paper provides an overview of deep learning methods used for medical image segmentation, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and generative adversarial networks (GANs).
The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of deep learning in medical image segmentation, such as the need for large annotated datasets and the interpretability of deep learning models.

Finally, the paper presents future directions and potential applications of deep learning in medical image segmentation, including the integration of multi-modal data and the development of personalized medicine approaches.
This paper presents a novel approach to fuzzy image segmentation using an evolutionary algorithm with self-configuration.
Fuzzy image segmentation is a challenging task due to the inherent uncertainty and ambiguity in image data.
The proposed method combines the advantages of fuzzy logic and evolutionary algorithms to automatically adapt the parameters of the fuzzy system for each image.
The self-configuration process is achieved through a genetic algorithm that optimizes the membership functions and rules of the fuzzy system.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach compared to existing methods.
The self-configuration capability of the algorithm allows it to adapt to different image characteristics and improve segmentation accuracy.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of fuzzy image segmentation by introducing a self-configuring evolutionary algorithm that can automatically adapt to different image datasets.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning the parameters of Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) using the Bethe approximation and Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) decoding.
CRFs are widely used in various machine learning tasks, such as natural language processing and computer vision, due to their ability to model complex dependencies between variables.
However, learning the parameters of CRFs is a challenging task, especially when dealing with large datasets.
The proposed method leverages the Bethe approximation, which provides an efficient approximation of the partition function in CRFs, and combines it with MAP decoding to learn the parameters.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method offers a promising solution for learning CRFs in large-scale applications.
This paper presents a fast constraint propagation algorithm for image segmentation.
The algorithm utilizes a graph-based representation of the image and propagates constraints through the graph to refine the segmentation.
The proposed algorithm is able to handle large images and complex segmentation tasks efficiently.
Experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm achieves comparable or better segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing computation time.
The algorithm is also shown to be robust to noise and able to handle various types of images.
Overall, the proposed fast constraint propagation algorithm offers a promising approach for efficient and accurate image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised image segmentation using global and local criteria optimization based on Bayesian networks.
The proposed method combines both global and local information to achieve accurate and robust segmentation results.

The global criteria optimization is performed by maximizing the posterior probability of the segmentation given the image data, while the local criteria optimization is performed by maximizing the posterior probability of the segmentation given the local image features.
The Bayesian network is used to model the dependencies between the image data and the segmentation labels, allowing for efficient inference and optimization.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
This paper presents a highly efficient method for forward and backward propagation in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for pixelwise classification tasks.
The proposed method utilizes a novel algorithm that reduces the computational complexity of both forward and backward passes by exploiting the sparsity of the input data.
The algorithm achieves this by dynamically skipping the computation of non-activated neurons, resulting in significant speedup without sacrificing accuracy.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both computational efficiency and classification accuracy.
The findings of this study have important implications for the development of efficient CNN architectures for pixelwise classification tasks.
This paper presents a method for fast edge detection using structured forests.
The proposed method leverages the power of structured forests, which are ensembles of decision trees, to efficiently detect edges in images.
The authors introduce a novel edge detection algorithm that combines the strengths of structured forests with a fast edge filtering technique.
The algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and speed.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing edge detection methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of edge detection and offers a practical solution for real-time edge detection applications.

Open-set person re-identification is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to match individuals across non-overlapping camera views in an open-set scenario, where the gallery set may contain individuals not present in the probe set.
This paper proposes a novel approach for open-set person re-identification using a combination of deep learning and metric learning techniques.

The proposed method leverages a deep convolutional neural network to extract discriminative features from person images, and then uses a metric learning algorithm to learn a distance metric that can effectively measure the similarity between different individuals.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in handling the open-set person re-identification problem, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of both identification accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various real-world applications, such as video surveillance and person tracking.
This paper presents a near-optimal keypoint sampling method for fast pathological lung segmentation.
The proposed method aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of lung segmentation in medical imaging.
The authors introduce a novel keypoint sampling algorithm that selects a subset of keypoints from the lung region, which are then used to generate a segmentation mask.
The algorithm is designed to minimize the number of keypoints while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves near-optimal performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The findings of this study have implications for improving the efficiency of lung segmentation in clinical practice.
This paper proposes a method for incorporating near-infrared (NIR) information into semantic image segmentation.
The authors argue that NIR data can provide valuable additional information for accurate segmentation, especially in scenarios where visible light data alone may be insufficient.
The proposed method involves training a deep neural network to jointly process both NIR and visible light data, using a novel fusion strategy.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy, particularly in challenging scenarios such as low-light conditions or complex backgrounds.
The findings of this study highlight the potential benefits of incorporating NIR information into semantic image segmentation and provide a promising direction for future research in this field.
This paper presents a variational image segmentation model that is coupled with image restoration achievements.
The proposed model aims to simultaneously perform image segmentation and restoration tasks by incorporating a restoration term into the energy functional of the segmentation model.
The restoration term is designed to encourage smoothness and preserve image details during the segmentation process.
The proposed model is formulated as an optimization problem, which is solved using an iterative algorithm.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model compared to existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and restoration quality.
The proposed model has potential applications in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and remote sensing.
In this paper, we propose a tiered move-making algorithm for general non-submodular pairwise energies.
The algorithm aims to efficiently solve optimization problems with non-submodular energies, which are commonly encountered in computer vision and machine learning tasks.
Our approach leverages the concept of tiered move-making, where moves are organized into tiers based on their potential to improve the energy function.
By prioritizing moves in a tiered manner, we are able to efficiently explore the solution space and find high-quality solutions.
We evaluate our algorithm on various benchmark datasets and compare it with existing state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our tiered move-making algorithm in solving optimization problems with non-submodular energies.
This paper presents an extension of the fuzzy c-means (FCM) algorithm for clustering using vector membership.
The FCM algorithm is a popular method for clustering data, but it has limitations when dealing with high-dimensional data.
The proposed extension addresses this limitation by introducing a vector membership approach, which allows for more flexibility in assigning data points to clusters.
The algorithm is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared to the original FCM algorithm.
The results show that the proposed extension improves the clustering performance, particularly for high-dimensional data.
This research contributes to the field of clustering algorithms by providing a new approach that can handle high-dimensional data more effectively.
This paper presents a novel approach for efficiently minimizing energy in order to enforce statistics in a given dataset.
The proposed method leverages the concept of Markov Random Fields (MRFs) and utilizes a graph-cut algorithm to find the optimal solution.
The key contribution of this work is the development of a new energy function that incorporates statistical constraints, allowing for the enforcement of desired statistical properties in the dataset.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach in enforcing statistics while maintaining high-quality results.
This work has potential applications in various domains such as image processing, computer vision, and data analysis.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting 3D medical images using the live-wire technique.
The live-wire technique is a popular method for segmenting 2D images, but its application to 3D images has been limited due to the computational complexity.
In this paper, we propose a modified live-wire algorithm that takes advantage of parallel processing and GPU acceleration to overcome the computational challenges.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a dataset of 3D medical images, achieving high segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
Our method has the potential to improve the segmentation process in medical imaging applications, leading to more accurate diagnoses and treatment planning.
This paper presents a robust image segmentation method specifically designed for low depth of field images.
Low depth of field images often suffer from blurred regions and inconsistent focus, making traditional segmentation algorithms ineffective.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of image enhancement techniques, edge detection, and region growing to accurately segment objects in low depth of field images.
Experimental results on a dataset of low depth of field images demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method compared to existing segmentation algorithms.
The proposed method can be applied to various applications such as object recognition, scene understanding, and image editing in low depth of field photography.
This paper presents a method for extracting gray images using fuzzy logic.
The proposed method utilizes fuzzy logic to determine the grayness of an image by considering the intensity values of its pixels.
The method first calculates the average intensity value of the image and then applies fuzzy logic to classify each pixel as either gray or non-gray based on its intensity value.
Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in extracting gray images compared to existing methods.
The method can be applied in various image processing applications where the extraction of gray images is required.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using 3D models.
Traditional image segmentation methods often struggle with complex scenes and objects due to the lack of contextual information.
In this work, we propose to leverage 3D models to assist the image segmentation process.
We first reconstruct a 3D model of the scene or object using depth information.
Then, we use this 3D model to guide the image segmentation algorithm by incorporating geometric constraints.
