Similarly, in genetic sequences, motifs (short patterns) can form larger structures such as genes, which in turn form chromosomes.
These hierarchical structures can be represented as nodes in a tree, where each node has potentially multiple parent nodes and multiple child nodes.
Such tree structures are referred to as tree patterns.
This paper addresses the problem of finding tree patterns with avoidance, where avoidance refers to the absence of a pattern from certain nodes in the tree.
We formalize the problem as a pattern avoidance problem in a task-precedence poset, and present a general algorithm that takes advantage of the hierarchical structure of trees.
The algorithm is based on dynamic programming, and employs a novel, general purpose, bottom-up, disaggregated recurrence, which we term fold-back.
This fold-back operator allows us to decompose the avoidance problem into a set of simpler problems, and to solve these problems in a bottom-up manner.
We implement our algorithm, and run experiments on a standard benchmark.

Our experiments show that our algorithm often outperforms the current state of the art in tree pattern avoidance, and is competitive with the best known algorithms for tree pattern matching, thus establishing pattern avoidance in trees as a new and challenging problem.
In this article, we study the quantitative volume space form rigidity under lower Ricci curvature bound for manifolds with boundary.

For a compact manifold M with non-negative scalar curvature and non-empty boundary, we show that if the volume function ν is a concave function on the boundary ∂M, then ν(x) ≳ δ≳ 0 for all x ∈ ∂M, where δ depends on the lower Ricci curvature bound and the volume of M. Furthermore, we show that if ν is a convex function on ∂M, then ν(x) ≪ δ≪ 0 for all x ∈ ∂M, where δ depends on the lower Ricci curvature bound and the volume of M.
These results show that the boundary behavior of the volume function is closely related to the lower Ricci curvature bound.

We study linear integral equations derived from the six-vertex model with a disorder parameter $\beta$. In a certain limiting case ($\beta \to \infty$), the equations reduce to a family of integral equations encountered in the study of the Shervatov model.
This latter model describes the propagation of chaos in the six-vertex model.
Using methods developed for the Shervatov model, we obtain sufficient conditions for the equations to have a solution, and we investigate the properties of these solutions.
In particular, we show that they are asymptotically proportional to the sine kernel as the spatial variable goes to infinity.
We present results of gamma-ray spectroscopy measurements of positron annihilation in glycerol performed at beam line 16C1 of the Institute for Basic Science, UNIST.
Gamma-ray emission from the title compound was detected in the energy range up to 3100 MeV.
The analysis of the obtained spectra allowed us to determine the lifetime and positron energy spectrum of the positronium (Ps) state in glycerol.
No evidence of the quasi-free Ps state was found.
We compare the results with recent ab initio calculations of the positron affinity and the positron state properties in glycerol.
Good agreement between the experimental results and theoretical predictions was obtained.
Abstract: The bag-of-frames model, composed of short segments of audio, is widely used to mimic the human auditory system in sound classification tasks.

In this paper, we analyze the performance of this model in the context of urban soundscapes, which entail challenges such as the variety of sound sources, their relative distance, and the influence of the environment on sound propagation.
We focus on the sound events most relevant to urban life, such as passing vehicles, human footsteps, and speech.
We collect a new dataset, namely the Google Audio Set Urban Soundscape Collection, which comprises a diverse set of soundscapes from different cities and environments.
By evaluating the performance of the bag-of-frames model on this new dataset, we show that it fails to generalize well, especially in noisy conditions.
To address these issues, we propose a simple yet effective post-processing method based on spectral similarity and harmonicity to improve the performance of the bag-of-frames model.
We show that this method significantly improves the performance in most cases, especially when the signal-to-noise ratio is low.

We demonstrate the asymptotic equivalence of fixed heat flux and fixed temperature thermal boundary conditions for convection in a rotating spherical shell in the Rayleigh number regime $10^{10} \leq Ra \leq 10^{12}$.
The equivalence is shown to hold in the asymptotic limit of rapidly-rotating convection, where the Coriolis number is much larger than the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers.

A similarity solution for the fixed heat flux problem is used to predict the flow fields and thermal fields for the fixed temperature problem, and excellent agreement is found between the similarity solution and direct numerical simulations of the full problem, validating the asymptotic equivalence.
The implications of these findings for the design of solar energy converters are discussed.
This paper proposes a method for enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions in semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
The authors argue that existing methods often struggle with accurately segmenting hard regions in medical images due to limited labeled data.
To address this issue, they propose a novel framework that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to enforce mutual consistency between the predictions of hard regions.
The proposed method consists of two steps: initial segmentation using a deep neural network and refinement using a consistency regularization term.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy for hard regions.
The authors conclude that their method can effectively improve the performance of semi-supervised medical image segmentation by enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions.

Efficient Hybrid Transformer: Learning Global-local Context for Urban Scene Segmentation

Urban scene segmentation is a challenging task due to the complex and diverse nature of urban environments.
In this paper, we propose an efficient hybrid transformer model for urban scene segmentation that effectively captures both global and local context information.

The hybrid transformer model combines the strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers, leveraging the spatial information captured by CNNs and the long-range dependencies captured by transformers.
To improve the efficiency of the hybrid transformer model, we introduce a novel global-local attention mechanism that selectively attends to relevant global and local context information.
This attention mechanism allows the model to focus on important regions while ignoring irrelevant regions, leading to improved segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
We evaluate our proposed model on several benchmark datasets for urban scene segmentation and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our hybrid transformer model achieves competitive performance while being more computationally efficient.

Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components of our model and provide insights into the importance of global-local context for urban scene segmentation.

Overall, our proposed efficient hybrid transformer model with the global-local attention mechanism shows promising results for urban scene segmentation, highlighting the potential of transformer-based models in computer vision tasks.
Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning.
In recent years, deep learning models, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation tasks.
However, CNNs have limitations in capturing long-range dependencies and suffer from high computational costs.
In this paper, we propose a novel medical image segmentation model called MISSFormer, which is based on the Transformer architecture.
We introduce a multi-scale self-attention mechanism to capture both local and global contextual information in medical images.
Additionally, we design a hybrid loss function that combines the Dice loss and the focal loss to address the class imbalance issue in medical image segmentation.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image datasets demonstrate that our proposed MISSFormer model outperforms state-of-the-art CNN-based models in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed model shows great potential for improving medical image segmentation tasks and can be applied to various clinical scenarios.
Domain generalization is a challenging task in medical image segmentation due to the lack of labeled data from diverse domains.
In this paper, we propose a Hierarchical Consistency Framework for Domain Generalization (HCDG) to address this problem.
HCDG leverages a hierarchical structure to model the relationships between different domains and learns a shared representation that is consistent across domains.
We introduce a novel consistency loss function that encourages the model to produce consistent predictions for similar images from different domains.
Experimental results on a medical image segmentation dataset demonstrate that HCDG outperforms existing domain generalization methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance.
Our framework provides a promising approach for improving the generalization capability of medical image segmentation models across diverse domains.
This paper presents a survey on machine learning techniques for auto labeling of video, audio, and text data.
Auto labeling is the process of automatically assigning labels or tags to data without human intervention.
The paper provides an overview of the different machine learning algorithms and approaches that have been used for auto labeling in the context of video, audio, and text data.
It discusses the challenges and limitations of these techniques and provides insights into the current state of the field.
The survey also highlights the potential applications and future directions for research in this area.
Overall, this paper serves as a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners interested in auto labeling of video, audio, and text data using machine learning techniques.
This paper presents a novel approach called Box-Adapt for domain-adaptive medical image segmentation using bounding box supervision.

The proposed method leverages the availability of bounding box annotations in the source domain to improve the segmentation performance in the target domain, where only image-level annotations are available.
The Box-Adapt framework consists of two main components: a bounding box adaptation module and a segmentation network.

The bounding box adaptation module learns to transform the bounding box annotations from the source domain to the target domain, while the segmentation network is trained using the adapted bounding box annotations and image-level annotations in the target domain.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Box-Adapt approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in domain-adaptive medical image segmentation tasks.

The proposed method has the potential to improve the generalization and transferability of medical image segmentation models across different domains, leading to more accurate and reliable segmentation results in clinical applications.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
In recent years, transformer-based models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in various natural language processing tasks.
In this paper, we propose a fully transformer network for semantic image segmentation, where the entire network is composed of transformer layers.
We introduce a novel self-attention mechanism that incorporates spatial information into the transformer architecture, allowing the model to capture both local and global context.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with existing methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our fully transformer network achieves competitive performance and outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Our findings suggest that transformer-based models have great potential for semantic image segmentation tasks.
This paper proposes a self-paced contrastive learning approach for semi-supervised medical image segmentation with meta-labels.
The method leverages the unlabeled data to improve the performance of the segmentation model by learning from the contrastive loss.
The proposed approach incorporates meta-labels, which are generated by a pre-trained model, to guide the learning process.
The self-paced learning strategy is employed to gradually increase the difficulty of the training samples, allowing the model to learn more effectively.
Experimental results on two medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to existing approaches.
The proposed approach shows promise for improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation tasks.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, accurate segmentation is challenging due to the presence of imperfect 3D bounding boxes, which are commonly used as initializations for segmentation algorithms.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to address this issue by incorporating a bounding box refinement step into the segmentation pipeline.
Our method leverages a deep learning framework to learn the relationship between the imperfect bounding boxes and the corresponding segmentations.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that our approach significantly improves segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods.
This work has important implications for improving the reliability and efficiency of medical image segmentation in clinical practice.
This paper presents a novel approach for reconstructing the morphology of neurons using Hidden Markov Modeling (HMM) and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE).
The proposed method leverages the temporal dependencies in the data to accurately estimate the hidden states of the neuron, which correspond to its branching structure.
The HMM framework allows for the incorporation of prior knowledge about the neuron's morphology, such as its connectivity and spatial constraints.
The MLE algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the HMM model, resulting in an accurate reconstruction of the neuron's morphology.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on synthetic and real neuronal data, showing significant improvements over existing reconstruction techniques.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of neuron reconstruction and offers a promising approach for accurately modeling the complex morphology of neurons.
Few-shot medical image segmentation is a challenging task due to the limited availability of annotated data.
In this paper, we propose a recurrent mask refinement approach for few-shot medical image segmentation.
Our method leverages a pre-trained segmentation network and a few annotated images to generate initial segmentation masks.
These masks are then refined iteratively using a recurrent neural network.
The recurrent network takes the initial masks as input and produces refined masks as output.
We evaluate our method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods.
Our results demonstrate that our recurrent mask refinement approach achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in our method.
Overall, our proposed approach shows promising potential for improving few-shot medical image segmentation.
Open-World Entity Segmentation is a novel approach to the problem of segmenting entities in open-world scenarios.
In open-world scenarios, the number and types of entities are not known in advance, making traditional segmentation methods inadequate.
This paper proposes a two-step approach that first detects potential entities using a deep learning model and then refines the segmentation using a graph-based algorithm.
The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets and demonstrates robustness in handling open-world scenarios.
The paper also provides an extensive analysis of the proposed method and discusses its limitations and potential future directions.
Overall, Open-World Entity Segmentation presents a promising solution to the challenging problem of segmenting entities in open-world scenarios.

This paper presents a novel segmentation network called Crosslink-Net, which utilizes a double-branch encoder architecture to fuse vertical and horizontal convolutions for improved segmentation performance.
The proposed network consists of two encoder branches, each employing a different convolutional operation, and a decoder branch for feature fusion and segmentation.
The vertical branch focuses on capturing vertical contextual information, while the horizontal branch captures horizontal contextual information.
The two branches are then fused at multiple levels to enhance the overall segmentation accuracy.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the Crosslink-Net outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation networks in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed network has the potential to advance the field of semantic segmentation in computer vision applications.
This paper investigates the impact of different image features on the accuracy of housing market predictions.
Using a dataset of real estate images and corresponding housing market data, we analyze various image features such as color, texture, and composition.
We employ machine learning algorithms to predict housing market prices based on these image features and compare the results with predictions made using only textual features.
Our findings suggest that certain image features, such as color saturation and image resolution, significantly improve the accuracy of housing market predictions.
These results have implications for real estate agents and online platforms that rely on images to market properties and make predictions about housing market trends.
This paper investigates the impact of domain shift on the performance of U-Net layers in MRI segmentation.
Domain shift refers to the differences between the training and testing data distributions, which can negatively affect the accuracy of segmentation models.
The authors analyze the anatomy of domain shift by examining the changes in feature maps and activation patterns at different layers of the U-Net architecture.
They propose a novel method to mitigate the effects of domain shift by adapting the feature maps using domain adaptation techniques.
Experimental results on a dataset of MRI brain images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving segmentation accuracy under domain shift conditions.
The findings of this study provide insights into the behavior of U-Net layers in the presence of domain shift and offer a practical solution to address this challenge in MRI segmentation tasks.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical imaging analysis, as it enables accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, existing segmentation methods often struggle with uncertain and ambiguous regions in medical images.
In this paper, we propose a new approach called Medical Matting, which combines traditional segmentation techniques with uncertainty estimation.
Our method leverages the concept of alpha matting to estimate the uncertainty of each pixel in the segmentation result.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of Medical Matting on various medical image datasets, showing improved segmentation accuracy and robustness to uncertain regions.
Additionally, we compare our method with state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms and show that Medical Matting outperforms them in terms of both accuracy and uncertainty estimation.
Overall, our work presents a new perspective on medical segmentation, highlighting the importance of uncertainty estimation in improving segmentation results.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
In recent years, deep learning models have shown promising results in medical image segmentation.
However, most existing models rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which may not effectively capture long-range dependencies in medical images.
In this paper, we propose a novel model called Medical Transformer, which utilizes a gated axial-attention mechanism to capture both local and global contextual information in medical images.

Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets for medical image segmentation, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing complex spatial relationships in medical images.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components in our model and provide insights into its design choices.
Overall, our work contributes to the development of more accurate and robust models for medical image segmentation.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, it is challenging due to the high variability and complexity of medical images.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for robust medical image segmentation using cooperative training and latent space data augmentation.
Our method leverages the power of multiple models trained on different subsets of the data to improve segmentation accuracy.
Additionally, we introduce a latent space data augmentation technique that generates realistic and diverse augmented samples to enhance the generalization capability of the models.
We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of medical images and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior segmentation performance and outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Our findings suggest that cooperative training and latent space data augmentation can significantly improve the reliability and effectiveness of medical image segmentation algorithms.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting two-dimensional structures using strided tensor networks.
The proposed method leverages the hierarchical structure of tensor networks to efficiently capture local and global dependencies in the input data.
The segmentation task is formulated as a binary classification problem, where each pixel is assigned a label indicating whether it belongs to the foreground or background.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting two-dimensional structures, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed approach has the potential to be applied to a wide range of image segmentation tasks in various domains, including medical imaging and computer vision.
Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a promising approach for automatically designing neural network architectures.
However, recent studies have shown that NAS algorithms are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where an attacker can manipulate the search space to bias the search towards suboptimal architectures.

In this paper, we propose a novel attack strategy called Poisoning the Search Space (PSS) that aims to degrade the performance of NAS algorithms by injecting a small number of malicious architectures into the search space.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of PSS on several state-of-the-art NAS algorithms and show that it can significantly degrade their performance.
Furthermore, we propose a defense mechanism called Adversarial Training for NAS (AT-NAS) that can mitigate the impact of PSS attacks.
Our experimental results show that AT-NAS can effectively defend against PSS attacks and improve the robustness of NAS algorithms.
Overall, our work highlights the importance of considering security and robustness in NAS algorithms and provides insights into potential defense mechanisms against adversarial attacks.
This paper presents a novel approach for semantics-aware multi-modal domain translation, specifically from LiDAR point clouds to panoramic color images.
The proposed method leverages the semantic information present in the LiDAR point clouds to generate more accurate and visually appealing panoramic color images.
The authors introduce a new network architecture that combines a semantic segmentation network with a generative adversarial network to perform the translation.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in generating high-quality panoramic color images that preserve the semantic information from the LiDAR point clouds.
The proposed method has potential applications in various domains such as autonomous driving and virtual reality.
This paper presents a novel approach for automatically measuring the thickness of head overcoats using a NASNet-Large-Decoder neural network.
The proposed method utilizes a deep learning architecture to analyze microscopic images of head overcoats and accurately estimate their thickness.
The NASNet-Large-Decoder net is trained on a large dataset of annotated images to learn the relationship between image features and thickness measurements.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving high accuracy and outperforming existing techniques.

The automatic head overcoat thickness measure with NASNet-Large-Decoder net has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of head overcoat thickness measurement in various industries.
Vision Transformers (ViTs) have recently emerged as a powerful approach for image classification tasks.
However, training ViTs effectively requires careful consideration of data, augmentation, and regularization techniques.
In this paper, we investigate the impact of different data strategies, augmentation methods, and regularization techniques on the performance of ViTs.
We conduct extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets and analyze the results to provide insights into the best practices for training ViTs.
Our findings demonstrate the importance of large-scale datasets, diverse augmentation techniques, and regularization methods such as dropout and weight decay.
We also propose a novel regularization technique called patch-level dropout, which improves the performance of ViTs by encouraging the model to attend to different parts of the image.
Overall, our study provides valuable guidelines for training ViTs and sheds light on the factors that contribute to their success in image classification tasks.
This paper proposes a novel approach called CMF (Cascaded Multi-model Fusion) for referring image segmentation.
Referring image segmentation is the task of segmenting an object in an image based on a natural language expression.
The proposed CMF approach consists of two stages: a coarse segmentation stage and a fine segmentation stage.
In the coarse segmentation stage, multiple models are trained to generate initial segmentations based on the input expression.
These initial segmentations are then fused using a fusion network to obtain a refined segmentation.
In the fine segmentation stage, a refinement network is trained to further improve the segmentation by incorporating contextual information.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the CMF approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed approach has the potential to be applied in various applications such as image editing, object recognition, and scene understanding.
This paper proposes a novel adversarial segmentation loss for the task of sketch colorization.
The goal of sketch colorization is to automatically add color to grayscale sketches.
Existing methods for sketch colorization often suffer from issues such as color bleeding and lack of fine-grained details.
To address these challenges, we introduce an adversarial segmentation loss that encourages the model to generate colorized sketches that are visually similar to the ground truth colored images.
Our approach leverages a discriminator network to distinguish between the generated colorized sketches and the ground truth colored images.
By incorporating this adversarial loss into the training process, we are able to improve the quality of the colorization results.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches in terms of colorization accuracy and visual quality.
This paper presents a novel approach for left ventricle contouring in cardiac images using deep reinforcement learning.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the optimal contouring policy from a large dataset of annotated cardiac images.
The CNN is trained using a combination of supervised and reinforcement learning techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the contouring process.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing contouring algorithms in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The findings of this study have significant implications for improving the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Supervised contrastive learning has recently emerged as a powerful technique for learning visual representations.
However, existing methods often overlook the importance of attending to informative regions in the image during the contrastive learning process.
In this paper, we propose a novel attention-guided supervised contrastive learning framework for semantic segmentation.
Our method leverages attention mechanisms to guide the contrastive learning process, enabling the model to focus on informative regions and improve the segmentation performance.
We conduct extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Furthermore, we provide qualitative analysis and ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of our attention-guided approach.

Overall, our work contributes to the field of semantic segmentation by introducing a novel framework that combines attention mechanisms with supervised contrastive learning to achieve superior segmentation performance.
This paper presents an analysis of vision-based abnormal red blood cell classification.
The study aims to develop an automated system for the detection and classification of abnormal red blood cells using computer vision techniques.
The proposed system utilizes image processing algorithms to extract relevant features from microscopic images of blood samples.
These features are then used to train a machine learning model for the classification of normal and abnormal red blood cells.
The performance of the system is evaluated using a dataset of blood samples with known abnormalities.

The results show that the proposed system achieves high accuracy in the classification of abnormal red blood cells, demonstrating its potential for use in clinical settings for the early detection of blood disorders.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting SPECT/CT images using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and fuzzy clustering.
SPECT/CT images are commonly used in medical imaging for diagnosing and monitoring various diseases.
However, accurate segmentation of these images is challenging due to the presence of noise and artifacts.
The proposed method combines the strengths of CNNs and fuzzy clustering to overcome these challenges.
The CNN is trained to learn the features of the SPECT/CT images, while the fuzzy clustering algorithm is used to refine the segmentation results.
Experimental results on a dataset of SPECT/CT images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment planning for various diseases using SPECT/CT imaging.
SemSegLoss is a Python package that provides a collection of loss functions for semantic segmentation tasks.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental problem in computer vision, where the goal is to assign a class label to each pixel in an image.
The choice of an appropriate loss function is crucial for training accurate and robust semantic segmentation models.
This paper introduces SemSegLoss, a comprehensive package that includes a variety of loss functions commonly used in the field.
The package is designed to be flexible and easy to use, allowing researchers and practitioners to experiment with different loss functions and select the most suitable one for their specific task.
The paper provides a detailed description of the implemented loss functions, along with examples of their usage and performance evaluation on benchmark datasets.
The SemSegLoss package is publicly available and can be easily integrated into existing deep learning frameworks, making it a valuable resource for the semantic segmentation community.
This paper proposes a novel approach for semi-supervised volumetric medical image segmentation using momentum contrastive voxel-wise representation learning.
The proposed method leverages the momentum contrastive learning framework to learn voxel-wise representations from unlabeled medical images.
By maximizing the agreement between differently augmented views of the same voxel, the model learns to capture meaningful features that are useful for segmentation.
The learned representations are then used to train a segmentation network in a semi-supervised manner, where both labeled and unlabeled data are utilized.

Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in semi-supervised volumetric medical image segmentation tasks.

The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, which can greatly benefit clinical applications and research in the field of medical imaging.
This paper presents a boundary-aware segmentation network for mobile and web applications.
The proposed network leverages the power of deep learning to accurately segment objects in images, with a particular focus on preserving object boundaries.
The network architecture incorporates a boundary-aware module that enhances the segmentation performance by explicitly modeling the object boundaries.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed network outperforms existing segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and boundary preservation.
The network is lightweight and efficient, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained mobile and web platforms.
Overall, this work contributes to the development of advanced segmentation techniques for mobile and web applications.
This paper proposes an encoder fusion network with co-attention embedding for referring image segmentation.
Referring image segmentation is the task of segmenting a specific object or region in an image based on natural language instructions.
The proposed network combines the strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) by fusing their encoders.
Additionally, a co-attention mechanism is introduced to capture the relationship between the image and the referring expression.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed network outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The encoder fusion network with co-attention embedding provides a promising approach for referring image segmentation tasks.
This paper explores the limitations of pixel-wise supervision for image segmentation tasks and proposes the use of global shape descriptors as an alternative approach.
The authors argue that pixel-wise supervision can be computationally expensive and may not capture the overall shape of objects accurately.
They introduce several global shape descriptors, such as the convex hull and bounding box, and demonstrate their effectiveness in segmenting objects in various datasets.
The results show that these global shape descriptors can achieve comparable or even better performance than pixel-wise supervision, while requiring less computational resources.
The findings suggest that global shape descriptors have the potential to improve segmentation tasks and should be further explored in future research.
This paper explores the benefits of linear conditioning with metadata for image segmentation.
Image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, and recent advancements have shown the effectiveness of deep learning models for this task.
However, these models often require a large amount of labeled data for training, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages metadata information to improve the performance of image segmentation models.
Specifically, we introduce a linear conditioning mechanism that incorporates metadata features into the model's architecture.
We conduct experiments on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Furthermore, we show that our method is able to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer labeled samples, making it a more cost-effective solution for image segmentation tasks.
Overall, our findings highlight the potential benefits of linear conditioning with metadata for improving the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation models.

ObjectAug: Object-level Data Augmentation for Semantic Image Segmentation

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurate labeling of each pixel in an image with its corresponding object class.
Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in this task, but they often require large amounts of labeled data for training.
Data augmentation techniques have been widely used to artificially increase the size of the training dataset and improve the generalization ability of the models.
However, most existing data augmentation methods operate at the image level and do not consider the object-level information.
In this paper, we propose ObjectAug, a novel object-level data augmentation method for semantic image segmentation.
ObjectAug leverages the object-level annotations in the training dataset to generate realistic and diverse augmented samples.
Specifically, we introduce three types of object-level transformations: object insertion, object deletion, and object replacement.
These transformations are applied to the training images while preserving the semantic consistency between the objects and the background.
To evaluate the effectiveness of ObjectAug, we conduct extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets for semantic image segmentation.
The results demonstrate that ObjectAug significantly improves the performance of deep learning models compared to traditional image-level data augmentation methods.
Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different augmentation strategies and provide insights into the benefits of object-level data augmentation.

In conclusion, ObjectAug is a valuable addition to the field of semantic image segmentation, as it addresses the limitations of existing data augmentation methods by considering object-level information.
The proposed method achieves superior performance and provides a more realistic and diverse training dataset for deep learning models.
ObjectAug has the potential to advance the state-of-the-art in semantic image segmentation and other related tasks in computer vision.
Label smoothing is a common technique used in machine learning to regularize models and improve generalization.
However, traditional label smoothing methods assume that the uncertainty in the labels is constant across the entire dataset.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Spatially Varying Label Smoothing (SVLS) that captures the spatial variation in uncertainty from expert annotations.
We introduce a spatial uncertainty map that encodes the uncertainty at each pixel location, which is then used to adaptively smooth the labels.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of SVLS on various image segmentation tasks and show that it outperforms traditional label smoothing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Additionally, we provide insights into the spatial variation of uncertainty in expert annotations and discuss the implications for future research in this area.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
Deep learning models have shown promising results in this field, but their performance can be further improved by combining multiple models.
In this paper, we propose a two-layer ensemble of deep learning models for medical image segmentation.
The first layer consists of multiple individual models trained on different subsets of the training data.
The outputs of these models are then combined using a weighted average approach.
The second layer consists of a fusion model that takes the combined outputs of the first layer as input and further refines the segmentation results.

Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed ensemble approach outperforms individual models and achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical image segmentation.
Our findings suggest that ensemble methods can effectively improve the accuracy and robustness of deep learning models for medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel scale-space filtering framework called Hierarchical Image Peeling (HIP) that allows for flexible and efficient image processing.
HIP is based on the concept of peeling layers of an image, where each layer represents a different scale of the image.
The proposed framework provides a hierarchical representation of an image, allowing for the extraction of multi-scale features and the generation of scale-space pyramids.
The paper describes the theoretical foundations of HIP and presents several applications, including image denoising, edge detection, and texture analysis.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework compared to existing scale-space filtering methods.
Overall, HIP offers a flexible and powerful tool for image processing tasks that require multi-scale analysis.
Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is an important problem in machine learning, as it helps to identify instances that do not belong to the training distribution.
Existing methods for OOD detection often rely on task-specific assumptions or require access to labeled OOD data.
In this paper, we propose a task-agnostic approach for OOD detection using kernel density estimation (KDE).
Our method leverages the inherent structure of the training data to estimate the density of the in-distribution instances and uses this estimate to detect OOD instances.
We evaluate our method on various benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art OOD detection methods.
The results show that our approach achieves competitive performance without relying on task-specific assumptions or labeled OOD data.
Our method can be easily applied to different tasks and datasets, making it a versatile solution for OOD detection in machine learning applications.
DiNTS is a novel approach for automatically searching for the optimal neural network topology for 3D medical image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method leverages differentiable architecture search techniques to efficiently explore a large search space of network topologies.
By incorporating a differentiable relaxation of the discrete search space, the method enables end-to-end training and gradient-based optimization of the network architecture.

Experimental results on various medical image segmentation tasks demonstrate that DiNTS achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods, while significantly reducing the computational cost of architecture search.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of 3D medical image segmentation, thereby facilitating the development of advanced medical imaging applications.
Deformable image registration (DIR) is a fundamental task in medical image analysis that involves aligning two or more images by estimating a deformation field.
Traditional approaches to DIR rely on optimization-based methods that require manual tuning of parameters and are computationally expensive.
In recent years, there has been growing interest in learning-based approaches to DIR, which aim to automatically learn the registration process from data.
This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of learning-based DIR methods, including their perspective, modules, bilevel training, and future directions.
The authors discuss the advantages and limitations of learning-based DIR and highlight the key challenges in this field.
They also propose a novel bilevel training framework for learning-based DIR, which combines the strengths of optimization-based and learning-based methods.
The proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets and demonstrates the potential of learning-based DIR for improving clinical applications.
Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the field of learning-based DIR and offers guidance for future research in this area.
This paper proposes a novel approach to improve image co-segmentation using deep metric learning.
Image co-segmentation is the task of simultaneously segmenting common objects from a set of images.
Existing methods often suffer from limitations such as high computational complexity and low accuracy.

To address these issues, the authors propose a deep metric learning framework that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn discriminative features for image co-segmentation.
The proposed framework consists of two main components: a feature extraction network and a metric learning network.

The feature extraction network is responsible for extracting high-level features from input images, while the metric learning network learns a similarity metric to measure the similarity between image patches.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The findings of this study have implications for various computer vision applications, such as object recognition and image retrieval.
This paper presents a semi-supervised learning approach for eye image segmentation.
Eye image segmentation is an important task in various medical applications, such as diagnosing eye diseases and monitoring treatment progress.
However, obtaining a large amount of labeled data for training segmentation models is often challenging and time-consuming.
In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised learning framework that leverages both labeled and unlabeled eye images to improve segmentation performance.
Our approach combines a deep convolutional neural network with a graph-based semi-supervised learning algorithm.
We evaluate our method on a dataset of eye images and compare it with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques.

The experimental results demonstrate that our semi-supervised learning approach achieves superior segmentation accuracy compared to fully supervised methods, even when using a limited amount of labeled data.
This work contributes to the field of eye image segmentation by providing an effective and efficient solution for training segmentation models with limited labeled data.
This paper proposes a semi-supervised learning method for aggregated multilayer graphs using diffuse interface methods and fast matrix vector products.
The method leverages the structure of the multilayer graph to improve the accuracy of the learning process.
The diffuse interface methods are used to model the diffusion process on the graph, while the fast matrix vector products are employed to efficiently compute the diffusion operator.
The proposed method is evaluated on several real-world datasets and compared to existing approaches.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method in semi-supervised learning tasks on aggregated multilayer graphs.
This paper presents a new approach to outline in vitro cell colonies using principal component-based image segmentation.

The proposed method utilizes principal component analysis to extract the most relevant features from the input image and then applies a segmentation algorithm to identify the boundaries of the cell colonies.
The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through experiments on a dataset of in vitro cell colony images, where it achieves high accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods.
The results suggest that principal component-based image segmentation can be a valuable tool for analyzing cell colonies in biomedical research and related fields.
Semantic segmentation of medical images plays a crucial role in various clinical applications.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in this task, but they often struggle to capture fine-grained morphological features due to the limited receptive field of convolutional layers.

In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Morphological Operation Residual Blocks (MORBs) to enhance the representation of 3D morphological features in CNNs for semantic segmentation of medical images.
MORBs incorporate morphological operations, such as erosion and dilation, within residual blocks to capture local and global morphological information.
We evaluate our proposed architecture on two publicly available medical image datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that MORBs significantly improve the performance of CNNs in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise and artifacts.

Our findings suggest that incorporating morphological operations within residual blocks can effectively enhance the representation of 3D morphological features in CNNs for semantic segmentation of medical images.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting retinal layers in optical coherence tomography (OCT) images using a semi-supervised learning framework.
The proposed method leverages the uncertainty information obtained from a deep learning model to guide the segmentation process.
The uncertainty is estimated using a Bayesian deep learning model, which provides a measure of confidence for each pixel in the image.
This uncertainty information is then used to guide the segmentation algorithm, allowing for more accurate and robust segmentation results.
The proposed method is evaluated on a large dataset of OCT images and compared to state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The results demonstrate that the uncertainty-guided approach achieves superior segmentation performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.

This work has important implications for the field of medical image analysis, as it provides a new approach for improving the segmentation of retinal layers in OCT images, which can aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of various retinal diseases.
This paper presents a novel approach for extracting face masks in video sequences.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of deep learning techniques and image processing algorithms to accurately detect and segment face masks from video frames.
The approach involves training a convolutional neural network on a large dataset of annotated face mask images to learn the features and patterns associated with face masks.
The trained network is then used to classify pixels in video frames as either belonging to the face mask or background.
Additionally, post-processing techniques such as morphological operations and contour detection are applied to refine the segmentation results.
Experimental results on a diverse set of video sequences demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach in accurately extracting face masks.
The proposed method has potential applications in various domains such as surveillance, healthcare, and augmented reality.
This paper investigates the issue of overfitting in neural networks for image segmentation tasks, specifically in the context of class imbalance.
Overfitting occurs when a model becomes too specialized to the training data and performs poorly on unseen data.
Class imbalance refers to the situation where the number of samples in different classes is significantly different.
The authors propose a comprehensive analysis of overfitting under class imbalance in neural networks for image segmentation.
They conduct experiments on various datasets with different levels of class imbalance and evaluate the performance of different neural network architectures.
The results show that overfitting is more pronounced in the presence of class imbalance, leading to poor generalization performance.
The authors also propose several strategies to mitigate overfitting, such as data augmentation and class weighting.

Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the challenges of overfitting in image segmentation tasks and offers practical solutions to improve the performance of neural networks in the presence of class imbalance.
This paper proposes a self-paced and self-consistent co-training approach for semi-supervised image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages the strengths of both self-paced learning and self-consistent learning to improve the performance of image segmentation.
The self-paced learning strategy gradually selects reliable samples for training, while the self-consistent learning strategy enforces consistency between the predictions of two co-trained models.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method provides a promising solution for semi-supervised image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for enhancing the resolution of underdrawings in artworks using generative adversarial deep neural networks (GANs) and style transfer techniques.
Underdrawings, which are preliminary sketches or outlines hidden beneath the final layers of paint or ink, often suffer from low resolution and visibility.
The proposed method leverages the power of GANs to generate high-resolution versions of underdrawings by learning from a dataset of paired low-resolution and high-resolution images.
The style transfer technique is then applied to refine the generated images and align them with the original artwork's style.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing the resolution and visibility of underdrawings, providing valuable insights for art restoration and preservation.
This paper proposes a novel approach called Deeply Supervised Active Learning (DSAL) for biomedical image segmentation.
The goal is to leverage both strong and weak labelers to improve the performance of deep learning models.
DSAL combines active learning and deep supervision techniques to iteratively select informative samples for annotation and train a deep learning model.
The proposed method is evaluated on two biomedical image segmentation tasks and compared with other active learning methods.
The results demonstrate that DSAL outperforms existing approaches and achieves state-of-the-art performance.
The findings suggest that DSAL can effectively leverage both strong and weak labelers to improve the accuracy of biomedical image segmentation models.
This paper presents a novel approach to active learning for medical image segmentation, with the goal of reducing uncertainty within the training pool.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of uncertainty sampling and query-by-committee techniques to select the most informative samples for annotation.
The uncertainty of each sample is estimated using a deep neural network, which is trained on a small initial labeled dataset.
The selected samples are then annotated by experts and added to the training set, iteratively improving the segmentation model.

Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional random sampling and achieves comparable performance to fully supervised learning with a significantly smaller labeled dataset.
The findings of this study have implications for improving the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper introduces a novel approach for modelling spatially correlated aleatoric uncertainty in stochastic segmentation networks.
The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial correlation present in many segmentation tasks to improve uncertainty estimation.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on several benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of uncertainty estimation.
The results suggest that incorporating spatial correlation in aleatoric uncertainty modelling can lead to more accurate and reliable segmentation predictions.
The proposed method has the potential to enhance the performance of various computer vision applications that rely on segmentation networks.
Domain adaptation is a crucial task in machine learning, especially when dealing with multiple sources of data.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach called mDALU (Multi-Source Domain Adaptation and Label Unification) that addresses the challenges of domain adaptation and label unification using partial datasets.
Our method leverages the information from multiple source domains to adapt the target domain and unify the labels across domains.
We introduce a novel label unification loss function that encourages the model to learn a shared label space across domains.
Additionally, we propose a partial dataset learning strategy that handles the scenario where only a subset of the data is available for training.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the performance of domain adaptation and label unification tasks.
This paper explores the concept of morphological neurons and their potential in creating a morphological network.
The authors investigate the capabilities and limitations of morphological neurons in terms of information processing and computational power.
They propose a framework for constructing a morphological network and discuss its potential applications in various fields such as robotics, artificial intelligence, and cognitive science.
The paper concludes by highlighting the challenges and future directions for research in this area.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring.
Deep learning-based methods have achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation, but they often require a large amount of annotated data for training.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable annotations is time-consuming and expensive.
To address this issue, high-level prior-based loss functions have been proposed to guide the training process by incorporating prior knowledge into the loss function.
In this survey, we provide a comprehensive overview of high-level prior-based loss functions for medical image segmentation.
We categorize these loss functions into different groups based on the types of prior knowledge they utilize, such as shape priors, anatomical priors, and spatial priors.
We also discuss the advantages and limitations of each type of loss function and provide insights into future research directions.

This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of medical image segmentation, helping them understand the current state-of-the-art techniques and guiding them in the development of new loss functions for improved medical image segmentation.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic image segmentation using dilated convolutions with lateral inhibitions.

Dilated convolutions allow us to increase the receptive field of the network without sacrificing spatial resolution, while lateral inhibitions help to suppress irrelevant activations and enhance the discriminative power of the network.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves competitive performance and outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

Overall, our work contributes to the field of semantic image segmentation by introducing a new architecture that combines dilated convolutions and lateral inhibitions to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation task.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into multiple regions or objects.
Deep learning has emerged as a powerful technique for image segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on various datasets.
This paper presents a comprehensive survey of recent advances in image segmentation using deep learning.
We review different deep learning architectures and techniques that have been proposed for image segmentation, including fully convolutional networks, U-Net, and Mask R-CNN.
We also discuss various datasets and evaluation metrics commonly used in the field.
Furthermore, we analyze the strengths and limitations of different approaches and identify future research directions.
This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in understanding the current state of the art in image segmentation using deep learning.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate annotations for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a contrastive learning framework for medical image segmentation that leverages both global and local features.
Specifically, we introduce a global feature encoder and a local feature encoder to extract discriminative features from medical images.
These features are then used to train a segmentation network using a contrastive loss function.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.

Our experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves competitive performance with limited annotations, highlighting its potential for improving medical image segmentation in scenarios with limited expert annotations.
This paper presents a method for segmenting gastric histopathology images using a hierarchical conditional random field (CRF) model.
The proposed method utilizes both low-level and high-level features to capture the complex structures and textures present in the images.
The hierarchical CRF model incorporates spatial dependencies between neighboring pixels and regions, allowing for accurate segmentation of different tissue types in the gastric histopathology images.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to aid in the diagnosis and treatment of gastric diseases by providing accurate and reliable segmentation of histopathology images.
Semantic segmentation of high-resolution satellite imagery is a challenging task due to the presence of fine-grained details and large spatial extent.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called PP-LinkNet for improving the accuracy of semantic segmentation in high-resolution satellite imagery.
PP-LinkNet combines the advantages of both LinkNet and Pyramid Pooling modules to effectively capture both local and global contextual information.
Additionally, we introduce a multi-stage training strategy that progressively refines the segmentation results by leveraging the knowledge learned from previous stages.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PP-LinkNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed architecture and training strategy have the potential to significantly improve the performance of semantic segmentation in high-resolution satellite imagery applications.
Realistic Image Normalization for Multi-Domain Segmentation is an academic paper that proposes a novel method for image normalization in the context of multi-domain segmentation.
The authors argue that existing normalization techniques often fail to account for the variations in image appearance across different domains, leading to suboptimal segmentation results.

To address this issue, they propose a two-step normalization approach that first aligns the images based on their global statistics and then applies domain-specific normalization to account for local variations.
The authors evaluate their method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving segmentation accuracy across different domains.
They also compare their approach with existing normalization techniques and show that it outperforms them in terms of segmentation performance.
Overall, this paper presents a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation by addressing the challenge of realistic image normalization in multi-domain scenarios.
Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Deep learning methods have achieved remarkable success in this field, but real-time performance remains a challenge.
This paper presents a comprehensive survey of deep learning methods for semantic image segmentation in real-time.
We review various architectures, such as fully convolutional networks (FCNs), encoder-decoder networks, and dilated convolutions, and discuss their advantages and limitations.
We also analyze different strategies for improving real-time performance, including network compression, parallel processing, and hardware acceleration.
Furthermore, we provide an overview of benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics commonly used in this domain.
Finally, we discuss open challenges and future directions for real-time semantic image segmentation using deep learning methods.
This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners working in the field of computer vision and deep learning.
In recent years, deep learning has shown promising results in various medical image segmentation tasks.
However, most existing methods focus on 2D image segmentation and do not fully exploit the spatial information in 3D medical images.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called UXNet for 3D medical image segmentation.
UXNet utilizes a multi-level feature aggregation strategy to capture both local and global contextual information.
Specifically, it consists of a feature extraction module, a multi-level feature aggregation module, and a segmentation module.
The feature extraction module extracts high-level features from the input 3D medical image.
The multi-level feature aggregation module aggregates features from different levels of the feature extraction module to capture both local and global contextual information.
Finally, the segmentation module generates the segmentation mask based on the aggregated features.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that UXNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D medical image segmentation tasks.
The proposed architecture shows great potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, which can benefit various clinical applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for domain generalization in style transfer tasks by integrating shape and spatial information.
The authors introduce a Random Style Transfer based Domain Generalization Network (RST-DGN) that leverages a random style transfer module to generate diverse style images.
These style images are then used to train a domain generalization network that learns to extract shape and spatial information from the input images.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the generalization performance of style transfer models across different domains.
The RST-DGN achieves state-of-the-art performance and outperforms existing methods in terms of both visual quality and domain generalization capability.
Overall, this paper presents a promising solution for addressing the domain shift problem in style transfer tasks.
This paper presents a framework called MCU-Net that aims to improve decision support systems for patient referrals in healthcare contexts by incorporating uncertainty representations.
The framework utilizes a combination of deep learning models and probabilistic graphical models to capture and represent uncertainties in the decision-making process.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of MCU-Net through experiments on a real-world dataset, showing that it outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and reliability.
The results suggest that incorporating uncertainty representations can enhance the decision-making process in healthcare and improve patient outcomes.
Semantic video segmentation is a challenging task that requires accurate and efficient processing of large amounts of video data.
In this paper, we propose TapLab, a fast framework for semantic video segmentation that leverages compressed-domain knowledge.
TapLab utilizes a tap-based approach to efficiently process video frames by tapping into compressed-domain information.
We introduce a TapNet architecture that combines a tap-based encoder-decoder network with a compressed-domain feature extractor.
Our experiments demonstrate that TapLab achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and speed on various benchmark datasets.
Furthermore, we show that TapLab is robust to compression artifacts and can effectively handle videos with different compression levels.
Overall, TapLab provides a fast and efficient solution for semantic video segmentation by exploiting compressed-domain knowledge.
This paper proposes a domain adaptive medical image segmentation method using adversarial learning of disease-specific spatial patterns.
The method aims to address the challenge of limited labeled data in medical image segmentation tasks by leveraging unlabeled data from different domains.
The proposed approach consists of two main components: a segmentation network and a domain adaptation network.

The segmentation network is trained to perform pixel-wise segmentation on labeled data, while the domain adaptation network learns to align the feature distributions between the labeled and unlabeled data.
The domain adaptation network includes a generator and a discriminator, which are trained in an adversarial manner to generate domain-invariant features.
Experimental results on two medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving segmentation performance on unseen domains.

The proposed approach shows promise in addressing the domain shift problem in medical image segmentation and has the potential to improve the generalization capability of segmentation models in clinical practice.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in various clinical applications, but it is often challenging due to the inherent uncertainty in the segmentation process.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for uncertainty quantification in medical image segmentation using normalizing flows.
Normalizing flows are a flexible class of generative models that can capture complex distributions.
We adapt normalizing flows to the task of medical image segmentation by training them to model the posterior distribution of the segmentation given the input image.
We then use the trained normalizing flows to estimate the uncertainty in the segmentation by sampling from the posterior distribution.
We evaluate our approach on a dataset of brain MRI scans and compare it to existing uncertainty quantification methods.
Our results demonstrate that our method provides accurate and reliable uncertainty estimates, which can be valuable for clinical decision-making and downstream analysis.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of medical image segmentation by providing a principled and effective approach for uncertainty quantification.
This paper presents an end-to-end trainable deep active contour model for automated image segmentation, specifically focusing on delineating buildings in aerial imagery.
The proposed model combines the strengths of deep learning and active contour models to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The model is trained using a large dataset of aerial imagery and ground truth annotations.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The paper also discusses the potential applications of the proposed model in various domains, such as urban planning and disaster response.
Overall, this work contributes to the field of automated image segmentation by introducing a novel approach that can effectively delineate buildings in aerial imagery.
This paper presents AinnoSeg, a novel approach for panoramic segmentation with high performance.
The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation of panoramic images.
AinnoSeg incorporates a panoramic feature extraction module to capture the unique characteristics of panoramic images, followed by a segmentation module that utilizes a modified U-Net architecture.
The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on various benchmark datasets, outperforming existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of AinnoSeg in various segmentation tasks, including object segmentation and semantic segmentation.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various real-world applications, such as autonomous driving and virtual reality.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
While single stage encoder-decoder networks have achieved impressive results in this domain, they often struggle with capturing fine-grained details and producing accurate boundaries.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called deep decoders for semantic image segmentation.
Our method involves incorporating multiple decoder modules into the network architecture, each responsible for capturing different levels of detail.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and boundary quality.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the impact of different decoder configurations and provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of our method.
Overall, our work highlights the importance of incorporating deep decoders into the network design for improved semantic image segmentation.
Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, but it often suffers from limited data and annotations, which hinders the performance of existing models.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to tackle this problem by leveraging unsupervised learning and transfer learning techniques.
We first use unsupervised learning to generate pseudo-labels for the unlabeled data, which helps to increase the size of the training set.
Then, we employ transfer learning to transfer knowledge from a pre-trained model to the target task of semantic segmentation.
Our experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the performance of semantic segmentation models, even with limited data and annotations.
This work provides a promising solution to address the challenges of limited data and annotations in semantic segmentation, and opens up new possibilities for future research in this area.
This paper proposes a novel approach for instrument segmentation in robotic surgery using unsupervised learning with cycle-consistent adversarial networks (CycleGANs).
The goal is to automatically segment surgical instruments from the background in surgical videos without the need for manual annotations.

The proposed method leverages the cycle-consistency property of CycleGANs to learn a mapping between the instrument and background domains, enabling the generation of synthetic instrument images from background images and vice versa.
The generated synthetic images are then used to train a segmentation model, which is evaluated on a dataset of real surgical videos.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting instruments in robotic surgery, highlighting its potential for improving surgical workflow and assisting surgeons in real-time.
This paper presents a novel approach for medical image segmentation using a technique called Meta Corrupted Pixels Mining (MCPM).
The proposed method leverages the concept of corrupted pixels to improve the accuracy and efficiency of segmentation algorithms.
The MCPM algorithm first identifies corrupted pixels in the input image and then uses these pixels to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the MCPM algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
