The proposed method outperforms existing unsupervised domain adaptation methods and shows promise for improving the generalization of segmentation models in medical imaging applications.
This paper introduces a novel architecture called Contextual Hourglass Networks (CHN) for the tasks of segmentation and density estimation.
The CHN architecture is based on the popular Hourglass Networks, but incorporates contextual information to improve the accuracy of these tasks.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of CHN on various benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results in both segmentation and density estimation tasks.
The proposed architecture shows promising potential for applications in computer vision and image analysis.
BoxNet is a deep learning framework for biomedical image segmentation that leverages the use of boxes as the only form of annotation.
Traditional methods for image segmentation require pixel-level annotations, which can be time-consuming and costly to obtain.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that only requires bounding box annotations, making the annotation process more efficient.
We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict the bounding boxes and segment the images simultaneously.
Our experiments on various biomedical datasets demonstrate that BoxNet achieves comparable or even better segmentation performance compared to pixel-level annotation methods.
Additionally, we show that BoxNet can generalize well to unseen datasets, indicating its potential for broader applications in biomedical image analysis.
Overall, our work presents a promising solution for biomedical image segmentation that reduces the annotation burden while maintaining high accuracy.
This paper presents a deep structured prediction model for fine image segmentation that incorporates complex relations between image regions.
The model utilizes a convolutional neural network to extract features from the input image, and then employs a conditional random field to model the dependencies between the regions.
The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing complex relations for fine image segmentation tasks.
The results suggest that incorporating complex relations can significantly improve the accuracy of image segmentation models.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using a piecewise flat embedding technique.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional segmentation algorithms by considering the piecewise flatness of image regions.
The algorithm first computes an initial segmentation using a graph-based approach, and then refines it by iteratively optimizing a piecewise flatness energy function.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and visually pleasing segmentations.
The proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation by introducing a novel technique that leverages the piecewise flatness of image regions.
Semantic segmentation is a critical task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic segmentation that involves iteratively refining densely connected representation levels.
Our method leverages the power of densely connected convolutional networks (DenseNets) to capture rich spatial information at multiple scales.
We introduce a new architecture called IterDenseNet, which consists of multiple DenseNet blocks that are iteratively refined through a series of upsampling and downsampling operations.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Our results suggest that the iterative refinement of densely connected representation levels is a promising direction for improving semantic segmentation performance.
This paper presents a novel approach for multi-channel image segmentation using derivative-based component-trees.
The proposed method utilizes the concept of component-trees, which represent the hierarchical structure of image regions, to segment multi-channel images.
The key contribution of this work is the use of derivative-based measures to construct the component-trees, which allows for more accurate and robust segmentation results.
The experimental evaluation on various datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of multi-channel image segmentation and offers a promising approach for future research in this area.
This paper presents a novel approach for portrait segmentation using a boundary-sensitive network.
Traditional methods for portrait segmentation often struggle with accurately capturing the boundaries of the portrait, leading to suboptimal results.
To address this issue, we propose a network architecture that incorporates boundary information into the segmentation process.
Our network consists of two main components: a boundary detection module and a segmentation module.
The boundary detection module is responsible for identifying the boundaries of the portrait, while the segmentation module uses this information to generate a high-quality segmentation mask.
We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of portrait images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our boundary-sensitive network outperforms existing methods in terms of boundary accuracy and overall segmentation quality.
Additionally, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of each component in our network.
Overall, our approach provides a promising solution for portrait segmentation, particularly in capturing accurate boundaries.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting several landmarks in running rodents using superpixels.
The proposed method utilizes the concept of superpixels to group pixels with similar characteristics and reduce the complexity of the segmentation task.
The algorithm first generates superpixels from the input image and then applies a combination of color and texture features to classify each superpixel into one of the predefined landmark categories.
Experimental results on a dataset of running rodent images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high segmentation accuracy and outperforming existing methods.
The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, including neuroscience and behavioral analysis, where accurate landmark segmentation is crucial for understanding animal behavior.
This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques to medical image segmentation.
Deep learning has emerged as a powerful tool in various fields, including computer vision, and has shown promising results in medical image analysis.
The paper provides an overview of deep learning algorithms, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and their variants, and discusses their application to medical image segmentation tasks.
The authors review recent studies that have utilized deep learning for segmenting various medical images, such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), and ultrasound images.

The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of deep learning in medical image segmentation, including the need for large annotated datasets and the interpretability of deep learning models.
Overall, this paper highlights the potential of deep learning in improving medical image segmentation and provides insights into future research directions in this field.
This paper presents a recurrent segmentation approach for variable computational budgets.
The proposed method utilizes a recurrent neural network to iteratively refine the segmentation results based on the available computational resources.
The model is trained using a combination of supervised and reinforcement learning techniques to optimize the segmentation performance under different computational constraints.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving high-quality segmentation results with limited computational resources.
The recurrent segmentation method shows promise for applications in real-time or resource-constrained scenarios where computational budgets may vary.
This paper presents a novel approach for long-term visual localization using semantically segmented images.
The proposed method leverages the semantic information in the images to improve the accuracy and robustness of visual localization over extended periods of time.
The approach involves training a deep neural network to perform semantic segmentation on the images, and then using the resulting semantic maps to guide the localization process.

Experimental results on a large-scale dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially in challenging scenarios such as changing lighting conditions and occlusions.
The findings of this study have significant implications for various applications, including autonomous navigation and augmented reality.
This paper presents a novel approach for image inpainting of high-resolution textures using convolutional neural network (CNN) texture synthesis.
Image inpainting is the process of filling in missing or corrupted parts of an image.
Traditional methods for image inpainting often struggle with high-resolution textures due to their complex and intricate patterns.
In this paper, we propose a CNN-based approach that leverages the power of deep learning to generate realistic and visually coherent inpainted textures.
Our method consists of two main steps: texture synthesis and texture transfer.
First, we train a CNN to learn the underlying texture patterns from a set of high-resolution texture images.
Then, we use this trained network to synthesize new textures that are visually similar to the original ones.
Finally, we transfer the synthesized textures onto the inpainted regions of the target image, resulting in a seamless and visually appealing inpainted image.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our approach compared to existing methods in terms of both visual quality and computational efficiency.
Self-supervised semantic segmentation has gained significant attention in recent years due to its ability to learn from unlabeled data.
However, existing methods often rely on a single pre-defined set of augmentation policies, which may not be optimal for all images.
In this paper, we propose a mix-and-match tuning approach for self-supervised semantic segmentation, where multiple augmentation policies are combined and tuned to improve performance.
We introduce a novel policy generator that generates diverse augmentation policies, and a policy tuner that optimizes the combination of these policies.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that our mix-and-match tuning approach outperforms existing methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance in self-supervised semantic segmentation.
This paper proposes a novel approach for cardiac segmentation and automated cardiac diagnosis using fully convolutional multi-scale residual DenseNets (FCMRD).
The FCMRD architecture combines the advantages of DenseNets and residual networks to improve the accuracy of cardiac segmentation.
The proposed method also utilizes an ensemble of classifiers to automate the cardiac diagnosis process.
The experimental results demonstrate that the FCMRD approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods for cardiac segmentation and diagnosis.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of cardiac diagnosis in clinical practice.
Interactive video object segmentation is a challenging task that involves accurately segmenting objects of interest in videos.
Existing methods often rely on manual annotations or pre-trained models, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for interactive video object segmentation in the wild.
Our method leverages the power of deep learning and interactive user guidance to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
We introduce a new dataset specifically designed for this task, which includes diverse and challenging video sequences.
We evaluate our method on this dataset and compare it with state-of-the-art approaches.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our approach, highlighting its potential for real-world applications.
Multi-object tracking (MOT) is a challenging task in computer vision that involves simultaneously detecting and tracking multiple objects in a video sequence.
Existing MOT methods often rely on object category information to improve tracking performance.
However, in real-world scenarios, object categories may not be available or may be unreliable.
In this paper, we propose a category-agnostic vision-based multi-object tracking approach that does not rely on object category information.
Our method first performs object detection and then uses a novel tracklet-based approach to associate detections into tracks.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art category-aware MOT methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our category-agnostic approach achieves competitive performance, even without category information.
Our approach has the potential to be applied in various real-world applications where object category information is not available or reliable.
Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
Atrous convolution, also known as dilated convolution, has been widely used in recent years to improve the performance of semantic image segmentation models.
However, the current approach of using atrous convolution in a deep neural network has limitations in terms of capturing both local and global contextual information.
In this paper, we propose a new approach called "Rethinking Atrous Convolution" that addresses these limitations.
Our approach involves using multiple atrous rates in parallel to capture both local and global contextual information.
We also introduce a new module called the "ASPP" (Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling) module, which further enhances the performance of our approach.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, our work provides a new perspective on the use of atrous convolution for semantic image segmentation and offers a promising direction for future research in this field.
This paper presents a novel approach for automatic spine segmentation using a convolutional neural network (CNN) and redundant generation of class labels for 3D spine modeling.
The proposed method utilizes a CNN architecture to learn the features of the spine from 2D axial slices of CT scans.

To address the challenge of limited training data, the authors introduce a redundant generation of class labels technique, which involves generating multiple class labels for each voxel in the training data.
This approach helps to increase the diversity of the training data and improve the performance of the CNN.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate and robust spine segmentation, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to be applied in clinical settings for automated spine segmentation and 3D modeling, which can aid in diagnosis and treatment planning for spinal disorders.
This paper presents a novel approach for designing efficient and invariant convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for dense prediction tasks.
The proposed method leverages the concept of group equivariant CNNs to achieve translation invariance while reducing computational complexity.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on various dense prediction tasks, including semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing the computational cost compared to traditional CNN architectures.
The authors also provide insights into the design choices and hyperparameters that contribute to the efficiency and invariance of the proposed CNNs.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of deep learning for dense prediction tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for direct perception in autonomous driving using fast recurrent fully convolutional networks (R-FCNs).
The proposed R-FCNs leverage the advantages of both recurrent and fully convolutional networks to achieve real-time perception tasks.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various datasets, including KITTI and Cityscapes.
The results show that the R-FCNs outperform existing methods in terms of accuracy and speed, making them a promising solution for direct perception in autonomous driving.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
In recent years, deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance on this task.

In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called the One Hundred Layers Tiramisu (OHT), which combines the strengths of Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs) and DenseNets for semantic segmentation.
The OHT architecture consists of a downsampling path, an upsampling path, and skip connections that enable the model to capture both local and global context information.
We evaluate the OHT architecture on several benchmark datasets and compare it with other state-of-the-art models.
Our experimental results demonstrate that the OHT architecture achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components in the OHT architecture.
Overall, our findings suggest that the OHT architecture is a promising approach for semantic segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for interactive medical image segmentation using deep learning with image-specific fine-tuning.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning models for initial segmentation and then incorporates user feedback to refine the results.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on a dataset of medical images, achieving high segmentation accuracy and reducing the need for manual annotation.
The results suggest that this interactive approach can improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning affinity between image pixels using spatial propagation networks.
The proposed method leverages the spatial relationships between pixels to propagate information and learn affinity scores.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on various image segmentation tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets.
The spatial propagation networks are shown to capture long-range dependencies and improve the accuracy of affinity estimation.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of computer vision by introducing a new method for learning affinity that outperforms existing approaches.
This paper presents UI-Net, an interactive artificial neural network framework for iterative image segmentation based on a user model.
The proposed framework combines the strengths of both human expertise and machine learning algorithms to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation tasks.
The user model is created by incorporating user feedback into the training process, allowing the network to learn from the user's preferences and adapt its segmentation results accordingly.
The iterative nature of the framework enables the user to refine the segmentation results in real-time, leading to a more interactive and user-friendly segmentation process.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of UI-Net in achieving high-quality segmentation results while reducing the user's effort and time required for the task.
Overall, UI-Net provides a promising approach for interactive image segmentation that leverages the power of artificial neural networks and user expertise.
This paper presents a novel approach for interactive image segmentation using a seeded Laplacian eigenfunction solution.
The proposed method leverages user scribbles as input to guide the segmentation process.
The algorithm first constructs a graph representation of the image, where each pixel is a node and the edges represent the similarity between pixels.
The user scribbles are then used to assign labels to the nodes, which are used to compute the Laplacian matrix.
By solving the eigenvalue problem of the Laplacian matrix, the algorithm obtains the eigenfunctions, which are used to segment the image.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing approaches.
This paper proposes a novel approach for training group orthogonal neural networks (GONNs) using privileged information.
GONNs are a type of neural network architecture that can effectively model complex relationships between input and output variables.
However, training GONNs can be challenging due to the need for large amounts of labeled data.
To address this issue, the authors introduce the concept of privileged information, which refers to additional information that is available during training but not during testing.
They propose a framework that leverages privileged information to improve the training of GONNs.
The authors conduct experiments on various datasets and demonstrate that their approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and generalization.
Overall, this paper presents a promising technique for training GONNs with privileged information, which has the potential to enhance the performance of neural networks in various applications.
Instance segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves detecting and segmenting multiple objects within an image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for instance segmentation that incorporates object priority, which aims to prioritize the detection and recognition of prominent objects in an image.
We introduce a new network architecture that combines a prominent object detection module with a recognition module, allowing for the simultaneous detection and recognition of objects.
We also propose a new loss function that takes into account the importance of each object in the image, based on its prominence.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in instance segmentation.
Our approach has the potential to improve various applications in computer vision, such as object detection, image understanding, and scene understanding.
This paper presents a convolutional neural network (CNN) based approach for the segmentation of medical imaging data.
The segmentation of medical images is a crucial step in various clinical applications, such as tumor detection and organ delineation.
Traditional segmentation methods often rely on handcrafted features and require extensive manual intervention.
In contrast, CNNs have shown promising results in various computer vision tasks, including image segmentation.
In this work, we propose a CNN architecture specifically designed for medical image segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on a dataset of medical images and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
Our results demonstrate that the proposed CNN-based approach achieves superior segmentation accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.

The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation, thereby facilitating better diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical image analysis, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
In this paper, we propose a novel adversarial network called SegAN for medical image segmentation.
SegAN consists of a generator network and a discriminator network, which are trained in an adversarial manner.
To improve the segmentation accuracy, we introduce a multi-scale $L_1$ loss, which encourages the generator to produce more accurate segmentations at different scales.
We evaluate SegAN on two publicly available medical image datasets and compare it with several state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that SegAN achieves superior segmentation performance and outperforms the existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Our proposed SegAN has the potential to be applied in various medical image analysis tasks and contribute to the improvement of healthcare outcomes.
This paper presents a robust regression approach for image binarization under heavy noises and nonuniform background.
The proposed method utilizes a robust regression model to estimate the background intensity and noise level, which are then used to adaptively threshold the image.
Experimental results on various synthetic and real images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing binarization techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method is particularly effective in scenarios with heavy noises and nonuniform background, making it suitable for a wide range of practical applications.
This paper presents a deep active learning framework called Suggestive Annotation for biomedical image segmentation.
The framework aims to reduce the annotation effort required for training deep learning models by selecting the most informative samples for annotation.
The authors propose a novel uncertainty-based sampling strategy that combines both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties to identify the most uncertain regions in the images.
These regions are then annotated by human experts, and the annotated data is used to fine-tune the deep learning model.
The authors evaluate the framework on two publicly available biomedical image datasets and compare it with other active learning strategies.
The results show that the Suggestive Annotation framework outperforms other strategies in terms of segmentation accuracy while requiring fewer annotations.
The proposed framework has the potential to significantly reduce the annotation effort and improve the efficiency of biomedical image segmentation tasks.
Dense Transformer Networks (DTNs) are a novel architecture that combines the strengths of both dense connections and transformer models.
This paper introduces DTNs and demonstrates their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks, including machine translation and text classification.
The authors propose a modified transformer model that incorporates dense connections between layers, allowing for better information flow and improved performance.
Experimental results show that DTNs outperform traditional transformer models on multiple benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results in several tasks.
The paper also provides insights into the inner workings of DTNs and discusses potential future directions for research in this area.
Overall, this work presents a promising approach for enhancing the performance of transformer models in natural language processing tasks.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Convolutional Random Walk Networks (CRWN) for semantic image segmentation.
CRWN combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and random walk algorithms to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The proposed method utilizes a CNN to extract high-level features from the input image and then applies a random walk algorithm to refine the segmentation boundaries.
We evaluate the performance of CRWN on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that CRWN achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the contributions of different components in CRWN.
Overall, our proposed method shows promising potential for semantic image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for RGBD semantic segmentation using spatio-temporal data-driven pooling.
The proposed method, called STD2P, leverages both spatial and temporal information to improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation.
The authors introduce a new pooling operation that combines RGB and depth features in a spatio-temporal manner, allowing the network to capture both appearance and motion cues.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that STD2P outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed approach shows promising potential for various applications, such as robotics and autonomous driving, where accurate scene understanding is crucial.
This paper proposes a novel approach for semantic image segmentation using loss max-pooling.
The traditional max-pooling operation in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is modified to incorporate loss information during training.
The loss max-pooling operation selects the maximum value not only based on the input feature maps but also on the corresponding loss maps.
This allows the network to focus on regions with high loss, improving the segmentation accuracy.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed loss max-pooling approach outperforms traditional max-pooling and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed approach provides a promising direction for improving semantic image segmentation in CNNs.
This paper presents a computer-aided detection (CAD) system for the identification of anemia-like pallor in medical images.
Anemia is a common blood disorder characterized by a decrease in the number of red blood cells or a decrease in the amount of hemoglobin in the blood.
Pallor, a clinical manifestation of anemia, refers to a pale appearance of the skin, mucous membranes, and conjunctiva.
The proposed CAD system utilizes image processing techniques to automatically detect and quantify the degree of pallor in medical images.
The system first preprocesses the images to enhance the contrast and remove noise.
Then, it extracts relevant features from the images using various image analysis algorithms.
These features are then used to train a machine learning model to classify the images as either normal or exhibiting anemia-like pallor.
The performance of the CAD system is evaluated using a dataset of medical images collected from patients with confirmed cases of anemia.

The results show that the proposed system achieves high accuracy in detecting anemia-like pallor, demonstrating its potential as a valuable tool for assisting healthcare professionals in the diagnosis and monitoring of anemia.
This paper presents a robust and fully automated method for segmenting the mandible from CT scans.

The proposed method utilizes a combination of image processing techniques, including thresholding, region growing, and morphological operations, to accurately extract the mandible from the surrounding tissues.
The method is able to handle various types of CT scans, including those with low contrast and noise.
Experimental results on a dataset of CT scans demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, achieving high accuracy and efficiency compared to manual segmentation.
The proposed method has the potential to greatly improve the efficiency and accuracy of mandible segmentation in clinical practice and research.
This paper presents an efficient decomposition framework for discriminative segmentation with supermodular losses.
The proposed framework leverages the structure of supermodular functions to decompose the loss function into submodular and modular components, which can be optimized separately.
This decomposition allows for efficient optimization algorithms to be applied, resulting in faster and more accurate segmentation.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework compared to existing methods.
Overall, this paper provides a novel approach for discriminative segmentation that improves both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper presents a method for efficiently computing piecewise flat embeddings for data clustering and image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages the concept of piecewise flat embeddings, which represent data points as vertices in a graph and use edge weights to capture the similarity between points.
The authors introduce a novel algorithm that efficiently computes these embeddings by iteratively updating the edge weights based on the current clustering or segmentation.
The algorithm is designed to minimize the computational complexity while still producing accurate results.
The authors evaluate the proposed method on various datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving high-quality clustering and segmentation results.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of data clustering and image segmentation by introducing an efficient method for computing piecewise flat embeddings.
Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
Deep learning models have achieved impressive results in this task, but they often suffer from over-segmentation and lack of spatial coherence.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with Gaussian conditional random fields (CRFs) to improve the accuracy and spatial coherence of semantic image segmentation.
Our method is fast, exact, and capable of handling multi-scale inputs.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Additionally, we provide an open-source implementation of our method to facilitate further research in this area.
Flood-Filling Networks (FFNs) are a class of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) designed for 3D image segmentation tasks.
This paper introduces a novel architecture for FFNs that improves their performance and efficiency.
The proposed architecture incorporates a recurrent neural network (RNN) module to iteratively refine the segmentation results.
Additionally, a new loss function is introduced to address the challenges of training FFNs.

Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed FFN architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D image segmentation tasks, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The paper also provides insights into the inner workings of FFNs and discusses potential applications and future research directions.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into different regions or objects.
In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown promising results in various computer vision tasks, including image segmentation.
This paper presents SegNet, a deep convolutional encoder-decoder architecture specifically designed for image segmentation.
The proposed architecture consists of an encoder network that extracts high-level features from the input image and a decoder network that reconstructs the segmented image.

The encoder network utilizes a series of convolutional and pooling layers to progressively downsample the input image, while the decoder network uses upsampling and deconvolutional layers to recover the spatial resolution of the segmented image.
Additionally, skip connections are introduced to preserve fine-grained details during the upsampling process.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SegNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in image segmentation tasks, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed architecture shows great potential for various applications, such as medical imaging, autonomous driving, and object recognition.
This paper presents a novel method for automated segmentation of retinal layers from optical coherent tomography (OCT) images using geodesic distance.
The proposed method utilizes the concept of geodesic distance to accurately identify the boundaries between different retinal layers.
The method is based on a graph representation of the OCT image, where each pixel is represented as a node and the edges represent the geodesic distance between pixels.
The geodesic distance is calculated using a fast marching algorithm.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of OCT images and compared with existing segmentation methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment of retinal diseases by providing accurate and automated segmentation of retinal layers from OCT images.
VoxResNet is a deep learning framework for volumetric brain segmentation that utilizes voxelwise residual networks.
The paper presents a novel architecture that combines the benefits of residual networks and voxelwise processing to improve the accuracy and efficiency of brain segmentation tasks.
The proposed VoxResNet model is evaluated on various brain segmentation datasets and achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting brain structures from volumetric brain images, making it a promising tool for clinical applications and neuroscience research.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
In recent years, deep learning methods have achieved remarkable success in this task.
However, most existing approaches rely on fully convolutional networks (FCNs) that suffer from the loss of spatial information due to pooling operations.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Global Deconvolutional Network (GDN) that addresses this limitation by incorporating global context information into the segmentation process.
GDN consists of two main components: a global pooling module and a deconvolutional module.

The global pooling module captures the global context information by aggregating features from the entire image, while the deconvolutional module upsamples the feature maps to recover the spatial information lost during the pooling operations.
We evaluate our proposed GDN on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that GDN achieves superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency, highlighting its potential for various applications in computer vision.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has various applications in fields such as object recognition and medical imaging.
This paper proposes a combined approach for image segmentation based on fuzzy classification and contextual region growing.
The fuzzy classification method is used to assign initial labels to pixels based on their similarity to predefined prototypes.
The contextual region growing method then refines these initial labels by considering the spatial relationships between neighboring pixels.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the performance of image segmentation algorithms in various applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation called HeMIS (Hetero-Modal Image Segmentation).
The proposed method leverages the complementary information from multiple modalities, such as color and depth, to improve the accuracy and robustness of image segmentation.
The authors introduce a new loss function that combines both modalities and design a deep neural network architecture that effectively integrates the heterogeneous data.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that HeMIS outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness, especially in challenging scenarios with complex backgrounds and occlusions.
The proposed approach has the potential to advance the field of image segmentation and contribute to various applications, such as object recognition and scene understanding.
V-Net is a fully convolutional neural network architecture designed for volumetric medical image segmentation.
The paper presents a novel approach that combines 3D convolutional layers with a modified U-Net architecture to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation of medical images.
The V-Net model is trained on a large dataset of volumetric medical images and evaluated on various segmentation tasks, including liver and lung segmentation.
The results demonstrate that V-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

The paper also provides insights into the design choices and hyperparameters of the V-Net model, making it a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of medical image analysis.
This paper presents an interactive medical image segmentation framework that utilizes iterative refinement to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.
The framework incorporates user interaction to guide the segmentation algorithm, allowing the user to provide initial seed points and refine the segmentation results in real-time.
The proposed framework combines a graph-cut algorithm with a region growing algorithm to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The framework has the potential to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation tasks and improve the overall quality of medical diagnosis and treatment.
This paper presents a novel approach for automated resolution selection in image segmentation tasks.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, and the choice of resolution greatly affects the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.
However, manually selecting the optimal resolution for each image can be time-consuming and subjective.
To address this issue, we propose a method that automatically determines the optimal resolution based on the characteristics of the input image.
Our approach leverages a deep learning model to extract relevant features from the image and uses a decision tree algorithm to select the resolution.
We evaluate our method on a large dataset of diverse images and compare it with existing resolution selection techniques.
The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, our automated resolution selection method can significantly improve the effectiveness and efficiency of image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a fuzzy clustering based segmentation method for vertebrae in T1-weighted spinal MR images.
The proposed method utilizes the fuzzy c-means algorithm to partition the image into different clusters representing different tissue types.
The algorithm incorporates spatial information to improve the accuracy of the segmentation.
Experimental results on a dataset of T1-weighted spinal MR images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting vertebrae.
The proposed method can be potentially used in clinical applications such as spinal disease diagnosis and treatment planning.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called ScribbleSup, which combines scribble annotations with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation.
Scribble annotations are a form of weak supervision that provide rough outlines of object boundaries.
We introduce a new loss function that leverages these annotations to guide the training of CNNs.
Our experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that ScribbleSup outperforms existing weakly supervised methods and achieves competitive results compared to fully supervised approaches.
Furthermore, we show that ScribbleSup is robust to noise in the scribble annotations and can handle complex scenes with multiple objects.
Overall, our work highlights the potential of using scribble annotations for semantic segmentation and opens up new avenues for weakly supervised learning in computer vision.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation of cross-country scenes captured in the infrared (IR) spectrum.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of traditional image processing techniques and machine learning algorithms to accurately segment different objects and regions in the IR images.
The paper also introduces a new dataset of cross-country scenes captured in the IR spectrum, which can be used for training and evaluating the proposed segmentation method.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting different objects and regions in the IR images, outperforming existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, including military surveillance, autonomous navigation, and environmental monitoring.
This paper presents a robust technique for segmenting and analyzing cDNA microarray images using the Hough circle transform.
The proposed method addresses the challenges of noise, uneven illumination, and overlapping spots in microarray images.
The Hough circle transform is used to detect circular spots in the image, which are then segmented and analyzed.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique in accurately segmenting and analyzing cDNA microarray images, even in the presence of noise and other challenges.
The proposed method can be a valuable tool for researchers in the field of genomics and bioinformatics.
This paper proposes a novel method for generating discriminative object proposals using submodular ranking.
Object proposal generation is an important task in computer vision, as it helps in reducing the search space for object detection algorithms.
The proposed method leverages the submodularity property of the ranking function to select a diverse set of object proposals that cover a wide range of object instances.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with existing state-of-the-art methods.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms other methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for generating discriminative object proposals that can improve the performance of object detection algorithms.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning sparse high-dimensional filters for image filtering tasks.
The proposed method combines the strengths of dense conditional random fields (CRFs) and bilateral neural networks to achieve efficient and effective filtering.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various image filtering tasks, including denoising, deblurring, and inpainting.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image filtering and highlights the potential of sparse high-dimensional filters for various image processing tasks.
This paper presents a novel algorithm inspired by quorum sensing, a mechanism used by bacteria to communicate and coordinate their behavior.
The algorithm is designed for dynamic clustering in wireless sensor networks, where nodes need to self-organize into clusters to efficiently perform tasks.
The proposed algorithm utilizes a decentralized approach, where nodes exchange information about their local environment and make decisions based on a consensus reached by a quorum of nodes.
The algorithm is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing clustering algorithms.
The results show that the quorum sensing inspired algorithm outperforms other algorithms in terms of cluster stability, energy efficiency, and scalability.
This research contributes to the field of dynamic clustering in wireless sensor networks and provides insights into the potential applications of quorum sensing in artificial systems.
This paper presents a method for generating a random field using stochastic cliques.
The authors propose a novel approach that starts with a random graph and gradually transforms it into a fully connected random field.
The method involves iteratively adding edges to the graph based on a stochastic process.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through simulations and provide theoretical analysis to support their findings.
The results show that the proposed method can generate random fields that exhibit desired properties, such as spatial smoothness and connectivity.
The authors also discuss potential applications of their method in various fields, including image processing and machine learning.
Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of random field generation and provides a practical approach for creating fully connected random fields.
This paper presents a deep-structured fully-connected random field model for structured inference.
The proposed model combines the strengths of deep learning and random fields to capture complex dependencies in structured data.
The model is trained using a variational inference algorithm that maximizes the evidence lower bound.
Experimental results on various structured prediction tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in capturing dependencies and achieving state-of-the-art performance.
The model also shows robustness to missing data and noise, making it suitable for real-world applications.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of structured inference by introducing a novel deep learning approach that can handle complex structured data.
This paper presents a deep learning approach for object saliency detection and image segmentation.
Object saliency detection aims to identify the most visually significant objects in an image, while image segmentation aims to partition an image into meaningful regions.
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, which is trained on a large dataset of annotated images.
The network is able to learn high-level features that capture the salient objects and regions in an image.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The paper also provides insights into the learned features and their relevance to object saliency and image segmentation.
Overall, this work contributes to the field of computer vision by providing an effective and efficient deep learning approach for object saliency detection and image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel deep learning approach called DeepEdge for top-down contour detection.
The proposed method utilizes a multi-scale bifurcated deep network architecture that combines both global and local information to accurately detect object boundaries.
The network consists of two branches, one for global context extraction and the other for local feature learning.
These branches are then fused at multiple scales to generate high-resolution contour maps.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DeepEdge outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of contour detection accuracy.
Additionally, the proposed method is computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.
This paper presents a scalable variational inference algorithm for log-supermodular models.
Log-supermodular models are a class of probabilistic models that arise in various applications, including social network analysis and combinatorial optimization.
The proposed algorithm leverages the structure of log-supermodular models to develop an efficient variational inference procedure.
The algorithm is scalable to large datasets and can handle high-dimensional parameter spaces.
Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing methods.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of variational inference by providing a scalable solution for log-supermodular models.
This paper presents a novel approach for clothing co-parsing, which involves jointly segmenting and labeling clothing items in images.
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to extract features from the input image and generate pixel-wise segmentation masks.
Additionally, a conditional random field model is employed to incorporate contextual information and refine the segmentation results.
The authors evaluate the performance of their approach on a large-scale dataset and compare it with several state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy and outperforms existing approaches in terms of both segmentation and labeling tasks.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of clothing co-parsing and offers insights into the potential applications of joint image segmentation and labeling techniques.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting meaningful objects from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images using a multi-scale non-local active contour model.
SAR images are known for their complex and noisy nature, making object segmentation a challenging task.
The proposed method addresses this challenge by incorporating both local and non-local information into the active contour model.
The non-local information is obtained by considering the similarity between image patches at different scales.
Experimental results on a dataset of SAR images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting meaningful objects.
The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise.
The findings of this study have implications for various applications, such as target detection and recognition in SAR imagery.
This paper introduces a novel approach for structured prediction tasks using candidate constrained conditional random fields (CRFs).
The proposed method incorporates a loss-aware framework that allows for more accurate predictions by considering the potential loss associated with each candidate label.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various benchmark datasets, showing significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to traditional CRF models.
Additionally, the paper provides insights into the underlying mechanisms of the proposed method and discusses potential applications in natural language processing and computer vision.
Overall, this work contributes to the field of structured prediction by introducing a loss-aware framework that enhances the accuracy of predictions in various domains.
This paper proposes a novel algorithm, called the Multi-Plane Block-Coordinate Frank-Wolfe (MP-BCFW) algorithm, for training Structural Support Vector Machines (SVMs) with a costly max-Oracle.
The max-Oracle is a key component in the training process of Structural SVMs, but it can be computationally expensive to compute.
The MP-BCFW algorithm addresses this issue by introducing a multi-plane block-coordinate strategy that reduces the number of max-Oracle calls required during training.
The algorithm iteratively updates the model parameters by solving a series of subproblems on different planes, each of which corresponds to a different subset of the training data.

Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the MP-BCFW algorithm achieves comparable performance to existing methods while significantly reducing the computational cost of the max-Oracle.
This paper presents a novel approach for face identification using second-order pooling.
The proposed method leverages the second-order statistics of facial features to improve the accuracy of face identification.
The authors conducted experiments on several benchmark datasets and compared the performance of their method with existing state-of-the-art approaches.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of more accurate and reliable face identification systems.
The paper presents CIDI-Lung-Seg, a single-click annotation tool for automatic delineation of lungs from CT scans.
The tool utilizes a deep learning model to segment the lungs and provides a user-friendly interface for annotators to correct and refine the segmentation.
The performance of CIDI-Lung-Seg is evaluated on a dataset of CT scans and compared with other state-of-the-art methods.
The results demonstrate that CIDI-Lung-Seg achieves high accuracy and efficiency in lung segmentation, making it a valuable tool for medical professionals in various clinical applications.
This paper introduces a novel approach called multi-utility learning for structured-output learning tasks with multiple annotation-specific loss functions.
Traditional structured-output learning methods typically use a single loss function to optimize the model parameters.
However, in many real-world applications, different annotations may have different levels of importance or uncertainty, and using a single loss function may not capture this heterogeneity.
The proposed multi-utility learning framework addresses this issue by allowing the use of multiple annotation-specific loss functions.

The authors present a theoretical analysis of the framework and demonstrate its effectiveness through experiments on various structured-output learning tasks, including image segmentation and natural language processing.

The results show that the multi-utility learning approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, highlighting its potential for improving performance in real-world applications.
This paper presents a texture-based image segmentation method for chili pepper X-ray images using Gabor filters.

The proposed method aims to accurately segment the chili pepper regions from the background in X-ray images, which is a challenging task due to the complex texture and shape variations of chili peppers.
The Gabor filter is used to extract texture features from the X-ray images, which are then fed into a clustering algorithm for segmentation.
Experimental results on a dataset of chili pepper X-ray images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting chili pepper regions.
The proposed method can be potentially applied in automated chili pepper sorting and grading systems.
This paper presents a novel approach for brain tumor detection based on mathematical analysis and symmetry information.
The proposed method utilizes mathematical techniques such as Fourier analysis and wavelet transform to extract relevant features from brain MRI images.
These features are then used to train a machine learning model for tumor classification.
Additionally, symmetry information is incorporated into the analysis to improve the accuracy of tumor detection.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy and sensitivity in detecting brain tumors.
This research contributes to the field of medical image analysis and provides a promising method for early detection of brain tumors.
Active contours, also known as snakes, are widely used in image segmentation tasks.
However, traditional active contour models suffer from limitations such as sensitivity to initialization and poor convergence to object boundaries.
In this paper, we propose a novel template-based active contour model that addresses these limitations.
Our approach incorporates a template matching step to initialize the active contour, which improves the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation.
We also introduce a new energy function that combines both image and template information to guide the contour evolution.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in accurately segmenting objects with complex boundaries.
The proposed template-based active contour model shows promising potential for a wide range of applications in computer vision and medical imaging.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for solving the constrained maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference problem.
We introduce the concept of multi-dimensional parametric mincuts, which allows us to efficiently explore the solution space while satisfying the given constraints.
Our method leverages the power of mincuts to find the optimal solution by iteratively updating the parameters and performing mincut computations.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various benchmark datasets and compare it with existing methods.
The experimental results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, our work provides a promising solution for solving the constrained MAP inference problem in multi-dimensional settings.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using a contrario selection of optimal partitions.
The proposed method aims to find the most suitable partition of an image by comparing it to a set of reference partitions.
The selection process is based on a statistical analysis of the differences between the image and the reference partitions.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various image datasets, showing improved segmentation results compared to existing methods.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various fields such as computer vision and medical imaging.
This paper presents a probabilistic approach for image segmentation in video sequences.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, and it involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for image segmentation often fail to handle the temporal coherence in video sequences.
In this paper, we propose a probabilistic framework that models the temporal dependencies between consecutive frames.
We use a Markov random field to represent the spatial and temporal relationships between pixels in the video sequence.
We then formulate the image segmentation problem as an energy minimization task, where the goal is to find the optimal labeling of pixels that minimizes the energy function.
We propose an efficient algorithm based on graph cuts to solve this optimization problem.
Experimental results on various video sequences demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately segmenting objects in video sequences.
Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
This paper presents a feature-based fuzzy rule base design for image extraction.
The proposed method utilizes fuzzy logic and feature extraction techniques to extract relevant information from images.
The feature extraction process involves identifying key features in the image and representing them as fuzzy sets.
These fuzzy sets are then used to construct a fuzzy rule base, which is used to extract the desired information from the image.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on various image datasets.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a novel approach to image extraction using feature-based fuzzy rule base design.
This paper introduces a new concept called combinatorial continuous maximal flows, which extends the traditional notion of maximal flows in graph theory to continuous domains.
We define a combinatorial continuous maximal flow as a function that assigns a flow value to each edge in a graph, subject to certain constraints.
We provide a formal definition of combinatorial continuous maximal flows and prove several properties and theorems related to this concept.
We also present algorithms for computing combinatorial continuous maximal flows and discuss their complexity.
Finally, we demonstrate the practical applications of combinatorial continuous maximal flows in various domains, such as transportation networks and resource allocation problems.
Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and application of maximal flows in continuous domains, opening up new possibilities for solving optimization problems in a wide range of fields.
Automatic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for automatic image segmentation called dynamic region merging.
Our method utilizes a hierarchical region merging strategy to iteratively merge similar regions based on a set of predefined criteria.
We introduce a dynamic thresholding technique to adaptively adjust the merging criteria, allowing for more accurate and robust segmentation results.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method compared to state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.
Additionally, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the impact of different parameters on the segmentation performance.
Overall, our approach offers a promising solution for automatic image segmentation and can be applied to a wide range of real-world applications.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on strong shape priors, which require accurate prior knowledge about the shape of the objects in the image.
However, obtaining such priors can be challenging and time-consuming.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for image segmentation using weak shape priors.
Our method leverages a combination of weak shape priors and deep learning techniques to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results show that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, our work contributes to the development of image segmentation techniques that can be applied in real-world scenarios where strong shape priors are not readily available.

This paper presents a fish recognition system that combines robust feature selection, image segmentation, and geometrical parameter techniques using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Decision Tree (DT) algorithms.
The proposed system aims to accurately identify fish species based on their visual characteristics.
The feature selection process is performed to extract the most discriminative features from the fish images.
Image segmentation is then applied to separate the fish from the background, improving the accuracy of the recognition process.
Geometrical parameters such as length, width, and aspect ratio are extracted to further enhance the recognition accuracy.
The extracted features and geometrical parameters are used as inputs to both ANN and DT algorithms for classification.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in accurately recognizing fish species, achieving high recognition rates.

The combination of robust feature selection, image segmentation, and geometrical parameter techniques with ANN and DT algorithms provides a promising approach for fish recognition in various applications such as fisheries management and biodiversity conservation.
This paper presents a new algorithm for interactive structural image segmentation.
The algorithm utilizes a combination of graph cuts and active contours to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The proposed algorithm incorporates user interaction in the form of scribbles to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm in achieving high-quality segmentations while minimizing user effort.
The algorithm also outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, the proposed algorithm provides a promising approach for interactive structural image segmentation.
This paper investigates the magnetic properties of Sn/1-x/Cr/x/Te diluted magnetic semiconductors.
The samples were prepared using a solid-state reaction method and characterized using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry.
The results show that the samples exhibit ferromagnetic behavior at low temperatures, with the Curie temperature increasing with increasing Cr concentration.
The magnetic properties are attributed to the formation of Cr-doped SnTe phases.
The study provides insights into the magnetic behavior of Sn/1-x/Cr/x/Te diluted magnetic semiconductors and their potential applications in spintronics.
This paper explores the concept of dynamical boson stars, which are compact objects composed of self-gravitating scalar fields.
The authors investigate the dynamical behavior of these objects by solving the Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations numerically.
They find that dynamical boson stars can exhibit a rich variety of behaviors, including oscillations, collapse, and fragmentation.
The authors also study the stability of these objects and find that they can be stable over long timescales.
This work has implications for understanding the formation and evolution of compact objects in the universe, such as black holes and neutron stars.
The paper investigates the limits of the Navier slip model in the context of the moving contact line problem.
The Navier slip model is commonly used to describe the behavior of fluid flow near a solid surface.
However, it has been observed that the model fails to accurately capture the behavior of the moving contact line, which is the interface between a liquid and a solid surface.
The paper explores the reasons for this failure and proposes alternative models that can better describe the behavior of the moving contact line.
The findings of the study have implications for various applications, such as microfluidics and coating processes, where accurate modeling of the moving contact line is crucial.
This paper provides a critical review of biases in Twitter studies on political collective action.
It examines the various biases that can arise in the collection and analysis of Twitter data, including selection bias, measurement bias, and interpretation bias.
The paper argues that these biases can significantly impact the findings and conclusions of Twitter studies on political collective action.
The authors highlight the need for researchers to be aware of and address these biases in their studies to ensure the validity and reliability of their findings.
The paper concludes by offering recommendations for future research to mitigate these biases and improve the understanding of political collective action on Twitter.
The paper "Summing the curious series of Kempner and Irwin" explores the mathematical properties and convergence of two curious series, known as the Kempner series and the Irwin series.
The Kempner series is defined as the sum of the reciprocals of all positive integers that do not contain the digit 9, while the Irwin series is the sum of the reciprocals of all positive integers.
The authors investigate the convergence of these series and provide a proof that the Kempner series converges to a finite value, while the Irwin series diverges.
The paper also discusses the implications of these results and potential applications in number theory and analysis.
This paper presents a particle multi-target tracker for superpositional measurements using labeled random finite sets.

The proposed tracker is able to handle the challenges of tracking multiple targets in a superpositional measurement scenario, where the measurements are ambiguous and can be attributed to multiple targets.
The tracker utilizes a particle filter framework and incorporates a labeled random finite set representation to model the uncertainty in target identities.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed tracker in accurately tracking multiple targets in superpositional measurement scenarios.
This paper presents a formalization of datatype defining rewrite systems for natural numbers and integers.
The authors introduce a new datatype definition for natural numbers and integers, and provide a set of rewrite rules that define the behavior of these datatypes.
The paper also discusses the properties of these rewrite systems, including termination and confluence.
The authors demonstrate the usefulness of these rewrite systems by applying them to various examples and proving the correctness of the resulting computations.
Overall, this paper contributes to the formalization of datatype defining rewrite systems for naturals and integers, providing a foundation for further research in this area.
This paper presents a novel approach to the theory of relativity, proposing a refoundation of its fundamental principles.
The traditional theory of relativity, developed by Albert Einstein, has been highly successful in explaining various phenomena, but it also faces certain conceptual and mathematical challenges.
In this paper, we introduce a new framework that addresses these challenges and provides a more comprehensive understanding of the nature of space, time, and gravity.
Our approach incorporates insights from quantum mechanics and incorporates a modified version of the principle of relativity.
We demonstrate the compatibility of our refounded theory with existing experimental evidence and discuss potential implications for future research.
Overall, this paper offers a fresh perspective on the theory of relativity and opens up new avenues for exploration in the field of theoretical physics.
This paper investigates the pricing of European and Asian options under exponential Lévy processes.
The authors propose a new method for pricing these options based on the characteristic function of the underlying process.
They derive closed-form expressions for the prices of European and Asian options and compare them to existing pricing methods.
The results show that the proposed method provides accurate and efficient pricing for both types of options.
The paper also discusses the implications of the findings for option pricing and risk management in financial markets.
This paper discusses the integration of R Markdown, a reproducible analysis tool, into an introductory statistics course.
The authors describe the benefits of using R Markdown for teaching statistics, including its ability to combine code, text, and output in a single document.
They also discuss the challenges and solutions for implementing R Markdown in the classroom, such as providing students with templates and guidelines for creating their own reports.
The authors conclude that R Markdown is a valuable tool for teaching statistics, as it promotes reproducibility and enhances students' understanding of statistical concepts.
In the paper titled "Ebert's asymmetric three person three color Hat Game," the authors explore a variation of the classic hat game where three players are each assigned a hat of one of three colors.
The players are not allowed to see their own hat color but can see the colors of the other players' hats.
The objective of the game is for the players to correctly guess the color of their own hat.
The authors analyze different strategies and propose a new strategy that allows the players to achieve a higher success rate than previously known strategies.
The paper also discusses the implications of this game for understanding decision-making and communication in asymmetric information scenarios.
The paper presents a simple parallel algorithm called the projector algorithm for computing Voronoi diagrams and Delaunay graphs.
The algorithm is based on the concept of projecting points onto a line and uses a divide-and-conquer approach to efficiently compute the Voronoi diagram and Delaunay graph.
The paper provides a detailed description of the algorithm and its implementation, along with an analysis of its time complexity and parallel efficiency.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm in terms of both speed and scalability.
Overall, the projector algorithm offers a straightforward and efficient solution for computing Voronoi diagrams and Delaunay graphs in parallel.
This paper presents a formal framework for specifying and orchestrating service contracts using automata.
The authors propose a new language, called Service Contract Automata (SCA), which allows for the specification of service contracts in a concise and expressive manner.
They also introduce a novel orchestration mechanism, called Contract Orchestration Automata (COA), which enables the automated execution and enforcement of service contracts.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through a case study involving a real-world service-oriented system.
The results show that SCA and COA provide a powerful and flexible means for specifying and orchestrating service contracts, leading to improved system reliability and performance.
This paper investigates the transition of Charlier polynomials to the Hermite function.
