It suggests that a process-based primitive ontology may be more suitable for describing the fundamental nature of the universe, and that this may have implications for our understanding of the world around us.

Overall, the paper argues that a shift in our understanding of the fundamental nature of the universe, away from objects and towards processes, may be necessary in order to fully resolve the quantum mechanical paradoxes of collapse theories.
We use a simple statistical mechanical model to study the equilibrium properties of a protein aggregate.
The model treats proteins as ideal gases with a square well potential to account for protein-protein interactions.
We determine the conformational states of the monomers and the fraction of water in the system as a function of temperature and protein concentration.
In agreement with experiments, we find that the fraction of water in the system increases with temperature.
We propose that the phase diagram of the model can be used to elucidate the kinetics of protein aggregation.
We present a preliminary study toward a typology and profiling framework of human-machine networks (HUMANETS).

HUMANETS are formed by the interplay between (i) human users networked together to achieve a common goal through their interactions with AI-powered tools, and (ii) operational technologies that leverage AI to optimize the performance of human activities.

To develop a preliminary understanding of HUMANETS, we conducted an exploratory study of two case-study domains where HUMANETS can be observed: collaborative information retrieval and multi-agent systems.

Our results suggest that HUMANETS can be characterized through (i) the structure of the user community, (ii) the nature of user interactions, (iii) the role of AI systems, and (iv) the properties of the tasks undertaken.
We also propose a preliminary profiling framework to assess the performance of HUMANETS, which considers community structure, user experiences, and task outcomes.
We hope that our initial study offers a starting point for further research on the typology and profiling of HUMANETS.
We present a new computational framework for effectively and accurately modeling flow of aggregated particulate suspensions.

The framework is based on coupling of (i) a discrete element method (DEM) module, capable of resolving contacts between individual particles and between particles and the boundaries of the flow domain, and (ii) a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) module, treating the fluid phase of the suspension.
The coupled DEM-CFD model is applied to simulate yielding and flow of dry and wet sand aggregates sheared by an inclined plane.

In order to assess the accuracy and efficiency of the DEM-CFD coupling technique we compare its predictions with available experimental data and with results of fully coupled DEM-CFD simulations, where the DEM and CFD computations are coupled directly at the interface level, via the ghost cell method.

We show that the proposed framework is computationally efficient and provides accurate predictions of the steady-state shear stress and velocity profiles in wet and dry sand aggregates, as well as of the volume change accompanying the yielding event.
We construct a bordered Floer homology for manifolds with torus boundary, as an analog of the usual Floer homology for manifolds with boundary.
Borders are described by immersed curves in the manifold, and the bordered Floer homology is obtained by considering the spaces of these curves, with various boundary conditions, as a chain complex.
We define a boundary map on this chain complex, and show that it is a chain homotopy equivalence to a chain complex of curves without boundary, thus giving rise to a well-defined Floer homology.

As an application, we compute the bordered Floer homology of the manifold obtained by attaching a 2-handle to a 3-torus, and use this to recover the well-known result that the quantum homology of this manifold is isomorphic to that of the 3-sphere.

We study portfolio choice problems in continuous time for a stochastic factor model without assuming normality of the factor returns, using the recent generalized method of moments (GMM) approach of Bansal and Ovtchinnikov (2008).
We derive the optimal portfolio strategy and the corresponding GMM estimator of the investor's mean-variance utility, as well as a confidence interval for the latter.
We investigate the impact of the model's parameters on the portfolio strategy and discuss the conditions under which the investor diversifies her portfolio.
Finally, we illustrate the methods using daily data for the SP500 index and the CBOE's Put-Call Ratio from 1993 to 2003.
Articular cartilage plays an essential role in the functioning of joints, as it allows for smooth articulation and dissipation of loads.
However, it is highly susceptible to injury and degradation, particularly in the presence of repetitive loading.
In this research paper, a comprehensive finite element model is presented to investigate the effects of cyclic loading on articular cartilage lesion formation.
The model incorporates the material properties and morphology of articular cartilage, allowing for a realistic representation of the tissue's behavior.
The results of the simulation show that cyclic loading significantly contributes to the formation of articular cartilage lesions.
The model was able to capture the progression of damage in the cartilage tissue, highlighting the regions of highest stress and strain that were susceptible to injury.
This information is valuable in understanding the mechanisms of articular cartilage injury and developing effective strategies for its prevention.
The findings of this research highlight the importance of considering the effects of cyclic loading in the development of articular cartilage lesions.
By understanding the underlying mechanisms of injury, it may be possible to develop targeted interventions to prevent or mitigate the formation of these lesions.
This may involve the optimization of loading conditions or the use of protective devices to minimize the impact of repetitive loading on articular cartilage.
Ultimately, this research contributes to the ongoing effort to improve the longevity and functionality of articular cartilage in the presence of cyclic loading.

We consider the following natural extension of the constraint satisfaction problem (CSP): given a CSP instance I with a constraint language ${\mathcal{C}}$, and a partially-ordered set ${\mathcal{Q}}$ of quantifications of constraints from ${\mathcal{C}}$, find an assignment to the variables of I that satisfies all constraints in ${\mathcal{C}}$, such that the constraint graph of I under the assignment has no directed path from a constraint in ${\mathcal{C}}$ to a constraint in the inverse of ${\mathcal{Q}}$. We show that this problem is NP-complete, even when the constraint language is fixed and each constraint from this language is satisfied independently of the others.
This result establishes the first known NP- completeness result for an algorithmic problem involving arc consistency.

Let ${\mathbb{Q}}^n_{(>)}$ and ${\mathbb S}^n_{(>)}$ denote the sets of vectors and points on the unit sphere in ${\mathbb R}^{n}$ with coordinates whose absolute values are rational numbers greater than $0$.
We show that these sets are linearly independent.

This solves an open problem and generalizes a known result for ${\mathbb R}^3$. In order to do this, we introduce an operation for vectors in ${\mathbb R}^{n}$, which we call “rotation", that exploits the symmetry between coordinates.
We use this operation to simplify proofs.
This paper continues a program initiated in [@Andruskiewitsch-et-al:axiomatic], where the authors studied the axiomatics of rational convex sets in ${\mathbb R}^{n}$.

We argue that the most relevant issue in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is to provide a sound theoretical foundation for the empirical observation of dome-shaped temperature-pressure diagrams.

Within the framework of the real-space pairing theory, we construct a statistically consistent mean-field theory for superconductivity in the presence of incommensurate charge density wave (CDW) order and phonon-mediated attraction.
In the case of underdoped cuprates, the incommensurate CDW order is induced by a longitudinal phonon mode whose frequency enters the phonon spectrum as a result of electron-phonon interaction.
A finite CDW gap as well as an energy gap in the phonon spectrum are derived as a consequence of the mean-field theory.
We show that the phonon-induced incommensurate CDW order in an underdoped cuprate can give rise to dome-shaped temperature-pressure curves, in agreement with available experimental observations.
We report on a novel scheme for optical excitation of individual ions in silicon.
We show that the Coulomb interaction with a nanoscale charge island significantly modifies the absorption properties of a single Erbium ion implanted into a silicon matrix.
By monitoring the fluorescence of the Erbium ion, we experimentally demonstrate single-ion optical excitation.
Our results open up new possibilities for light-based control of single dopants in a nanoscale optical circuit.

We extend the results of optimal transportations of vector-valued measures on the Euclidean space ${\mathbb R}^n$, classically addressed in the case of finite measures, to the case of vector-valued martingales.

Namely, given two vector-valued martingales with respective values in Banach spaces $(\mathcal M_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\mathcal N_t)_{t \geq 0}$, we study the optimal transportation plan $(\pi_t)_{t \geq 0}$ sending $\mathcal M_t$ to $\mathcal N_t$, i.e. such that for all $t \geq 0$, $$\pi_t(M_t)=N_t,$$ where $M_t$ and $N_t$ are the laws of $\mathcal M_t$ and $\mathcal N_t$ respectively.

The definition of optimal transportation plan in the martingale case relies on a notion of Wasserstein distance between vector-valued martingales, only defined thanks to a tightness result we prove in this paper.
We thereafter characterize the optimality in a Kantorovich duality framework.

We perform a nonlinear double-slit experiment studying the appearance of interference fringes in the transmitted light when the optical path length of one of the slits is modulated at a frequency of 2 MHz.
In linear optics, the interference pattern is independent of the modulation frequency.
However, we show that in nonlinear optics a beat-note effect can lead to modulation of the transmitted intensity at the modulation frequency.
We perform measurements for various input powers and demonstrate that the effect is more pronounced for higher powers.
Our results are in agreement with theoretical predictions based on linear and nonlinear Schrödinger equations.

We study the polarization properties of a multi-moded concentrator and find that the plane-of-polarization visibility of light transmitted through the multi-moded concentrator depends on the orientation of the input polarizer with respect to the optical axes of the multimode fibers comprising the concentrator.
This behavior is quantified by plotting the plane-of-polarization visibility as a function of the polarizer angle for various input launch conditions and fiber configurations.
We also investigate the effect of launching light from a range of input polarizer positions along the concentrator axis.
In this case, the plane-of-polarization visibility shows strong dependence on the input polarizer position, with the optimum position depending on the configuration of the multimode fibers.
By understanding and quantifying these dependencies, we can better optimize the performance of multi-moded concentrators for applications such as free-space optical communication.

Let $X$ be a complex projective hypersurface in $\mathbb P^n$ given by an equation of bidegree ($m, m$), with $m\geq 2$. Neeman proved that if $X$ is non-singular away from a singular point $x\in X$, then $X$ is topologically equivalent to a rational homogeneous variety if and only if the Milnor number of $X$ at $x$ is at most $m-2$.
We prove the same theorem in positive characteristic, under the additional assumption that the characteristic is greater than or equal to $m-1$.
We review the progress in computing weak decays using the method of regions, both at next-to-leading order (NLO) and at next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO).
After recalling the formalism of the method of regions, we present some selected results, mostly for decays of τ leptons and B mesons.
We also discuss on-going improvements to the methods and highlight a few outstanding challenges.

This article was originally published in Chinese in CAIA Core Journal of Contemporary Physics (in Chinese: 科学前沿《科学前沿》), a peer-reviewed scientific journal published in China since 1980 and sponsored by the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
This English edition is published for the purpose of promoting the exchange of scientific information and progress.
The article was translated from Chinese by staff of the Academy, and the translation responsibility lies with the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

A determinantal representation of a polynomial system is a system of linear forms in the coefficients of the polynomials which equals the determinant of a matrix with the coefficients of the polynomials stacked into columns.
We give a simple necessary condition for a polynomial system to admit a determinantal representation, and show that this condition is also sufficient in a special case.
Along the way, we prove a conjecture of Cools and De Loore on the roots of tensor products of modular forms.
We continue our study of the topology of Fatou components for endomorphisms of C^k, answering a question of Dinh about the presence of periodic points in the boundary of the largest Fatou component.
In order to do so, we define a current that is linked with the Green current via boundary continuity, and show that this current has a simple description in terms of periodic points.
In particular, a component of its support contains a periodic point if and only if the corresponding component of the Green current does.
We introduce delta-shock and vacuum states in the framework of the flux approximation for zero-pressure gas dynamics.
The delta-shock state is a particular solution of the gas dynamic equations that corresponds to a discontinuity in the gas velocity.
The vacuum state is a particular solution that corresponds to a region where the gas density approaches zero.
We derive the conditions under which these states are stable and the conditions under which they are unstable.
We also discuss the physical implications of our results and provide some examples of the different types of behavior that can occur in zero-pressure gas dynamics.
This paper studies a fourth-order gradient plasticity model which is based on the concept of energy.
We derive the localization result of this model which indicates that the energies of all the critical points are unbounded below.
The proof is based on the estimation of the energies along the pseudo-gradient flows and a compactness argument.
In the paper, we present several new results on Ramsey-type theorems for lines in 3-space.
These results concern finite configurations of lines, and they generalize results of Erdos, Shelah, and Wagon about graphs.
We also pose some unsolved problems about 2-folds in 4-space, and we relate our results to a recent paper of Connes and Consani.
We study the multiplicity one property of convex sets in the context of the Isoda condition and the group action method.

In particular, we show that if the action of a subgroup of the isometry group on a proper convex set in $\mathbb R^n$ has the property that for every orbit, the intersection with the unit ball is bounded, then the convex set has multiplicity one.
This generalizes a result of Jean-Jacques Risler who showed that if the action is cocompact then this property holds.
We develop a theory of weakly nonlinear self-sustained detonations of premixed combustible gases with simplified thermodynamics.
The theory is based on the one-dimensional hydrodynamic equations with the simplified chemical kinetics, and it is applicable to a wide range of initial gas compositions and ignition strengths.
We obtain traveling wave solutions of the detonation equations and study their stability.

It is shown that the self-sustained detonations exist only for a limited range of the molecular weight ratio of the combustible mixture, and there exists a critical value of the ignition strength below which the detonations are not self-sustained.
The results of the theoretical analysis are compared with the available experimental data.
The enhancement of ion heating observed in JET experiments with high-field side-launching of lower hybrid waves is investigated in the context of particle transport simulations.
An increase of ion heating by lower hybrid waves via resonant charge exchange in comparison to non-resonant diffusion is found at high collision frequencies, but not at low collision frequencies.
This quantifies the increase of ion heating due to the increase of driven currents with increasing collision frequency.

The transport simulations show that lower hybrid waves, launched at a tilt with respect to the magnetic field, lead to a spatial pattern of ion heating in the scrape-off layer that is very different from typical ion heating scenarios, like, e.g., ICRH or lower hybrid waves launched perpendicularly to the magnetic field.
The strong modification of ion temperature profiles obtained in the JET experiments are reproduced in the simulations.

The increase of ion temperatures is traced back to acceleration of ions at the position of the resonant charge exchange, where the electric field of the lower hybrid wave is directed opposite to the ambient electric field.
It is confirmed that at the location of the resonant charge exchange the lower hybrid drive currents are increased compared to a launch perpendicular to the magnetic field.
We give a complete description of all on line and pseudoline configurations of ordered sets of 4 points in the projective plane, and of the associated ball-quotients.
This completes the description of ball-quotients associated to simple configurations in the projective plane that was started in previous papers.
We study the anomalous mass defect of strange stars in the framework of the field corrector method.
To this end, we generalize the formalism to compute the mass defect for macroscopic objects described by a scalar field non-minimally coupled to gravity.
It is shown that the correction to the mass defect is given by an effective gravitational potential which is induced by the change in the gravitational field due to the presence of the scalar field.
This result ensures the conservation of the gravitational Noether charge and provides a physical interpretation of the obtained correction in terms of the gravitational mass.

We apply the formalism to the strange star scenario and show that the correction to the mass defect is positive and depends on the strange quark mass, the scalar field self-coupling, and the non-minimal coupling to gravity.
This result suggests that strange stars might be heavier than predicted by conventional theories, yet consistent with observational data.
In this paper, we consider p-adic differential equations with separation of variables.
We show that such equations can be solved using a modification of the classical Charpit method, and we obtain estimates for the convergence of the solution.

The method is applied to a class of p-adic differential equations that are motivated by number theory, and we obtain approximations for the solutions that are analogous to the classical modular form solutions of Dirichlet's hyperbola equation.

We also show that the p-adic differential equations with separation of variables satisfy a modified version of the classical Liouville theorem, and we use this result to prove that the p-adic differential equations with separation of variables and regular singular points are analytically solvable.

This work may be considered as a first step towards the development of p-adic differential algebra, which is intended to provide solutions to p-adic differential equations that are analogous to the solutions of classical differential equations.

We consider the problem of non-adaptive group testing on graphs where one wants to identify defective items in a set of items, each represented by a vertex of a graph, using a minimum number of group tests where each group test involves grouping items into distinct groups and then performing a test on each group to identify defective items.

We give an algorithm that achieves an approximation ratio of O(log^3(n)/log(w)), where n is the number of items and w is the number of defective items, which is an improvement over the previously best approximation ratio of O(log^2(n)/log(w)).
In addition, we show that the problem is APX-hard when the graph of items is restricted to be a tree.
We give a brief overview of the structure of the moduli space of formal modules over a local ring, with a focus on the case of formal modules over the formal disc.
We discuss the topology of this space, including the computation of its cohomology groups, and we compare the formal module case with the well-studied case of formal schemes.
We have calculated the uncertainties in the sunspot numbers from 1917 to 1992, based on the deviations between the official International Sunspot Number (ISN) and two other sunspot number records.
The uncertainties are found to vary with the solar cycle phase and increase significantly during the solar minima.
There are also long-term trends in the uncertainties.
Our results show a generally good agreement with the uncertainties obtained using the official ISN uncertainties for the recent solar cycles.
However, the uncertainties obtained in this study are generally larger than those from the official ISN uncertainties, especially for the earlier solar cycles.

We have analyzed the causes of the uncertainties and found that the differences in the sunspot numbers are mainly due to the magnetic perturbations in the sunspot regions, and that the uncertainties are also related to the observing practices and the selection of sunspot groups.

The uncertainties derived in this study represent the actual uncertainties in the sunspot numbers, and can be used for better understanding the solar activity and for studying the solar-terrestrial relations.
Gradient magnitude similarity deviation (GMSD) is a newly proposed image quality index.
It is founded on an observation that the gradient magnitude similarity between a distorted image and its original serves as a precise measure for image quality.
In this paper, we provide a comprehensive performance evaluation of GMSD as an image quality index, and explore its applications as a perceptual metric for no-reference image quality assessment.
We further analyze the properties of GMSD and propose a fast algorithm to compute it.
Finally, we present a series of experiments to validate the efficacy of GMSD.
Results show that GMSD achieves state-of-the-art performance on the IQA database.

Dynamics of conflicts in Wikipedia:
A complex network and statistical mechanics approach

Introduction— Wikipedia is a multilingual online encyclopedia with editions maintained by registered volunteers, known as editors.
It has become a popular resource for obtaining information, and its articles are widely used in search engines.
However, the quality of articles varies widely, and the accuracy of information is variable.
Users can modify articles directly, and it is estimated that there are more than 100,000 active contributors to Wikipedia.
Editing of articles is generally collaborative and conversational, with editors expressing opinions and discussing changes.
Whilst many of the edits are undisputed, some lead to edit wars (long sequences of successive edits by editors with opposing views).

It is believed that a better understanding of the dynamics of these conflicts may allow automatic tools to be developed that could detect potentially problematic edits and reduce the likelihood of edit wars occurring.
Method— We investigate conflicts in Wikipedia by considering the edit history of articles, and the associated discussion pages.
We describe a systematic data extraction process that extracts networks of editors and talk pages, and we characterize the community structure of these networks.
We then introduce a new statistical mechanics approach to model the dynamics of conflicts, and we show how it may be used to identify contentious edits and discuss pages.

Results— We find that the network of editors exhibits a small world community structure with a characteristic path length of 4.4 edits, and that the network of talk pages exhibits a similar community structure with a characteristic path length of 5.1 edits.
Using the proposed statistical mechanics approach, we are able to identify contentious edits in a automated manner, and we are able to characterize the dynamics of conflicts on Wikipedia.

Conclusions— The results presented here demonstrate that it is possible to characterize the community structure of networks of editors and talk pages, and to use a statistical mechanics approach to model the dynamics of conflicts in Wikipedia.
We believe that the methods presented here could be used to develop automated tools for detecting potentially problematic edits and for reducing the likelihood of edit wars occurring on Wikipedia.

Recent developments in the study of the dynamics of viscous, heat-conducting fluids in three-dimensional Euclidean space, for the case of the Boussinesq equation, have shown that there exist non-compressible solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations that are characterized by a vector field that is a sum of a curl-free and a divergence-free vector field, both of which are independent of the spatial variable.

It is shown that such vector fields correspond to a class of non-compressible solutions to the full Navier-Stokes equations, which are characterized by a scalar field that is a sum of a curl-free and a divergence-free function, both of which are independent of the spatial variable.
It is further shown that the scalar field can be expressed in terms of a single function of the time variable, which satisfies a modified heat equation.

This result suggests that there may exist a class of non-compressible fluids that are characterized by a single function of the time variable, which satisfies a modified heat equation, and that this class of fluids may have some of the same properties as space time.

Let $G$ be a finite group and let $A$ be the algebra obtained as the symmetric group $S_G$-module algebra of the regular representation of $G$. Let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(A)$ be an automorphism of $A$ preserving the units of $A$.
Denoting by $\operatorname{Inv}(\alpha)$ the set of all $x\in A$ fixed by $\alpha$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $\operatorname{Inv}(\alpha)$ to be a group identity of $A$.
We consider the optimization of a smooth, non-convex, and non-concave function, which is a typical problem in many fields.
We show that Chebyshev polynomial upper and lower bounds for the global optimum can be constructed in a systematic way.

The bounds are of particular interest when the objective function is noisy, as in practice, because they are (globally) convex and concave, respectively, and therefore especially easy to maximize and minimize.

In contrast to previously known bounds for smooth functions, constructed via Taylor polynomials, the new bounds are explicit, i.e., given by a finite number of points, and therefore allow for a better assessment of the quality of the bounds.
Finally, we discuss how to use the new bounds in a trust region framework.

We study gradient systems in one unbounded spatial dimension, which are given by an autonomous equation of the form $\dot{x} = f(x)$ with a superlinearly growing gradient and a uniformly attracting equilibrium.
We show that every bounded solution converges to an equilibrium, providing a global result on the long-time behaviour of gradient systems that complements recent local results.

In a second part, we consider a class of systems for which the previous result fails dramatically: There exist gradient systems with a bistable behaviour, i.e. solutions that oscillate indefinitely between two different equilibria.

We show that, nevertheless, any such solution stays in a strip of width $O(\sqrt{t})$, thereby showing an intermediate behaviour between the global attraction to an equilibrium and the existence of bounded oscillations.

We perform direct numerical simulations of particle trajectories in strained turbulent flow with a focus on the acceleration of heavy particles, where the strain rate is balanced by the pressure gradient.
We observe that heavy particles are accelerated primarily by the strain rate, while the effect of the pressure gradient is to deflect the particle trajectories.
The strain rate accelerates light particles and weakly entrains heavy particles, in line with previous studies of homogeneous strained turbulence.

However, when the strain rate is balanced by the pressure gradient, the weak particle entrainment by the strain rate leads to a significant accumulation of heavy particles in the streaky regions of the flow.
This accumulation enhances particle mixing in the streaky regions of the flow, compared to what would be expected from the strain rate alone.
We validate our results by comparing the particle acceleration with a theoretical model for the acceleration of heavy particles due to the strain rate in homogeneous turbulence.
Our results shed light on the conditions under which strained turbulence can enhance particle mixing in general and in particular in atmospheric and geophysical flows.

Let $G$ be a finite group whose commutator subgroup $G'$ has order $o(G')=q$. It is known that $G$ cannot be soluble if $q$ is a prime power, but the question of whether this statement remains true when $q$ is an arbitrary small number remains open.
In this note we prove that if $q\ne 19$, then $G$ must be soluble.
This resolves a special case of a question proposed by Hall and Senior.
Along the way we present two new results on soluble groups.
We study a model of superconductivity which combines the mechanisms of pair hopping and magnetic interactions at half-filling.
By means of numerical linked-cluster expansions, we determine the ground state and low-lying excitations of the two-dimensional model.
We observe a phase transition between a normal phase and a superconducting phase.
The order parameter exhibits a four-fold symmetry and nodes.
An analysis of the spectral function indicates the presence of Andreev bound states in the superconducting phase.
We introduce the notion of $q$-log-convexity for non-negative functions and study some of its properties.
We show that $q$-log-convex functions are closed under certain linear transformations and composition of functions.
We also present a sufficient condition for a polynomial with only real zeros to be $q$-log-convex in terms of the zeros of the polynomial.
Furthermore, we investigate the relationship between $q$-log-convex functions and the notion of $q$-convexity, and show that for $q \geq 1$, $q$-log-convex functions are $q$-convex.
We find necessary and sufficient conditions for a vector field to couple to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant of a compact 2-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
This gives examples of coupled vector fields which do not preserve the Gauss-Bonnet invariant, thus providing a negative answer to a question of C. Villani.
This paper proposes a parameter decoupling strategy for semi-supervised 3D left atrium segmentation.
The strategy aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process by decoupling the parameters related to the shape and appearance of the left atrium.
The proposed strategy is evaluated on a dataset of 50 patients and compared with other state-of-the-art methods.
The results show that the parameter decoupling strategy achieves higher segmentation accuracy and faster computation time compared to the other methods.
The paper concludes that the proposed strategy can be a valuable tool for accurate and efficient left atrium segmentation in clinical practice.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, existing segmentation frameworks often suffer from limited robustness and generalization, leading to unreliable results and reduced clinical utility.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach towards a robust and generalized medical image segmentation framework.

Our method leverages a combination of deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks, to improve segmentation accuracy and generalization across different medical imaging modalities and datasets.
We evaluate our framework on a diverse set of medical image datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Our results suggest that our proposed framework has the potential to significantly enhance the reliability and clinical utility of medical image segmentation in various healthcare applications.
This paper presents a case study on the application of Neural Architecture Search (NAS) in the operational context of remote sensing.
NAS is a technique that automates the design of neural network architectures, allowing for the discovery of optimal architectures for specific tasks.
In this study, NAS is applied to the task of land cover classification using remote sensing data.
The authors propose a NAS framework that incorporates domain-specific knowledge and constraints to guide the search process.
The results show that the NAS approach outperforms traditional handcrafted architectures in terms of classification accuracy.
The study also highlights the challenges and limitations of applying NAS in the operational context, such as computational requirements and the need for domain expertise.
Overall, this paper demonstrates the potential of NAS in improving the efficiency and effectiveness of remote sensing applications.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical image analysis, as it plays a vital role in various clinical applications.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Pyramid Medical Transformer (PMT) for medical image segmentation.

PMT combines the strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers, leveraging the spatial information captured by CNNs and the global context modeling capabilities of transformers.
The proposed architecture consists of a pyramid feature extraction module, a transformer encoder, and a decoder.
The pyramid feature extraction module extracts multi-scale features from the input image, which are then fed into the transformer encoder for global context modeling.
The decoder module generates the final segmentation map based on the fused features from the encoder.
Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that PMT achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods.
The proposed architecture shows promising potential for accurate and efficient medical image segmentation, which can benefit various clinical applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for ultra-high resolution image segmentation using locality-aware contextual correlation.
The proposed method leverages the contextual information within local regions of an image to improve the accuracy of segmentation.

The authors introduce a locality-aware contextual correlation module that captures the relationships between pixels within a local context and uses this information to refine the segmentation results.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The findings of this study contribute to the field of image segmentation and provide a new perspective on leveraging contextual information for improved segmentation results.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Existing methods typically rely on either image-level or semantic-level context to improve segmentation accuracy.
However, these methods often fail to capture the full range of contextual information available.
In this paper, we propose a novel framework called ISNet that integrates both image-level and semantic-level context for semantic segmentation.
ISNet consists of two modules: an image-level context module and a semantic-level context module.

The image-level context module captures global contextual information by aggregating features from multiple scales, while the semantic-level context module captures local contextual information by incorporating semantic information from neighboring pixels.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that ISNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Furthermore, ablation studies show that the integration of image-level and semantic-level context is crucial for achieving superior performance.
Overall, our proposed ISNet framework provides a comprehensive solution for semantic segmentation by effectively leveraging both image-level and semantic-level context.
PoissonSeg is a novel approach for semi-supervised few-shot medical image segmentation using Poisson learning.
The proposed method leverages a small amount of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data to improve the segmentation performance.

The Poisson learning framework is utilized to model the relationship between the labeled and unlabeled data, and a graph-based propagation algorithm is employed to propagate the labels from the labeled data to the unlabeled data.
Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that PoissonSeg achieves superior segmentation performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation, which is crucial for various clinical applications.
In this paper, we propose a simple contrastive voxel-wise representation distillation method, called SimCVD, for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
SimCVD leverages the unlabeled data to distill the knowledge from a teacher model to a student model.
Specifically, we introduce a voxel-wise contrastive loss to encourage the student model to learn similar representations to the teacher model.
We also design a novel voxel-wise consistency regularization term to further enhance the consistency between the teacher and student models.
Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SimCVD in improving the segmentation performance with limited labeled data.
SimCVD achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to other semi-supervised segmentation methods.
This paper proposes a contrastive semi-supervised learning approach for 2D medical image segmentation.
The goal is to leverage unlabeled data to improve the performance of the segmentation model.
The proposed method uses a contrastive loss function to encourage the model to learn meaningful representations of the unlabeled data.
The authors evaluate the approach on a dataset of 2D medical images and compare it to other semi-supervised learning methods.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms the baseline methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance in 2D medical image segmentation.
The findings suggest that contrastive semi-supervised learning can be an effective approach for improving the accuracy of medical image segmentation models.
This paper proposes a method to improve the quantification of aleatoric uncertainty in multi-annotated medical image segmentation using normalizing flows.
Aleatoric uncertainty refers to the inherent variability in the data, which can arise from factors such as noise or ambiguity in the annotations.
The authors introduce a novel framework that combines normalizing flows, which are powerful generative models, with a multi-annotated segmentation task.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and compared to existing approaches.

The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better uncertainty quantification compared to baseline methods, indicating its potential for improving the reliability and robustness of medical image segmentation.
This paper explores the use of transductive image segmentation techniques, specifically self-training and uncertainty estimation, to improve the accuracy of segmentation algorithms.
The authors propose a novel approach that combines these two techniques to achieve better segmentation results.

The self-training method involves iteratively refining the segmentation model using unlabeled data, while the uncertainty estimation technique helps identify regions of high uncertainty and prioritize them for further refinement.
The authors evaluate their approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods.
The results suggest that the combination of self-training and uncertainty estimation can significantly enhance the performance of transductive image segmentation algorithms.
This paper explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for mapping vulnerable populations.
Vulnerable populations, such as those affected by poverty, natural disasters, or health crises, often face unique challenges that require targeted interventions.
Traditional methods of mapping these populations can be time-consuming and resource-intensive.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages AI algorithms to analyze various data sources, including satellite imagery, social media posts, and demographic data, to identify and map vulnerable populations.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through case studies in different contexts, including disaster response and public health planning.
Our findings suggest that AI-based mapping can provide valuable insights for policymakers and aid organizations to better understand and address the needs of vulnerable populations.

However, we also discuss the ethical considerations and potential limitations of using AI in this context, emphasizing the importance of transparency, accountability, and inclusivity in the development and deployment of these technologies.

Overall, this paper contributes to the growing body of literature on AI applications for social good and highlights the potential of AI in mapping vulnerable populations for more effective and targeted interventions.
Vessel-CAPTCHA: an efficient learning framework for vessel annotation and

segmentation

Abstract:

Vessel annotation and segmentation are crucial tasks in medical image analysis, particularly in the field of retinal imaging.
However, manual annotation of vessels is a time-consuming and labor-intensive process.

In this paper, we propose Vessel-CAPTCHA, a novel learning framework that combines the strengths of human annotators and machine learning algorithms to efficiently annotate and segment vessels in retinal images.
The framework leverages the concept of CAPTCHA, commonly used to distinguish humans from bots, to generate vessel annotation tasks that are easy for humans but challenging for machines.
These tasks are then used to train a deep learning model to automatically annotate vessels in retinal images.
Experimental results on a large dataset of retinal images demonstrate that Vessel-CAPTCHA achieves high accuracy and efficiency in vessel annotation and segmentation, outperforming existing methods.

The proposed framework has the potential to significantly reduce the time and effort required for vessel annotation in retinal imaging, enabling faster and more accurate diagnosis of retinal diseases.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
The Claw U-Net architecture has shown promising results in this domain by combining the U-Net architecture with a claw-like attention mechanism.
However, the Claw U-Net suffers from limited modeling capacity and struggles to capture long-range dependencies in the images.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called TransClaw U-Net, which incorporates transformers into the Claw U-Net to address these limitations.
The transformers enable the model to capture global contextual information and long-range dependencies, leading to improved segmentation performance.
We evaluate the TransClaw U-Net on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the TransClaw U-Net outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
Our proposed architecture shows great potential for advancing medical image segmentation tasks and can contribute to improved diagnosis and treatment planning in the healthcare domain.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable segmentation masks is challenging due to the limited availability of annotated data.
In this paper, we propose a hierarchical self-supervised learning framework for medical image segmentation based on multi-domain data aggregation.
Our approach leverages the inherent hierarchical structure of medical images to learn representations at different levels of abstraction.
We also introduce a novel data aggregation strategy that combines data from multiple domains to improve the generalization performance of the model.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
Our framework has the potential to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of medical image segmentation in clinical practice.
This paper introduces a novel approach to image segmentation using flexibly regularized mixture models.
Traditional mixture models often assume that the data is generated from a fixed number of Gaussian distributions, which may not accurately capture the complex structure of images.
In this work, we propose a flexible regularization framework that allows the number of components in the mixture model to vary spatially across the image.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various image segmentation tasks, including medical image segmentation and object recognition.
Our results show that the flexibly regularized mixture models outperform traditional methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
This work has the potential to significantly improve the performance of image segmentation algorithms in various applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for interactive volumetric image segmentation using a quality-aware memory network.
The proposed method leverages the memory network to store and retrieve high-quality image patches, which are then used to guide the segmentation process.
The quality-awareness is achieved by incorporating a quality estimation module that assigns a confidence score to each stored patch.
The network is trained using a combination of supervised and reinforcement learning techniques to optimize the segmentation performance.
Experimental results on various volumetric image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The quality-aware memory network outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

This work contributes to the field of interactive volumetric image segmentation by introducing a novel approach that combines memory networks and quality-awareness to improve segmentation performance.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
In recent years, deep learning models, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in this field.
However, CNNs have limitations in capturing long-range dependencies and modeling global context information.
To address these limitations, we propose a novel hybrid transformer architecture, called UTNet, for medical image segmentation.
UTNet combines the strengths of both CNNs and transformers by integrating a CNN backbone with transformer encoders.
The CNN backbone extracts local features, while the transformer encoders capture long-range dependencies and global context information.
We evaluate UTNet on three publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
Experimental results demonstrate that UTNet achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the contributions of different components in UTNet.
Overall, our proposed UTNet architecture shows great potential for improving medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a case study on myocardial segmentation in contrast echocardiography using multiple acceptable annotations.
The study aims to address the challenges of manual segmentation in medical imaging by exploring the use of multiple annotations from different experts.
The authors propose a novel approach that combines the annotations using a consensus-based algorithm to generate a final segmentation result.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of contrast echocardiography images and compared with traditional single-annotation segmentation methods.

The results demonstrate that the multiple-annotation approach improves the accuracy and robustness of myocardial segmentation, highlighting its potential for enhancing clinical decision-making and improving patient care in the field of cardiology.
Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications.
In this paper, we propose a novel multi-compound transformer (MCT) for accurate biomedical image segmentation.
The MCT combines the strengths of both transformers and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve segmentation performance.
We introduce a compound transformer module that integrates multiple transformer layers with CNN layers, allowing for better feature extraction and spatial context understanding.
Additionally, we propose a compound attention mechanism that adaptively combines the attention maps from different transformer layers to enhance the segmentation accuracy.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed MCT outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The MCT has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy of biomedical image segmentation, leading to better diagnosis and treatment in the medical field.
This paper proposes a novel approach to improve semi-supervised image segmentation by incorporating global and local mutual information regularization.
The authors argue that existing methods often suffer from limited performance due to the lack of effective regularization techniques.

To address this issue, they introduce a two-step framework that first estimates the global mutual information between the labeled and unlabeled regions, and then utilizes this information to guide the local mutual information estimation.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The authors conclude that the incorporation of global and local mutual information regularization can significantly enhance the performance of semi-supervised image segmentation algorithms.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable ground truth labels for training deep learning models is challenging due to the inherent variability and subjectivity in medical image interpretation.
In this paper, we propose a novel framework for robust medical image segmentation with noisy labels.
Our approach leverages the concept of distillation, where a teacher network with access to clean labels is used to guide the training of a student network with noisy labels.
We introduce a novel loss function that combines the supervised loss from the teacher network and a consistency loss to encourage the student network to produce consistent predictions.
Experimental results on a large dataset of medical images demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to label noise.
Our findings suggest that distillation can be an effective strategy for improving the performance of medical image segmentation models in the presence of noisy labels.
This paper proposes a novel approach called Positional Contrastive Learning (PCL) for volumetric medical image segmentation.
PCL leverages the concept of contrastive learning to learn representations of medical images by maximizing the agreement between positive pairs and minimizing the agreement between negative pairs.
The proposed method incorporates positional information into the contrastive learning framework by introducing a positional encoding module.
This module encodes the spatial information of the medical images, enabling the model to capture the positional relationships between different regions.
Experimental results on various medical image segmentation tasks demonstrate that PCL outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.

The proposed method shows promise for improving the performance of volumetric medical image segmentation and has the potential to contribute to advancements in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is a challenging task in medical image segmentation due to the lack of labeled data in the target domain.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Optimal Latent Vector Alignment (OLVA) for UDA in medical image segmentation.
OLVA aims to align the latent representations of the source and target domains by minimizing the discrepancy between their distributions.
We achieve this by introducing a domain discriminator and a latent vector alignment loss.
We evaluate our method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art UDA methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that OLVA outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.
Our approach provides a promising solution for UDA in medical image segmentation, which can potentially improve the performance of computer-aided diagnosis systems in clinical practice.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called DS-TransUNet, which combines the strengths of the U-Net and the Swin Transformer for accurate and efficient medical image segmentation.
The DS-TransUNet architecture consists of a dual pathway encoder-decoder U-Net, where the encoder is based on the Swin Transformer.
We introduce a dual attention mechanism to capture both local and global contextual information, enabling the model to effectively handle both fine-grained details and large-scale structures.
We evaluate our proposed method on three publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
Experimental results demonstrate that DS-TransUNet achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency, outperforming existing methods by a significant margin.
Our proposed architecture shows great potential for improving medical image segmentation tasks and can be readily applied to various medical imaging modalities.
This paper proposes a few-shot segmentation method for medical images using meta-learning with implicit gradients.
The method aims to address the challenge of limited annotated data in medical image segmentation tasks.
The proposed approach leverages a meta-learning framework to learn a model that can quickly adapt to new segmentation tasks with only a few annotated samples.
The model is trained using a combination of explicit and implicit gradients, which allows for efficient and effective adaptation to new tasks.
Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust segmentation with limited annotated data.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks, which can have significant implications for clinical applications.
IPatch is a novel approach to generating adversarial patches that can be remotely applied to images to deceive deep learning models.
Unlike previous methods that require physical access to the target image, IPatch leverages the power of generative adversarial networks (GANs) to create patches that can be applied remotely.
The proposed method consists of two stages: patch generation and patch application.
In the patch generation stage, a GAN is trained to generate patches that are visually similar to the target image but contain adversarial perturbations.
In the patch application stage, the generated patch is applied to the target image remotely, fooling the deep learning model into misclassifying the image.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of IPatch in evading state-of-the-art deep learning models, highlighting the potential security risks associated with remote adversarial attacks.
This paper presents a novel approach called DAAIN (Detection of Anomalous and Adversarial Input using Normalizing Flows) for detecting anomalous and adversarial inputs in machine learning models.
The proposed method utilizes normalizing flows, a type of generative model, to learn the underlying distribution of the training data.
By comparing the likelihood of a given input with the learned distribution, DAAIN can identify inputs that deviate significantly from the normal data distribution.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of DAAIN on various benchmark datasets and compare it with existing anomaly detection methods.
The results show that DAAIN outperforms other approaches in terms of detection accuracy and robustness against adversarial attacks.

Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of anomaly detection and highlights the potential of normalizing flows for detecting anomalous and adversarial inputs in machine learning models.

BoundarySqueeze: Image Segmentation as Boundary Squeezing

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.

Traditional approaches to image segmentation often rely on pixel-level classification or region-based methods, which can be computationally expensive and may not accurately capture the boundaries between different objects.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation called BoundarySqueeze, which formulates the task as a boundary squeezing problem.
The key idea behind BoundarySqueeze is to iteratively squeeze the boundaries between different objects in an image until they are sufficiently separated.
This is achieved by applying a series of squeezing operations that gradually push the boundaries towards the interior of the objects.
We introduce a new boundary squeezing operator that combines both local and global information to effectively capture the shape and context of the objects.
To evaluate the performance of BoundarySqueeze, we conduct experiments on several benchmark datasets and compare our approach with state-of-the-art methods.
The results demonstrate that BoundarySqueeze achieves competitive performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we show that our approach is robust to variations in image quality and can handle complex scenes with multiple objects.
Overall, our work presents a novel perspective on image segmentation by formulating it as a boundary squeezing problem.
We believe that this approach has the potential to advance the field of image segmentation and open up new possibilities for applications in computer vision.
This paper presents a voxel-level Siamese representation learning approach for abdominal multi-organ segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a Siamese network architecture to learn a shared representation for pairs of input volumes, which are then used to predict the segmentation masks for multiple organs.

The Siamese network is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning, where the supervised loss is computed based on the Dice coefficient between the predicted and ground truth segmentation masks, and the unsupervised loss is computed based on the similarity between the learned representations of the input volumes.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods for abdominal multi-organ segmentation.
The voxel-level Siamese representation learning approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of abdominal multi-organ segmentation in clinical applications.

VICE: Visual Identification and Correction of Neural Circuit Errors

Neural circuit reconstruction is a fundamental task in neuroscience research, enabling the study of brain connectivity and function.
However, the process of reconstructing neural circuits from electron microscopy (EM) images is prone to errors, which can lead to inaccurate circuit representations.
In this paper, we propose VICE, a novel framework for the visual identification and correction of neural circuit errors.
VICE leverages deep learning techniques to automatically detect and classify errors in reconstructed neural circuits.
It then provides an interactive visualization interface that allows neuroscientists to visually inspect and correct these errors.

We evaluate VICE on a large-scale EM dataset and demonstrate its effectiveness in identifying and correcting various types of errors, including missing synapses, false connections, and misaligned segments.
Our results show that VICE significantly improves the accuracy of reconstructed neural circuits and reduces the time and effort required for error correction.

We believe that VICE has the potential to greatly enhance the quality and reliability of neural circuit reconstructions, enabling more accurate and insightful studies of brain connectivity and function.
Geodesic active contours are widely used in image segmentation tasks.
However, existing algorithms often suffer from limitations such as sensitivity to initialization and inability to handle complex image structures.
In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm for geodesic active contours based on characteristic functions.
Our algorithm addresses these limitations by incorporating a characteristic function that captures the image structure and guides the contour evolution.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through experiments on various image segmentation tasks, showing improved accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods.
Additionally, we provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's computational complexity and discuss potential applications and future directions for research.
Overall, our proposed algorithm offers a promising approach for geodesic active contour-based image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for automatic citrus segmentation using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques.
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction and a clustering algorithm for unsupervised segmentation.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of annotated citrus images to learn discriminative features.
The clustering algorithm then groups similar pixels together based on their feature representations.
Experimental results on a dataset of citrus images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy and robustness in citrus segmentation.

The combination of supervised and unsupervised learning allows for the automatic segmentation of citrus fruits without the need for manual annotation, making it a valuable tool for agricultural applications.
This paper presents a novel deep learning architecture called CASSOD-Net, which is designed for embedded vision systems and applications.
The proposed architecture utilizes cascaded and separable structures of dilated convolution to improve the efficiency and accuracy of image processing tasks.
The cascaded structure allows for the integration of multiple dilated convolution layers, enabling the network to capture both local and global contextual information.
The separable structure further reduces the computational complexity by decomposing the convolution operation into depthwise and pointwise convolutions.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that CASSOD-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy while maintaining a low computational cost, making it suitable for real-time embedded vision applications.
MIDeepSeg is a deep learning-based approach for the minimally interactive segmentation of unseen objects from medical images.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of a pre-trained deep neural network and a user-guided interactive segmentation process to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The pre-trained network is fine-tuned using a small set of annotated images, and the interactive segmentation process allows the user to provide minimal input to refine the segmentation.

The experimental results demonstrate that MIDeepSeg outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising tool for medical image analysis and clinical applications.
DatasetGAN is a novel approach to generating labeled datasets for machine learning tasks with minimal human effort.
Traditional methods of dataset creation require extensive manual annotation, which is time-consuming and expensive.
In this paper, we propose a generative adversarial network (GAN) based framework that can automatically generate labeled datasets by synthesizing realistic data samples.
Our approach leverages the power of GANs to learn the underlying data distribution and generate new samples that are indistinguishable from real data.
We also introduce a novel labeling mechanism that allows the GAN to generate labeled samples by conditioning the generator on class labels.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach can generate high-quality labeled datasets with minimal human effort, achieving comparable performance to manually annotated datasets.
DatasetGAN has the potential to significantly reduce the cost and time required for dataset creation, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of machine learning.
This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using a combination of Markov Random Fields (MRF) and U-Net architectures.
The proposed method, called MRF-UNet Product of Experts, leverages the strengths of both MRF and U-Net models to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation tasks.
The MRF component captures the spatial dependencies between pixels, while the U-Net component extracts high-level features from the input image.
The Product of Experts framework combines the predictions from both models to generate the final segmentation result.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The MRF-UNet Product of Experts presents a promising direction for further advancements in image segmentation research.
This paper proposes a novel approach for polyp segmentation using deep ensembles based on Stochastic Activation Selection (SAS).
The authors argue that current methods for polyp segmentation often suffer from high false positive rates and low accuracy.
To address these issues, they introduce SAS, which randomly selects a subset of activation maps from a deep neural network during training.
This stochastic selection process helps to reduce overfitting and improve generalization performance.
The authors evaluate their approach on a large dataset of colonoscopy images and compare it to several state-of-the-art methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and lower false positive rates, demonstrating its effectiveness for polyp segmentation.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for improving polyp segmentation using deep ensembles and stochastic activation selection.
This paper presents a novel approach for decomposing 3D scenes into objects using unsupervised volume segmentation.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning techniques to automatically segment volumetric data into individual objects without the need for manual annotation.
The approach combines a 3D convolutional neural network with a clustering algorithm to identify and separate objects within a scene.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately decomposing complex 3D scenes into their constituent objects.
The proposed approach has potential applications in various fields such as computer vision, robotics, and virtual reality.
The paper proposes a new evaluation metric called Boundary IoU for object-centric image segmentation.
The metric aims to address the limitations of existing metrics such as IoU and Dice coefficient, which do not consider the quality of object boundaries.
Boundary IoU measures the overlap between the predicted object boundaries and the ground truth boundaries, taking into account both the spatial and boundary information.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of Boundary IoU through experiments on various datasets and compare it with other metrics.
The results show that Boundary IoU provides a more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of object-centric image segmentation algorithms.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of Boundary IoU in the field of computer vision.
This paper presents a novel approach for interpreting the behavior of bi-modal and encoder-decoder transformers using a generic attention-model explainability technique.
The proposed method leverages the attention mechanism in transformers to generate attention maps that highlight the important regions in the input data.
The attention maps are then used to explain the model's decision-making process and provide insights into the model's internal workings.

The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through experiments on various bi-modal and encoder-decoder transformer models, showing improved interpretability and performance compared to existing methods.
The results highlight the potential of the generic attention-model explainability technique for understanding and analyzing complex transformer models.
Image registration is a fundamental task in computer vision and medical imaging, which involves aligning two or more images of the same scene or object.
Traditional image registration methods rely on pre-training a model on a large dataset and then applying it to new images at test time.
However, this approach may not generalize well to unseen images or scenes.
In this paper, we propose a novel test-time training approach for deformable multi-scale image registration.
Our method leverages a small set of labeled images during test time to fine-tune the model and improve its performance on unseen images.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various datasets and show that it outperforms traditional pre-training methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Our method also has the advantage of being computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of image registration by introducing a new test-time training approach that improves the performance of deformable multi-scale image registration models.
This paper presents a novel approach for interior object detection and color harmonization in indoor scenes.
The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework to detect and segment objects within an image.
The detected objects are then analyzed for their color properties, and a color harmonization algorithm is applied to ensure a visually pleasing color scheme within the scene.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately detecting objects and achieving color harmonization in various indoor scenes.
The proposed method has potential applications in interior design, virtual reality, and augmented reality.
Domain adaptation is a crucial task in medical image segmentation, as it allows models trained on a source domain to be applied to a target domain with different characteristics.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Margin Preserving Self-paced Contrastive Learning (MP-SPCL) for domain adaptation in medical image segmentation.
MP-SPCL aims to learn domain-invariant representations by leveraging self-paced contrastive learning and preserving the margin between different classes.
We evaluate our method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with several state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that MP-SPCL outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness across different domains.
Our findings suggest that MP-SPCL can effectively address the domain shift problem in medical image segmentation and improve the generalization capability of models in real-world scenarios.
PointFlow is a novel approach for aerial image segmentation that leverages the concept of point clouds to flow semantics through points.

Traditional methods for aerial image segmentation often suffer from the limitations of pixel-based approaches, such as the inability to capture fine-grained details and the lack of robustness to occlusions.
In contrast, PointFlow represents aerial images as point clouds, allowing for more accurate and detailed segmentation.
The proposed method consists of two main components: a point cloud generator and a point cloud segmentation network.
The point cloud generator converts aerial images into point clouds by sampling points from the image and assigning them semantic labels.
The point cloud segmentation network then takes these point clouds as input and predicts the semantic labels for each point.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PointFlow outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to occlusions.
Furthermore, ablation studies are conducted to analyze the effectiveness of different components of PointFlow.
Overall, PointFlow provides a promising solution for aerial image segmentation by effectively flowing semantics through points.
This paper presents a novel approach for capturing omni-range context in the task of omnidirectional segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of panoramic images and depth maps to capture a comprehensive view of the environment.
The panoramic images are processed using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features, while the depth maps are used to generate a depth-aware attention map.
The attention map is then combined with the features extracted from the panoramic images to obtain a context-aware representation.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in omnidirectional segmentation tasks.
The proposed approach has the potential to enhance various applications such as autonomous navigation and augmented reality.
This paper proposes a novel framework called CoTr that efficiently combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers for 3D medical image segmentation.
CNNs have been widely used for this task, but they struggle with capturing long-range dependencies in the data.
Transformers, on the other hand, excel at modeling such dependencies but are computationally expensive.
CoTr addresses this issue by introducing a hybrid architecture that leverages the strengths of both CNNs and transformers.
It uses a CNN backbone to extract local features and a transformer module to capture global dependencies.
Additionally, CoTr introduces a novel cross-scale fusion mechanism to integrate information from different scales.
Experimental results on various medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that CoTr outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed framework has the potential to improve the performance of 3D medical image segmentation tasks and facilitate the development of more advanced medical imaging techniques.
This paper proposes a novel approach for generative synthetic augmentation in the context of nuclei image segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes label-to-image translation techniques to generate synthetic images that closely resemble real nuclei images.
These synthetic images are then used to augment the training dataset, thereby increasing its size and diversity.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on a benchmark dataset, showing significant improvements in segmentation performance compared to traditional data augmentation methods.
The proposed method has the potential to enhance the accuracy and robustness of nuclei image segmentation models, leading to improved performance in various biomedical applications.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, the performance of segmentation models often deteriorates when applied to unseen domains due to domain shift.
In this paper, we propose MixSearch, a novel approach for searching domain generalized medical image segmentation architectures.
MixSearch leverages a mixture of experts framework to combine multiple segmentation models trained on different domains.
We introduce a search space that includes both domain-specific and domain-agnostic operations, allowing the model to adapt to different domains while maintaining generalization capabilities.

We evaluate MixSearch on three medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of both domain-specific and domain-generalized segmentation accuracy.
Our results highlight the potential of MixSearch for improving the robustness and generalization capabilities of medical image segmentation models.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach to solving the self-repelling snake model using the Split Bregman algorithm.
The self-repelling snake model is a widely used method for image segmentation, but it suffers from slow convergence and sensitivity to initialization.
