The Split Bregman algorithm, on the other hand, is a powerful optimization technique that has been successfully applied to various image processing problems.
We demonstrate that by incorporating the Split Bregman algorithm into the self-repelling snake model, we can significantly improve its convergence speed and robustness to initialization.
We provide experimental results on various image datasets to validate the effectiveness of our proposed approach.
Our findings suggest that the Split Bregman algorithm can be a valuable tool for solving the self-repelling snake model and improving the accuracy of image segmentation.
TransUNet is a novel approach for medical image segmentation that utilizes transformers as strong encoders.
The paper introduces a new architecture that combines the benefits of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers.
The proposed model, TransUNet, achieves state-of-the-art performance on various medical image segmentation tasks, surpassing previous methods that rely solely on CNNs.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of TransUNet on three different datasets, including brain tumor segmentation, cardiac segmentation, and retinal vessel segmentation.
The results show that TransUNet outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and generalization ability.
The paper also provides insights into the interpretability of the model by visualizing the attention maps generated by the transformer layers.
Overall, TransUNet presents a promising approach for medical image segmentation, leveraging the power of transformers to improve performance in this critical domain.
This paper presents a method for utilizing uncertainty estimation in deep learning segmentation of fluorescence microscopy images with missing markers.
The authors propose a novel approach that combines a deep learning model with a probabilistic framework to estimate uncertainty in the segmentation results.

The method is evaluated on a dataset of fluorescence microscopy images with missing markers, and the results show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The authors also demonstrate the usefulness of uncertainty estimation in identifying regions of high uncertainty, which can be further investigated by domain experts.

Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of deep learning segmentation in fluorescence microscopy images and highlights the importance of uncertainty estimation in improving segmentation accuracy.
This paper presents a novel approach for object segmentation in images using personal fixations.
The proposed method combines object localization and boundary preservation techniques to accurately segment objects of interest.
The approach leverages the fixations of individual users to identify the most salient regions in an image, which are then used to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and boundary preservation.
The findings of this study have implications for various computer vision applications, such as image recognition and object tracking.
This paper presents a novel framework for natural image segmentation called Affinity Fusion Graph-based Framework.
The proposed framework utilizes a graph-based representation of the image, where nodes represent image pixels and edges represent the affinity between pixels.
The affinity between pixels is computed using a combination of color similarity and spatial proximity.
The framework then applies a fusion algorithm to merge similar regions in the graph, resulting in the segmentation of the image into coherent regions.
Experimental results on various natural images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in achieving accurate and visually pleasing image segmentation.
The proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, the Affinity Fusion Graph-based Framework provides a promising approach for natural image segmentation.
This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework called Deep Class-Specific Affinity-Guided Convolutional Network (DCAG-CNN) for multimodal unpaired image segmentation.
The proposed framework leverages the class-specific affinity information between different modalities to guide the segmentation process.
Specifically, the DCAG-CNN consists of two main components: a modality-specific feature extraction module and a class-specific affinity-guided segmentation module.

The modality-specific feature extraction module extracts discriminative features from each modality separately, while the class-specific affinity-guided segmentation module utilizes the affinity information to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results on two publicly available multimodal datasets demonstrate that the proposed DCAG-CNN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed framework has the potential to improve the performance of multimodal unpaired image segmentation tasks in various applications, such as medical image analysis and remote sensing.
Computer stereo vision is a key technology for enabling autonomous driving systems to perceive and understand the surrounding environment.
This paper presents a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art techniques and algorithms used in computer stereo vision for autonomous driving.
The paper discusses the fundamental principles of stereo vision, including camera calibration, disparity estimation, and depth map generation.
It also explores various approaches for handling challenges such as occlusions, dynamic scenes, and low-texture regions.
Additionally, the paper examines the integration of stereo vision with other perception sensors, such as LiDAR and radar, to enhance the robustness and accuracy of autonomous driving systems.
The paper concludes with a discussion on the future directions and potential advancements in computer stereo vision for autonomous driving.
This paper presents a novel approach for achieving meticulous object segmentation in images.
Object segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and plays a crucial role in various applications such as image recognition and scene understanding.
Existing methods often struggle with accurately segmenting objects with complex boundaries or fine details.
In this work, we propose a two-step approach that combines a deep learning-based semantic segmentation network with a refinement module.
The semantic segmentation network is trained on a large dataset to learn high-level features and generate initial object masks.
The refinement module then refines these masks by incorporating low-level features and leveraging contextual information.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and boundary delineation.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in our approach.
Overall, our method achieves meticulous object segmentation and shows great potential for advancing the field of computer vision.
Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining a large-scale dataset with fully annotated labels for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for robust medical image segmentation on small-scale data with incomplete labels.
Our method leverages the concept of self-training and semi-supervised learning to effectively utilize the available labeled and unlabeled data.
We introduce a consistency regularization term to encourage the model to produce consistent predictions on unlabeled data, which helps improve the segmentation performance.

Additionally, we propose a novel uncertainty estimation technique to identify the most uncertain predictions and prioritize them for expert annotation, thereby iteratively improving the quality of the labeled data.

Experimental results on a small-scale medical image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, achieving competitive segmentation performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Our method shows promise for robust medical image segmentation on small-scale data with incomplete labels, which can greatly benefit clinical applications in resource-constrained settings.
This paper proposes a method for segmenting overlapping wear particles in microscopic images with limited labelled data and imbalanced samples.
The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework and incorporates a novel data augmentation technique to address the scarcity of labelled data.
Additionally, a weighted loss function is introduced to handle the imbalanced nature of the dataset.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness, even with limited labelled data and imbalanced samples.
This research contributes to the field of wear particle analysis and provides a practical solution for segmenting overlapping wear particles in microscopic images.
Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have shown remarkable success in generating realistic images.
However, one common issue with GANs is the lack of perceptual consistency, where small changes in the input can result in significant changes in the generated output.
In this paper, we propose a method to enforce perceptual consistency on GANs by using the Normalised Laplacian Pyramid Distance (NLPD).
The NLPD measures the perceptual similarity between two images by comparing their Laplacian pyramid representations.
We incorporate the NLPD into the loss function of the GAN, encouraging the generator to produce images that are perceptually consistent with the input.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that our method effectively improves the perceptual consistency of GAN-generated images, leading to more visually pleasing and coherent outputs.

Furthermore, we conduct a user study to evaluate the perceptual quality of the generated images, and the results show that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of perceptual consistency.
Overall, our work contributes to addressing the perceptual consistency issue in GANs and provides a practical solution for generating high-quality and visually consistent images.
Video semantic segmentation is a challenging task due to the presence of various distortions in video frames.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Distortion-Aware Feature Correction (DAFC) for video semantic segmentation.
DAFC leverages the temporal information in videos to correct the feature representations of distorted frames.
Specifically, we introduce a distortion-aware feature correction module that adaptively adjusts the feature maps based on the distortion level.
We also propose a distortion-aware loss function that encourages the model to focus on correcting the features of distorted frames.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness to distortions.
Furthermore, ablation studies show the effectiveness of each component in our approach.
Overall, our work provides a promising solution for video semantic segmentation in the presence of distortions.
This paper presents a novel 3D deep coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation.
The proposed framework consists of two stages: a coarse segmentation stage and a fine segmentation stage.
In the coarse segmentation stage, a 3D fully convolutional network is used to generate an initial segmentation map.
This map is then refined in the fine segmentation stage using a 3D U-Net network.
The framework is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning, with the unsupervised learning component being used to generate adversarial examples.

The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated on a dataset of volumetric medical images, and the results show that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Additionally, the framework is shown to be robust against adversarial attacks, with the generated adversarial examples having minimal impact on the segmentation performance.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for volumetric medical image segmentation that can potentially improve the accuracy and reliability of clinical diagnoses.
This paper presents a weakly-supervised learning approach for catheter segmentation in 3D frustum ultrasound images.
The proposed method leverages a combination of weak annotations and a novel loss function to train a deep neural network for accurate catheter segmentation.
The weak annotations are obtained by projecting 2D annotations onto the 3D frustum ultrasound images.
The novel loss function incorporates both pixel-level and region-level information to guide the network training.

Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in catheter segmentation, outperforming existing weakly-supervised and fully-supervised methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of catheter segmentation in clinical applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach called Domain-oriented Feature Embedding (DoFE) for generalizable fundus image segmentation on unseen datasets.
The DoFE method leverages the domain knowledge of fundus images to learn domain-specific feature embeddings, which are then used to train a segmentation model.
The authors evaluate the performance of DoFE on multiple unseen datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The results show that DoFE achieves superior segmentation accuracy and generalizability, making it a promising approach for fundus image segmentation in clinical applications.
This paper presents a deep learning approach for segmenting earth images using imperfect polyline labels with annotation errors.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to learn the segmentation task.
The authors introduce a novel loss function that takes into account the imperfections and errors in the polyline labels.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of earth images and compared with existing segmentation techniques.
The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The findings of this study contribute to the field of earth image analysis and provide insights into the challenges of working with imperfect polyline labels.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate pixel-level annotations for training deep learning models is time-consuming and expensive.
In this paper, we propose a weakly supervised approach for medical image segmentation that leverages extreme points as weak annotations.
We introduce a novel loss function that encourages the model to focus on the extreme points during training.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art weakly supervised methods.
Our results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive segmentation performance while significantly reducing the need for expensive pixel-level annotations.
This work has the potential to accelerate the development of deep learning models for medical image segmentation by reducing the annotation burden on medical experts.
This paper presents LAMP, a framework for training large deep neural networks with automated model parallelism for image segmentation tasks.
Image segmentation is a challenging problem in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into different regions or objects.
Deep neural networks have shown promising results in image segmentation, but training large networks can be computationally expensive and memory-intensive.
LAMP addresses these challenges by automatically partitioning the model across multiple GPUs, enabling efficient parallel training.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of LAMP on various image segmentation datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing training time and memory requirements.
The proposed framework provides a scalable solution for training large deep nets for image segmentation tasks.
This paper proposes a novel approach for object recognition using contour sparse representation with SDD (Shape Descriptor Distribution) features.
The proposed method aims to address the limitations of existing object recognition techniques by leveraging the contour information of objects and incorporating SDD features.
The contour information is extracted using the Canny edge detection algorithm, and the SDD features are computed based on the distribution of shape descriptors.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed method shows promise for improving object recognition accuracy and robustness in various applications.
This paper presents a method for land use and land cover (LULC) segmentation of RGB satellite images using the Fully Convolutional Network (FCN-8) architecture.
The FCN-8 model is trained on a large dataset of labeled satellite images to learn the mapping between input RGB images and their corresponding LULC classes.
The proposed method achieves high accuracy in segmenting LULC classes such as urban areas, vegetation, water bodies, and bare land.

The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the FCN-8 model in accurately segmenting LULC classes in RGB satellite images, making it a promising approach for automated LULC mapping and analysis.
This paper presents a novel algorithm for image labeling using a neural Markovian multiresolution approach.

The proposed algorithm leverages the power of neural networks to learn the underlying structure of images and combines it with a Markovian framework to capture the spatial dependencies between neighboring pixels.
Additionally, the algorithm incorporates a multiresolution strategy to handle images of varying scales and resolutions.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
The algorithm shows promising potential for applications in image segmentation, object recognition, and scene understanding.
This paper explores the concept of learning to pay attention to mistakes and its impact on cognitive processes and performance.
The authors argue that individuals who are able to effectively recognize and learn from their mistakes are more likely to improve their performance and achieve better outcomes.
The paper reviews existing literature on the topic and presents empirical evidence from various studies to support this claim.
Additionally, the authors discuss the potential mechanisms through which learning from mistakes occurs, including attentional processes and metacognitive strategies.

The paper concludes by highlighting the implications of these findings for educational and professional settings, suggesting that promoting a culture of learning from mistakes can enhance individual and organizational performance.
This paper presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields.
Fuzzy active contour models are a popular approach for image segmentation due to their ability to handle complex and ambiguous image data.
The paper provides an overview of the basic concepts and principles of fuzzy active contour models, including the use of fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic in the segmentation process.
It then reviews several recent advancements in fuzzy active contour models, including the incorporation of spatial information, texture information, and shape priors.
The paper also discusses the evaluation metrics used to assess the performance of fuzzy active contour models and provides a comparative analysis of different models based on these metrics.
Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions in the field of fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation.
Overall, this paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in the latest developments in fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting greenhouses on high-resolution optical satellite imagery using deep learning techniques.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to automatically learn and extract relevant features from the input images.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of labeled greenhouse images, enabling it to accurately classify pixels as either greenhouse or non-greenhouse.
The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a test dataset, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately segmenting greenhouses.

The proposed approach offers a promising solution for automating the process of greenhouse segmentation, which can have various applications in agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.
This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised learning of image segmentation based on differentiable feature clustering.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep neural networks to learn meaningful representations of image features and then applies a clustering algorithm to group similar features together.
The key contribution of this work is the introduction of a differentiable clustering loss function that allows end-to-end training of the segmentation model.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust image segmentation without the need for manual annotations.
The proposed approach has the potential to significantly advance the field of unsupervised image segmentation and has implications for various applications in computer vision and image analysis.
This paper proposes a novel approach for medical image segmentation using superpixel-guided label softening.
The traditional approach of directly assigning hard labels to pixels can lead to inaccurate segmentation results, especially in the presence of noise and artifacts.
To address this issue, the authors introduce a superpixel-guided label softening technique that incorporates the spatial information provided by superpixels to improve the accuracy of segmentation.
The proposed method first generates superpixels from the input image and then assigns soft labels to the pixels within each superpixel based on their similarity to the superpixel centroid.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise and artifacts.
The findings of this study have the potential to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation algorithms and improve the diagnosis and treatment of various medical conditions.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, the privacy and security of medical data pose significant challenges in developing accurate and reliable segmentation algorithms.
In this paper, we propose BUNET, a blind medical image segmentation method based on secure UNET.
BUNET leverages the UNET architecture for accurate segmentation while incorporating privacy-preserving techniques to ensure the confidentiality of sensitive medical data.
We evaluate the performance of BUNET on a dataset of medical images and compare it with existing segmentation methods.
The results demonstrate that BUNET achieves competitive segmentation accuracy while maintaining the privacy and security of medical data.
Our proposed method has the potential to enhance the development of secure and reliable medical image segmentation algorithms.
Superpixel segmentation is an important step in many computer vision applications.
In this paper, we propose a novel superpixel segmentation algorithm using dynamic and iterative spanning forest.
The algorithm starts by constructing an initial spanning forest based on the image gradient.
Then, it iteratively updates the forest by merging and splitting the superpixels based on the local image information.
The proposed algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both boundary adherence and compactness.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing methods.
This paper presents a new approach for interactive image segmentation using complex network construction based on particle competition and cooperation.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by leveraging the power of complex networks.
The approach involves representing an image as a graph, where each pixel is a node and the relationships between pixels are represented by edges.
The construction of the complex network is achieved through a particle competition and cooperation algorithm, which assigns weights to the edges based on the similarity between pixels.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The findings of this study contribute to the field of interactive image segmentation and provide a new perspective on the use of complex networks in computer vision tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for automated pavement crack segmentation using a U-Net-based convolutional neural network (CNN).
Pavement crack segmentation is a crucial task in road maintenance and inspection, as it helps in identifying and assessing the severity of cracks.
The proposed method utilizes a U-Net architecture, which has been proven effective in various image segmentation tasks.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of pavement crack images, and the resulting model is capable of accurately segmenting cracks from input images.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy and efficiency in pavement crack segmentation.
The automated system can potentially assist road maintenance and inspection teams in identifying and prioritizing areas that require repair or maintenance.
Automated image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields.
In this paper, we propose a deep learning approach for automated image segmentation that combines region, edge, and contour models into a unified framework.
Our method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to learn and extract features from the input images.
We then employ a multi-task learning strategy to simultaneously train the region, edge, and contour models.
The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive experiments and analysis to provide insights into the learned representations and the impact of different components in our model.

Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of automated image segmentation techniques and provides a comprehensive framework for integrating region, edge, and contour models using deep learning.
This paper proposes a method for learning pose variations within a shape population using constrained mixtures of factor analyzers.
The method aims to capture the underlying structure of the shape population by modeling the pose variations as a mixture of factor analyzers.
The proposed method incorporates constraints on the factor analyzers to ensure that the learned pose variations are consistent with the observed data.
Experimental results on a dataset of human body shapes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in capturing and modeling pose variations within a shape population.
The findings of this study have implications for various applications such as computer vision, robotics, and human-computer interaction.
This paper presents ACNN, a full resolution deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) for medical image segmentation.
ACNN is designed to address the challenges of segmenting medical images with high resolution and complex structures.
The network architecture consists of multiple convolutional layers followed by upsampling layers to preserve the full resolution of the input image.
ACNN also incorporates skip connections to enable information flow between different levels of the network.
The proposed network is trained using a combination of pixel-wise cross-entropy loss and Dice loss.
Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that ACNN achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed network has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation tasks, which can benefit various clinical applications.
This paper presents a deep learning-based automated image segmentation method for concrete petrographic analysis.
Concrete petrography is a critical task in civil engineering, as it involves the identification and characterization of various components in concrete samples.
Traditional manual methods for image segmentation in concrete petrography are time-consuming and subjective.
In this study, we propose a deep learning approach using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically segment concrete images into different components.
The proposed method is trained on a large dataset of annotated concrete images and achieves high accuracy in segmenting various components such as aggregates, cement paste, and air voids.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional manual methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

The proposed deep learning-based automated image segmentation method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of concrete petrographic analysis in civil engineering applications.
This paper proposes a multi-task deep learning approach for image segmentation using recursive approximation tasks.
The authors introduce a novel framework that leverages the power of deep learning to perform image segmentation tasks by recursively approximating the ground truth segmentation masks.
The proposed method is able to learn from multiple tasks simultaneously, leading to improved segmentation performance.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The authors also provide insights into the inner workings of the proposed framework and discuss potential future directions for research in this area.
This paper proposes a novel self-ensembling model for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
The model leverages the consistency regularization framework to enforce transformation consistency between augmented versions of the same input image.
This approach improves the robustness and generalization of the segmentation model by reducing the impact of data augmentation on the final segmentation results.

Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed model has the potential to enhance the accuracy and reliability of medical image segmentation tasks, leading to improved clinical decision-making and patient care.
Few-shot image segmentation is a challenging task that requires the ability to segment objects in images with only a few annotated examples.
In this paper, we propose SimPropNet, an improved similarity propagation method for few-shot image segmentation.

SimPropNet leverages the power of deep neural networks to learn a similarity metric between pixels in the image and propagate the segmentation labels from the annotated examples to the unlabeled pixels.
We introduce a novel similarity propagation module that incorporates both local and global context information to improve the accuracy of the segmentation.
We evaluate SimPropNet on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that SimPropNet achieves superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Our method shows great potential for practical applications in the field of image segmentation.
This paper proposes a spatially constrained deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for nerve fiber segmentation in corneal confocal microscopic images.
The aim is to address the challenge of inaccurate annotations in the training data, which can lead to poor segmentation performance.
The proposed method incorporates a spatial constraint into the CNN architecture to improve the accuracy of nerve fiber segmentation.

Experimental results on a dataset of corneal confocal microscopic images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy, especially when dealing with inaccurate annotations.

The findings of this study have implications for improving the reliability and efficiency of nerve fiber segmentation in corneal confocal microscopic images, which can aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of various ocular diseases.
This paper proposes a novel approach for panoptic image segmentation and the task of splitting unfamiliar objects into parts.
The proposed method utilizes a Generator Evaluator-Selector Net (GES-Net) that combines the strengths of generative models, evaluative models, and selective models.
The GES-Net is trained in a two-step process, where the generator first generates potential object proposals, and the evaluator then evaluates the quality of these proposals.
The selector then selects the most accurate proposals and splits them into parts.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed GES-Net in achieving state-of-the-art performance in both panoptic image segmentation and object splitting tasks.
The proposed method has the potential to advance the field of computer vision and contribute to various applications such as object recognition and scene understanding.
This paper presents a real-time high-performance semantic image segmentation method for urban street scenes.
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The network is trained on a large-scale dataset of street scene images with pixel-level annotations.
The method incorporates several key techniques, including dilated convolutions, atrous spatial pyramid pooling, and skip connections, to improve the segmentation performance.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and speed.
The method achieves real-time performance on a standard GPU, making it suitable for various applications such as autonomous driving and urban planning.
This paper presents a weakly-supervised multi-class semantic segmentation method for Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar data.
The proposed method, called RSS-Net, leverages the rich spatial and temporal information provided by FMCW radar to perform semantic segmentation without the need for pixel-level annotations.
RSS-Net consists of two main components: a radar signal processing module and a segmentation network.
The radar signal processing module extracts features from the raw radar data, while the segmentation network utilizes these features to perform semantic segmentation.
To train RSS-Net, a weak supervision strategy is employed, where only image-level labels are used.
Experimental results on a publicly available FMCW radar dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of RSS-Net in accurately segmenting multiple classes in radar data.
The proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art weakly-supervised and fully-supervised semantic segmentation methods.
Overall, RSS-Net provides a promising approach for multi-class semantic segmentation in FMCW radar data without the need for pixel-level annotations.
Lane detection is a critical task in autonomous driving systems, as it provides crucial information for vehicle control and navigation.
Existing methods for 3D lane detection often suffer from limited generalization and scalability, as they are designed for specific scenarios or require extensive manual annotation.
In this paper, we propose Gen-LaneNet, a novel approach for 3D lane detection that is both generalized and scalable.
Gen-LaneNet leverages a deep neural network architecture that can be trained on diverse datasets without the need for extensive manual annotation.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of Gen-LaneNet on various challenging scenarios and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Our approach has the potential to significantly improve the performance and scalability of 3D lane detection systems in autonomous driving applications.
Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is an important task in machine learning, as it helps identify samples that do not belong to any known classes.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for OOD detection in multi-label datasets using the latent space of a β-variational autoencoder (β-VAE).
We first train a β-VAE on the multi-label dataset and then use the learned latent space to detect OOD samples.
We introduce a novel OOD score based on the reconstruction error and the KL-divergence between the latent space of the β-VAE and a reference distribution.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results show that our method achieves superior performance in OOD detection, outperforming existing approaches.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components of our method.
Overall, our proposed approach demonstrates the effectiveness of using the latent space of a β-VAE for OOD detection in multi-label datasets.
This paper presents a novel approach for semi-supervised semantic image segmentation using self-correcting networks.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the accuracy of segmentation results.
The self-correcting network consists of two components: a segmentation network and a correction network.
The segmentation network generates initial segmentation masks, while the correction network refines these masks by iteratively updating them based on the unlabeled data.
The correction network learns to correct the errors made by the segmentation network, leading to improved segmentation results.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing semi-supervised segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The self-correcting network approach shows promise for improving the performance of semantic image segmentation tasks.
Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, accurate and robust segmentation remains challenging due to the complexity and heterogeneity of brain tumors.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for robust multimodal brain tumor segmentation.

Our method leverages feature disentanglement and gated fusion to effectively integrate information from multiple modalities, including T1-weighted, T1-weighted contrast-enhanced, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images.
We first disentangle the features of each modality using a disentanglement module, which helps to capture modality-specific information.
Then, we employ a gated fusion module to selectively combine the disentangled features, allowing the network to adaptively fuse information from different modalities.

Experimental results on a publicly available brain tumor segmentation dataset demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
Our method also achieves competitive performance on a challenging dataset with a large number of brain tumor subtypes.
Overall, our approach shows promise for improving the accuracy and robustness of brain tumor segmentation, which can have a significant impact on clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.
PointRend is a novel approach to image segmentation that treats the task as a rendering problem.
Traditional segmentation methods typically assign a single label to each pixel, which can result in inaccurate boundaries and loss of fine-grained details.
In contrast, PointRend leverages a set of randomly sampled points within each object instance to generate high-resolution masks.
These points are then used to render the final segmentation mask, resulting in improved boundary quality and preservation of fine details.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that PointRend outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and visual quality.
Additionally, PointRend is computationally efficient and can be easily integrated into existing segmentation pipelines.
Overall, this work presents a promising approach to image segmentation that bridges the gap between traditional pixel-wise methods and rendering-based techniques.
Liver segmentation is an important task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in various clinical applications.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for liver segmentation in abdominal CT images using an auto-context neural network and self-supervised contour attention.

The auto-context neural network is designed to capture the contextual information of the liver region, while the self-supervised contour attention mechanism helps to refine the segmentation results by focusing on the liver boundary.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of liver segmentation in clinical practice, thereby facilitating the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.
Community detection is a fundamental problem in network analysis, with applications in various domains including social networks and biological networks.
In this paper, we propose an unsupervised community detection method based on a Potts model Hamiltonian.
We develop an efficient algorithm to solve the optimization problem associated with the Potts model, which allows us to detect communities in large-scale networks.
We apply our method to digital pathology data, where the goal is to identify distinct regions within tissue samples.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately detecting communities in both synthetic and real-world networks.
Our method has the potential to significantly advance the field of digital pathology by enabling automated analysis of tissue samples.
This paper presents a novel approach for robust submodular minimization, with applications to cooperative modeling.
The proposed method leverages the concept of submodularity to efficiently solve optimization problems in cooperative modeling scenarios.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various datasets.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of cooperative modeling by providing a robust and efficient solution for submodular minimization.
Deep learning-based segmentation methods have shown promising results in medical image analysis tasks.
However, these methods typically require a large number of labeled atlases for training, which can be time-consuming and costly to obtain.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that demonstrates that only a few labeled atlases are necessary for accurate segmentation.

We introduce a framework that combines a deep learning model with a transfer learning strategy to leverage the information from a small number of labeled atlases and a large number of unlabeled images.
Our experiments on a dataset of brain MRI scans show that our approach achieves comparable segmentation performance to methods that use a larger number of labeled atlases.

These findings suggest that our approach can significantly reduce the burden of obtaining labeled atlases for deep learning-based segmentation, making it more accessible and cost-effective for medical image analysis tasks.
Efficient Video Semantic Segmentation with Labels Propagation and Refinement is an academic paper that proposes a novel approach for video semantic segmentation.
The paper introduces a two-step process that combines label propagation and refinement techniques to improve the efficiency and accuracy of video segmentation.
The first step involves propagating labels from keyframes to neighboring frames using a graph-based method.
The second step refines the propagated labels using a convolutional neural network.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of the proposed approach.
Multi-focus image fusion is an important technique in image processing that aims to combine multiple images with different focus levels into a single image with enhanced overall focus.
In this paper, we propose a novel multi-focus image fusion method based on similarity characteristics.
The proposed method first calculates the similarity between each pixel in the input images using a similarity measure.
Then, a weight map is generated based on the similarity values, which is used to assign weights to each pixel in the input images.
Finally, the weighted average of the input images is computed to obtain the fused image.

Experimental results on a dataset of multi-focus images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and objective evaluation metrics.
The proposed method is also computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.
This paper presents a novel method called OASIS (One-pass aligned Atlas Set) for image segmentation.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by aligning multiple atlases in a one-pass manner.
The authors introduce a new alignment algorithm that aligns the atlases to a target image using a hierarchical registration strategy.
The aligned atlases are then used to generate a segmentation map for the target image.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the OASIS method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various medical imaging applications, such as tumor detection and organ segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for interactive 3D medical image segmentation using multi-agent reinforcement learning.
The proposed method leverages the strengths of both human expertise and machine learning algorithms to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The system consists of multiple agents, each responsible for a specific region of interest, and a human expert who provides initial guidance.
The agents are trained using a combination of supervised learning and reinforcement learning, with an iterative refinement process to improve segmentation accuracy.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving superior segmentation performance compared to existing approaches.
The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation, leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
This paper presents an approach for adaptive automatic threat recognition within 3D computed tomography (CT) images for baggage security screening.
The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning framework to automatically detect and classify potential threats within CT images.
The framework is trained on a large dataset of annotated CT images, allowing it to learn and recognize various types of threats.
Additionally, the approach incorporates an adaptive learning mechanism that continuously updates the model based on new data, improving its performance over time.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy in threat detection and classification.
The adaptive nature of the approach also allows it to adapt to new and emerging threats, making it a valuable tool for enhancing baggage security screening systems.
QANet is a novel quality assurance network designed specifically for image segmentation tasks.
Image segmentation is a critical step in many computer vision applications, and ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the segmentation results is of utmost importance.
QANet addresses this challenge by leveraging a deep neural network architecture that combines both local and global information to generate high-quality segmentation masks.
The network is trained using a large dataset of annotated images and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets.

Additionally, QANet incorporates a novel quality assessment module that provides a quantitative measure of the segmentation quality, enabling users to evaluate and compare different segmentation algorithms.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of QANet in improving the quality of image segmentation results.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task that requires pixel-level labeling of objects in an image.
Weakly supervised semantic image segmentation, where only image-level labels are available, is even more challenging.
In this paper, we propose a novel loss function called Gated CRF Loss for weakly supervised semantic image segmentation.
The Gated CRF Loss combines the advantages of Conditional Random Fields (CRF) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) by incorporating a gating mechanism.
This gating mechanism allows the model to selectively apply the CRF loss based on the confidence of the CNN predictions.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed Gated CRF Loss outperforms existing weakly supervised semantic image segmentation methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
Furthermore, we provide an ablation study to analyze the effectiveness of the different components of our proposed loss function.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of weakly supervised semantic image segmentation by introducing a novel loss function that improves the accuracy of the segmentation results.
This paper presents a novel approach for liver segmentation using a deeply self-supervised contour embedded neural network.
Liver segmentation is a crucial step in medical image analysis and plays a vital role in various clinical applications.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning and self-supervised learning to accurately segment the liver from abdominal CT scans.
The contour embedding technique is employed to capture the fine details and boundaries of the liver, enhancing the segmentation performance.
Extensive experiments on a large dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art results in liver segmentation.
The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of liver segmentation in clinical practice, leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper presents a novel approach for post-mortem iris recognition using deep-learning-based image segmentation.
The proposed method aims to address the challenges posed by post-mortem iris images, such as degradation and discoloration.
The authors propose a deep learning architecture that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a U-Net for accurate and robust iris segmentation.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of post-mortem iris images, and the U-Net is used to refine the segmentation results.

Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving high segmentation accuracy and improved iris recognition performance compared to existing methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to enhance the reliability and applicability of iris recognition in forensic investigations and other post-mortem scenarios.

TFLMS: Large Model Support in TensorFlow by Graph Rewriting

Abstract:

Deep learning models have become increasingly complex and require large amounts of memory to train and deploy.
However, existing deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow have limitations in handling large models due to memory constraints.
In this paper, we propose TFLMS, a novel approach to address this issue by introducing large model support in TensorFlow through graph rewriting.
TFLMS leverages the concept of graph rewriting to dynamically allocate and deallocate memory for model parameters, allowing for efficient training and deployment of large models.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of TFLMS through experiments on various deep learning tasks, including image classification and natural language processing.
Our results show that TFLMS significantly reduces memory usage and improves training and inference performance compared to existing approaches.
Furthermore, TFLMS is compatible with existing TensorFlow models and can be easily integrated into the TensorFlow ecosystem.
Overall, TFLMS provides a practical solution for handling large models in TensorFlow, enabling researchers and practitioners to train and deploy complex deep learning models more efficiently.
This paper proposes a novel approach for tumor growth prediction using spatio-temporal convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks.
The method leverages 4D longitudinal patient data, consisting of three-dimensional (3D) medical images captured at multiple time points, to predict tumor growth over time.
The proposed model incorporates both spatial and temporal information by applying convolutional operations on the 3D images and LSTM units to capture temporal dependencies.
Experimental results on a real-world dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately predicting tumor growth, outperforming existing methods.
The proposed model has the potential to assist clinicians in making informed decisions and improving patient outcomes in the field of oncology.
This paper proposes a novel approach for two-phase medical image segmentation using a phase collaborative network.
The proposed network consists of two sub-networks, one for each phase, which collaborate to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The sub-networks are trained separately and then combined using a collaborative mechanism that leverages the complementary information from both phases.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The phase collaborative network shows promise for improving the accuracy of two-phase medical image segmentation, which has important applications in medical diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper proposes a novel approach for automatic image pixel clustering using the Mussels Wandering Optimization (MWO) algorithm.
The MWO algorithm is inspired by the behavior of mussels in their natural habitat and is known for its ability to find optimal solutions in complex optimization problems.
In this study, the MWO algorithm is applied to the task of image pixel clustering, where the goal is to group similar pixels together based on their color and spatial information.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving accurate and efficient image pixel clustering.
The proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art clustering algorithms in terms of clustering accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for automatic image pixel clustering that can be applied to various computer vision tasks.
This paper presents a customizable architecture search method for semantic segmentation tasks.
The proposed method aims to automatically discover the optimal network architecture for semantic segmentation by searching through a large space of possible architectures.
The search process is guided by a customizable search space, which allows users to define their own set of architectural components and their connections.
The method also incorporates a novel search algorithm that efficiently explores the search space and identifies promising architectures.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The customizable nature of the method also allows users to easily adapt it to different semantic segmentation tasks and datasets.

Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of semantic segmentation by introducing a customizable architecture search method that can significantly improve the performance of semantic segmentation models.
This paper presents a weakly supervised segmentation method that utilizes a deep geodesic prior.
The proposed method aims to address the challenge of segmenting objects in images with limited or noisy annotations.
The deep geodesic prior is learned from a large-scale dataset and is used to guide the segmentation process.
The method combines the deep geodesic prior with a weakly supervised learning framework, which allows for training with only image-level labels.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust segmentation results, even with limited supervision.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of the proposed method.
SFSegNet is a deep learning model designed to parse freehand sketches without the need for explicit parsing annotations.
The model utilizes a fully convolutional network architecture to learn the semantic segmentation of sketches.
The proposed model is trained on a large dataset of freehand sketches and achieves competitive performance compared to existing parsing methods that rely on explicit annotations.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the SFSegNet model in accurately parsing freehand sketches, opening up new possibilities for applications in sketch-based image retrieval, virtual reality, and human-computer interaction.
This paper presents a high accurate unhealthy leaf detection method using deep learning techniques.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify leaf images into healthy or unhealthy categories.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of labeled leaf images, which includes various types of unhealthy leaves caused by diseases, pests, and environmental factors.
The trained model achieves a high accuracy rate in detecting unhealthy leaves, outperforming existing methods.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method in detecting unhealthy leaves in different environmental conditions.
The proposed method has potential applications in agriculture and plant disease diagnosis, enabling early detection and prevention of leaf diseases.
This paper presents a study on the application of deep learning architectures for the segmentation of nuclear images in immunofluorescence-based assays.
The authors propose and evaluate several deep learning models, including U-Net, Mask R-CNN, and DeepLabv3+, for this task.
The models are trained and tested on a large dataset of immunofluorescence images, and their performance is compared in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.
The results show that the deep learning models achieve high accuracy in segmenting nuclear images, outperforming traditional image processing techniques.
The study also investigates the impact of different hyperparameters and data augmentation techniques on the performance of the models.
Overall, the findings demonstrate the potential of deep learning architectures for accurate and efficient nuclear image segmentation in immunofluorescence-based assays.
This paper proposes a novel approach for fundus image segmentation using a combination of boundary and entropy-driven adversarial learning.
The proposed method leverages the strengths of both boundary and entropy-based techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of fundus image segmentation.

The boundary-driven adversarial learning module focuses on capturing fine details and boundaries of the fundus images, while the entropy-driven adversarial learning module aims to enhance the overall segmentation performance by reducing uncertainty and noise.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.

The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of fundus image analysis and can potentially contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable diagnostic tools for various retinal diseases.
This paper presents a novel approach for incremental class discovery in semantic segmentation using RGBD sensing.
The proposed method leverages the depth information provided by RGBD sensors to improve the accuracy of class discovery.
The authors introduce a new algorithm that incrementally learns and updates the class models based on the RGBD data.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of semantic segmentation and can contribute to the development of more advanced and accurate algorithms for class discovery.
Video segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, with applications in various domains such as autonomous driving and video surveillance.
However, existing methods for video segmentation often suffer from high computational costs, limiting their real-time performance.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Separable Convolutional LSTMs (SC-LSTMs) for faster video segmentation.
SC-LSTMs leverage the separability property of convolutional operations to reduce the number of parameters and computational complexity.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of SC-LSTMs on several benchmark datasets and show that our approach achieves comparable or even better segmentation accuracy than state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the computational time.
Our results indicate that SC-LSTMs have the potential to enable real-time video segmentation in resource-constrained environments.
Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their inner workings remain largely opaque.
This paper proposes a divide-and-conquer approach to gain a better understanding of deep networks.
The approach involves breaking down the network into smaller subnetworks and analyzing their behavior individually.
By studying the subnetworks, we can gain insights into the network's decision-making process and identify important features and patterns.

Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving interpretability and providing valuable insights into the functioning of deep networks.
The findings of this study contribute to the broader goal of making deep networks more transparent and explainable.
This paper presents a deep active learning approach for axon-myelin segmentation on histology data.
The proposed method combines deep learning models with active learning strategies to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation task.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on a large dataset of histology images.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional segmentation methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance.
The paper also discusses the potential applications of the proposed approach in neuroscience research and clinical practice.
Overall, this work contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing a novel and effective approach for axon-myelin segmentation on histology data.
This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised image segmentation using the max-flow problem.
The max-flow problem is a well-known optimization problem in computer vision, but existing methods for solving it often suffer from inconsistent estimation.
In this paper, we propose a new algorithm that addresses this issue and provides consistent estimation of the max-flow problem.
Our algorithm is based on a combination of graph cuts and belief propagation, and it incorporates a novel energy function that captures both local and global image information.
We evaluate our algorithm on a variety of image segmentation tasks and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing methods.
Our approach has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of unsupervised image segmentation, making it a valuable tool for various computer vision applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for memory-efficient volumetric image segmentation using a partially reversible U-Net architecture.
The proposed method addresses the challenge of limited memory resources in deep learning models for volumetric image segmentation tasks.
The partially reversible U-Net architecture allows for efficient memory utilization by selectively storing and reusing intermediate feature maps during the forward and backward passes.

Experimental results on various volumetric image segmentation datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves comparable segmentation performance to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing memory consumption.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of memory-efficient deep learning models for volumetric image analysis tasks.
Data augmentation is a common technique used in machine learning to improve the generalization performance of models.
However, it is often assumed that the augmented data should be representative of the unseen test data, leading to the use of domain generalization techniques.
In this paper, we challenge this assumption and propose a new perspective on data augmentation.

We argue that in certain cases, unseen domain generalization is unnecessary and that data augmentation can still improve model performance even if the augmented data does not perfectly match the test data distribution.
We provide empirical evidence to support our argument and demonstrate that data augmentation can be effective even when the augmented data is not representative of the unseen test data.

Our findings suggest that researchers and practitioners should reconsider the role of unseen domain generalization in data augmentation and explore alternative approaches that focus on improving model robustness and generalization rather than matching the test data distribution.
VoteNet is a deep learning label fusion method proposed for multi-atlas segmentation.
The method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the relationship between the input image and the corresponding label maps from multiple atlases.
The CNN is trained using a large dataset of labeled images and then used to predict the label maps for new images.
The predicted label maps are then combined using a voting scheme to generate the final segmentation result.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that VoteNet outperforms existing label fusion methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the performance of multi-atlas segmentation in various medical imaging applications.
This paper presents a fast neural architecture search (NAS) method for compact semantic segmentation models using auxiliary cells.
The proposed method aims to reduce the computational cost and memory requirements of NAS while maintaining high segmentation performance.
The authors introduce auxiliary cells, which are small and lightweight network modules, to assist in the search process.
These auxiliary cells are designed to capture low-level features and can be easily integrated into the main network architecture.

The authors conduct experiments on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that their method achieves competitive segmentation performance with significantly reduced computational cost and memory usage compared to existing NAS methods.
Overall, this paper provides a practical and efficient approach for searching compact semantic segmentation models using auxiliary cells.
This paper presents an open-source baseline system for presentation attack detection in iris recognition.
The system utilizes deep learning techniques to detect presentation attacks, such as printed images or contact lenses, that attempt to deceive iris recognition systems.
The proposed system is evaluated on a publicly available dataset and achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The open-source nature of the system allows for easy replication and further development by the research community.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in detecting presentation attacks, highlighting its potential for enhancing the security of iris recognition systems.
This paper presents a novel approach for small target detection in search and rescue operations using distributed deep learning and synthetic data generation.
The proposed method leverages the power of distributed computing to train a deep learning model on a large dataset of synthetic images.
These synthetic images are generated using a combination of computer graphics techniques and real-world data.
The trained model is then used to detect small targets in real-world images captured by search and rescue drones.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately detecting small targets in challenging environments.
The use of synthetic data generation allows for the creation of a diverse and representative dataset, which improves the generalization capabilities of the deep learning model.
The distributed nature of the training process enables efficient utilization of computational resources and reduces the training time.

Overall, this work contributes to the advancement of small target detection techniques for search and rescue operations, with potential applications in various domains such as disaster response and wildlife conservation.
This paper presents a novel approach to region growing algorithms using the Logarithmic Image Processing (LIP) framework.
The LIP framework is a mathematical model that allows for the representation and manipulation of images using logarithmic operations.
In this study, we propose a region homogeneity measure based on the LIP framework, which takes into account the local statistical properties of image regions.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on various image datasets.
The results show that our region homogeneity measure outperforms existing measures in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of region growing algorithms and provides a new perspective on image processing in the LIP framework.
This paper presents a novel approach for the automatic segmentation of porous media in tomography images using 3D quantum cuts.
The proposed method leverages the concept of quantum cuts, which are a graph-based segmentation technique, to accurately identify and separate the different phases present in the porous media.
The algorithm takes advantage of the 3D nature of the tomography images to capture the spatial relationships between the voxels and improve the segmentation results.
Experimental results on a dataset of tomography images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high segmentation accuracy and outperforming existing methods.

The 3D quantum cuts method shows promise for applications in various fields, such as material science and geology, where accurate segmentation of porous media is crucial for understanding their properties and behavior.
This paper proposes a novel approach for data augmentation in the context of one-shot medical image segmentation.
The authors introduce a method that learns transformations from a small set of annotated images and applies them to a larger unlabeled dataset.
The learned transformations are then used to generate augmented images, which are subsequently used to train a segmentation model.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on a dataset of medical images, showing improved segmentation performance compared to traditional data augmentation techniques.
Overall, this work presents a promising method for enhancing the training data in one-shot medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper proposes a few-shot brain segmentation method using deep heteroscedastic multi-task networks trained on weakly labeled data.
The authors address the challenge of limited annotated data for brain segmentation by leveraging weak labels and few-shot learning techniques.
They introduce a novel heteroscedastic multi-task network architecture that can handle uncertainty in the weak labels and learn from limited annotated data.
The proposed method is evaluated on a publicly available brain segmentation dataset and achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The findings suggest that the proposed approach can effectively leverage weakly labeled data for few-shot brain segmentation tasks.
Automatic liver lesion segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.
In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning architecture called Feature Fusion Encoder Decoder Network (FFED-Net) for automatic liver lesion segmentation.
The FFED-Net combines the strengths of both encoder-decoder networks and feature fusion techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of liver lesion segmentation.
We evaluate the performance of the FFED-Net on a publicly available liver lesion segmentation dataset and compare it with several state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the FFED-Net achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Our proposed FFED-Net has the potential to assist radiologists in accurately and efficiently segmenting liver lesions, thereby facilitating the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.
MobileNetV2 is a state-of-the-art deep neural network architecture designed for efficient mobile and embedded vision applications.
This paper presents the design principles and implementation details of MobileNetV2, which builds upon the success of the original MobileNet architecture.
The key contributions of MobileNetV2 include the use of inverted residuals with linear bottlenecks, which improve the efficiency and accuracy of the network.
The inverted residuals allow for better information flow and gradient propagation, while the linear bottlenecks reduce the computational cost of the network.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that MobileNetV2 achieves higher accuracy and efficiency compared to previous architectures, making it a promising solution for resource-constrained devices.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting roots in soil using the U-Net architecture.
The U-Net architecture is a convolutional neural network that has been widely used for image segmentation tasks.
In this study, we adapt the U-Net architecture to segment roots in soil images.
We propose a modified U-Net architecture that incorporates skip connections and data augmentation techniques to improve the accuracy of root segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on a dataset of soil images with ground truth annotations for root segmentation.
Our results show that the proposed U-Net architecture achieves high accuracy in segmenting roots in soil images, outperforming existing methods.
This work has implications for plant biology research and agricultural applications, as accurate root segmentation is crucial for studying root growth and understanding plant-soil interactions.

This paper proposes a method to exploit fully automatic low-level segmented positron emission tomography (PET) data for training high-level deep learning algorithms for the corresponding computed tomography (CT) data.
The authors demonstrate that by utilizing the segmented PET data, the deep learning algorithms can be trained to accurately predict the corresponding CT data.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of PET and CT scans, and the results show that the trained deep learning algorithms achieve high accuracy in predicting the CT data.
This approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of CT data analysis in medical imaging applications.
This paper presents a method for fine-grained semantic segmentation of motion capture data using dilated temporal fully-convolutional networks (DT-FCNs).
Motion capture data is widely used in various applications such as animation, virtual reality, and robotics.
However, the existing methods for segmenting motion capture data into semantic categories are limited in their ability to capture fine-grained details.

The proposed DT-FCN approach addresses this limitation by incorporating dilated convolutions in the temporal dimension, allowing for the capture of both short-term and long-term dependencies in the data.
The method is evaluated on a publicly available motion capture dataset and achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting motion capture data into fine-grained semantic categories.
Salient object detection is an important task in computer vision, with applications in various fields such as remote sensing and medical imaging.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for salient object detection on hyperspectral images using features learned from an unsupervised segmentation task.
