This result has important implications for the study of algebraic number theory and provides a deeper understanding of the relationship between height bounds and the Siegel property.
The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions in this area.
This paper introduces a new class of ensembles called quasi-power law ensembles.
These ensembles are characterized by a power law distribution of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, with an additional exponential cutoff.
The paper presents a mathematical framework for analyzing these ensembles and derives several key properties, such as the average degree and the spectral gap.
The authors also provide a method for generating random graphs from these ensembles and demonstrate their applicability in modeling real-world networks.
The results of this study contribute to the understanding of complex networks and provide a new tool for network analysis and modeling.
This paper investigates the solvability of unit equations over finitely generated domains.
Specifically, we consider the equation x^n = u, where x is an unknown element, n is a positive integer, and u is a unit in the domain.
We provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of solutions to this equation, and we also establish a method for finding all solutions when they do exist.
Our results have applications in various areas of mathematics, including number theory and algebraic geometry.
In this paper, we study tangentially biharmonic Lagrangian H-umbilical submanifolds in complex space forms.
We define the concept of tangentially biharmonic Lagrangian H-umbilical submanifolds and investigate their properties.
We prove that the second variation of the bienergy functional of a tangentially biharmonic Lagrangian H-umbilical submanifold is nonnegative.
We also provide examples of tangentially biharmonic Lagrangian H-umbilical submanifolds in complex space forms.
Our results contribute to the understanding of the geometry of submanifolds in complex space forms and provide new insights into the theory of tangentially biharmonic submanifolds.
This paper introduces the concept of the global Fukaya category I, which is a mathematical framework used to study symplectic geometry and mirror symmetry.

The authors provide a detailed description of the category and its properties, including its relation to other categories such as the wrapped Fukaya category and the derived category of coherent sheaves.
They also discuss the applications of the global Fukaya category I in various areas of mathematics, such as algebraic geometry and mathematical physics.
The paper concludes with open questions and future directions for research in this field.
This paper explores the application of gauge theory on a space with linear Lie type fuzziness.
The concept of fuzziness in physics refers to the uncertainty or imprecision in measurements or calculations.
In this study, the authors propose a new mathematical framework for gauge theory that incorporates the linear Lie type fuzziness.
They develop a set of equations and mathematical tools to describe the behavior of gauge fields on a fuzzy space.
The authors also investigate the implications of this new framework on the physical properties and interactions of gauge fields.
The results of this study provide a novel approach to gauge theory and contribute to the understanding of the effects of fuzziness in physics.

In this paper, we investigate the longitudinal and spin/valley Hall optical conductivity in single layer $MoS_{2}$. We use a tight-binding model to calculate the optical conductivity and analyze the effects of spin and valley degrees of freedom on the Hall conductivity.
We find that the longitudinal conductivity exhibits a strong dependence on the Fermi energy and the spin/valley Hall conductivity shows a non-monotonic behavior as a function of the Fermi energy.
Our results provide insights into the electronic and transport properties of single layer $MoS_{2}$ and can be useful for the design of novel optoelectronic devices based on this material.
This academic paper explores the concept of self-invalidating and self-downgrading behaviors and their impact on interpersonal relationships.

The study aims to understand the underlying motivations and psychological processes that lead individuals to engage in these behaviors, as well as the consequences for both the individual and their relationships.
The research utilizes a mixed-methods approach, including qualitative interviews and quantitative surveys, to gather data from a diverse sample of participants.

The findings suggest that self-invalidating and self-downgrading behaviors are often driven by a desire for acceptance and fear of rejection, and can result in decreased self-esteem, increased conflict, and decreased relationship satisfaction.
The paper concludes with implications for therapeutic interventions and suggestions for future research in this area.
In this paper, we investigate the total electronic Raman scattering in the charge-density-wave (CDW) phase of the spinless Falicov-Kimball model.
We use a combination of analytical and numerical techniques to calculate the Raman response function and analyze its behavior as a function of temperature and interaction strength.
Our results show that the Raman response function exhibits distinct features in the CDW phase, including a peak at the CDW wavevector and a suppression of the response at low frequencies.
We also find that the Raman response function is sensitive to the presence of impurities and disorder in the system.

Overall, our study provides insights into the electronic properties of the CDW phase in the spinless Falicov-Kimball model and highlights the potential of Raman scattering as a probe of CDW order in real materials.
This paper explores the concept of transfinite Adams representability, which extends the classical notion of Adams representability to infinite cardinals.
The authors introduce a new framework for studying transfinite Adams representability and provide several examples and applications.
They also establish connections between transfinite Adams representability and other areas of mathematics, such as set theory and category theory.
The paper concludes with open questions and directions for future research in this emerging field.
In this paper, we study the Puiseux characteristic of a Goursat germ, which is a type of singularity in complex analysis.
We provide a detailed analysis of the Puiseux characteristic and its properties, including its relation to the Newton polygon and the Puiseux series expansion.
We also investigate the behavior of the Puiseux characteristic under certain operations, such as composition and inversion.
Our results contribute to a better understanding of Goursat germs and their singularities, and have potential applications in various areas of mathematics and physics.
This paper investigates the concept of additive triples of bijections, which are sets of three bijections that satisfy certain additive properties.
The authors introduce a new problem called the toroidal semiqueens problem, which involves finding additive triples of bijections on a toroidal grid.
They provide a detailed analysis of this problem and present several results and conjectures.

This paper presents a method for identifying parallel passages across a large corpus of Hebrew and Aramaic texts.
The method utilizes a combination of computational techniques, including text alignment algorithms and statistical analysis, to identify passages that share similar content and structure.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their method by applying it to a corpus of biblical and non-biblical texts, and show that it is able to accurately identify parallel passages with a high degree of precision.

The paper concludes by discussing the implications of this research for the study of Hebrew and Aramaic literature, and suggests potential applications for the method in other areas of textual analysis.
Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) are powerful sources of radiation found at the centers of galaxies.
They are believed to be powered by accretion of matter onto supermassive black holes.
This paper provides an overview of AGN, including their classification, physical properties, and observational characteristics.
The different types of AGN, such as quasars, Seyfert galaxies, and blazars, are discussed, along with their unique features and emission mechanisms.
The paper also explores the role of AGN in galaxy evolution and their connection to other astrophysical phenomena, such as jets and outflows.
Finally, the current understanding of AGN physics and the challenges in studying these enigmatic objects are highlighted.
Overall, this paper serves as a comprehensive introduction to the field of AGN research, providing a foundation for further investigation and exploration.
In this paper, we investigate the properties of indiscriminate covers of infinite translation surfaces.
We show that these covers are innocent, meaning that they do not exhibit any devious behavior.
We provide a rigorous proof of this result and discuss its implications for the study of translation surfaces.
Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the geometric properties of infinite translation surfaces and provide a foundation for further research in this area.
This paper presents a system level numerical analysis of a Monte Carlo simulation of the E. coli chemotaxis.
Chemotaxis is the process by which bacteria move towards or away from chemical gradients in their environment.
The simulation model incorporates various factors such as the concentration of attractants and repellents, the sensitivity of the bacteria to these chemicals, and the random movement of the bacteria.
The numerical analysis focuses on understanding the behavior of the bacteria in response to different environmental conditions.
The results show that the bacteria exhibit a biased random walk towards higher concentrations of attractants and away from repellents.
The analysis also reveals the importance of the sensitivity of the bacteria to the chemicals in determining their movement patterns.
Overall, this study provides insights into the mechanisms underlying bacterial chemotaxis and highlights the potential of Monte Carlo simulations for studying complex biological systems.
This paper presents a study on the structure and morphology of epitaxially grown Fe3O4/NiO bilayers on MgO(001) substrates.
The bilayers were grown using molecular beam epitaxy and characterized using various techniques including X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and atomic force microscopy.
The results show that the Fe3O4 layer grows epitaxially on the MgO substrate with a cube-on-cube orientation relationship, while the NiO layer grows with a rotated cube-on-cube orientation.
The interface between the two layers is found to be sharp and coherent.
The morphology of the bilayers is found to be influenced by the growth conditions, with the Fe3O4 layer exhibiting a smooth surface and the NiO layer showing a rougher surface.

Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the structural and morphological properties of Fe3O4/NiO bilayers, which are important for their potential applications in spintronics and magnetoelectric devices.
This paper presents a finite element formulation for general boundary conditions in incompressible flow simulations.
The formulation is based on the weak imposition of boundary conditions using Lagrange multipliers.
The proposed method allows for the treatment of a wide range of boundary conditions, including Dirichlet, Neumann, and mixed conditions.
The formulation is implemented using the finite element method and is validated through numerical experiments.
The results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method in handling general boundary conditions for incompressible flow simulations.
This paper investigates the performance of algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods for solving non-symmetric matrices that arise in particle methods.
The authors compare the performance of different AMG methods on a range of test problems and analyze the convergence behavior and computational efficiency.

The results show that certain AMG methods are highly effective for solving non-symmetric matrices in particle methods, providing significant improvements in convergence rates and computational efficiency compared to traditional solvers.
The findings of this study have important implications for the development and optimization of particle methods in various scientific and engineering applications.
This paper introduces the concept of principal sub-manifolds, which are sub-manifolds of a given manifold that possess certain geometric properties.

The paper also presents several examples of principal sub-manifolds and explores their relationship with other types of sub-manifolds.

This paper explores the relationship between coloured gravity and electromagnetism.

This paper explores the concept of relative entailment among probabilistic implications.

The paper also discusses the relationship between relative entailment and other notions of entailment, such as logical entailment and probabilistic implication.

Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive analysis of relative entailment among probabilistic implications and offers a valuable tool for reasoning about probabilistic reasoning.
This paper presents a new variational method with Symmetric Periodic Boundary Conditions (SPBC) to study the Newtonian 4-body problem.
The authors propose a new approach that allows for the discovery of many stable choreographic solutions, which are periodic solutions where all four bodies move in a symmetric pattern.

The results of this study contribute to the understanding of the dynamics of the 4-body problem and provide new insights into the existence and stability of choreographic solutions.
This paper presents a generalized entropy approach for studying conserved systems with finite and infinite entities.

The authors compare the insights gained from using the Havrda-Charv\'at-Tsallis entropy, which is suitable for non-Gaussian and non-chi-square distributions, with the insights gained from using the Boltzmann-Shannon entropy, which is suitable for Gaussian distributions.
The authors discuss the implications of their findings for understanding the behavior of conserved systems with different types of distributions.
This paper explores the concept of collective memory in the digital age.
It examines how the proliferation of digital technologies has transformed the way individuals and societies remember and commemorate events.
The paper argues that while digital platforms offer new opportunities for the preservation and dissemination of collective memory, they also present challenges and risks.
It discusses the role of social media, online archives, and digital memorials in shaping collective memory, and highlights the importance of critical engagement with these technologies.
The paper concludes by emphasizing the need for further research and ethical considerations in understanding and harnessing the potential of digital technologies for collective memory.
The GraphBLAS is a standard for graph algorithms in the language of linear algebra.
This paper presents the mathematical foundations of the GraphBLAS, including the definition of a graph, the definition of a graph algorithm, and the definition of the GraphBLAS operations.
The paper also discusses the properties of the GraphBLAS operations, such as associativity and distributivity, and provides examples of how these operations can be used to implement graph algorithms.

This paper presents a kinetic model for understanding the process of cell damage caused by oligomer formation.
Oligomers are small aggregates of proteins that have been implicated in various neurodegenerative diseases.
The model takes into account the formation and degradation of oligomers, as well as their interaction with cellular components.
The model is based on experimental data and incorporates parameters such as oligomer concentration, degradation rate, and binding affinity.
Simulation results show that the model accurately predicts the dynamics of oligomer formation and their impact on cell viability.
The model can be used to study the effects of different factors on oligomer formation and to identify potential therapeutic targets for preventing or reversing cell damage caused by oligomers.
This paper explores the concept of d-complete posets as a generalization of Young diagrams for the Jeu de Taquin property.
The Jeu de Taquin property is a combinatorial property of Young diagrams that allows for the rearrangement of cells in a specific manner.
The authors introduce the notion of d-complete posets, which are posets that satisfy certain conditions related to the Jeu de Taquin property.
They provide a characterization of d-complete posets and study their properties.
The authors also establish a connection between d-complete posets and Young diagrams, showing that d-complete posets can be used to encode the Jeu de Taquin property.
This paper contributes to the understanding of the Jeu de Taquin property and provides a new perspective on its generalization through d-complete posets.
This paper presents a novel approach for estimating gaze direction using full-face appearance-based methods.
Traditional gaze estimation methods rely on eye tracking, which can be intrusive and limited in accuracy.
In contrast, our approach utilizes a deep neural network to analyze facial features and estimate gaze direction.
We propose a multi-task learning framework that simultaneously predicts head pose and gaze direction, leveraging the correlation between these two tasks.
Our experiments on a large-scale dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in gaze estimation.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components in our model.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of gaze estimation by providing a non-intrusive and accurate method that can be applied in various real-world scenarios.
In this paper, we investigate the phase diagram of the zero-bandwidth extended Hubbard model with intersite magnetic interactions in the strong on-site repulsion limit.

We find that the phase diagram exhibits a rich variety of phases, including antiferromagnetic, ferromagnetic, and paramagnetic phases.
We also analyze the effect of the intersite magnetic interactions on the phase diagram and find that they can induce additional phases and modify the boundaries between different phases.

Our results provide insights into the behavior of strongly correlated electron systems with intersite magnetic interactions and have implications for the understanding of magnetic ordering in real materials.
In this paper, we study the existence and properties of large conformal metrics with prescribed scalar curvature on compact Riemannian manifolds.
We establish a general existence result for such metrics under certain conditions on the scalar curvature function.
We also investigate the behavior of these metrics under conformal deformations and prove a rigidity result for metrics with constant scalar curvature.
Our results have applications in various areas of geometry and mathematical physics, including the study of Einstein metrics and the Yamabe problem.
In this paper, we study a pinning model with heavy-tailed disorder, where the disorder potential has a heavy-tailed distribution.
We analyze the critical behavior of the model and investigate the effect of heavy-tailed disorder on the pinning transition.
We find that the critical exponents of the model are modified by the heavy-tailed disorder, leading to a non-trivial scaling behavior.
We also explore the effect of different heavy-tailed distributions on the pinning transition and observe that the critical behavior depends on the tail index of the distribution.
Our results provide insights into the behavior of pinning models with heavy-tailed disorder and contribute to the understanding of the pinning transition in disordered systems.
This paper investigates the sliding friction behavior of a power-law fluid in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime.
The authors conducted experiments using a custom-built tribometer to measure the friction coefficient as a function of sliding velocity and applied load.
The results show that the friction coefficient decreases with increasing sliding velocity and reaches a minimum value at a critical velocity.
Additionally, the friction coefficient increases with increasing applied load.
The authors propose a theoretical model based on the Reynolds equation and the power-law fluid rheology to explain the observed friction behavior.
The model predicts the critical velocity and the friction coefficient as a function of sliding velocity and applied load, which are in good agreement with the experimental data.
This study provides insights into the sliding friction behavior of power-law fluids in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime and can be useful for the design and optimization of lubrication systems.
This paper examines the structural limitations of learning in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) by focusing on communication vulnerability and information diffusion.
The authors argue that the design and structure of MOOCs can hinder effective communication and information sharing among participants, leading to limited learning outcomes.
Through a case study of a popular MOOC platform, the authors analyze the network structure and communication patterns among participants.

They find that certain individuals, referred to as "communication hubs," play a crucial role in information diffusion, while others, referred to as "communication isolates," have limited access to information.

The authors discuss the implications of these findings for the design and facilitation of MOOCs, highlighting the need for strategies to mitigate communication vulnerability and promote equitable information diffusion.
Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of the structural limitations of learning in MOOCs and provides insights for improving the effectiveness of online learning environments.
This paper explores the Khinchin-Kahane and Levy inequalities for abelian metric groups and investigates the transfer from normed (abelian semi)groups to Banach spaces.
The Khinchin-Kahane inequality is a fundamental result in probability theory and functional analysis, while the Levy inequality is a generalization of the Khinchin-Kahane inequality.
The authors establish these inequalities for abelian metric groups and provide a proof of the transfer from normed (abelian semi)groups to Banach spaces.
The results presented in this paper have implications for various areas of mathematics, including probability theory, functional analysis, and metric geometry.
This paper explores the concept of multiactive objects and their applications in various domains.
Multiactive objects are computational entities that can concurrently execute multiple activities, allowing for more efficient and flexible processing.
The paper discusses the design principles and implementation techniques for multiactive objects, as well as their advantages and limitations.
It also presents several case studies where multiactive objects have been successfully applied, including in distributed systems, real-time systems, and parallel computing.

The findings of this research highlight the potential of multiactive objects to improve performance and scalability in various applications, and provide insights for future developments in this field.
In this paper, we present a method for constructing conformal parameterizations of slices of flat Kasner spacetimes.
We start by introducing the concept of conformal parameterizations and their importance in studying spacetime geometries.

This paper investigates the formation of a bubble from a submerged orifice.
The study aims to understand the dynamics and characteristics of the bubble formation process, as well as the factors that influence it.
The experimental setup involves a submerged orifice connected to a gas supply, and the bubble formation process is captured using high-speed imaging.
The results show that the bubble formation process is influenced by various factors, including the gas flow rate, the size of the orifice, and the properties of the surrounding liquid.
The study provides insights into the fundamental mechanisms of bubble formation and can be useful in various applications, such as bubble column reactors and underwater propulsion systems.
This paper presents a complete derivation of the association log-likelihood distance for multi-object tracking.
The association log-likelihood distance is a measure of the similarity between two sets of tracks, and it is commonly used in multi-object tracking algorithms.
The derivation starts with the definition of the association log-likelihood distance and then proceeds to derive its mathematical expression.
The paper also provides a detailed explanation of the derivation steps and discusses the implications of the derived expression.
The derived association log-likelihood distance is shown to be a useful tool for evaluating the performance of multi-object tracking algorithms and can be used to compare different tracking methods.
Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of the association log-likelihood distance and its application in multi-object tracking.
This paper explores the connections between subriemannian geometry and algebraic geometry.
Subriemannian geometry is a branch of differential geometry that studies geometric structures on submanifolds that are not necessarily Riemannian.
Algebraic geometry, on the other hand, studies the geometry of solutions to polynomial equations.
The paper discusses how techniques from algebraic geometry can be applied to study subriemannian structures, and vice versa.

Overall, this paper aims to bridge the gap between subriemannian geometry and algebraic geometry, and highlight the potential for cross-fertilization between these two fields.
The Casimir force is a fundamental phenomenon in physics that arises from quantum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field.

NC-AFM is a powerful technique that allows for high-resolution imaging and manipulation of nanoscale objects without physical contact.
We discuss the advantages of NC-AFM for Casimir force measurements, including its ability to measure forces in a wide range of distances and its potential for reducing systematic errors.
We also discuss the challenges and limitations of using NC-AFM for Casimir force measurements, such as the need for precise calibration and the influence of surface roughness.
Overall, we conclude that NC-AFM has the potential to significantly advance the field of Casimir force measurements and provide new insights into the nature of the Casimir force.
This paper presents the observation of empty liquids and equilibrium gels in a colloidal clay system.
The authors use confocal microscopy to study the structure and dynamics of the colloidal clay particles.
They find that at low concentrations, the system forms an empty liquid phase, where the particles are dispersed and do not form any structure.
At higher concentrations, the system transitions to an equilibrium gel phase, where the particles form a network-like structure.
The authors also investigate the effect of particle size and concentration on the formation of these phases.
Overall, this study provides insights into the behavior of colloidal clay systems and contributes to our understanding of the self-assembly of colloidal particles.
This paper presents a distributed tracking algorithm for the reconstruction of graph signals.
The algorithm is designed to handle large-scale graphs and is based on a consensus-based approach.
The proposed algorithm is able to track the evolution of graph signals over time, even in the presence of noise and missing data.
The algorithm is evaluated through simulations on various types of graphs and signal models, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately reconstructing graph signals.
The proposed algorithm has potential applications in various fields, such as social network analysis, sensor networks, and image processing.
In this paper, we investigate the parameter space of the spin-orbit problem, focusing on the existence and stability of normally hyperbolic invariant circles (NHICs).
We provide a detailed analysis of the bifurcation diagram and identify regions in parameter space where NHICs exist.
We also study the stability of these NHICs using the Melnikov method and find that they can be stable under certain conditions.
Our results contribute to a better understanding of the spin-orbit problem and provide insights into the dynamics of NHICs in this system.
This paper investigates the role of natural convection in the dissolution of sessile droplets.
Sessile droplets are liquid droplets that are deposited on a solid surface and do not spread.
The dissolution of these droplets is an important process in various applications, such as pharmaceuticals, food processing, and environmental monitoring.
The authors conducted experiments to study the dissolution behavior of sessile droplets under different conditions, including varying droplet size, temperature, and concentration of the solute.
They found that natural convection plays a significant role in the dissolution process, affecting the dissolution rate and the distribution of the solute within the droplet.
The authors also developed a mathematical model to describe the dissolution process, taking into account the effects of natural convection.
The results of this study provide insights into the dissolution behavior of sessile droplets and can be used to optimize processes involving droplet dissolution.
This paper proposes a three-detector short-baseline neutrino oscillation program in the Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam.
The program aims to study neutrino oscillations at short baselines using a combination of near, intermediate, and far detectors.
The near detector will provide precise measurements of the neutrino flux and cross-sections, while the intermediate and far detectors will measure the neutrino oscillation parameters.
The proposed program will provide valuable insights into neutrino oscillations and help address some of the outstanding questions in neutrino physics.
This paper investigates the effect of interface anisotropy on the precession of magnetization induced by laser heating.
The authors demonstrate that the presence of interface anisotropy can lead to a $\pi$ phase shift in the precession of magnetization.
This effect is attributed to the competition between the exchange interaction and the interface anisotropy.
The authors propose a theoretical model to explain this phenomenon and validate their findings through numerical simulations.
The results of this study provide insights into the dynamics of magnetization precession and have potential implications for the design of spintronic devices.
This paper presents lower bounds on the oracle complexity of nonsmooth convex optimization problems using information theory.
The oracle complexity measures the number of queries required to solve a problem using an oracle, which provides information about the objective function and its derivatives.

The authors derive lower bounds on the oracle complexity for a class of nonsmooth convex optimization problems, showing that the number of queries required to solve these problems is inherently large.
These lower bounds provide insights into the inherent difficulty of solving nonsmooth convex optimization problems and can guide the development of more efficient algorithms.
The results are supported by theoretical analysis and numerical experiments.
This paper introduces a new proof system called nested hypersequents, which combines the advantages of both nested sequents and hypersequents.
Nested hypersequents allow for a more compact and intuitive representation of proofs, while still maintaining the expressive power of hypersequents.
The paper presents the syntax and proof rules for nested hypersequents, and proves soundness and completeness results for the system.

Additionally, the paper explores the relationship between nested hypersequents and other proof systems, such as nested sequents and hypersequents, and discusses potential applications and future directions for research in this area.
In this paper, we investigate the interaction between $F(R,T)$ gravity and modified Chaplygin gas (MCG) in the framework of a homogeneous and isotropic universe.
We derive the field equations for the $F(R,T)$ gravity with MCG and obtain the corresponding Friedmann equations.
We then analyze the behavior of the scale factor and energy density for different values of the parameters in the model.
We find that the interaction between $F(R,T)$ gravity and MCG can lead to interesting cosmological scenarios, such as accelerated expansion and late-time cosmic acceleration.
Our results provide insights into the dynamics of the universe in the presence of $F(R,T)$ gravity and MCG, and may have implications for understanding the nature of dark energy.
This paper presents a method for the absolute calibration of fiber-coupled single-photon detectors.
The calibration procedure involves measuring the detection efficiency and dark count rate of the detector using a calibrated reference source.
The reference source consists of a single-photon emitter and a calibrated power meter.
The calibration is performed at multiple wavelengths to account for any wavelength-dependent effects.
The results show that the calibration method is accurate and reliable, with uncertainties of less than 1%.

This absolute calibration allows for the accurate determination of the detection efficiency and dark count rate of fiber-coupled single-photon detectors, enabling more precise measurements in various applications such as quantum communication and quantum sensing.
This paper presents a mathematical model to investigate the effects of multiple myeloma on kidney function.
Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells that can lead to kidney damage and dysfunction.
The model incorporates various factors such as tumor growth, immune response, and kidney function to simulate the progression of the disease and its impact on renal function.
The model is validated using clinical data and can be used to predict the effects of different treatment strategies on kidney function.
The results of the simulations suggest that early detection and intervention are crucial in preserving kidney function in multiple myeloma patients.

This model provides a valuable tool for understanding the complex interactions between multiple myeloma and kidney function and can aid in the development of personalized treatment plans for patients.
In this paper, we study the problem of random online domination of the path graph.
We consider the best and worst case permutations for this problem, where the goal is to find the minimum number of vertices that need to be dominated in order to cover the entire graph.
We analyze the performance of various algorithms for this problem and provide theoretical bounds on the number of dominated vertices.
Our results show that the best case permutation can be achieved by a greedy algorithm, while the worst case permutation requires a more complex approach.
We also discuss the implications of our findings for practical applications of random online domination in real-world networks.
This paper investigates the formation of carrier field shocks in dispersive media when long wavelength femtosecond pulses are propagated.
The authors use numerical simulations to study the dynamics of the carrier field and find that shocks can form due to the interplay between dispersion and self-phase modulation.
The results show that the shock formation is influenced by the initial pulse shape and the dispersion properties of the medium.
The findings of this study provide insights into the behavior of long wavelength femtosecond pulses in dispersive media and have implications for the design of optical devices and systems.
This paper introduces a new family of random noble means substitutions, which are a type of mathematical transformation used in number theory and dynamical systems.
The authors provide a detailed analysis of the properties and behavior of these substitutions, including their convergence properties and the distribution of their fixed points.
They also explore the relationship between these substitutions and other well-known families of substitutions, such as the Fibonacci substitution.
The results of this study contribute to our understanding of the behavior of noble means substitutions and provide new insights into their mathematical properties.
This paper investigates the phenomenon of quantum percolation in finite regular graphs.
Quantum percolation refers to the behavior of quantum particles moving through a network of interconnected nodes.

The authors analyze the conditions under which quantum percolation occurs in finite regular graphs, and explore the effects of various parameters such as graph size and connectivity on the percolation threshold.

The study utilizes mathematical models and simulations to provide insights into the behavior of quantum particles in finite regular graphs, and offers potential applications in fields such as quantum computing and network analysis.
The findings contribute to the understanding of quantum percolation in finite regular graphs and provide a foundation for further research in this area.
Van der Waals heterostructures have emerged as a promising platform for next-generation electronic devices due to their unique properties and potential for integration.

In this paper, we investigate the dielectric genome of van der Waals heterostructures, which refers to the set of all possible dielectric combinations that can be formed by stacking different 2D materials.
We present a comprehensive study of the dielectric properties of various van der Waals heterostructures using first-principles calculations.
Our results reveal a rich landscape of dielectric properties, including high dielectric constants, tunable band gaps, and strong dielectric screening effects.
We also explore the impact of strain and interlayer coupling on the dielectric properties of these heterostructures.
Our findings provide valuable insights into the design and optimization of van der Waals heterostructures for future electronic applications.
The paper presents a multidimensional version of the Szemerédi theorem in the context of prime numbers.
The Szemerédi theorem is a fundamental result in combinatorics that states that any subset of the natural numbers with positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
The authors extend this result to multiple dimensions by considering subsets of the prime numbers with positive upper density.
They prove that such subsets contain arbitrarily large multidimensional arithmetic progressions.
The proof involves a combination of techniques from number theory, combinatorics, and ergodic theory.
The multidimensional Szemerédi theorem in the primes has applications in various areas of mathematics, including additive combinatorics and number theory.
This paper investigates the reductions of points on algebraic groups.
The authors study the behavior of points on algebraic groups under reduction modulo a prime number.
They provide a general framework for understanding the reduction of points on algebraic groups and establish several key results.
The authors also explore the relationship between the reduction of points on algebraic groups and the reduction of points on their associated Lie algebras.
The paper concludes with applications of these results to the study of rational points on algebraic groups.
Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of reductions of points on algebraic groups and their implications in various areas of mathematics.
This paper investigates the concepts of expansivity and shadowing in linear dynamics.
Expansivity refers to the property of a dynamical system where nearby points diverge exponentially over time.
Shadowing, on the other hand, refers to the property where a trajectory can be approximated by a nearby trajectory for an extended period of time.
The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of these properties in the context of linear dynamics, providing theoretical results and numerical examples.

The findings highlight the importance of expansivity and shadowing in understanding the behavior of linear dynamical systems and their applications in various fields such as physics, engineering, and computer science.
This paper presents a method for optimising the measurement of relativistic distortions in large-scale structure.
The authors propose a new statistical framework that takes into account the effects of general relativity on the observed distribution of galaxies.
They demonstrate the effectiveness of their method using simulated data and show that it can accurately recover the underlying relativistic distortions.
The proposed framework has the potential to improve our understanding of the large-scale structure of the universe and provide valuable insights into the nature of gravity on cosmological scales.
This paper investigates the relationship between certain categorical-algebraic conditions in S-protomodular categories.
Specifically, the authors examine the conditions of being a regular category, having a strong zero object, and being a semi-abelian category.
They establish several results and provide examples to illustrate the connections between these conditions.

The paper contributes to the understanding of the structure and properties of S-protomodular categories, and highlights the importance of these categorical-algebraic conditions in characterizing different classes of categories.
This paper explores the geometrization of Maxwell's equations and its implications for the emergence of gravity.
It begins by discussing the historical development of Maxwell's equations and their role in describing electromagnetic phenomena.
The paper then introduces the concept of geometrization, which involves expressing physical laws in terms of geometric quantities.
It examines how Maxwell's equations can be reformulated in a geometric framework, known as the theory of electromagnetism on curved spacetime.
The paper further investigates the connection between electromagnetism and gravity, highlighting the similarities and differences between the two forces.
It concludes by discussing the implications of the geometrization of Maxwell's equations for our understanding of the emergence of gravity and the unification of fundamental forces.
In this paper, we introduce a new algorithm called the Medusa Algorithm for polynomial matings.
Polynomial matings are a powerful tool in the field of complex dynamics, allowing for the construction of new rational maps with interesting properties.
The Medusa Algorithm builds upon existing algorithms for polynomial matings and introduces several novel techniques to improve efficiency and accuracy.
We provide a detailed description of the algorithm and its implementation, along with a thorough analysis of its performance.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the Medusa Algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of both speed and accuracy, making it a valuable tool for researchers in the field of complex dynamics.
This paper presents a virtual microscope for big data analytics, which aims to contextualize geometric data analysis and related data analytics.
The virtual microscope provides a platform for analyzing large datasets and extracting meaningful insights.
The paper discusses the challenges and opportunities in the field of geometric data analysis and proposes a framework for integrating various data analytics techniques.
The virtual microscope is designed to handle the complexity and scale of big data, enabling researchers to explore and analyze data in a more efficient and effective manner.
The paper also presents case studies and experimental results to demonstrate the effectiveness of the virtual microscope in real-world scenarios.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of data analytics by providing a comprehensive framework for contextualizing geometric data analysis and related techniques.
In this paper, we study the existence and properties of interior bubbling solutions for the critical Lin-Ni-Takagi problem in dimension 3.
The Lin-Ni-Takagi problem is a nonlinear elliptic equation involving the critical Sobolev exponent.
We consider the case where the equation is posed in a bounded domain with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
We prove the existence of interior bubbling solutions, which are solutions that concentrate their energy at a finite number of interior points.
We also investigate the behavior of these solutions near the concentration points and establish some qualitative properties.
Our results provide new insights into the behavior of critical nonlinear elliptic equations in dimension 3 and contribute to the understanding of interior bubbling phenomena.
This paper presents a radiative transfer model for contaminated rough slabs.
The model takes into account the effects of surface roughness and contamination on the radiative transfer process.
The model is based on the Monte Carlo method and incorporates the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) to accurately simulate the scattering of light by rough surfaces.
The effects of contamination on the surface are modeled using a modified version of the radiative transfer equation.
The model is validated against experimental data and shows good agreement.
The model can be used to study the radiative properties of contaminated rough slabs and can be applied to various fields such as remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and industrial processes.
This paper presents a novel algorithm for approximately sampling elements with fixed rank in graded posets.
Graded posets are partially ordered sets where each element is assigned a rank.
The problem of sampling elements with fixed rank in graded posets is challenging due to the large number of elements and the need for efficient sampling methods.
The proposed algorithm utilizes a combination of random sampling and importance sampling techniques to approximate the desired elements.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the algorithm compared to existing methods.
The algorithm has potential applications in various domains, such as social network analysis and recommendation systems.
Differential privacy is a widely used framework for privacy-preserving data analysis.
However, the semantics of differential privacy have been a subject of debate, with different interpretations leading to different algorithms and guarantees.
In this paper, we propose a Bayesian formulation of differential privacy that provides a unified framework for understanding and comparing different approaches.
We show that our formulation captures the intuitive notion of privacy and allows for a more nuanced analysis of privacy guarantees.
We also demonstrate the practical implications of our formulation through experiments on real-world datasets.
Our results highlight the importance of considering the semantics of differential privacy when designing and evaluating privacy-preserving algorithms.
This paper presents a novel approach for blind facial image quality enhancement using non-rigid semantic patches.
The proposed method leverages the semantic information of facial images to enhance their quality without requiring any prior knowledge about the specific image degradation.
The non-rigid semantic patches are generated by segmenting the facial image into different regions based on their semantic meaning.
These patches are then used to estimate the local image quality and guide the enhancement process.
Experimental results on a large dataset of facial images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the quality of blind facial images.
The proposed approach can be applied to various applications such as face recognition, facial expression analysis, and facial attribute detection.
This paper explores the use of information theoretic inequalities as bounds in superconformal field theory.
Superconformal field theory is a powerful framework for studying quantum field theories with extended symmetries.

The authors propose a new approach to deriving bounds in superconformal field theory using information theoretic inequalities, which provide a measure of the amount of information contained in a system.
They demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by deriving new bounds on the central charges of superconformal field theories.
The results of this study have important implications for understanding the fundamental properties of superconformal field theories and may lead to new insights in the field.
This paper presents a novel chaotic image encryption algorithm using a generalized threshold function.
The proposed algorithm utilizes a chaotic map to generate a sequence of random numbers, which are then used to encrypt the image.
The generalized threshold function is employed to enhance the security of the encryption process.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves high security and robustness against various attacks, while maintaining a reasonable encryption speed.
The algorithm also exhibits good resistance against statistical analysis and key space analysis.
Overall, the proposed algorithm provides an effective and efficient solution for image encryption.
The paper investigates the factorization of the Low Power Mode (LPM) effect in sequential bremsstrahlung.
The LPM effect refers to the suppression of radiation due to multiple scattering of the emitting particle.
The authors derive a factorization formula for the LPM effect in the case of sequential bremsstrahlung, where the emitting particle undergoes multiple scatterings before emitting radiation.
The factorization formula allows for a systematic treatment of the LPM effect and provides a framework for calculating the radiation spectrum in the presence of multiple scatterings.
The results of the paper have implications for understanding and predicting the radiation emitted by high-energy particles in various astrophysical and particle physics scenarios.
This paper presents a study of the magnetic properties of Co/Ti bilayer thin films using ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy.
The Co/Ti bilayer thin films were prepared using magnetron sputtering technique and their magnetic properties were characterized using FMR measurements.
The FMR spectra were analyzed to determine the magnetic anisotropy and damping parameters of the Co/Ti bilayer thin films.
The results showed that the magnetic anisotropy of the Co/Ti bilayer thin films can be controlled by varying the thickness of the Ti layer.
The damping parameter was found to be dependent on the Co layer thickness.
These findings provide valuable insights into the magnetic properties of Co/Ti bilayer thin films and can be useful for the development of magnetic devices and spintronic applications.
In this paper, we investigate the elastic properties of mono- and polydisperse two-dimensional crystals composed of hard-core repulsive Yukawa particles.
We use molecular dynamics simulations to study the effects of particle size and polydispersity on the elastic constants of these crystals.
We find that the elastic constants decrease with increasing particle size and polydispersity, indicating a decrease in the stiffness of the crystals.
Additionally, we observe that the elastic constants exhibit anisotropic behavior, with different values along different crystallographic directions.
Our results provide insights into the mechanical properties of two-dimensional crystals and have implications for the design and engineering of materials with desired elastic properties.
This paper presents a quantum phase-space representation for curved configuration spaces.
The authors propose a new mathematical framework that allows for the description of quantum systems in curved configuration spaces, which are spaces with non-trivial geometries.
The proposed representation is based on the Wigner function, a well-known tool in quantum mechanics, and is shown to be applicable to a wide range of physical systems.

The authors demonstrate the usefulness of their approach by applying it to the study of quantum systems in curved configuration spaces, such as curved manifolds and spaces with non-trivial topologies.

The results obtained using the proposed representation are compared to those obtained using other existing methods, and it is shown that the proposed approach provides a more accurate and comprehensive description of quantum systems in curved configuration spaces.
Overall, this paper presents a novel and valuable contribution to the field of quantum mechanics and provides a new tool for the study of quantum systems in curved configuration spaces.
This paper presents a novel approach to the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm by incorporating a time-variant optimum stepsize derived from a Bayesian network perspective.
The NLMS algorithm is widely used in adaptive filtering applications, but it often suffers from slow convergence and poor tracking performance.

By introducing a time-variant optimum stepsize, the proposed algorithm is able to adaptively adjust the stepsize based on the current state of the system, leading to improved convergence and tracking performance.
The Bayesian network perspective provides a theoretical framework for deriving the time-variant optimum stepsize and allows for a better understanding of the algorithm's behavior.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in various scenarios, highlighting its potential for practical applications in adaptive filtering.
This paper presents a four-dimensional understanding of quantum mechanics and its connection to Bell violation.
The authors propose a new framework that incorporates the concept of time as a fourth dimension in addition to the three spatial dimensions.
They argue that this four-dimensional perspective provides a more comprehensive understanding of quantum phenomena and allows for a deeper analysis of Bell violation.
The paper includes a detailed mathematical formulation of the four-dimensional framework and presents experimental results that support its validity.
The findings suggest that the four-dimensional understanding of quantum mechanics can provide new insights into the nature of quantum entanglement and its violation of Bell inequalities.
Super-resolution is a technique used to enhance the resolution of low-resolution images.
In recent years, low-rank matrix decomposition has emerged as a powerful tool for super-resolution.
This paper investigates how low-rank matrix decomposition can aid in both internal and external learnings for super-resolution.
Internal learning refers to the process of learning the low-rank structure of the image itself, while external learning involves leveraging external data to improve super-resolution performance.
The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of various low-rank matrix decomposition methods and their impact on internal and external learnings for super-resolution.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of low-rank matrix decomposition in improving super-resolution performance and highlight the importance of selecting appropriate decomposition methods for different scenarios.

The findings of this study contribute to the understanding of how low-rank matrix decomposition can be utilized to enhance super-resolution techniques and provide insights for future research in this field.
This paper presents a family of Nikishin systems with periodic recurrence coefficients.
Nikishin systems are a class of orthogonal polynomials that have applications in various areas of mathematics and physics.
The recurrence coefficients of these systems are typically assumed to be non-periodic.
However, in this paper, we introduce a family of Nikishin systems with periodic recurrence coefficients.
We derive the properties of these systems and study their behavior.
We also provide numerical examples to illustrate the effectiveness of these systems in solving certain problems.
Our findings suggest that these periodic Nikishin systems have potential applications in various fields, including approximation theory and numerical analysis.
This paper explores the dimensions of multi-fan algebras, which are a generalization of the classical fan algebras.
The authors provide a comprehensive analysis of the dimensions of these algebras, including their relationship with the dimensions of the underlying fans.
They also investigate the behavior of the dimensions under various operations on multi-fan algebras, such as taking direct sums and tensor products.
The results obtained in this study contribute to a deeper understanding of multi-fan algebras and their properties.
This paper investigates the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a non-autonomous Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy system with a mass source term that models tumor growth.
The authors establish the existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to the system using a combination of variational techniques and energy estimates.
They also prove the existence of a global attractor, which characterizes the long-time behavior of the system.
The results provide important insights into the mathematical modeling of tumor growth and contribute to the understanding of the dynamics of the Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy system.
In this paper, we study the relationship between defects in conformal field theories and the super-Poincar\'{e} line bundle.

We show that defects can be described by certain line bundles on the worldsheet, and that these line bundles are related to the super-Poincar\'{e} line bundle through a fermionic T-duality transformation.
We provide explicit examples of this relationship in the context of the N=2 superconformal algebra, and discuss the implications for defect operators in conformal field theories.
Our results shed light on the geometric interpretation of defects and provide a new perspective on the role of fermionic T-duality in conformal field theory.
This paper presents a subspace leakage analysis and an improved direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method for scenarios with small sample sizes.
The subspace leakage analysis investigates the effect of subspace leakage on DOA estimation accuracy, particularly in scenarios with limited data.
The improved DOA estimation method utilizes a modified covariance matrix to mitigate the impact of subspace leakage.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of DOA estimation accuracy, especially when the sample size is small.
This research contributes to the field of signal processing by providing insights into subspace leakage and offering a practical solution for accurate DOA estimation in scenarios with limited data.
This paper presents a comprehensive study on modelling galaxy spectra in the presence of interstellar dust.
The authors extend their previous work to include both nearby galaxies and those in the distant Universe.
They develop a new model that takes into account the effects of dust on the observed spectra of galaxies, and apply it to a large sample of galaxies at various distances.
The results show that the presence of dust significantly affects the observed spectra, and the new model provides a better fit to the data compared to previous models.
The study also explores the implications of these findings for understanding the properties and evolution of galaxies in different environments.
Overall, this work contributes to our understanding of the role of interstellar dust in shaping the observed spectra of galaxies, and provides a valuable tool for future studies in this field.
In this paper, we study the Baum-Connes property for a quantum (semi-)direct product.
We introduce the concept of a quantum (semi-)direct product and provide a detailed analysis of its properties.
We then investigate the Baum-Connes property for this type of product and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for it to hold.
Our results provide a deeper understanding of the Baum-Connes property and its applicability to quantum (semi-)direct products.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Anomalous Hall Effect in Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te Composite System" discusses the investigation of the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in a composite system composed of Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te.
The AHE is a phenomenon where a transverse voltage is generated in the presence of a magnetic field, and it has been extensively studied in various materials.
In this study, the authors synthesized the composite system using a combination of molecular beam epitaxy and ion implantation techniques.
They then characterized the material using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.

The AHE measurements were performed using a four-probe method in a temperature range of 5-300 K and magnetic fields up to 9 T. The results showed a clear AHE signal in the composite system, indicating the presence of a nontrivial Berry curvature.
The authors also observed a strong dependence of the AHE on the Mn concentration, suggesting a significant role of the Mn dopants in the AHE mechanism.
Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the AHE in Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te composite systems and opens up new possibilities for the design and development of spintronic devices.
This paper explores the concept of "encyclopaedia inflationaris," a phenomenon in which the number of encyclopedic entries increases exponentially over time.
The authors analyze the causes and consequences of encyclopaedia inflationaris, including the impact on information overload, the quality of information, and the accessibility of knowledge.
The study also examines potential solutions to mitigate encyclopaedia inflationaris, such as improved curation, user-generated content moderation, and artificial intelligence algorithms.

The findings highlight the need for a balanced approach to managing encyclopaedia inflationaris, ensuring that the quantity and quality of information are both maintained to facilitate effective knowledge dissemination.
This paper investigates the phenomenon of free particle to complex Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) breathers through isospectral deformation.
The KdV equation is a well-known nonlinear partial differential equation that describes the behavior of waves in various physical systems.
The authors propose a method to generate complex KdV breathers, which are localized, periodic solutions of the KdV equation, starting from the solution of the free particle Schrödinger equation.
The isospectral deformation technique is used to transform the free particle solution into a complex KdV breather solution.
The authors provide numerical simulations to demonstrate the effectiveness of their method and discuss the implications of their findings for the study of nonlinear wave phenomena.
This research contributes to the understanding of the relationship between different types of wave solutions and provides a new approach for generating complex KdV breathers.
This paper investigates the large scale behavior of velocity-jump processes and their connection to non-local Hamilton-Jacobi equations.
The authors derive a macroscopic limit for the velocity-jump processes and show that it is governed by a non-local Hamilton-Jacobi equation.
They also establish the convergence of the solutions of the non-local Hamilton-Jacobi equation to the solutions of the velocity-jump processes as the scale of the system becomes large.
The results provide insights into the behavior of velocity-jump processes and their connection to non-local Hamilton-Jacobi equations in large scale systems.
The Galactic bulge is a dense region at the center of the Milky Way galaxy, and understanding its stellar populations is crucial for understanding the formation and evolution of galaxies.
In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of the stellar populations in the Galactic bulge using data from the Hubble Space Telescope.
We analyze the color-magnitude diagrams of a large sample of stars in the bulge and derive their ages, metallicities, and spatial distributions.
Our results reveal a complex mix of stellar populations in the bulge, including both old and young stars, as well as a range of metallicities.
We find evidence for a significant population of metal-rich stars, which suggests a rapid formation process in the bulge.
Additionally, we observe a gradient in the spatial distribution of stars, with a higher concentration towards the center of the bulge.
These findings provide important insights into the formation and evolution of the Galactic bulge, and have implications for our understanding of galaxy formation in general.
This paper presents a quantitative test of general theories of the intrinsic laser linewidth.
The authors propose a novel experimental setup that allows for precise measurements of the linewidth of different laser sources.
They compare the measured linewidths with the predictions of various theoretical models and find that none of the existing theories accurately describe the observed linewidths.
The authors conclude that further research is needed to develop a more comprehensive theory of the intrinsic laser linewidth.
The paper "On the Convex Pfaff-Darboux Theorem of Ekeland and Nirenberg" explores the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem, which is a fundamental result in convex analysis.
The authors provide a detailed proof of this theorem and discuss its implications in various areas of mathematics, including differential geometry and optimization theory.
The paper also presents several examples and applications of the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem, highlighting its importance in understanding the behavior of convex functions and their level sets.
Overall, this paper contributes to the existing literature on convex analysis and provides a comprehensive understanding of the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem.
This paper explores the concept of pattern avoidance for set partitions using the framework introduced by Klazar.
Set partitions are combinatorial objects that partition a set into non-empty subsets, and pattern avoidance refers to the absence of certain substructures within these partitions.
Klazar's framework provides a systematic approach to studying pattern avoidance by defining a partial order on set partitions based on the containment of certain substructures.
The paper presents several results related to pattern avoidance for set partitions, including characterizations of avoidance classes and enumeration formulas.
Additionally, the paper discusses the connections between pattern avoidance for set partitions and other areas of combinatorics, such as permutation patterns and graph theory.
Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of pattern avoidance in the context of set partitions and provides a foundation for further research in this area.
This paper presents a closed-form solution to the multi-period portfolio choice problem for a quadratic utility function.

The problem involves determining the optimal allocation of wealth across multiple periods, taking into account the investor's risk aversion and the expected returns and volatilities of different assets.
The closed-form solution allows for a more efficient and accurate calculation of the optimal portfolio allocation, compared to existing numerical methods.
The paper also provides empirical evidence of the effectiveness of the closed-form solution through a series of simulations.
Overall, the closed-form solution presented in this paper offers a valuable tool for investors and financial professionals in making optimal portfolio allocation decisions.
This paper presents a novel approach for simulating fluid-structure interactions with thermal fluctuations using stochastic Eulerian Lagrangian methods.
The proposed method combines the advantages of both Eulerian and Lagrangian approaches to accurately model the behavior of fluid and solid particles.
The thermal fluctuations are incorporated into the simulation by introducing stochastic forces that act on the particles.
The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through numerical experiments on various fluid-structure interaction problems.
The results show that the proposed method can accurately capture the thermal fluctuations and their effects on the fluid-structure system.

This research contributes to the development of more realistic and accurate simulations of fluid-structure interactions with thermal fluctuations, which have important applications in various fields such as bioengineering and materials science.
This paper presents SCOR, a software-defined constrained optimal routing platform for SDN.
SCOR aims to address the challenges of routing in SDN environments, such as scalability, flexibility, and efficiency.
It introduces a novel routing algorithm that takes into account various constraints, such as link capacity, delay, and cost, to optimize the routing decisions.
SCOR also provides a modular architecture that allows for easy integration with existing SDN controllers and network devices.
The experimental evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness and efficiency of SCOR in terms of routing performance and resource utilization.
Overall, SCOR offers a promising solution for achieving optimal routing in SDN environments.
In this paper, we investigate the stability of topological properties in a bismuth (111) bilayer.
Using first-principles calculations, we analyze the electronic band structure and topological invariants of the bilayer under various strain conditions.
We find that the bilayer exhibits a nontrivial topological phase with a large band gap, indicating the presence of topologically protected surface states.
Furthermore, we demonstrate that the topological properties of the bilayer are robust against strain, suggesting its potential for applications in topological quantum devices.

Our findings provide valuable insights into the stability of topological properties in bismuth-based materials and contribute to the development of topological materials for future technological advancements.
This paper presents GNU epsilon, an extensible programming language designed to provide flexibility and adaptability for various programming tasks.
The language incorporates a modular architecture that allows users to easily extend its functionality through the addition of new features and libraries.
The paper discusses the design principles and key features of GNU epsilon, including its syntax, type system, and support for metaprogramming.
Additionally, the paper provides examples of how GNU epsilon can be used to solve real-world programming problems and compares it to other extensible programming languages.
Overall, GNU epsilon offers a powerful and customizable programming environment that can be tailored to meet the specific needs of individual developers and projects.
This paper investigates the well-posedness of a diffuse-interface model for two-phase incompressible flows with a thermo-induced Marangoni effect.
The model is derived from the Navier-Stokes equations and incorporates a phase-field variable to capture the interface between the two phases.
The authors establish the existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to the model using a combination of energy estimates and compactness arguments.
They also prove the continuous dependence of the solutions on the initial and boundary data.

The results provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for studying the dynamics of two-phase flows with thermo-induced Marangoni effect and can be used to guide the development of numerical methods for simulating such flows.
This paper presents a novel approach to belief propagation, a popular algorithm for inference in graphical models.

The proposed method, called Sigma Point Belief Propagation, extends the traditional belief propagation algorithm by incorporating sigma points, which are a set of carefully chosen points that approximate the distribution of a random variable.
By using sigma points, the algorithm is able to capture the non-linearities and correlations in the graphical model more accurately, leading to improved inference results.

The paper provides a detailed description of the Sigma Point Belief Propagation algorithm and presents experimental results on various benchmark datasets to demonstrate its effectiveness compared to traditional belief propagation and other state-of-the-art inference algorithms.

The results show that Sigma Point Belief Propagation achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence in a wide range of graphical models, making it a promising approach for inference in real-world applications.
This paper investigates the Fourier-Mukai transform and autoduality for compactified Jacobians.
The authors introduce a new construction of the compactified Jacobian as a moduli space of stable sheaves on a smooth projective curve.
They then study the Fourier-Mukai transform on this moduli space and establish its properties.
In particular, they prove an autoduality result for the compactified Jacobian, showing that it is isomorphic to its dual under the Fourier-Mukai transform.
This result has applications in algebraic geometry and mathematical physics.
This paper presents a survey on security issues in file management in cloud computing environments.
Cloud computing has become increasingly popular for storing and managing files due to its scalability and cost-effectiveness.
However, it also introduces various security challenges that need to be addressed.
The survey examines different security issues such as data privacy, data integrity, and access control in cloud file management.
It also discusses various security mechanisms and techniques that can be employed to mitigate these issues.
The findings of the survey highlight the importance of implementing robust security measures in cloud file management systems to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data.
The paper concludes with recommendations for future research in this area.
Collective chemotaxis, the directed movement of a group of cells in response to a chemical gradient, is a fundamental process in many biological systems.
It is commonly assumed that individual cells sense and respond to the gradient, leading to coordinated movement.
However, recent studies have suggested that collective chemotaxis can emerge even in the absence of single-cell gradient sensing.
In this paper, we present a theoretical model and experimental evidence to support this idea.
Our model incorporates cell-cell communication and mechanical interactions between cells, allowing for the emergence of collective chemotaxis.
We demonstrate that this emergent behavior can arise from simple rules governing cell movement and communication, without the need for individual cells to sense the gradient.
Our findings challenge the prevailing view of collective chemotaxis and provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying coordinated cell movement.
The paper "Graphs, Matrices, and the GraphBLAS: Seven Good Reasons" explores the GraphBLAS framework and its benefits for graph analytics.
The GraphBLAS is a standardized API for graph algorithms that leverages the power of linear algebra and matrix operations.
The paper presents seven compelling reasons why the GraphBLAS is a valuable tool for graph analytics.

These reasons include the ability to express graph algorithms as matrix operations, the potential for parallel and distributed computing, the ability to leverage existing linear algebra libraries, the support for graph algorithms on GPUs, the potential for performance optimizations, the ability to combine graph algorithms with other linear algebra operations, and the potential for interoperability and code reuse.
The paper concludes by highlighting the importance of the GraphBLAS in advancing graph analytics and encouraging further research and development in this area.
This paper presents a study on gridless sparse methods for line spectral estimation from complete and incomplete data.
Line spectral estimation is an important problem in signal processing and has applications in various fields such as wireless communication and radar.
The authors propose a gridless approach that does not rely on a predefined grid for estimating the frequencies of the spectral lines.
They compare the performance of their method with existing grid-based methods using both complete and incomplete data.
The results show that the gridless sparse methods outperform the grid-based methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially when dealing with incomplete data.
The findings of this study have implications for improving line spectral estimation techniques in practical applications.
This paper presents a mathematical model and control strategy for an active constrained layer (ACL) beam actuated by two voltage sources, with and without magnetic effects.
The ACL beam is composed of a piezoelectric layer and a constraining layer, and is subjected to an external magnetic field.
The mathematical model is derived using the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and the constitutive equations for the piezoelectric and magnetic materials.
The control strategy is based on a combination of feedback and feedforward control techniques.
Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and control strategy in achieving accurate and robust control of the ACL beam.
The findings of this study have potential applications in the design and control of ACL beams for various engineering applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for dimension reduction in semidefinite programs using Jordan algebras.
Semidefinite programs are a class of optimization problems that involve optimizing a linear objective function subject to linear matrix inequality constraints.
The proposed method leverages the properties of Jordan algebras to reduce the dimensionality of the problem, thereby improving computational efficiency.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through numerical experiments on various benchmark problems.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing dimension reduction techniques in terms of both solution quality and computational time.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of semidefinite programming and offers a promising avenue for future research in dimension reduction techniques.
This paper presents a correction to the well-posedness results of semilinear stochastic wave equations with H\"{o}lder continuous coefficients.
The original paper contained an error in the proof of the main theorem, which has been identified and corrected in this paper.
The corrected proof establishes the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the semilinear stochastic wave equations under certain conditions on the coefficients.
The corrected results provide a solid foundation for further research and applications of semilinear stochastic wave equations.
