The paper demonstrates that d-complete posets retain the key characteristics of Young diagrams, thereby providing a broader framework for understanding the Jeu de Taquin property.
The findings of this study contribute to the existing body of knowledge on combinatorial theory and offer new perspectives for future research.
This academic paper presents a novel approach to gaze estimation, a critical aspect of human-computer interaction.
Traditionally, gaze estimation has been focused on the eye region, but this paper proposes a full-face appearance-based method.
The study demonstrates that the entire face contributes to gaze direction and that utilizing full-face information significantly improves gaze estimation accuracy.
The paper also introduces a new large-scale dataset for gaze estimation, collected under diverse conditions.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing eye-based methods, particularly in real-world, unconstrained environments.
This research has significant implications for the development of more natural and efficient human-computer interaction systems.
This paper investigates the phase diagram of the zero-bandwidth extended Hubbard model with intersite magnetic interactions under the condition of strong on-site repulsion limit.
The study employs a combination of analytical and numerical methods to explore the model's phase structure.
The results reveal a rich phase diagram, including charge ordered, spin ordered, and coexisting phases.
The paper also discusses the implications of these findings for understanding the behavior of strongly correlated electron systems.

The results provide valuable insights into the interplay between charge and spin degrees of freedom in these systems, and may have implications for the design of novel materials with tailored electronic properties.
This paper investigates the problem of prescribing scalar curvature on compact surfaces through the use of large conformal metrics.
We delve into the existence and non-existence of such metrics, providing a comprehensive analysis of the conditions under which they can be found.

The study employs various mathematical techniques, including geometric analysis and partial differential equations, to explore the interplay between the geometry and topology of the surface and the prescribed scalar curvature.

The results contribute to our understanding of the geometric structure of surfaces and have potential applications in theoretical physics, particularly in the study of spacetime geometry in general relativity.
This paper presents a comprehensive study of the pinning model with heavy-tailed disorder.
The pinning model is a fundamental concept in statistical physics, used to describe the interaction between a polymer and a defect line.
The study focuses on the impact of heavy-tailed disorder, a scenario where extreme events are more likely than in standard models.
The paper explores the critical behavior of the model, highlighting the significant influence of heavy-tailed disorder on the phase transition and critical exponents.
The results provide new insights into the understanding of disordered systems and have potential applications in various fields, including material science and polymer physics.
This paper investigates the sliding friction in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime for a power-law fluid.
The study employs a theoretical approach to understand the behavior of non-Newtonian fluids under varying conditions of pressure and velocity.
The results reveal that the friction factor is significantly influenced by the power-law index and the operating conditions.
The findings provide valuable insights into the design and optimization of mechanical systems involving power-law fluids, such as polymer processing equipment and biomedical devices.
The study also highlights the need for further research to explore the complex rheological properties of non-Newtonian fluids in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime.
This paper investigates the structural limitations of learning in a crowd, specifically focusing on communication vulnerability and information diffusion in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs).
Using network analysis, the study explores how the structure of social interactions in MOOCs can limit the potential for information diffusion and collaborative learning.
The findings reveal that the communication network in MOOCs is highly vulnerable due to its sparse and hub-dominated structure, which can hinder effective information exchange and learning.
The paper concludes by suggesting strategies to improve communication and learning in MOOCs, such as promoting more balanced and dense network structures.
This paper explores the Khinchin-Kahane and Levy inequalities within the context of abelian metric groups, and the transfer from normed (abelian semi)groups to Banach spaces.
The study delves into the mathematical intricacies of these inequalities, providing a comprehensive analysis of their properties and applications.
The paper also investigates the transfer process from normed groups to Banach spaces, offering new insights into this complex mathematical transition.
The findings contribute to the broader understanding of these inequalities and their role in the field of functional analysis.
The paper also provides a foundation for further research into the applications of these inequalities in other mathematical domains.
This paper explores the concept of multiactive objects, a novel approach in the field of object-oriented programming.
Multiactive objects are entities that can perform multiple activities simultaneously, thereby enhancing the efficiency and performance of software applications.
The paper delves into the theoretical underpinnings of multiactive objects, their design, and implementation.
It also discusses various applications of multiactive objects in diverse fields such as artificial intelligence, data processing, and software engineering.
The paper concludes with an analysis of the potential benefits and challenges associated with the use of multiactive objects, providing a comprehensive understanding of this emerging paradigm.
This paper presents a detailed study on the conformal parameterizations of slices of flat Kasner spacetimes.
The research focuses on the mathematical and physical properties of these parameterizations, providing a comprehensive analysis of their geometric structure and dynamics.
The paper also explores the implications of these findings for the understanding of cosmological models and the nature of singularities in general relativity.
The results reveal a rich structure of the parameter space, with a variety of different types of slices corresponding to different regions.
This study contributes to the ongoing research in theoretical physics and cosmology, offering new insights into the complex nature of spacetime singularities.
This paper investigates the formation of a bubble from a submerged orifice, a phenomenon that plays a crucial role in various scientific and industrial applications.
The study employs a combination of experimental observations and theoretical analysis to understand the underlying physics of bubble formation.
The paper presents a detailed description of the bubble formation process, including the initial growth phase, detachment, and subsequent rise in the fluid.
The results reveal the influence of various parameters such as orifice diameter, fluid properties, and pressure conditions on the bubble formation process.

The findings provide valuable insights that can enhance the efficiency of processes involving bubble formation, such as gas-liquid reactors, underwater breathing apparatus, and effervescence in carbonated beverages.
This paper presents a comprehensive derivation of the Association Log-Likelihood Distance (ALLD) for multi-object tracking.
The ALLD is a crucial metric used in data association, which is a fundamental step in multi-object tracking.
The paper begins with a detailed introduction to multi-object tracking and the role of data association.
It then delves into the mathematical derivation of the ALLD, explaining each step in detail.
The paper also discusses the properties of the ALLD and its advantages over other data association metrics.
Finally, it presents several simulations to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrates the effectiveness of the ALLD in improving the accuracy of multi-object tracking.
This paper explores the intricate connections between Subriemannian Geometry and Algebraic Geometry, two distinct but interrelated branches of mathematics.
The study delves into the foundational principles of these geometries, highlighting their unique characteristics and the mathematical structures they encompass.
The primary focus is on the 'bridges' that link these two fields, particularly the transfer of concepts, techniques, and results.
The paper also discusses the potential implications of these connections, suggesting new avenues for research and applications in various scientific domains.
The findings underscore the importance of interdisciplinary approaches in advancing mathematical understanding and innovation.
This paper explores the potential contributions of noncontact atomic force microscopy (nc-AFM) in future Casimir force measurements.
The Casimir force, a quantum mechanical phenomenon, is challenging to measure due to its minute nature and the influence of various environmental factors.
The paper discusses the principles of nc-AFM and its advantages over traditional methods in measuring the Casimir force.
It also highlights the potential improvements in accuracy, sensitivity, and resolution that nc-AFM can bring to Casimir force measurements.
The paper further discusses the challenges and potential solutions in implementing nc-AFM for Casimir force measurements.
The findings suggest that nc-AFM holds significant promise for advancing our understanding of the Casimir force and its implications in various scientific fields.
This paper presents an in-depth study on the observation of empty liquids and equilibrium gels in a colloidal clay.
The research utilizes advanced microscopy techniques to examine the structural and dynamic properties of these unique states of matter.
The findings reveal that empty liquids and equilibrium gels exhibit distinct characteristics and behaviors, which are influenced by factors such as particle concentration and temperature.
The study also provides insights into the potential applications of these materials in various fields, including materials science and nanotechnology.
The results contribute to the broader understanding of colloidal systems and their complex phase behavior.
This paper presents a novel distributed tracking algorithm for the reconstruction of graph signals.
The algorithm is designed to handle the challenges of tracking and reconstructing graph signals in a distributed network, where nodes have limited communication and computational capabilities.
The proposed method leverages the sparsity of graph signals in the graph Fourier domain to achieve efficient and accurate reconstruction.
The algorithm's performance is evaluated through extensive simulations, demonstrating its superiority over existing methods in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency.

The results suggest that the proposed algorithm can be effectively applied in various fields, including sensor networks, social networks, and power grids, where distributed signal processing is required.
This paper explores the parameter space of the spin-orbit problem, focusing on normally hyperbolic invariant circles (NHICs).
The spin-orbit problem is a fundamental issue in celestial mechanics, describing the motion of a small body under the gravitational influence of two larger bodies.
The study investigates the existence and stability of NHICs in the spin-orbit problem, which are crucial for understanding the dynamics of the system.
The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the parameter space, identifying regions where NHICs exist and their stability properties.
The results contribute to the understanding of the complex dynamics of the spin-orbit problem and have potential applications in space mission design and celestial mechanics.
This paper investigates the role of natural convection in the dissolution of sessile droplets.
The study employs a combination of experimental and numerical methods to examine the dissolution process of sessile droplets in a quiescent environment.
The results reveal that natural convection significantly influences the dissolution rate and pattern of sessile droplets.
The findings also suggest that the shape of the droplet and the properties of the surrounding fluid play a crucial role in the dissolution process.

This research provides valuable insights into the fundamental understanding of droplet dissolution, which has implications for various applications in fields such as material science, environmental science, and pharmaceuticals.
This paper presents a proposal for a three-detector short-baseline neutrino oscillation program in the Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam.
The program aims to definitively address the anomalous results from the LSND and MiniBooNE experiments that suggest the existence of sterile neutrinos.
The proposed experimental design includes the use of three LAr-TPC detectors positioned along the Booster Neutrino Beam at Fermilab.
The paper discusses the potential of this setup to provide a comprehensive test of the short-baseline neutrino oscillation phenomenon, and to measure neutrino-argon cross-sections.
The proposed program could significantly advance our understanding of neutrino physics and potentially uncover new physics beyond the Standard Model.
This paper investigates the phenomenon of a π phase shift induced by interface anisotropy in the precession of magnetization initiated by laser heating.
The study employs a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental observations to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.
The results reveal that the interface anisotropy plays a significant role in the precession of magnetization, leading to a π phase shift.
This finding has potential implications for the development of spintronic devices and the understanding of ultrafast magnetization dynamics.

The paper also discusses the potential for manipulating the phase of magnetization precession through the control of interface anisotropy, opening up new avenues for research in the field of magnetism and spintronics.
This paper presents a comprehensive study on the oracle complexity of nonsmooth convex optimization problems.
By leveraging information theory, we establish lower bounds on the oracle complexity for these problems.
Our analysis is based on the concept of entropy and involves a novel application of Fano's inequality.
The results provide a deeper understanding of the inherent difficulty of nonsmooth convex optimization and offer a theoretical benchmark for the performance of optimization algorithms.
The findings also highlight the importance of incorporating information-theoretic tools in the study of computational complexity in optimization.
This paper presents a novel approach to combining hypersequents and nested sequents, two powerful formalisms in structural proof theory.
The study introduces a method of grafting hypersequents onto nested sequents, thereby creating a new system that inherits the strengths of both.
This system is shown to be sound and complete, and it is demonstrated how it can be used to provide cut-free sequent calculi for a variety of non-classical logics.
The paper also explores the potential benefits of this new system, such as increased expressivity and flexibility in proof construction.
The results suggest that the grafting of hypersequents onto nested sequents offers a promising direction for future research in proof theory.
This paper investigates the interaction of $F(R,T)$ gravity with modified Chaplygin gas in the context of cosmology.

The $F(R,T)$ gravity model, where R represents the Ricci scalar and T the trace of the energy-momentum tensor, is considered as an alternative to dark energy for explaining the accelerated expansion of the universe.
The modified Chaplygin gas is a model that unifies dark matter and dark energy.
We derive the field equations and study their solutions, focusing on the evolution of the scale factor and the deceleration parameter.
We also analyze the stability of the solutions and the behavior of the equation of state parameter.
Our results show that the interaction between $F(R,T)$ gravity and modified Chaplygin gas can lead to a viable cosmological model that is consistent with observational data.
This paper presents a detailed study on the absolute calibration of a fiber-coupled single-photon detector.
The research focuses on the development and implementation of a method for accurately calibrating these detectors, which are crucial in quantum information science and technology.
The calibration method is based on the use of a low-noise, high-stability laser source, and a high-precision power meter.
The paper discusses the experimental setup, the calibration procedure, and the uncertainty analysis.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a reliable and accurate calibration of the detector's quantum efficiency, with an uncertainty of less than 1%.
This work contributes to the advancement of quantum technologies by improving the accuracy and reliability of single-photon detection.
This paper presents a comprehensive model to understand the impact of Multiple Myeloma (MM) on kidney function.
MM, a plasma cell cancer, often leads to kidney damage, a major cause of morbidity and mortality among patients.
The study employs a combination of clinical data, mathematical modeling, and computational simulations to predict the progression of kidney damage in MM patients.
The model also explores the potential effects of various treatment strategies on preserving kidney function.
The results indicate a significant correlation between MM progression and kidney impairment, highlighting the need for early detection and intervention.
This model could serve as a valuable tool for clinicians in managing MM patients and potentially improving their prognosis.
This paper investigates the best and worst case permutations for random online domination of the path.
The study focuses on the online version of the domination game, where the player's objective is to minimize the number of dominators.
The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the game on paths, identifying the best and worst case permutations and providing a detailed explanation of the strategies leading to these outcomes.

The results reveal that the worst case scenario occurs when the vertices are presented in increasing order of their distances from the endpoints, while the best case scenario occurs when they are presented in decreasing order.
The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the game's complexity and offer valuable insights for developing more efficient strategies.
This paper investigates the shock formation of long wavelength femtosecond pulses in dispersive media, a phenomenon that has significant implications for the field of optics and photonics.
The study employs a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to explore the dynamics of carrier field shock formation.
The results reveal that the shock formation is highly dependent on the initial pulse parameters and the dispersion properties of the medium.
The findings also suggest that the shock formation can be manipulated and controlled, opening up new possibilities for the design of ultrafast optical devices.

This research contributes to our understanding of nonlinear wave propagation in dispersive media and has potential applications in areas such as optical communications, laser technology, and biomedical imaging.
This paper investigates a family of random noble means substitutions, a concept derived from number theory and probability theory.
The study explores the properties and behavior of these substitutions, including their ergodicity, invariant measures, and spectral characteristics.
The paper also delves into the implications of these properties in the context of symbolic dynamics and theoretical computer science.

The results provide a deeper understanding of the complex nature of random noble means substitutions, offering new insights that could potentially influence future research in mathematics and computer science.
This paper investigates the phenomenon of quantum percolation in finite regular graphs.
We explore the interplay between quantum mechanics and graph theory, focusing on the behavior of quantum particles in a disordered medium modeled by finite regular graphs.
We introduce a quantum percolation model and study its properties, including the critical threshold and the nature of the quantum phase transition.
Our findings reveal that quantum percolation exhibits unique characteristics compared to classical percolation, with implications for understanding quantum transport in disordered systems.
This study provides a foundation for further research into quantum percolation and its potential applications in quantum computing and condensed matter physics.
This paper explores the dielectric genome of van der Waals heterostructures, a critical aspect of two-dimensional (2D) materials with significant implications for the field of nanotechnology.
The study delves into the dielectric properties of these heterostructures, including their permittivity, breakdown field, and dielectric loss, among others.
The paper also discusses the impact of these properties on the performance of devices based on van der Waals heterostructures.
The results of this study provide a comprehensive understanding of the dielectric genome, paving the way for the design of more efficient and reliable nanoscale devices.
This paper presents a generalization of Szemerédi's theorem to the prime numbers in a multidimensional setting.
Szemerédi's theorem, a cornerstone in combinatorics and number theory, asserts that any subset of the integers having positive density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
We extend this theorem to the primes, a set of zero density in the integers, by employing methods from additive combinatorics, Fourier analysis, and sieve theory.
Our results provide new insights into the distribution of prime numbers and open up new avenues for research in number theory and combinatorics.
This paper explores the concept of reductions of points on algebraic groups, a fundamental aspect of algebraic geometry.
The study delves into the theoretical underpinnings of this concept, providing a comprehensive analysis of its properties and applications.
The paper also presents new methodologies for calculating reductions, offering a fresh perspective on this complex mathematical operation.
The results of this research not only contribute to the existing body of knowledge on algebraic groups but also open up new avenues for further exploration in the field.
The paper concludes with a discussion on the potential implications of these findings for related areas of mathematics.
This paper delves into the intricate concepts of expansivity and shadowing within the realm of linear dynamics.
It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of these phenomena and their implications in the study of dynamical systems.
The paper first elucidates the theoretical underpinnings of expansivity and shadowing, followed by an exploration of their interplay in linear dynamics.
It further investigates the conditions under which a linear dynamical system exhibits expansivity and the existence of shadowing.
The paper also presents various examples and counterexamples to illustrate these concepts.
The findings contribute to the broader understanding of the behavior of linear dynamical systems and open up new avenues for future research.
This paper presents a comprehensive study on the optimisation of measuring relativistic distortions in large-scale structure.
The research focuses on the development and application of advanced techniques to improve the accuracy and precision of these measurements.
The study also explores the potential implications of these distortions on our understanding of the universe's structure and evolution.
The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the measurement of relativistic distortions, providing a more accurate picture of the large-scale structure of the universe.
This research contributes to the ongoing efforts in cosmology to understand the fundamental properties and behaviours of the universe.
This paper investigates the categorical-algebraic conditions in S-protomodular categories.
It delves into the structural properties of these categories, focusing on the interplay between algebraic and categorical aspects.

The study provides a comprehensive analysis of the conditions under which a category is S-protomodular, and explores the implications of these conditions for the structure and behavior of the category.
The paper also presents new results on the relationship between S-protomodularity and other categorical properties, contributing to the broader understanding of category theory.
The findings of this research have potential applications in various fields of mathematics, including algebra, topology, and theoretical computer science.
This paper explores the geometrization of Maxwell's equations and the subsequent emergence of gravity.
It delves into the mathematical transformation of Maxwell's equations, which describe electromagnetic fields, into a geometric form.
This transformation reveals a deep connection between electromagnetism and gravity, suggesting that gravity itself may be an emergent phenomenon.
The paper further investigates the implications of this connection, including potential insights into quantum gravity and the unification of fundamental forces.
The study provides a novel perspective on the nature of gravity and its relationship with other fundamental forces, potentially paving the way for new developments in theoretical physics.
This paper introduces the Medusa Algorithm, a novel computational method for polynomial matings.
Polynomial mating is a complex process in the field of complex dynamics, which involves the merging of two polynomials to create a new dynamical system.
The Medusa Algorithm simplifies this process by providing a systematic approach to polynomial matings, reducing the computational complexity and increasing the efficiency of the process.
The paper provides a detailed description of the algorithm, its mathematical foundation, and its implementation.
It also presents several examples demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and potential applications in various fields of mathematics and computer science.
This paper presents an in-depth exploration of Geometric Data Analysis (GDA) and related data analytics within the context of big data.
It introduces a novel concept of a 'Virtual Microscope' for big data analytics, a tool designed to handle, analyze, and interpret large and complex datasets.
The paper discusses the theoretical underpinnings of GDA, its applications, and its relevance in the era of big data.
It also elaborates on the functionality and potential of the proposed Virtual Microscope, demonstrating its efficacy in managing big data challenges.
The paper concludes with insights into the future of GDA and big data analytics, emphasizing the role of innovative tools like the Virtual Microscope in transforming data analysis processes.
This paper investigates the critical Lin-Ni-Takagi problem in three dimensions, focusing on the existence and behavior of interior bubbling solutions.
The Lin-Ni-Takagi problem is a mathematical model used in the study of chemotaxis, a biological phenomenon describing the movement of cells or organisms in response to chemical stimuli.
The paper presents a detailed analysis of the problem, employing advanced mathematical techniques to explore the properties of solutions.
The main result is the demonstration of the existence of interior bubbling solutions under certain conditions.
This finding contributes to the understanding of the Lin-Ni-Takagi problem and has potential implications for the study of chemotaxis.
This paper presents a comprehensive study on the radiative transfer model for contaminated rough slabs.
The research focuses on understanding the interaction of radiation with rough slab surfaces contaminated with various materials.
The model developed incorporates the effects of surface roughness and contamination, which are often overlooked in traditional models.

The paper discusses the mathematical formulation of the model, its validation through comparison with experimental data, and its potential applications in fields such as remote sensing, climate modeling, and material science.
The results demonstrate that the model provides a more accurate representation of radiative transfer in real-world scenarios, thereby improving the reliability of predictions and simulations.
This paper presents a novel approach to approximately sampling elements with fixed rank in graded partially ordered sets (posets).
The study introduces a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that generates a uniform random sample of elements of a given rank in a graded poset.
The algorithm's performance is evaluated through rigorous theoretical analysis and empirical experiments, demonstrating its efficiency and accuracy.
The paper also explores the implications of this method in various fields, including computer science, mathematics, and operations research.
This research contributes to the understanding of graded posets and provides a practical tool for sampling problems in these structures.
This paper presents a novel interpretation of differential privacy, a widely adopted privacy standard, from a Bayesian perspective.
We propose a Bayesian formulation of differential privacy that provides a semantic interpretation of the privacy guarantee.
This interpretation is based on the posterior predictive distribution, which quantifies the uncertainty about an individual's private information given the differentially private output.
We demonstrate that our Bayesian differential privacy satisfies the same worst-case privacy guarantee as the classical differential privacy.
Furthermore, we show that it provides a more informative privacy measure in the average case, which can be used to design more efficient privacy-preserving algorithms.
Our results bridge the gap between the worst-case privacy guarantee and the average-case privacy risk, and provide a new perspective on understanding and applying differential privacy.
This paper presents a novel approach to blind facial image quality enhancement using non-rigid semantic patches.
The study focuses on improving the quality of facial images that are degraded due to various factors such as low resolution, noise, and poor lighting conditions.
The proposed method involves the use of non-rigid semantic patches, which are flexible and adaptable to different facial structures and expressions.
The method is blind, meaning it does not require any prior knowledge about the degradation process.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both subjective and objective evaluations.
The paper also discusses potential applications of this method in fields such as facial recognition, image editing, and social media.
This paper explores the application of information theoretic inequalities as bounds in superconformal field theory.
We delve into the mathematical intricacies of superconformal field theory and how information theoretic inequalities can be used to establish bounds in this complex field.
The study provides a comprehensive analysis of the role of entropy inequalities in quantum field theory and their implications in the context of superconformal symmetry.
The results demonstrate the potential of these inequalities to provide new insights into the structure and behavior of superconformal field theories.
This research opens up new avenues for further exploration in the realm of quantum information theory and its intersection with high energy physics.

This paper explores the concept of pattern avoidance in set partitions, following the methodology of Klazar.

This paper analyzes the global behavior of gradient systems in one unbounded spatial dimension.
Specifically, it focuses on the behavior of bistable solutions, which are solutions that exist in two stable states.
The paper studies the conditions under which these solutions are stable and the mechanisms by which they transition between the two states.
The paper also explores the effects of various parameters on the stability of the solutions and the conditions under which they undergo a bifurcation.
The results of this paper have applications in many fields, including physics, engineering, and economics.
Abstract.
A quantitative theoretical analysis of the inertial acceleration of individual particles in strained turbulent flow is performed.
Particle acceleration is driven by velocity differences across individual turbulent eddies and is modulated by straining of the flow.
Using a correlation-based stochastic model for the flow velocity field, probability density functions (PDFs) for particle acceleration are derived.
The PDFs are found to be asymmetric and exhibit a dynamic range of several orders of magnitude, features that are characteristic of chaotic processes.
The shape of the PDF as well as the dynamic range depend on the Reynolds number and the rate of strain.
Direct numerical simulations of particle trajectories confirm the predicted acceleration statistics and demonstrate the importance of flow straining for particle dynamics.
In this paper, we investigate the nonsoluble length of finite groups with commutators of small order.
We show that if the commutator order of a finite group G is strictly less than the solvable length of G, then the nonsoluble length of G is at most 3.
This result is best possible in a sense.

We also show that if the commutator order of a finite group G is equal to the solvable length of G, then the nonsoluble length of G can be 2, 3, or infinite, depending on the prime factorization of the order of G.
These results shed some light on the relationship between the commutator order and the nonsoluble length of finite groups.
The model of a superconductor with pair hopping and magnetic interactions at half-filling is a system of great interest due to its promising applications in quantum computing.
In this paper, we study some properties of this model.
We find that the ground state of the system is unique and corresponds to a superconducting state.
We also examine the stability of the superconducting state and find that it is stable under certain conditions.
In addition, we explore the effects of pair hopping and magnetic interactions on the superconducting state.
Our results suggest that these effects can enhance the superconducting state.
This research provides new insights into the properties of a superconductor with pair hopping and magnetic interactions at half-filling.
By understanding these properties, we can advance our knowledge of superconductivity and explore new ways to improve it.
This knowledge may also contribute to the development of quantum computers that use superconducting circuits.
These findings are of significance in the field of quantum physics and materials science.
The results can be useful for understanding and improving superconductivity and for developing quantum technologies based on superconducting circuits.

This paper provides a theoretical framework for studying the model of a superconductor with pair hopping and magnetic interactions at half-filling, which can be applied to other systems with similar properties.

An algebraic variety $V$ over the complex numbers is said to be $q$-log-convex if every $q$-irrational point on $V$ is log-convex, that is, the intersection of $V$ with any $q$-disc centered at the point is an intersection of $q$-discs.
In this paper, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for a complex variety to be $q$-log-convex in terms of linear transformations and polynomials with only real zeros.
This extends a previous result on log-convexity.
The Gauss-Bonnet invariant, which quantifies the geometric properties of a manifold, can be coupled to vector fields through the divergence of the vector field.
This coupling provides a relationship between the curvature of the manifold and the behavior of the vector field.
In this paper, we explore this coupling and its implications for the behavior of vector fields on manifolds.
We show that the coupling of the Gauss-Bonnet invariant to vector fields can be used to characterize the geometric properties of the manifold and the behavior of the vector field.
Furthermore, we demonstrate that the coupling of the Gauss-Bonnet invariant to vector fields can be used to develop new methods for analyzing the behavior of vector fields on manifolds.
These methods can be used to study the behavior of vector fields on a variety of manifolds, including those with high curvature and complex geometry.

This paper provides a valuable contribution to the understanding of the relationship between the Gauss-Bonnet invariant and vector fields, and offers new ways to analyze the behavior of vector fields on manifolds.
Abstract: Interior sensing is an important task in the automotive industry, as it enables various applications such as driver monitoring, seat-belt detection, and airbag deployment.
In this paper, we focus on background-foreground segmentation, a fundamental problem in interior sensing, for effective understanding of the vehicle's interior.
We propose a novel deep learning architecture, called Interior Segmentation Network (ISNet), to perform background-foreground segmentation for complex real-world indoor scenes.

ISNet leverages a novel Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module to capture multi-scale context and a fusion module to effectively combine multi-scale features for accurate and robust segmentation.
Furthermore, we propose a novel online training scheme to address the challenge of limited training data.
Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the publicInteriorNet dataset and demonstrates the efficiency of our method on a recent smart-device based platform.
We present a semi-supervised learning framework for medical image segmentation, tailored for training on limited amounts of labelled data from a single domain.

Our method leverages the power of meta-learning (also known as ‘learning to learn’) whilst accounting for the scarcity of labelled data in medical imaging, by using a semi-supervised meta-learning approach.
We propose to use a variational autoencoder in the latent space of which the generative component is a cycle Consistent Adversarial Network (Cycle-CAN).
We introduce a novel unsupervised domain generalisation (UDG) objective which promotes disentanglement of the Cycle-CAN’s latent space.
This disentanglement helps the network to learn a domain-invariant representation and improves generalisation performance on unseen domains.
We demonstrate the efficacy on three different public cardiac MRI segmentation benchmarks, two of which were unseen during training, and achieve state-of-the-art performance.
Recent progress in MRI acquisition has led to an explosion of big data, with the consequence that exhaustive segmentation of every image becomes unfeasible.
Furthermore, the lack of large annotated datasets with ground truth segmentation masks constitutes an additional bottleneck.
In this work, we present an unsupervised learning approach for patch-based segmentation of MRI brain images.
Our method is based on the concept of privileged information, which entails that patches from the same anatomical region should share a common intrinsic structure.
This common structure is learned in an unsupervised fashion by a non-parametric tensor-based quantization of the patch descriptor space, from which the segmentation is derived.
We show that the proposed method is capable of accurately segmenting different brain structures, such as gray/white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, in a fully unsupervised manner.

Recent progress in clinical imaging, such as whole slide imaging and whole-body imaging, has resulted in a sharp increase in the size of pathological images, leading to large computational costs in training deep learning models.
To address this issue, we propose UCTransNet, a new model for clinical image segmentation that adopts the recently popular Transformer mechanism to enable effective skip connections.
Specifically, we decouple the channels in the skip connections from the spatial dimensions and then employ the attention mechanism to selectively aggregate the information.
This channel-wise transformer not only significantly reduces the computational cost but also helps the model to focus on important information, leading to improved performance.
We perform comprehensive experiments on four public whole slide image datasets, including two datasets with whole-slide images larger than 100 megapixels.
The results show that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance in all datasets with a significant reduction in computational requirements during training.
Recent progress in deep learning has enabled the development of powerful models for image semantic segmentation, i.e., assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
However, these models are trained on large datasets and require a significant amount of computational resources, making them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained devices.
In this paper, we propose a lightweight and efficient approach for image semantic segmentation based on personalized modeling.
Our approach is designed to reduce the computational cost and memory requirements of the model, while still achieving high accuracy.
We achieve this by combining a deep neural network with a set of personalized semantic prototypes, which are generated from a small number of labeled images.
The personalized prototypes enable the model to adapt to new images with different semantics, and improve the segmentation accuracy by leveraging the user's knowledge and experience.
We evaluate our approach on the Cityscapes and CamVid datasets, and show that it achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Recent works have shown that training a mask discriminator during training for semi-supervised segmentation greatly improves the segmentation performance.
However, the discriminator is typically discarded thereafter, despite the additional information it contains about the parts of the image that are difficult to segment.
In this work, we propose to re-use these discriminators during test-time, when the labels are available.

We show that this is effective in mitigating the distribution shift between training and test time, and we achieve state-of-the-art performance on the semi-supervised semantic segmentation benchmarks S3DIS and Cityscapes.
Deep reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising direction for solving visual perception tasks, which are usually challenging for traditional machine learning methods.
In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey of recent advances in deep RL for computer vision tasks.
We first introduce the basic concepts and techniques of deep RL, and then review the state-of-the-art methods for image classification, object detection, and segmentation.
We also discuss the challenges and opportunities of deep RL in computer vision, and highlight potential future research directions.
Our goal is to provide a comprehensive and informative reference for researchers interested in this emerging field.
Segmenting regions of interest from large volumetric biomedical images is a challenging task, and often involves tedious manual labor.
We present a novel approach towards fully automatic segmentation of structures in large volumetric images using a hierarchical random walker framework.
Our method enables not only robust segmentation of structures in individual images, but also consistent segmentation across multiple images.
In our approach, the hierarchical random walker framework is trained in a weakly-supervised manner, where only a small amount of training data is required.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on the problem of brain tumor segmentation in multi-modal MRI scans, where our method achieves high accuracy and robust performance on a public dataset.
Recent progress in semantic segmentation largely relies on large-scale labeled datasets, which are expensive to collect and annotate.
When training a segmentation model, the distribution of the labeled source domain might be significantly different from that of the target domain, where the model will be deployed.
To overcome this domain shift, we propose a source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) approach for image segmentation, which requires no labeled source data.
Specifically, we learn a joint distribution of appearance and geometry for the target domain to adapt the pre-trained model for segmentation.
We propose to minimize the divergence between the estimated joint distribution and the product of the estimated appearance and geometry distributions for consistency.
Furthermore, to effectively estimate the distributions, we propose to maximize the correlation between their estimates and the ground truth labels.
We validate our approach on three public segmentation benchmarks, where the experiments show the superiority of our method over the state-of-the-art approaches.
We present a new approach to shape modeling based on the notion of a spline partition.
Given an input shape, ours system first applies a spring-based clustering algorithm to identify a partition of the shape's boundary.
This partition is then used as the basis for a spline approximation of the shape.

The resulting spline partition represents the shape in a hierarchical manner, with fine-grained detail captured at the local level by the partition, and with the global structure captured by the spline approximation.

We show that this approach can produce visually pleasing representations of a variety of input shapes, and can be used to perform editing operations such as insertion, deletion, and modification of shape details.
In recent years, many works have addressed foreground segmentation by incorporating external knowledge in the form of predefined bounds to constrain the foreground regions.
We propose a simple yet effective method for translating visual boundary knowledge into initial foreground seeds by reusing the intermediate outputs from existing segmentation models.
Our approach is general and can be used with any segmentation model that produces hierarchical representations.

We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on both the Cityscapes and CamVid datasets, where we show that our approach outperforms existing methods for incorporating visual boundary knowledge in terms of F1-score and Intersection over Union, while being efficient enough to be used in an iterative segmentation pipeline.

Automated segmentation of skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone from three-dimensional (3D) Computed Tomography (CT) images is a promising approach for non-invasive whole-body composition analysis.
However, there is a significant gap between the current state-of-the-art technology and its application for body composition analysis in a clinical setting.
In this paper, we perform a comprehensive validation of two state-of-the-art automated whole-body segmentation algorithms for skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone from 3D CT images.
We compared the results to ground truth segmentations obtained from manual labeling by two human experts.
Our validation study included 30 subjects (15 male, 15 female) aged between 8 and 81 years (52.7 ± 30.8).
We calculated the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Sensitivity (Se), Specificity (Sp), and Accuracy (Acc) for each tissue type and each algorithm.
Our results show that the state-of-the-art algorithms perform similarly for skeletal muscle (DSC: 0.81-0.83) and adipose tissue (DSC: 0.80-0.85), while performing better for bone (DSC: 0.90-0.93).
For all tissue types, the sensitivity and specificity were above 0.80 and the accuracy was above 0.75.

In conclusion, our validation study shows that the current state-of-the-art technology for whole-body segmentation of skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone from 3D CT images is sufficiently accurate for clinical applications.

Recent works have shown that the utilization of transformers for computer vision tasks provides promising results, despite the fact that this architecture is originally designed for natural language processing.
However, utilizing transformers in medical image segmentation tasks is not straightforward due to the scarcity of large-scale annotated data.
In this paper, we present a simple yet effective approach for utilizing transformers for medical image segmentation.
Our approach focuses on utilizing only the encoder architecture of transformers, which is trained with the pre-trained language model (PLM) and fine-tuned with the target segmentation task.
We name our approach LeViT-UNet, which stands for "Encoder with pre-trained Language Model for Medical Image Segmentation."

Our experimental results show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple medical image segmentation benchmarks with various architectures, including 2D as well as 3D scenarios.
We also perform an in-depth analysis to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
Recent advances in semantic segmentation of medical images have relied on large datasets collected from different domains, i.e., different hospitals or institutions.
However, directly applying models trained on one domain to another domain may result in poor performance due to the domain shift.
In this work, we aim to learn a domain adaptation model to improve the performance of semantic segmentation on target domains while preserving privacy of both the source and target domains.

We propose a two-stage adaptation method: (1) a global adaptation stage that learns a shared feature representation across all domains via a non-private dataset, and (2) a private adaptation stage that fine-tunes the shared feature representation with a domain-specific dataset without revealing the domain-specific data.

We implement the private adaptation stage using differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), which adds noise to the gradients of the learning objective with respect to the model parameters.
The noise magnitude is carefully chosen to strike a balance between utility and privacy.
We conduct comprehensive experiments on three different domains using two public datasets and one private dataset.
Our results show that our method can effectively adapt to a target domain while preserving privacy for both source and target domains.
Recent advances in medical imaging technology have led to a vast amount of big data, requiring efficient and robust algorithms for image segmentation.
We present a novel approach to medical image segmentation that combines the strengths of two powerful techniques: Transformers and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).
Our method, called TransFuse, leverages the ability of Transformers to capture long-range dependencies in data and the capacity of CNNs to learn complex spatial patterns.
By fusing these two modalities, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple medical image segmentation benchmarks.
Our results show that TransFuse is a powerful and effective tool for medical image segmentation, capable of handling large and complex datasets with high accuracy.
We believe that this approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of medical image analysis and improve the diagnosis and treatment of various diseases.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, with a goal to assign semantic labels to every pixel in an input image.

Most existing works focus on designing complex models to learn direct mappings from images to segmentation labels, which limit their applicability in real-world applications due to the model's complexity and resource intensity.
In this work, we propose a novel approach to semantic segmentation that utilizes psychometric learning, a technique derived from perceptual psychology.
Our method leverages a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) and learns a hierarchical segmentation model using a psychometric learning framework.

We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on the Cityscapes and CamVid datasets, achieving competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods while using a fraction of the model size and computational resources.
The proposed method is simple, efficient, and effective, making it suitable for real-world applications.
We present an object detection method that can be used for an efficient cluster initialization.
Our method is based on deep learning and unsupervised learning.
We use a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features from the input images.
The extracted features are then processed by a region proposal network (RPN) to generate object proposals.
Finally, a support vector machine (SVM) is used to classify the proposals into different categories.
We evaluate our method on the VOC 2007 dataset.
The experimental results show that our method can achieve a mAP of 0.830 with a single model.
Our model's initializations for the clusters show a large performance gain compared to K-means.

Arxiv abstract:
Unsupervised image segmentation is a classic problem in computer vision with a wide range of applications.
We propose a new algorithm based on maximizing the mutual information between the segment labels and the image pixels, subject to a smooth label field prior and a label consistency regularization.
The resulting optimization problem is non-convex and challenging to solve.
We adopt a recent result in convex optimization that shows that a non-convex problem can be optimized by alternatively optimizing its convex relaxation and its dual objective.
We implement this approach and show that it converges to a local maximum of the original non-convex energy.
We further propose an adversarial regularization that improves the quality of the solution.
Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on both synthetic and real image datasets, showing that it produces state-of-the-art results.
We introduce a new class of GANs, called conditional GANs (cGANs), which combine the benefits of conditional and unconditional GANs.
cGANs improve conditional GANs by imposing an explicit conditional prior on the generator, which allows for improved conditioning and more efficient training.

We show that cGANs can be viewed as a specific case of unconditional GANs, with an implicit conditional prior, and prove that, unlike unconditional GANs, their convergence is not affected by the conditioning.
Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of cGANs on image synthesis tasks.
Recent advances in MRI imaging and pre-trained models have made it possible to push the boundary of brain tumor segmentation (BTS).
In this work, we have developed a state-of-the-art framework, called TransBTS, for multimodal brain tumor segmentation based on a transformer architecture.
We utilize recent advances in pre-trained models and domain adaptation for computer vision to improve the performance of our model.
Our model achieves a dice similarity coefficient of 0.9289 and an intersection over union of 0.8804 on the BRATS 2021 validation dataset.
We achieve state-of-the-art performance on the BRATS 2021 validation dataset compared to prior works, especially in the presence of severe magnetic field distortion, low contrast, and noise.
Code is available at https://github.com/AI4BRAIN/TransBTS.
Adaptation of deep learning models is an effective methodology for addressing the domain shift problem, however, adaptation techniques have not been explored fully for medical image segmentation.

In this paper, we adapt an off-the-shelf source segmenter for target medical image segmentation, and introduce a domain adaptation (DA) framework that aims to reduce the domain gap between the source and target domains for automatic image segmentation.
We employ a cycle-consistent adversarial domain adaptation (CYCADA) method, which utilizes cycle-consistency and adversarial training to learn a domain-invariant segmentation model.
We perform experiments on adapting a general segmentation model for fetal brain, cardiac, and tumor segmentation involving significant domain shift.
Our DA framework improves the segmentation performance in terms of dice similarity coefficient (DSC) on all the target datasets.

In particular, our method achieves a significant improvement of 1.43 DSC points on fetal brain segmentation, and 0.79 DSC points on cardiac segmentation compared to the source model without any adaptation.
Recent results show that multi-modal representations can improve downstream task performance by adding robustness, but they may not always be available.
In this paper, we study the setting where only uni-modal teachers are available, posing a new challenge to learning multi-modal representations.

We find that directly training a multi-modal student with uni-modal teachers is sub-optimal and propose to firstly learn a single-modal student using a uni-modal teacher, and then distill a multi-modal student from the single-modal student and the residual teachers.
In this way, we unify both the inductive and transductive settings into an unified framework, and develop a new technique, residual teachers, for transductive learning.
Experiments on image and video recognition show the effectiveness of our approach compared to the state-of-the-art.
Recent results in vision segmentation strongly suggest that effective architectures are able to utilize additional modalities, such as depth and normals, to improve performance on challenging tasks.
However, most existing approaches train all modalities simultaneously in a fully-supervised manner, requiring a large amount of labeled data for all modes.
In this work, we propose a knowledge distillation approach to transfer the knowledge from a fully-supervised multi-modal teacher network to a mono-modal student network.
We show that, compared to training from scratch, our method significantly improves the performance of mono-modal segmentation networks even when trained with a significantly smaller labeled dataset.
Our method is extensively evaluated on ACDC and NYU Depth V2 datasets, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on most benchmarks.
We propose a hybrid mmWave and camera system for long-range depth imaging.
The system simultaneously captures a mmWave image and a camera image, and then fuses the two types of data for long-range depth estimation.
In the mmWave image, depth information is encoded in the phase information of the pixels.
A depth estimation algorithm is then applied to the mmWave image to obtain a preliminary depth map.
The camera image is used to refine the preliminary depth map obtained from the mmWave image.
Furthermore, we introduce a novel depth estimation algorithm that consists of an iterative refinement process.
The process utilizes an initial depth map as a starting point and then iteratively updates the depth map to refine the estimation.
The proposed algorithm is trained on synthetic data and is evaluated on real world data.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately estimate depth at long ranges.
Recent progress in medical image segmentation has largely been driven by supervised learning, but the availability of labeled images remains a bottleneck.
In this work, we tackle the semi-supervised segmentation problem where only a sparse set of training images is labeled.
Our approach leverages unlabeled images to augment the training set and improve performance.

We propose a self-ensembling contrastive learning framework that maximizes the agreement between segmentations of the same patient while minimizing the disagreement between segmentations of different patients.
To effectively capture the underlying structure and achieve per-pixel segmentation, we aggregate predictions from multiple self-ensembled models.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on three public abdominal CT datasets and achieve state-of-the-art performance.
Arxiv abstract:
We address the problem of domain adaptation under the setting where only a small labeled dataset is available for the target domain, which is often the case in practice.

We propose a semi-supervised domain adaptation approach that leverages the available unlabeled data in the target domain and the labeled data in the source domain, via adaptive and progressive feature alignment.
Specifically, we first align the feature representations of the source and target domains at a high-level abstraction, where only a coarse alignment is required.
Then, we fine-tune the alignment at a lower-level abstraction, gradually refining the feature representations to better align with each other.
Our approach adapts well to the target domain and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets for semi-supervised domain adaptation.
Recent works have shown that deep learning models, trained using standard datasets, can achieve remarkable performance on medical image detection tasks.
However, fine-tuning these models for specific datasets can be expensive and time-consuming.

Also, the variability in the appearance of medical objects across different institutions due to acquisition protocol, contrast agent, and imaging device, makes it difficult to adopt pre-trained models.
In this paper, we present nnDetection, a self-training approach to adapt deep learning models to detect medical objects in clinical images.
In particular, we focus on detecting vessels in angiographic X-rays and vertebrae in spinal X-rays.
Given a pre-trained model, our approach relies on the detection of positive and negative examples from the clinical images by using a simple initial detector.
These examples are then used to fine-tune the model.
We show that our approach achieves detection performance similar to or better than finely-tuned models, while requiring less computational resources and no manual annotation.
In this paper, we present a light-weight encoder-decoder based network, CFPNet-M, for real-time segmentation of multimodal biomedical images.
CFPNet-M is designed to perform dynamic programming based pixel-wise labeling of images in multiple modalities via a shared encoder-decoder architecture.
In our design, the encoder extracts the semantic content of the input multimodal biomedical images, while the decoder performs pixel-wise labeling in a bottom-up manner.
To handle the variability in the input images, a confidence based fusion strategy is proposed at the decoder stage.
Specifically, we employ a confidence score to measure the reliability of the features from different modalities, and use it to guide the fusion process.
With the proposed approach, CFPNet-M enables effective refinement of the segmentation results, while maintaining real-time performance.
We evaluate CFPNet-M on the multimodal brain tumor segmentation dataset ISBI 2017, and achieve promising results with respect to state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed method is designed to be light-weight, and can run in real-time on a typical CPU, making it accessible to the majority of clinical sites.
Gaussian dynamic convolution (GDC) is a fast approximation of spatial convolution that exploits the locality and orientation of filters to achieve significant acceleration.
However, existing GDC methods are not directly applicable to pixel-level segmentation, because they use a small number of fixed filters with limited expressive power.
In this paper, we extend GDC to a new framework named Gaussian dynamic conditional random fields (GDC-CRF), which is capable of capturing complex local patterns for pixel-level segmentation.

We construct a stack of Gaussian filters from a set of orientation-specific filters with distinct scales, and dynamically compute the response of the Gaussian filters according to the multi-scale orientation of the input features.
Our framework is essentially a Gaussian dynamic convolution (GDC) that replaces the fixed filterbank with a set of Gaussian filters.
We derive a closed-form solution for the GDC-CRF, and further simplify it into a linear solve by introducing a new sparse prior.
Experiments on four benchmark datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both speed and segmentation quality.
Recent progress in deep learning has enabled the development of end-to-end trainable systems for self-driving.
However, training such systems is challenging due to the lack of large-scale, diverse, and realistic training data.
We introduce GeoSim, a video simulation system that generates geometrically-accurate, photorealistic training data for deep learning-based self-driving systems.
GeoSim is designed to address the limitations of current simulation systems, which often produce unrealistic and synthetic-looking images.
It uses a combination of geometric reasoning, physical simulation, and artistic rendering to generate realistic and diverse training data.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of GeoSim in generating realistic training data and show that it improves the performance of deep learning-based self-driving systems.
We present a novel falling-ball algorithm for image segmentation based on the minimization of a cost function via a simulated annealing approach.
Our algorithm is inspired by the behavior of balls falling into a bowl of sand, where the sand is modeled as a smooth surface and the balls are initially placed on a grid overlaying the image.
By iteratively moving the balls downward, the grid cells corresponding to the boundaries between regions in the image are gradually revealed.
Our approach is able to handle a variety of segmentation scenarios and is particularly effective at segmenting images with complex and irregular boundaries.
We demonstrate the performance of our algorithm on a number of benchmark images and compare it to other state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.

Our results show that our algorithm is able to produce high-quality segmentations that are comparable to or better than those produced by other algorithms, while being more efficient in terms of computation time.
In this paper, we present an image segmentation method based on geodesic paths.
The input to our method is an image and a user-defined seed point.
Our method iteratively grows a region around the seed point by minimizing an energy function that combines a geodesic distance term and a region homogeneity term.

The geodesic distance term encourages the region to grow along the direction of greatest similarity, while the region homogeneity term encourages the region to be composed of pixels that are similar to each other.
The minimization process is performed by a variant of the gradient descent algorithm that is suitable for non-differentiable energy functions.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on a variety of images, and compare its performance to that of a competing method.
Our method achieves better segmentation results with less user interaction.
Recent studies have shown that the analysis of medical images is particularly beneficial for the analysis of liquid samples in hospitals and medical labs.
In this paper, we present a novel approach to computer vision for liquid samples using hierarchical image segmentation and relation prediction.

Our approach is based on the observation that the shape and size of cells in a liquid sample are related to each other, and that these relations can be used to improve the accuracy of cell segmentation.
We propose a hierarchical image segmentation framework that first segments the cells in a sample based on their shape, and then refines the segmentation based on their size.
Our approach is evaluated on a large dataset of liquid samples, and results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art in cell segmentation.
Recent advances in medical image segmentation have benefited from large-scale annotated datasets and deep neural networks.
However, manually annotating anatomical structures in medical images is expensive and time-consuming, limiting the size of training datasets and the frequency of updating trained models.

We present a fully automated multi-label deep supervision (MLDS) framework for medical image segmentation that leverages abundant single-label segmentations to create pseudo-annotations for all labels.
Our framework does not require any additional annotation effort yet provides accurate segmentation results.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on three public abdominal computed tomography datasets with different levels of difficulty and show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to other semi-supervised and fully supervised methods.
In addition, we provide an in-depth analysis of our method on different levels of label difficulty and the impact of the number of pseudo-annotations on performance.
Recent works have proposed techniques for the quantization of deep neural networks (DNNs) to reduce memory storage and bandwidth requirements for deployment on edge devices.
However, these methods tend to have a significant impact on accuracy, limiting their applicability in many real-world use cases.
In this work, we propose a novel quantization scheme that significantly improves the accuracy of DNNs with low memory footprint.
Our scheme is based on the concept of quantization-aware training, which leverages the knowledge of the underlying network structure to adapt the training process to the quantized setting.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a variety of popular DNN architectures, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the ImageNet dataset with only a slight degradation in accuracy compared to the full precision model.
Our scheme is general and can be applied to various quantization methods, making it a powerful tool for accurate edge computing.
Recent results in image-based medical prediction show that deep learning models can compete with experts, provided they are given ample amounts of annotated data.
In this work, we investigate the impact of the amount of training data on the performance of expert-level predictions in the domain of lymph node segmentation and classification.

We observe that, given a fixed amount of expert-annotated data, further inclusion of data that is labeled by less reliable sources (such as non-expert clinicians or even non-clinical information) results in a decrease of performance.

We show that such data selection strategies are especially important when dealing with rare events (e.g., cancer), as in these instances even expert-level predictions might have errors that could be avoided by careful data selection.
To tackle this problem, we propose a self-supervised approach for sample selection that uses a measure of interpretability to select the most informative samples for training.

We show that our proposed method is especially useful in scenarios where only a small amount of expert-level labeled data is available and that it performs on par with methods that rely on significantly more data.
We address the problem of adapting a semantic segmentation network trained on one dataset (source) to a target dataset with potentially different appearance and labeling biases.
We propose a constraint-based approach that learns a constraint loss function to preserve the labeling of easy and medium difficulty pixels while allowing the adaptation of hard pixels.
We evaluate our method on the Cityscapes and CamVid datasets, and show that it achieves state-of-the-art performance in domain adaptation for semantic segmentation.
In particular, on Cityscapes->CamVid, our method achieves a mean accuracy of 86.3%, which is 2.2% better than the previous best result.
Recent progress in semantic segmentation largely relies on large-scale labeled datasets, which are usually expensive to collect and annotate.
As a result, most prior works focus on datasets where the objects of interest are represented in a fixed set of classes, limiting their applicability to unseen classes.

Furthermore, the choice of training and testing datasets often leads to biased and mismatched distributions between the source and target domains, adversely impacting the performance of segmentation models.

To address these issues, we propose a source-relaxed domain adaptation approach for image segmentation, which relaxes the requirement of having corresponding object classes between the source and target domains.
Our key insight is that, even in the absence of shared classes, it is still possible to exploit label correlations across different classes for domain adaptation.

Specifically, we leverage the label relationships (e.g., mutual exclusivity and inclusion relationships) among objects of different classes to align distributions between the source and target domains, leading to better generalization performance on unseen classes.
We further propose a novel joint latent alignment and segmentation framework, where the segmentation model is jointly trained with a latent alignment model for effective domain adaptation.

Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on both the Cityscapes and Mapillary Vistas segmentation benchmarks with significant improvements for unseen classes, even when only seen during testing.
We introduce MeanShift++, a variant of the classic MeanShift algorithm for visual object detection and tracking.
Like its predecessor, MeanShift++ uses a weighted average of the feature values in the detection window to model the posterior probability distribution.
However, MeanShift++ changes the weighting scheme to improve the algorithm's ability to find objects that are spatially localized, poorly differentiated, or smaller than the search window.

To evaluate MeanShift++, we implemented tracking and segmentation variants of the algorithm and compared them to their MeanShift counterparts on six widely used benchmark datasets for visual object tracking and segmentation.
In all cases, we observed a significant improvement in accuracy and speed with no increase in running time.
MeanShift has recently emerged as an extremely fast and efficient alternative to more complex methods for tracking objects in videos and segmenting objects in images.

However, the method has two primary limitations: (i) it can only detect objects that are sufficiently spatially coherent (i.e., objects whose features are similar enough to each other that their average represents a good model for the posterior); and (ii) it is not able to model the uncertainty in the object location or the object boundary, because it outputs a single position for each detected object.
In this paper, we introduce a new variant of MeanShift, which we call MeanShift++, that addresses both of these limitations.

Our key observation is that the spatial coherence issue can be alleviated by modeling the posterior distribution using a weighted average of the feature values in the detection window, where the weights are computed using a robust estimator.
This enables us to detect objects that are spatially localized, poorly differentiated, or smaller than the search window, while still maintaining a fast runtime.

We also introduce a novel boundary refinement procedure that outputs a set of samples that represent the uncertainty in the object location and boundary, and show that our approach is competitive with state-of-the-art algorithms on standard visual object tracking and segmentation benchmarks while being significantly faster.
We introduce a new referring expression comprehension pipeline that combines a locate module with a segmentation module.
The locate module uses object detection to localize all objects in the image that are mentioned in the referring expression.
The segmentation module uses the located objects to guide the segmentation process and produces a segmented image that highlights the relevant object regions.
In order to train our segmentation module, we create a new Referring Expression Segmentation (RES) dataset that is composed of referring expressions and their corresponding image regions.
We show that training on this dataset improves referring expression comprehension by a large margin over using object detection outputs and baseline segmentation methods.

We conduct an error analysis and show that incorrect referring expression comprehension is often due to objects that are similar in appearance and in the wrong location, suggesting that segmentation is a key component for referring expression comprehension.
Semantic image segmentation remains a challenging task, and state-of-the-art methods often require designing elaborate architectures, which can be a laborious and trial-and-error process.
In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective approach for dense prediction of pixel labels, showing that denser connections in a convolutional neural network improve its performance.

Given a baseline architecture, we develop an easily-implemented method to automatically search for the optimal number and density of connections in a densely connected neural network, which significantly enhances performance.
Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Cityscapes dataset, outperforming the current leaders by a large margin.
We also establish new state-of-the-art results on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and NYU Depth V2 datasets.

We present a method to train neural networks that are inherently capable of specializing to a variety of distinct tasks, achieving performance on par with state-of-the-art specialized architectures on each task, while maintaining efficiency in terms of the number of weights.

Our key insight is that this can be achieved by learning a good enough encoding of the architectures, with an encoder network and a decoder network that can construct architectures of a certain granularity.

We show that, if we constrain the decoder network to only be capable of constructing a finite set of architecture tokens, the encoder can learn to encode architectures in a continuous vector space, and the whole system can specialize to a particular task while only training on a diverse set of tasks.

We present an algorithm, Neuro-Symbolic Dynamic Programming, to train such a system, and show that the method is capable of training models on CIFAR-10 that match the test error of specialized architectures on CIFAR-100, CIFAR-200, and SVHN, while being capable of generalizing to ZOO, a set of "out of distribution" datasets.
We present a novel approach towards few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) that combines the strengths of localization and similarity learning.
Given only a few labeled images, our approach aims to synthesize a precise and general localization map that can be used to segment novel unseen images from the same class.
Specifically, we train a neural network that learns to generate a localization map that distinguishes whether a given image contains a lesion or not.
