We propose a new approach for salient object detection, called Inner and Inter Label Propagation (IILP), which extends recent single-label methods to effectively handle multi-label inputs.
Our key insight is that the inter-label context, i.e., the presence of other objects, can assist in better distinguishing salient objects from the background.
We exploit this insight by iteratively refining object proposals through both inner and inter label propagation.
Specifically, we propagate labels within each proposal to capture the internal structure, and across proposals to capture the relationships between objects.
Our approach is fully automatic, i.e., it does not require any explicit bounding box annotations, and is applicable to both single- and multi-label inputs.
We evaluate IILP on the salient object detection benchmark, and demonstrate that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art on both single-label and multi-label datasets.
Abstract: This paper presents a new class of robust controllers for regular linear systems with infinite-dimensional exosystems.
The proposed controller is based on a novel approach to robust control that utilizes a systematic construction of a set of basis vectors for the system's state-space.
These basis vectors are utilized to formulate a linear matrix inequality (LMI) problem whose solution yields a robust controller.
The proposed controller is shown to be asymptotically stable and achieves an H-infinity performance criterion.
The efficacy of the proposed controller is demonstrated via numerical examples.
We give a simple construction of S-folds for N=3 superconformal field theories in four dimensions.
This construction is motivated by the study of topological strings and the recent development of the topological vertex.
As an application we provide a complete description of the S-fold moduli spaces for N=3 superconformal field theories in four dimensions.
We find a one-to-one correspondence between these S-fold moduli spaces and certain three-dimensional conformal field theories with N=3 superconformal symmetry.
We propose compressive temporal higher order cyclostationary (HOS) statistics as a means of realizing distributed, compressive spectrum sensing in asynchronous, narrowband sensor networks.

Our approach relies on a recently developed theory of higher order cyclostationarity, which allows one to extract a variety of second order statistics from a cyclostationary signal in a manner akin to spectral estimation in white noise.
By making use of higher order statistics, we show that it is possible to sense the spectrum of a cyclostationary signal at high resolutions with extremely low energy.
In particular, we show that under certain conditions it is possible to sense the spectrum to within 0.1% of the true spectrum using only a small number of cycles of the signal.
Finally, we present experimental results which demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method.

We investigate the complementary relation of quantum coherence and quantum correlations in multiple measurements, which illustrates that how the quantum coherence and quantum correlations are exchanged under various measurements.

When a quantum state undergoes projective measurements along two different bases, the coherence can evolve into quantum correlations via the measurement process, and this process can be realized by local operations and classical communication (LOCC).
Furthermore, if we measure the state along multiple bases, the coherence can be transformed into generalized quantum correlations, which describes the non-local properties of the state.
This transformation can be achieved by the help of quantum operations and classical communication (QOCC).
On the other hand, when generalized measurements are performed on the quantum state, the initial quantum correlations can be converted into coherence, and this conversion can be realized by LOCC.
Our analysis provides a new perspective to understand the complementary relation of coherence and correlations in the framework of multiple measurements.
We introduce a new estimator for the intrinsic dimension of a finite collection of data points, induced by the Gaussian core model.
This model captures the local geometry around a data point through a truncated multivariate normal distribution.
The intrinsic dimension is the dimension of the smallest space in which the data can be embedded in such a way that each data point has a neighborhood that is an analog of the model.
We show that our estimator is consistently estimated, and suggest an iterative algorithm to compute it.
This algorithm is validated against synthetic data, and the model is applied to several real world data sets.
In particular, we show that on the "Ising" model, the intrinsic dimension grows as the dimension of the ambient space grows.
In the last few years, the BaBar collaboration has measured the branching fractions and form factors of semileptonic $B$-meson decays with impressive precision.
I will present the most recent results, including the first measurement of the weak charge of the $b$ quark, $|q_b|=(4.08\pm 0.14)\times 10^{-3}$.
These results are consistent with the standard model, and some of them represent an improvement in precision by almost an order of magnitude.
We study the complexity of optimizing multicell coordinated beamforming with rate outage constraint, which maximizes the sum-rate of the network subject to a reliability requirement.
We first present a polynomial time algorithm to solve this non-convex problem to global optimality when the number of users is equal to or larger than the number of base stations.
This algorithm is based on a novel semi-definite programming (SDP) formulation of the problem, and on a block coordinate descent (BCD) method.
Then, we propose a low-complexity greedy algorithm that achieves a near-optimal performance with significantly reduced computational complexity.
The proposed greedy algorithm is based on a novel approximation of the optimal beamforming matrix, and on a thresholding technique that allows us to select the most beneficial users for cooperation.

Finally, we present numerical results that illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms in terms of sum-rate and outage probability, and that demonstrate the significant reduction in computational complexity achieved by the greedy algorithm.
The effect of bismuth (Bi) implantation on the electrical properties of amorphous selenium (a-Se) and tellurium (a-Te) films has been investigated.
The a-Se and a-Te films were deposited by thermal evaporation in a vacuum chamber.
The implantation of Bi was carried out at room temperature using an ion beam source.
The electrical properties of the films were evaluated by measuring the current-voltage characteristics.
The results show that the implantation of Bi significantly affects the electrical properties of a-Se and a-Te films.
The conductivity of the implanted films increases significantly compared to that of the unimplanted films.
This is attributed to the presence of Bi nanoparticles that act as additional charge carriers.
The activation energy of the implanted films is found to be lower than that of the unimplanted films, indicating that the Bi nanoparticles facilitate the movement of charge carriers.
The breakdown voltage of the implanted films is higher than that of the unimplanted films, suggesting that the Bi nanoparticles improve the stability of the films.

The results of this study show that Bi implantation can be used to modify the electrical properties of a-Se and a-Te films and provide new opportunities for applications in thin-film transistors and photodetectors.
We study global relaxation of bistable solutions for a class of gradient systems in one unbounded spatial dimension.

We show that, depending on the sign of the highest eigenvalue of the linearization matrix at a stable equilibrium, the relaxation either is fast (this occurs when the highest eigenvalue is negative) or slows down as t∼√(t), approaching a stable equilibrium (this occurs when the highest eigenvalue is positive).

In the case of slow relaxation, we establish that the relaxation is always faster when the system is perturbed away from the equilibrium in a direction corresponding to an eigenvector associated with a positive eigenvalue.
Finally, we present an example of a system for which the relaxation is as slow as t^{1/3}.
The results are based on a priori estimates combined with numerical simulations.
Components from different providers can work together smoothly, enabling modular systems that are scalable, flexible, and reusable.
However, in many cases, components from different providers must communicate asynchronously because of the lack of a global clock or a common ready-signal.

Unfortunately, asynchronous communication poses challenges to compatibility: a component can become ready to deliver a response before it has received all requests from the provider, or it can receive requests in a different order from their original sending order at the provider.
We introduce a simple formal model of compatibility for asynchronous communication and present an algorithm to check compatibility of components.
Our contributions are applicable to any setting in which components from different providers need to communicate asynchronously, independently of the programming model.
We have implemented our approach in the form of a tool and applied it to several case studies from the CloudBus ecosystem.
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be positive integers.
In this paper, we establish a recurrence formula for sums of powers modulo $m$ of the form $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \binom{i}{\alpha} \binom{n-i+\beta}{\beta} \pmod{m}$, where $m$ is a fixed positive integer.
This formula generalizes and simplifies previously known results on binomial sums.
Furthermore, we present a combinatorial interpretation of our main result in terms of paths in a dynamic allocation network.
This new perspective might be useful for obtaining more results on binomial sums in the future.
This paper presents a novel approach for background-foreground segmentation in the context of interior sensing in the automotive industry.
Interior sensing systems are becoming increasingly important for various applications such as driver monitoring, occupant detection, and gesture recognition.
Accurate segmentation of the background and foreground is a crucial step in these systems, as it allows for the extraction of relevant information from the scene.
However, existing methods often struggle with challenging scenarios such as low lighting conditions, occlusions, and complex backgrounds.
In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to achieve robust and accurate background-foreground segmentation.
Our method utilizes a combination of spatial and temporal information to improve the segmentation performance.
We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of interior sensing images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of interior sensing systems in the automotive industry by providing a reliable and efficient solution for background-foreground segmentation.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, the lack of annotated data in medical imaging limits the performance of deep learning models.
In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised meta-learning approach with disentanglement for domain-generalised medical image segmentation.
Our method leverages a small amount of annotated data from the target domain and a large amount of unannotated data from multiple source domains to learn a domain-generalised segmentation model.
We introduce a disentanglement module that separates the shared and domain-specific features, enabling the model to adapt to new domains more effectively.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalisation capability.
Our work provides a promising solution for improving medical image segmentation in scenarios with limited annotated data.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical imaging, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for patch-based medical image segmentation using Quantum Tensor Networks (QTNs).
QTNs are a powerful tool in quantum machine learning, capable of capturing complex patterns and relationships in data.
We apply QTNs to the task of medical image segmentation by representing image patches as quantum states and using quantum operations to extract features and classify pixels.
Our experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.

This work opens up new possibilities for using quantum computing techniques in medical image analysis and has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation.
The U-Net architecture has been widely used in various medical image segmentation tasks due to its effectiveness in capturing both local and global contextual information.
However, the traditional skip connections in U-Net may not fully exploit the channel-wise relationships between feature maps.
In this paper, we propose UCTransNet, a novel U-Net variant that incorporates the Transformer module to enhance the skip connections from a channel-wise perspective.
Specifically, we introduce a channel-wise attention mechanism to capture long-range dependencies and enhance feature representation.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that UCTransNet achieves superior performance compared to the original U-Net and other state-of-the-art methods.
Our findings suggest that rethinking skip connections in U-Net from a channel-wise perspective with Transformer can significantly improve the performance of medical image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for personalized image semantic segmentation.
The proposed method leverages deep learning techniques to learn personalized segmentation models for individual users.
The approach takes into account user-specific preferences and requirements, allowing for more accurate and tailored segmentation results.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving personalized image semantic segmentation.
The findings of this study have implications for various applications, such as image editing, object recognition, and scene understanding.
This paper proposes a method for test-time training under distribution shifts by re-using adversarial mask discriminators.
The authors introduce a novel framework that leverages the discriminators trained during adversarial training to generate masks for test-time training.
The proposed method is evaluated on various datasets and shows promising results in terms of accuracy and robustness to distribution shifts.
The findings suggest that re-using adversarial mask discriminators can be an effective approach for test-time training under distribution shifts.
Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a powerful approach for solving complex problems in computer vision.
This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the recent advancements in DRL for computer vision tasks.
We review the key concepts and techniques in DRL, including deep neural networks, reinforcement learning algorithms, and exploration-exploitation strategies.
We then discuss the applications of DRL in various computer vision tasks, such as object detection, image classification, and semantic segmentation.
Furthermore, we analyze the challenges and limitations of DRL in computer vision and propose potential directions for future research.
Overall, this survey provides a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art in DRL for computer vision and serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field.
This paper presents a hierarchical random walker segmentation method for large volumetric biomedical images.
The proposed method utilizes a multi-resolution approach to efficiently segment large images by dividing them into smaller sub-volumes.
The random walker algorithm is then applied to each sub-volume to obtain initial segmentations.
These initial segmentations are then refined using a hierarchical merging process that combines the segmentations from neighboring sub-volumes.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of large volumetric biomedical images and compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The results show that the hierarchical random walker segmentation method achieves accurate and efficient segmentations, making it suitable for large volumetric biomedical image analysis.
This paper proposes a novel approach for source-free domain adaptation in the context of image segmentation.
Traditional domain adaptation methods rely on labeled source domain data to train a model that can generalize to a target domain.
However, in many real-world scenarios, obtaining labeled source domain data is expensive or impractical.
To address this limitation, we introduce a source-free domain adaptation framework that leverages unlabeled source and target domain data.
Our approach combines a self-training strategy with a consistency regularization loss to encourage the model to produce consistent predictions on both domains.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving segmentation performance on the target domain without using any labeled source domain data.
Our results suggest that source-free domain adaptation can be a promising direction for overcoming the limitations of traditional domain adaptation methods.
This paper presents a novel approach for shape modeling using spline partitions.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of B-spline curves and partitioning techniques to represent complex shapes.
The key idea is to divide the shape into smaller regions using spline partitions, which are then individually modeled using B-spline curves.
This allows for more flexibility and control over the shape representation.
The paper provides a detailed description of the algorithm and presents experimental results to demonstrate its effectiveness in modeling various shapes.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Overall, this paper contributes to the field of shape modeling by introducing a new approach that combines spline partitions and B-spline curves to achieve more accurate and flexible shape representations.
This paper presents a novel approach for foreground segmentation in images using visual boundary knowledge translation.
The proposed method leverages the knowledge of visual boundaries to accurately separate foreground objects from the background.
The authors introduce a boundary-aware network architecture that incorporates boundary information into the segmentation process.
They also propose a boundary translation module that transfers boundary knowledge from annotated images to unannotated ones.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The findings of this study contribute to the field of computer vision and have potential applications in various domains such as object recognition and scene understanding.
Body composition analysis plays a crucial role in assessing overall health and disease risk.
Automated segmentation of skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone from 3D CT images is a promising approach for accurate and efficient body composition analysis.
However, comprehensive validation of these automated segmentation methods is lacking.
In this study, we aim to validate the accuracy and reliability of automated whole body skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone segmentation from 3D CT images.

We propose a comprehensive validation framework that includes comparison with manual segmentation, assessment of intra- and inter-observer variability, and evaluation of segmentation accuracy using various metrics.
Our results demonstrate that the automated segmentation methods achieve high accuracy and reliability, with minimal bias compared to manual segmentation.

This comprehensive validation of automated segmentation methods for body composition analysis paves the way for their widespread use in clinical and research settings, enabling more accurate and efficient assessment of body composition and its association with health outcomes.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical imaging, as it enables accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, existing methods for medical image segmentation often suffer from slow inference times due to the use of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as encoders.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called LeViT-UNet, which combines the efficiency of the Vision Transformer (ViT) with the accuracy of the U-Net for medical image segmentation.
Our approach replaces the CNN encoder in the traditional U-Net with a lightweight ViT encoder, resulting in faster inference times without sacrificing segmentation performance.

We evaluate our method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrate that LeViT-UNet achieves comparable or even better segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, while significantly reducing inference times.
Our findings suggest that LeViT-UNet has the potential to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of medical image segmentation in clinical practice.
This paper proposes a privacy-preserving domain adaptation method for semantic segmentation of medical images.
The goal is to improve the performance of semantic segmentation models trained on labeled data from a source domain when applied to a target domain with limited labeled data.
The proposed method leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) to learn a domain-invariant feature representation that can be used to adapt the source domain model to the target domain.
To preserve privacy, the GAN is trained using a privacy-preserving variant of the Wasserstein GAN.

Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to existing domain adaptation methods while preserving the privacy of sensitive patient information.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in this field, they struggle to capture long-range dependencies in images.
On the other hand, transformers have shown great potential in modeling long-range dependencies but are computationally expensive and struggle with spatial information.
In this paper, we propose TransFuse, a novel framework that combines the strengths of transformers and CNNs for medical image segmentation.
TransFuse utilizes a hybrid architecture that fuses the feature maps from a CNN backbone with the self-attention mechanism of transformers.
We evaluate TransFuse on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare its performance with state-of-the-art methods.
Our results demonstrate that TransFuse achieves superior segmentation accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency.
The proposed framework has the potential to enhance medical image analysis and improve clinical decision-making.
This paper presents a novel approach for hierarchical semantic segmentation using psychometric learning.
The proposed method leverages the human visual system's ability to perceive and categorize objects based on their semantic meaning.
The approach involves training a deep neural network using a psychometric learning framework, which allows the network to learn the hierarchical structure of object categories.
The network is trained on a large dataset of annotated images, and the learned hierarchical representation is used to perform semantic segmentation on new images.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The findings of this study have implications for various computer vision applications, such as autonomous driving and object recognition.
This paper proposes a deep learning object detection method for efficient clusters initialization.
The method utilizes a deep neural network to detect objects in an image and then uses the detected objects as initial clusters for a clustering algorithm.
The proposed method is compared with traditional methods on various datasets and shows superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the deep learning object detection method for clusters initialization, highlighting its potential for applications in computer vision and data analysis.
This paper presents a novel unsupervised image segmentation method that combines mutual information maximization and adversarial regularization.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of existing unsupervised segmentation techniques by leveraging the power of both mutual information and adversarial learning.

The mutual information maximization is used to measure the similarity between image patches, while the adversarial regularization is employed to encourage the segmentation network to generate more accurate and consistent segmentations.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method also shows promising results in challenging scenarios such as low-contrast images and complex backgrounds.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of unsupervised image segmentation and opens up new possibilities for further research in this area.

Conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs) have gained popularity in the field of generative modeling due to their ability to generate high-quality samples conditioned on specific input conditions.
However, it is unclear whether cGANs are explicitly conditioned on the input conditions or if they implicitly learn to generate samples based on these conditions.
In this paper, we investigate the explicit conditioning of cGANs by analyzing the network architecture and training process.
We propose a novel method to measure the degree of explicit conditioning in cGANs and apply it to several state-of-the-art models.
Our results show that while cGANs do exhibit some level of explicit conditioning, they also rely heavily on implicit learning.
These findings have implications for the interpretability and controllability of cGANs and suggest avenues for future research in improving the explicit conditioning of these models.
Brain tumor segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment planning of brain tumors.
In this paper, we propose TransBTS, a multimodal brain tumor segmentation method that utilizes the Transformer architecture.
TransBTS leverages the self-attention mechanism of Transformers to capture long-range dependencies and contextual information from multimodal MRI scans.
We evaluate TransBTS on the BraTS 2019 dataset and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that TransBTS achieves competitive performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of computational efficiency.

Our findings suggest that the Transformer architecture can be effectively applied to multimodal brain tumor segmentation tasks, offering a promising approach for improving the accuracy and efficiency of brain tumor diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper presents a method for adapting an off-the-shelf source segmenter for target medical image segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a transfer learning approach, where a pre-trained source segmenter is fine-tuned on target medical images.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their method on two different medical image segmentation tasks: liver segmentation and lung nodule segmentation.
Experimental results show that the adapted source segmenter achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods specifically designed for the target tasks.
The proposed method offers a practical and efficient solution for medical image segmentation by leveraging existing pre-trained models.
This paper proposes a novel approach to improve multi-modal learning by leveraging uni-modal teachers.
Multi-modal learning, which involves learning from multiple sources of information, has shown promising results in various domains.
However, it often requires a large amount of labeled data for each modality, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain.
In this paper, we introduce the concept of uni-modal teachers, which are pre-trained models that specialize in a single modality.
We then propose a framework that combines the predictions of these uni-modal teachers to improve the performance of a multi-modal model.
Our experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we show that our framework can effectively handle missing modalities and adapt to new modalities without retraining the entire model.
Overall, our findings suggest that leveraging uni-modal teachers can significantly enhance multi-modal learning and make it more accessible in real-world applications.
This paper presents a method for knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks.
The goal is to transfer the knowledge learned from a multi-modal segmentation network to a mono-modal segmentation network, in order to improve the performance of the latter.
The proposed method involves training a teacher network using multi-modal data and then distilling the knowledge from the teacher network to a student network using mono-modal data.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, with the student network achieving comparable or even better performance than the teacher network.
The findings of this study have implications for improving the performance of mono-modal segmentation networks using knowledge distillation techniques.
This paper presents a hybrid system that combines millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar and camera technology for long-range depth imaging.
The proposed system leverages the strengths of both technologies to overcome the limitations of each individual modality.
The mmWave radar provides accurate depth measurements at long distances, while the camera captures high-resolution images for detailed scene understanding.
The system architecture and data fusion algorithms are described, and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the hybrid system in various scenarios.
The proposed system has potential applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and surveillance systems, where accurate depth information is crucial for scene perception and object detection.
This paper proposes a novel self-ensembling contrastive learning approach for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation performance.
The self-ensembling mechanism is used to generate pseudo-labels for the unlabeled data, which are then used to train the segmentation model.
The contrastive learning objective is employed to encourage the model to learn meaningful representations of the medical images.

Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed method also achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods, indicating its potential for practical applications in medical image segmentation.
Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation via Adaptive and Progressive Feature Alignment

Abstract:

Domain adaptation is a critical task in machine learning, where the goal is to transfer knowledge from a source domain to a target domain with different distributions.
In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised domain adaptation method called Adaptive and Progressive Feature Alignment (APFA).
APFA leverages both labeled and unlabeled data from the source and target domains to learn a domain-invariant feature representation.
Our method consists of two main components: adaptive feature alignment and progressive feature alignment.

The adaptive feature alignment module adaptively adjusts the alignment strength based on the similarity between the source and target domains, allowing for more effective alignment in challenging scenarios.
The progressive feature alignment module gradually aligns the feature representations from the source and target domains, starting from a coarse alignment and refining it iteratively.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that APFA achieves superior performance in terms of classification accuracy and outperforms existing methods in challenging domain adaptation scenarios.
Overall, our proposed method provides a promising approach for semi-supervised domain adaptation by effectively aligning feature representations between different domains.
nnDetection is a self-configuring method for medical object detection that aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis.
The proposed method utilizes a neural network architecture that automatically adjusts its configuration based on the characteristics of the input data.
This self-configuring capability allows nnDetection to adapt to different medical imaging modalities and achieve optimal performance without the need for manual parameter tuning.
Experimental results on various medical datasets demonstrate that nnDetection outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to enhance the effectiveness of medical image analysis and facilitate the development of computer-aided diagnosis systems.
This paper presents CFPNet-M, a light-weight encoder-decoder based network designed for real-time segmentation of multimodal biomedical images.
The proposed network architecture consists of an encoder module that extracts high-level features from the input images and a decoder module that generates pixel-wise segmentation maps.
The network is trained using a combination of cross-entropy loss and dice loss to optimize the segmentation performance.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that CFPNet-M achieves competitive segmentation accuracy while maintaining real-time processing speed.
The proposed network can be a valuable tool for various biomedical image analysis tasks, such as tumor segmentation and cell counting, where real-time processing is crucial.
This paper proposes a novel approach for efficient single-image segmentation using Gaussian dynamic convolution.
The traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used for segmentation tasks often suffer from high computational costs and memory requirements.
To address this issue, the authors introduce a dynamic convolutional layer that adaptively selects a subset of input feature maps based on their relevance to the current input image.
This is achieved by modeling the relevance as a Gaussian distribution and using it to weight the feature maps.

Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable segmentation performance to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing computational costs and memory requirements.
Overall, this work presents a promising approach for efficient single-image segmentation using Gaussian dynamic convolution.
This paper presents GeoSim, a novel approach for generating realistic video simulations for self-driving applications.
The proposed method leverages geometry-aware composition techniques to generate high-quality video sequences that accurately represent real-world driving scenarios.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of GeoSim through extensive experiments and comparisons with existing simulation methods.
The results show that GeoSim outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of visual fidelity and realism, making it a promising tool for training and testing self-driving algorithms.
This paper presents a novel falling-ball algorithm for image segmentation.
The algorithm utilizes the concept of a falling ball to segment images into different regions based on their intensity values.
The proposed algorithm is compared with existing segmentation algorithms and is found to outperform them in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The algorithm is also tested on various types of images and shows robustness and adaptability.
Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed falling-ball algorithm for image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using geodesic paths and implicit region-based homogeneity enhancement.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by incorporating both local and global information.
The geodesic paths are computed based on the gradient of the image, and the homogeneity enhancement is achieved by iteratively updating the region boundaries.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and efficient image segmentation.
This paper presents a computer vision approach for analyzing liquid samples in hospitals and medical labs.
The proposed method utilizes hierarchical image segmentation and relations prediction techniques to accurately identify and classify different components within the liquid samples.

The hierarchical segmentation algorithm is able to partition the image into multiple regions based on their visual characteristics, while the relations prediction model predicts the spatial relationships between these regions.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately analyzing liquid samples, which can greatly benefit the medical field in terms of efficiency and accuracy.
Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable annotations for training deep learning models is a challenging and time-consuming task.
In this paper, we propose a multi-label deep supervision framework for medical image segmentation that leverages the information from both pixel-level and image-level annotations.
Specifically, we introduce a novel loss function that combines the pixel-wise cross-entropy loss with the image-level binary cross-entropy loss.
This allows us to effectively utilize the limited pixel-level annotations while also benefiting from the abundant image-level annotations.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components in our framework.
Our results suggest that every annotation, whether pixel-level or image-level, contributes to the overall performance of the segmentation model.

Overall, our work highlights the importance of leveraging multi-level annotations for medical image segmentation and provides a practical solution for improving the accuracy and efficiency of deep learning models in this domain.
This paper presents a method for quantizing deep neural networks (DNNs) to improve their accuracy in edge computing scenarios.
Edge computing refers to the deployment of computational resources closer to the data source, reducing latency and bandwidth requirements.
However, the limited computational resources at the edge often result in reduced accuracy of DNNs.
The proposed method utilizes quantization, a technique that reduces the precision of network parameters and activations, to reduce the computational and memory requirements of DNNs.
The authors demonstrate that by carefully selecting the quantization levels and applying a fine-tuning process, the accuracy of quantized DNNs can be significantly improved.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets show that the proposed method achieves comparable or even better accuracy than full-precision DNNs while reducing the memory footprint and computational requirements, making it suitable for edge computing applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for interpretability-driven sample selection using self-supervised learning for disease classification and segmentation.
The goal is to improve the interpretability of deep learning models by selecting representative samples that can provide insights into the decision-making process.

The proposed method utilizes self-supervised learning to learn meaningful representations from unlabeled data, which are then used to select informative samples for training the disease classification and segmentation models.

Experimental results on a medical imaging dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving interpretability while maintaining high classification and segmentation performance.
The findings suggest that interpretability-driven sample selection using self-supervised learning can be a valuable tool in medical image analysis tasks.
Domain adaptation is a crucial task in computer vision, particularly in image segmentation, where models trained on one domain often fail to generalize well to other domains.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called constrained domain adaptation for image segmentation.
Our method leverages both labeled source domain data and unlabeled target domain data to learn a domain-invariant feature representation.
We introduce a constraint that enforces the similarity between the source and target domain feature distributions, while also preserving the discriminative information for segmentation.
We formulate the problem as a constrained optimization task and propose an efficient algorithm to solve it.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods for image segmentation.
Our method shows promise for improving the generalization performance of image segmentation models across different domains.
Domain adaptation is a crucial task in computer vision, particularly in image segmentation, where models trained on one domain often fail to generalize well to other domains.
Existing domain adaptation methods typically rely on source domain data during adaptation, which can limit their effectiveness when the source domain data is scarce or unavailable.
In this paper, we propose a novel source-relaxed domain adaptation approach for image segmentation.
Our method leverages the target domain data and a small amount of labeled source domain data to learn a domain-invariant feature representation.
We introduce a source relaxation module that encourages the model to focus on the target domain while still utilizing the available source domain data.

Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness across different domains.

Our source-relaxed domain adaptation method shows promise for improving the generalization capabilities of image segmentation models in real-world scenarios where source domain data may be limited or unavailable.
MeanShift++ is a novel algorithm for mode-seeking that improves upon the original MeanShift algorithm by significantly reducing its computational complexity.
The algorithm achieves this by using a hierarchical clustering approach to efficiently identify the modes in a dataset.
The MeanShift++ algorithm is particularly well-suited for applications such as image segmentation and object tracking, where the identification of modes is a critical step.
Experimental results demonstrate that MeanShift++ outperforms existing mode-seeking algorithms in terms of both speed and accuracy, making it a valuable tool for various computer vision tasks.
This paper presents a strong pipeline for referring image segmentation, which involves locating the referred object in an image and then segmenting it.
The proposed pipeline consists of two stages: a localization stage and a segmentation stage.
In the localization stage, a region proposal network is used to generate potential object locations.
These locations are then refined using a bounding box regression network.
In the segmentation stage, a fully convolutional network is employed to segment the object within the refined bounding box.
The pipeline is trained end-to-end using a combination of supervised and weakly supervised learning.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed pipeline achieves state-of-the-art performance in referring image segmentation.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurate and efficient models.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Densely Connected Neural Architecture Search (DCNAS) for semantic image segmentation.
DCNAS combines the advantages of neural architecture search (NAS) and dense connectivity to automatically discover high-performing architectures for this task.
We introduce a search space specifically designed for semantic image segmentation and use reinforcement learning to search for the optimal architecture.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DCNAS achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in DCNAS.
Overall, our work provides a promising solution for automatic architecture search in semantic image segmentation.
This paper proposes a novel approach for learning versatile neural architectures by propagating network codes.
The authors introduce a new type of neural network layer called the network code layer, which is designed to capture and propagate useful information across different layers of the network.
The network code layer is trained using a novel learning algorithm that combines gradient-based optimization with a genetic algorithm.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on several benchmark datasets, showing that their method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both accuracy and generalization.
Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for learning versatile neural architectures that can adapt to different tasks and datasets.
Few-shot medical image segmentation is a challenging task due to the limited availability of annotated data.
In this paper, we propose a novel location-sensitive local prototype network (LSLPN) for few-shot medical image segmentation.
The LSLPN leverages the spatial information of the input image to generate local prototypes that capture the characteristics of different anatomical structures.
These local prototypes are then used to guide the segmentation process.
We evaluate the proposed method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the LSLPN outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.
Our findings suggest that incorporating location-sensitive information can significantly improve the performance of few-shot medical image segmentation models.
This paper presents a novel method for unsupervised adaptation of point-clouds and entropy minimization for multi-modal cardiac image segmentation.
The proposed method, called Adapt Everywhere, aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of cardiac image segmentation by adapting the segmentation model to different imaging modalities.
The method leverages unsupervised adaptation techniques to learn domain-invariant features from the source domain and applies entropy minimization to reduce the uncertainty in the target domain.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that Adapt Everywhere outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization across different imaging modalities.
The proposed method has the potential to enhance the clinical utility of cardiac image segmentation in various medical applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised image segmentation using deep superpixel cut.
The proposed method combines the advantages of deep learning and superpixel-based segmentation to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The deep superpixel cut algorithm first generates superpixels using the SLIC algorithm and then applies a deep neural network to learn the appearance and boundary cues of the superpixels.
The learned cues are then used to guide the graph cut algorithm for final segmentation.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed method has potential applications in various computer vision tasks such as object recognition and scene understanding.
The Weakly-Labeled Rand Index (WLRI) is a novel measure for evaluating the quality of weakly-labeled data in machine learning tasks.
Unlike traditional measures such as the Rand Index, which require fully-labeled ground truth data, the WLRI can handle weakly-labeled data where only partial or noisy labels are available.
The WLRI takes into account the uncertainty and noise in the weak labels, and provides a more accurate assessment of the agreement between weak labels and ground truth.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the WLRI in evaluating weakly-labeled data and its superiority over existing measures.
The WLRI can be a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners working with weakly-labeled data in various domains.
This paper proposes a novel approach for detecting embryo eggs using K-means segmentation based on the Lab color space.
The Lab color space is known for its ability to separate color information from luminance information, making it suitable for image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method first converts the input image to the Lab color space and then applies K-means clustering to segment the image into different regions.
The algorithm is evaluated on a dataset of embryo egg images and compared with other segmentation methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and better segmentation results compared to the other methods.
This approach has potential applications in the field of embryo egg detection and can contribute to advancements in reproductive biology and animal breeding.
This paper proposes a novel approach to predict urban expansion using a combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks.
The proposed approach aims to overcome the limitations of existing methods by leveraging the spatial and temporal characteristics of urban expansion.
The CNN-LSTM model is trained on a large dataset of satellite images and urban expansion data, allowing it to learn the complex relationships between land cover changes and urban growth patterns.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high prediction accuracy and outperforming existing methods.
The findings of this study have significant implications for urban planning and management, providing valuable insights into future urban growth patterns and supporting informed decision-making.
One-shot image semantic segmentation is a challenging task that requires learning from a single annotated image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Semantically Meaningful Class Prototype Learning (SMCPL) for one-shot image semantic segmentation.
Our approach leverages the semantic information of class prototypes to guide the segmentation process.
Specifically, we first generate class prototypes by aggregating feature representations from multiple images of the same class.
Then, we learn a mapping function that maps the input image to the class prototypes.
Finally, we use the mapped prototypes to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in one-shot image semantic segmentation.
Image Compositing for Segmentation of Surgical Tools without Manual Annotations

Abstract:

Segmentation of surgical tools in medical images is a crucial step in computer-assisted surgery and robotic surgery systems.
However, manual annotation of surgical tools is time-consuming and requires expert knowledge.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for segmenting surgical tools without the need for manual annotations.
Our method utilizes image compositing techniques to generate synthetic images of surgical tools with known ground truth segmentations.
These synthetic images are then used to train a deep learning model for surgical tool segmentation.
Experimental results on a dataset of laparoscopic images demonstrate that our approach achieves comparable performance to traditional methods that rely on manual annotations.
Moreover, our method significantly reduces the time and effort required for tool segmentation, making it a promising solution for real-time surgical applications.
This paper presents MudrockNet, a deep learning-based approach for semantic segmentation of mudrock scanning electron microscope (SEM) images.
Mudrocks are fine-grained sedimentary rocks that play a crucial role in various geological processes.
Accurate segmentation of mudrock SEM images is essential for understanding their composition and properties.
However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and subjective.
To address this challenge, we propose MudrockNet, a convolutional neural network architecture specifically designed for mudrock image segmentation.
We train MudrockNet on a large dataset of annotated mudrock SEM images and evaluate its performance on a separate test set.
Our results demonstrate that MudrockNet achieves high accuracy and outperforms existing methods for mudrock image segmentation.
The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of mudrock analysis in various geological applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for semi-supervised semantic segmentation using mask-based data augmentation.
The authors introduce a method that generates realistic masks for unlabeled images, which are then used to augment the labeled dataset.
The proposed approach leverages the power of deep learning models to generate accurate masks, and demonstrates improved performance compared to existing methods.
The authors evaluate the effectiveness of their approach on several benchmark datasets and show significant improvements in segmentation accuracy.
Overall, this paper presents a promising technique for semi-supervised semantic segmentation that can enhance the performance of existing models.
This paper presents a novel approach to finger vein recognition using a code generation technique.
Finger vein recognition is a biometric authentication method that has gained attention due to its high accuracy and non-invasiveness.
However, existing methods often suffer from high computational complexity and limited recognition performance.
In this paper, we propose a code generation technique that generates a unique code for each finger vein image.
This code is then used for recognition purposes.
Experimental results on a publicly available finger vein database demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving high recognition rates and low computational complexity.
The proposed method shows promise for practical applications in biometric authentication systems.
This paper proposes a map-guided curriculum domain adaptation approach for semantic nighttime image segmentation.
The authors introduce a novel uncertainty-aware evaluation metric to assess the performance of the segmentation model.
The proposed method utilizes a map-guided curriculum learning strategy to gradually adapt the model to nighttime scenes.
The uncertainty-aware evaluation metric takes into account the uncertainty of the model predictions, providing a more accurate assessment of the segmentation performance.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the segmentation accuracy for nighttime images.
The map-guided curriculum domain adaptation and uncertainty-aware evaluation contribute to the advancement of semantic nighttime image segmentation techniques.
RatLesNetv2 is a fully convolutional network designed for the segmentation of brain lesions in rodent models.
The network architecture is based on the U-Net model and incorporates dilated convolutions and residual connections to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The network was trained and evaluated on a large dataset of rodent brain MRI scans with manually annotated lesion masks.
The results demonstrate that RatLesNetv2 outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed network has the potential to facilitate the study of brain lesions in rodent models and improve the understanding of neurological disorders.
Histopathology image segmentation is a critical task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of various diseases.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable segmentation results is challenging due to the limited availability of labeled data.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for histopathology image segmentation that leverages unlabeled data to improve the performance of semi-supervised learning.

Our method combines a deep convolutional neural network with a self-training framework, where the network is trained on a small set of labeled data and then iteratively refined using a larger set of unlabeled data.
We also introduce a novel loss function that encourages consistency between the predictions of the network on labeled and unlabeled data.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.

Our findings suggest that incorporating unlabeled data can significantly enhance the performance of histopathology image segmentation, and our proposed method provides a promising solution for this challenging task.
This paper presents a domain adaptation approach for semantic segmentation of aerial images.
Aerial images often suffer from domain shift due to differences in lighting conditions, sensor characteristics, and geographical locations.
This domain shift can significantly degrade the performance of semantic segmentation models trained on one domain and applied to another.
To address this issue, we propose a domain adaptation framework that leverages a combination of unsupervised domain adaptation techniques and domain-specific knowledge.
Our approach involves training a source domain model on labeled aerial images and then adapting it to a target domain using unlabeled target domain images.
We also incorporate domain-specific knowledge, such as aerial image characteristics and semantic segmentation priors, to improve the adaptation process.
Experimental results on benchmark aerial image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the performance of semantic segmentation models across different domains.
This paper proposes a novel method called Prior-Guided Local (PGL) self-supervised learning for 3D medical image segmentation.
The PGL method utilizes prior knowledge from annotated 2D images to guide the learning process of 3D segmentation models.
The proposed method consists of two stages: pre-training and fine-tuning.
In the pre-training stage, a 2D segmentation model is trained using a large dataset of annotated 2D images.
The learned 2D model is then used to generate pseudo-labels for a set of 3D images.
In the fine-tuning stage, a 3D segmentation model is trained using the pseudo-labeled 3D images.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the PGL method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods while requiring fewer annotated 3D images.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of 3D medical image segmentation tasks.
In medical imaging, accurate segmentation of organs and tumors is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining fully labeled datasets for training deep learning models is often challenging and time-consuming.
In this paper, we propose a novel framework called DoDNet that leverages multiple partially labeled datasets to learn to segment multi-organ and tumors.
Our approach combines a self-training strategy with a dual-objective learning scheme to effectively utilize the available labeled and unlabeled data.
We evaluate DoDNet on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Our results show that DoDNet achieves high segmentation accuracy while reducing the reliance on fully labeled datasets, making it a promising tool for medical image segmentation tasks.
Semi-supervised learning has shown promising results in medical imaging tasks where labeled data is scarce.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Random Layer Mixup (ROAM) for semi-supervised learning in medical imaging.
ROAM leverages the concept of mixup, which combines two labeled samples to create a new sample, by randomly selecting layers from a pre-trained deep neural network and mixing them.
This process generates new samples that are used to augment the labeled data, thereby improving the performance of the model.
We evaluate ROAM on two medical imaging datasets and compare it with other state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that ROAM achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy and robustness, highlighting its potential for improving semi-supervised learning in medical imaging.
This paper presents a novel approach for interpreting and estimating disease features from medical images using deep learning techniques.
The proposed method combines the interpretability of deep learning models with the statistical estimation capabilities to provide accurate and explainable segmentation results.
The authors introduce a synergistic framework that leverages the strengths of both techniques to improve the overall performance of disease feature segmentation.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately identifying and explaining disease features in medical images.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of medical imaging and can potentially enhance the diagnosis and treatment of various diseases.
Segmentation of medical images is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, as it provides valuable information for diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, the accuracy of segmentation algorithms is often evaluated using ground truth annotations, which are prone to human error.
In this paper, we propose a method to disentangle human error from the ground truth in segmentation of medical images.
We introduce a novel framework that combines multiple expert annotations and leverages inter-observer variability to estimate the true underlying segmentation.
Our method is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and compared to traditional ground truth annotations.
The results demonstrate that our approach effectively reduces the impact of human error on segmentation accuracy, providing a more reliable evaluation metric for segmentation algorithms.
This work has important implications for the development and evaluation of medical image segmentation algorithms, ultimately improving the quality of medical imaging analysis.
This paper presents a novel evaluation criterion for ultra-high resolution cell membrane segmentation based on human perception.
The criterion takes into account the perceptual quality of the segmentation results by considering both the accuracy and the visual appearance of the segmented cell membranes.
The proposed criterion is validated using a dataset of ultra-high resolution microscopy images and compared with existing evaluation metrics.

The results show that the proposed criterion provides a more accurate and reliable assessment of the segmentation quality, making it a valuable tool for evaluating and comparing different segmentation algorithms in the field of cell biology.
This paper proposes a self-supervised approach for training few-shot medical image segmentation models without the need for manual annotation.
The method leverages superpixels to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled images, which are then used to train a segmentation model.
The proposed approach is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and compared to state-of-the-art methods.

The results show that the self-supervised approach achieves competitive performance, demonstrating its potential for training segmentation models in scenarios where manual annotation is scarce or expensive.
This paper presents a novel approach for referring image segmentation using cross-modal progressive comprehension.
The proposed method leverages the power of both textual and visual information to accurately segment objects in images based on natural language descriptions.
The approach consists of two stages: a comprehension stage and a segmentation stage.
In the comprehension stage, a cross-modal transformer model is used to encode the textual and visual information and generate a comprehensive representation.
This representation is then used in the segmentation stage, where a segmentation network is trained to predict the object masks based on the comprehensive representation.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in referring image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method has potential applications in various domains, such as image understanding, object recognition, and scene understanding.

This paper investigates the vulnerability of semantic image segmentation models to membership inference attacks, where an adversary aims to determine whether a specific image was used during the training of the model.
The authors propose a novel attack method called Segmentations-Leak, which leverages the inherent leakage of segmentation maps to infer membership.
They demonstrate the effectiveness of this attack on various state-of-the-art segmentation models and evaluate the impact of different factors such as model architecture and dataset size.
Additionally, the authors propose two defense mechanisms, including a privacy-preserving training approach and a post-processing technique, to mitigate the risk of membership inference attacks.

Experimental results show that these defenses can effectively reduce the success rate of the Segmentations-Leak attack, highlighting the importance of considering privacy concerns in semantic image segmentation models.
This paper introduces the concept of finite group equivariant neural networks (FG-ENNs) and explores their application in game playing.
FG-ENNs are a type of neural network architecture that can capture and exploit symmetries present in the input data.
The authors demonstrate how FG-ENNs can be used to improve the performance of game playing agents by leveraging the symmetries inherent in game states.
They present experimental results on several popular board games, showing that FG-ENNs outperform traditional neural networks in terms of both learning speed and final performance.
The paper concludes by discussing potential future directions for research in this area.
This paper presents a deep neural network approach for 3D surface segmentation based on contour tree hierarchy.
The proposed method utilizes a hierarchical structure to represent the contour tree of a 3D surface, which captures the topological relationships between different regions.
A deep neural network is then trained to learn the hierarchical features and perform segmentation based on the contour tree hierarchy.
Experimental results on various 3D surface datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing approaches.

The proposed deep neural network for 3D surface segmentation based on contour tree hierarchy has the potential to be applied in various applications such as medical imaging, computer graphics, and robotics.
This paper presents a novel approach for universal semantic segmentation of fisheye urban driving images.
Fisheye cameras are commonly used in autonomous vehicles to provide a wide field of view.
However, the distorted nature of fisheye images poses challenges for semantic segmentation algorithms.
The proposed method leverages a deep convolutional neural network architecture and a novel loss function to accurately segment objects in fisheye images.
The approach is evaluated on a large-scale dataset of fisheye urban driving images and achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for universal semantic segmentation in fisheye urban driving scenarios.
This paper proposes a novel approach for nuclear segmentation in digital pathology images using sparse coding driven deep decision tree ensembles.
The proposed method combines the advantages of sparse coding and deep decision tree ensembles to achieve accurate and efficient nuclear segmentation.
The sparse coding technique is used to learn a set of discriminative features from the input images, which are then fed into a deep decision tree ensemble for classification.

Experimental results on a large dataset of digital pathology images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the performance of nuclear segmentation in digital pathology, which is a critical task in cancer diagnosis and treatment.
This paper proposes a novel approach for domain adaptation in the context of scribble-based image segmentation.
Domain adaptation is a challenging task in computer vision, as it involves transferring knowledge from a source domain to a target domain with different characteristics.
In this work, we focus on the problem of adapting a scribble-based segmentation model trained on a source domain to a target domain.
We propose a co-segmentation framework that leverages the scribble annotations from both the source and target domains to improve the segmentation performance on the target domain.

Our approach consists of two main steps: (1) co-segmentation of the source and target images to generate pseudo-labels for the target domain, and (2) fine-tuning the segmentation model using the pseudo-labels.
We evaluate our method on two benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the segmentation performance on the target domain.
Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results and outperforms existing domain adaptation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of domain adaptation in scribble-based image segmentation and provides a promising direction for future research in this area.
This paper presents a novel approach for large scale image segmentation using deep learning techniques for connectome reconstruction.
The proposed method utilizes a structured loss function to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on a large dataset, achieving state-of-the-art results in connectome reconstruction.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of neuroscience and pave the way for more accurate and efficient connectome analysis.
This paper presents a deep learning approach for globally optimal segmentation of mutually interacting surfaces.
The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the relationship between neighboring surfaces and their interactions.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of labeled surface interactions to learn the optimal segmentation.
The trained model is then used to segment new input data into mutually interacting surfaces.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed method has potential applications in various fields such as computer vision, robotics, and medical imaging.
This paper proposes a novel approach called Naive-Student for urban scene segmentation in video sequences using semi-supervised learning.

The proposed method leverages the knowledge learned from a teacher network trained on a large labeled dataset and transfers it to a student network trained on a smaller labeled dataset combined with a larger unlabeled dataset.
The student network is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised losses to effectively utilize the unlabeled data.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the Naive-Student approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization to unseen data.
The proposed method shows promise for improving urban scene segmentation in video sequences using semi-supervised learning.
This paper presents a novel unsupervised image segmentation method based on autoregressive modeling.
The proposed method utilizes an autoregressive model to capture the spatial dependencies within an image and generate pixel-wise predictions.
The autoregressive model is trained using a self-supervised learning approach, where the model is trained to predict the value of each pixel based on its neighboring pixels.
The predicted values are then used to segment the image into different regions.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods.
Furthermore, the proposed method is computationally efficient and can be easily applied to large-scale images.
Overall, this paper provides a promising approach for unsupervised image segmentation using autoregressive modeling.
This paper investigates the problem of uncertainty estimation in active learning for image segmentation.
Active learning is a popular approach for reducing the annotation effort required in training deep learning models.
However, accurately estimating uncertainty is crucial for effective active learning.
The authors propose a novel method that combines a deep learning model with a Bayesian framework to estimate uncertainty in image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with existing uncertainty estimation techniques.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in uncertainty estimation, leading to improved active learning performance for image segmentation.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of more efficient and accurate active learning strategies in the field of image segmentation.
This paper presents a method for suggestive annotation of brain tumour images using gradient-guided sampling.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of brain tumour image annotation by leveraging the gradient information of the images.
The method first computes the gradient magnitude and direction of the images, and then uses a sampling algorithm to select representative pixels based on the gradient information.
These representative pixels are then used to generate suggestive annotations for the brain tumour images.

Experimental results on a dataset of brain tumour images demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher annotation accuracy compared to existing methods, while also reducing the annotation time.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of more efficient and accurate annotation techniques for brain tumour images.
This paper proposes a novel uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation and domain adaptation.
The framework leverages multiple views of the same image to improve segmentation accuracy and generalization across different domains.
It incorporates uncertainty estimation into the co-training process to guide the selection of informative samples for labeling.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and domain adaptation.
The framework has the potential to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation models and facilitate their deployment in real-world applications.
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various visual recognition tasks.
However, the traditional convolutional operation used in CNNs has limitations in capturing multi-scale information and handling objects with different sizes.

In this paper, we propose a new convolutional operation called Pyramidal Convolution, which addresses these limitations by incorporating multiple convolutional filters with different receptive field sizes.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of Pyramidal Convolution on several benchmark datasets, including ImageNet and COCO, and show that it outperforms traditional convolutional operations in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we analyze the properties of Pyramidal Convolution and provide insights into its working mechanism.
Overall, our work presents a novel approach to rethinking convolutional neural networks for visual recognition tasks.
This paper presents a method for multi-organ segmentation using partially labeled datasets and multi-scale feature abstraction.
The proposed method leverages the information from both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The authors introduce a novel multi-scale feature abstraction module that captures multi-scale contextual information and enhances the feature representation.
