They also propose a self-training strategy to iteratively refine the segmentation results using the unlabeled data.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the performance of multi-organ segmentation in medical imaging applications.
Transfer learning has shown promising results in various computer vision tasks, including medical image segmentation.
This paper presents a critical assessment of transfer learning for medical image segmentation using fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs).
The authors evaluate the performance of different pre-trained models, including VGG16, ResNet50, and DenseNet121, on three publicly available medical image datasets.
They compare the results with a baseline FCN model trained from scratch and analyze the impact of different transfer learning strategies, such as fine-tuning and feature extraction.
The experimental results demonstrate that transfer learning significantly improves the segmentation performance compared to training from scratch.
However, the choice of pre-trained model and transfer learning strategy has a significant impact on the final results.
The authors provide insights into the strengths and limitations of transfer learning for medical image segmentation and discuss potential avenues for future research.
This paper proposes a method to improve the calibration and out-of-distribution detection in medical image segmentation using convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

The authors highlight the importance of accurate and reliable segmentation in medical imaging applications and discuss the challenges associated with calibration and out-of-distribution detection in CNN-based segmentation models.
They introduce a novel calibration method that leverages the softmax output of the CNN to estimate the confidence of the segmentation predictions.
Additionally, they propose a method to detect out-of-distribution samples by comparing the softmax output of the CNN with a predefined threshold.
The proposed methods are evaluated on various medical image datasets and compared with existing calibration and out-of-distribution detection techniques.

The results demonstrate that the proposed methods significantly improve the calibration and out-of-distribution detection performance of CNN-based medical image segmentation models, thereby enhancing their reliability and applicability in clinical settings.
Clustering is a widely used technique in data analysis and pattern recognition.
Fuzzy clustering algorithms, such as the fuzzy C-means (FCM) algorithm, have been developed to handle data with uncertain or ambiguous membership.
However, evaluating the quality of fuzzy clustering results is a challenging task.
In this paper, we propose a new validity index for fuzzy-possibilistic C-means (FPCM) clustering, which combines the advantages of both fuzzy and possibilistic clustering.
The proposed index takes into account the compactness and separation of clusters, as well as the fuzziness and ambiguity of cluster membership.
Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed index compared to existing validity indices for fuzzy clustering.
This paper presents a novel approach to monitoring lake ice conditions using webcams and crowd-sourced images.
Traditional methods of lake ice monitoring rely on manual measurements or expensive remote sensing technologies.
In this study, we leverage the ubiquity of webcams and the increasing popularity of crowd-sourced image platforms to collect and analyze lake ice data.

We develop a computer vision algorithm to automatically detect and track ice coverage from webcam images, and we integrate this algorithm with a crowd-sourced image platform to gather a large dataset of lake ice images.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study of a lake in northern Canada, where we compare our webcam-based measurements with manual measurements and satellite data.
Our results show that our method provides accurate and timely lake ice information, with potential applications in climate research, winter tourism, and lake management.
Overall, this paper highlights the potential of webcams and crowd-sourced images as a cost-effective and scalable solution for lake ice monitoring.
This paper proposes a novel adversarial constrained-CNN loss (ACCL) for weakly supervised medical image segmentation.
The ACCL loss is designed to address the challenges of limited annotated data and the presence of noise in medical images.
The proposed method incorporates an adversarial learning framework to generate accurate segmentation masks by leveraging the information from both annotated and unannotated images.

Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that the ACCL loss outperforms existing weakly supervised segmentation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise.

The proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks, which can have significant implications for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper presents a novel approach called C2FNAS (Coarse-to-Fine Neural Architecture Search) for 3D medical image segmentation.
The proposed method aims to automate the process of designing neural network architectures for accurate and efficient segmentation of medical images.
The C2FNAS framework consists of two stages: a coarse search stage and a fine search stage.
In the coarse search stage, a set of candidate architectures is generated using a genetic algorithm.
These architectures are then evaluated on a small subset of the training data to select the top-performing ones.
In the fine search stage, the selected architectures are further refined using a reinforcement learning-based algorithm.
The final architecture is then trained on the full training dataset and evaluated on a separate test dataset.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that the proposed C2FNAS method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of medical image segmentation tasks, which can have important implications for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
This paper presents a task-agnostic adversarial attack method called Mimic and Fool.
The proposed method aims to generate adversarial examples that can fool multiple machine learning models across different tasks.
The approach leverages a generative model to mimic the decision boundaries of the target models and a reinforcement learning algorithm to optimize the attack strategy.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the Mimic and Fool method in generating adversarial examples that can successfully deceive various models on different tasks, including image classification and sentiment analysis.
The findings highlight the need for robust defenses against such task-agnostic attacks and provide insights into the vulnerabilities of machine learning models.
Conditional generative flow models have shown promising results in generating high-quality images and 3D point clouds.
However, existing methods often suffer from limitations such as limited expressiveness and difficulty in handling complex conditional distributions.
In this paper, we propose C-Flow, a novel conditional generative flow model that addresses these limitations.
C-Flow leverages the invertible architecture of flow models and introduces conditional coupling layers to model complex conditional distributions.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of C-Flow on various image and 3D point cloud datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of both visual quality and quantitative metrics.
Additionally, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components in C-Flow and provide insights into its working mechanism.
Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of conditional generative flow models and opens up new possibilities for generating realistic images and 3D point clouds.
Land cover segmentation is a crucial task in remote sensing applications, as it provides valuable information for various environmental and urban planning studies.
However, the performance of land cover segmentation algorithms can be affected by differences in satellite sensors and acquisition conditions.
In this paper, we propose a domain adaptation approach to improve land cover segmentation across different satellites.
We first train a segmentation model on a source dataset from one satellite and then adapt it to a target dataset from a different satellite using domain adaptation techniques.
Specifically, we employ a domain adversarial neural network to align the feature distributions between the source and target domains.
Experimental results on two publicly available land cover datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach in improving land cover segmentation accuracy across different satellites.

Our approach provides a practical solution for leveraging existing labeled data from one satellite to improve land cover segmentation on another satellite, which can greatly benefit remote sensing applications.
In the field of medical image segmentation, one of the major challenges is the lack of labeled data for training deep learning models.
This paper proposes a novel approach called LT-Net, which aims to address this challenge by leveraging a small amount of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data.

The key idea behind LT-Net is to learn a reversible voxel-wise correspondence between the labeled and unlabeled data, which allows for the transfer of labels from the labeled data to the unlabeled data.
The proposed method is evaluated on several medical image segmentation tasks and achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of LT-Net in leveraging unlabeled data to improve the performance of one-shot medical image segmentation.
StructBoost is a boosting method that aims to predict structured output variables.
Boosting is a popular machine learning technique that combines weak learners to create a strong learner.
However, most boosting methods are designed for predicting scalar variables and are not suitable for structured output variables, such as sequences or trees.
StructBoost addresses this limitation by introducing a novel framework that can handle structured output variables.
The proposed method leverages the concept of structured loss functions and uses a structured version of AdaBoost to iteratively train weak learners.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of StructBoost in predicting structured output variables, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Overall, StructBoost provides a valuable contribution to the field of machine learning by extending the applicability of boosting methods to structured output prediction tasks.
This paper proposes a novel approach for segmenting ultra-resolution medical images using a Meta Segmentation Network (MSN).
The MSN leverages the power of deep learning and meta-learning techniques to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The network is trained on a large dataset of ultra-resolution medical images and learns to adapt its segmentation strategy based on the specific characteristics of each image.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MSN outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The MSN also exhibits robustness to noise and artifacts commonly present in ultra-resolution medical images.
Overall, this paper presents a promising solution for segmenting ultra-resolution medical images, which can have significant implications for various medical applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using reinforced active learning.
The traditional active learning framework is extended by incorporating reinforcement learning techniques to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the segmentation process.
The proposed method utilizes a deep neural network to perform the initial segmentation and then selects the most informative samples for annotation using a reinforcement learning agent.
The agent is trained to maximize the expected reward, which is defined as the improvement in segmentation performance.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing active learning approaches in terms of both segmentation accuracy and annotation efficiency.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of image segmentation and can potentially be applied to other computer vision tasks as well.
This paper proposes a new clustering algorithm based on the point-set kernel.
The point-set kernel is a measure of similarity between two sets of points, which takes into account both the spatial distribution and the individual characteristics of the points.
The proposed algorithm first computes the point-set kernel matrix for the input data, and then applies a clustering algorithm to this matrix to obtain the final clustering result.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing clustering methods.
The point-set kernel based clustering algorithm has the potential to be applied in various domains, such as image analysis, bioinformatics, and social network analysis.
This paper presents a novel approach for efficient 2D neuron boundary segmentation using local topological constraints.
The proposed method leverages the inherent topological structure of neurons to improve the accuracy and efficiency of boundary segmentation.
The approach combines local intensity information with local topological constraints to accurately identify neuron boundaries.
Experimental results on a dataset of neuron images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The findings of this study have implications for the field of neuroscience and can contribute to the development of more efficient and accurate neuron boundary segmentation techniques.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, the accuracy and reliability of segmentation results can be affected by observer variation, which is the inconsistency in annotations made by different experts.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines deep learning and surrogate-assisted genetic algorithms to address this issue.
The deep learning model is trained on a large dataset of annotated medical images to learn the segmentation task.
The genetic algorithm is then used to optimize the segmentation results by iteratively refining the deep learning model.
To account for observer variation, we introduce a surrogate model that estimates the uncertainty of the segmentation results based on the annotations made by different experts.
This uncertainty is then used to guide the genetic algorithm in selecting the most reliable segmentation results.
Experimental results on a dataset of brain MRI images demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to observer variation.
This paper presents a novel approach for unpaired multi-modal segmentation using knowledge distillation.
The proposed method leverages the knowledge learned from a teacher network trained on paired multi-modal data to guide the training of a student network on unpaired multi-modal data.
The teacher network is used to generate pseudo-labels for the unpaired data, which are then used to train the student network.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods for unpaired multi-modal segmentation.
The approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of multi-modal segmentation tasks in medical imaging and other domains.
This paper proposes a method for generalizing deep models for overhead image segmentation using Getis-Ord Gi* pooling.
Overhead images provide a unique perspective for segmentation tasks, but existing deep models struggle to generalize well across different datasets.
The authors introduce a novel pooling method that captures spatial relationships in overhead images and improves generalization.
They evaluate their approach on multiple datasets and demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The results suggest that incorporating Getis-Ord Gi* pooling into deep models can significantly enhance their ability to segment overhead images.
Color constancy is an important aspect of computer vision, as it allows for accurate perception of object colors under varying lighting conditions.
Deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown remarkable performance in various computer vision tasks, but their susceptibility to color constancy errors remains a challenge.
This paper investigates the impact of color constancy errors on DNN performance and proposes a novel approach to address this issue.
The proposed method leverages a color constancy algorithm to preprocess input images before feeding them into the DNN.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves DNN performance, reducing the impact of color constancy errors.
The findings of this study highlight the importance of considering color constancy in DNN-based computer vision systems and provide a practical solution to mitigate its negative effects.
This paper presents a novel multi-sensor 3D object detection framework called PI-RCNN, which incorporates a point-based attentive cont-conv fusion module.
The proposed framework aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of 3D object detection by effectively fusing information from multiple sensors.

The point-based attentive cont-conv fusion module utilizes attention mechanisms to selectively aggregate features from different sensors, while the cont-conv fusion module integrates contextual information to enhance the discriminative power of the features.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed PI-RCNN framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed framework has the potential to contribute to various applications such as autonomous driving and robotics.
This paper proposes a novel approach for efficient 3D medical image segmentation using thickened 2D networks.
Traditional methods for 3D segmentation often suffer from high computational costs and memory requirements.
In this work, we introduce a thickened 2D network architecture that leverages the advantages of both 2D and 3D networks.
By thickening the 2D network with additional convolutional layers, we are able to capture more contextual information while maintaining computational efficiency.
We evaluate our approach on a dataset of 3D medical images and compare it to state-of-the-art 3D segmentation methods.
Our results demonstrate that the thickened 2D network achieves comparable segmentation accuracy with significantly reduced computational costs and memory requirements.
This approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and scalability of 3D medical image segmentation, making it more accessible for clinical applications.
Automatic image co-segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to simultaneously segment common objects from a set of images.
This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the state-of-the-art techniques and algorithms for automatic image co-segmentation.
The survey covers various aspects of co-segmentation, including different approaches, datasets, evaluation metrics, and applications.
The paper also discusses the strengths and limitations of existing methods and identifies potential directions for future research in this field.
Overall, this survey provides a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in automatic image co-segmentation.
Accurate segmentation of 3D medical images is crucial for various clinical applications.
However, existing segmentation methods often suffer from limitations such as high computational complexity and lack of generalizability.
In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning-based system called "One Network to Segment Them All" (ONETSTA) that addresses these challenges.
ONETSTA is a lightweight and generalizable system that achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple medical image segmentation tasks.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of ONETSTA on a diverse set of 3D medical image datasets, including brain MRI, lung CT, and cardiac MRI.
Our experimental results show that ONETSTA outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and generalizability.
Overall, ONETSTA provides a promising solution for accurate 3D medical image segmentation in a wide range of clinical applications.
Domain generalization is a challenging problem in machine learning, where a model trained on one domain fails to generalize well to other unseen domains.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Model-Agnostic Learning of Semantic Features (MALSF) for domain generalization.
MALSF leverages semantic features, which capture the underlying semantics of the data, to improve generalization across domains.
We introduce a model-agnostic learning framework that learns semantic features from multiple source domains and uses them to train a target domain model.
Our experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that MALSF outperforms state-of-the-art domain generalization methods, achieving significant improvements in generalization performance.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in MALSF and provide insights into its working mechanism.
Overall, our work contributes to the field of domain generalization by introducing a novel approach that effectively leverages semantic features for improved generalization across domains.
This paper proposes a novel approach for remote sensed image segmentation using an encoder-decoder based convolutional neural network (CNN) and fully connected conditional random fields (CRFs).

The encoder-decoder CNN is designed to capture both local and global contextual information, while the fully connected CRFs are used to refine the segmentation results by considering the spatial dependencies between pixels.
Experimental results on several remote sensed datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed approach has the potential to contribute to various applications in remote sensing, such as land cover classification and object detection.
This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using end-to-end deep convolutional active contours.
Traditional active contour models rely on handcrafted features and require manual initialization, which can be time-consuming and prone to errors.
In contrast, the proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to learn discriminative features directly from the input image.
The network is trained in an end-to-end manner, allowing it to automatically initialize and refine the active contour.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve image segmentation tasks in various domains, such as medical imaging and computer vision.
This paper investigates the issue of overfitting in neural networks when dealing with class imbalance in the context of image segmentation.
Class imbalance refers to the situation where one class is significantly underrepresented compared to others.
The authors analyze the impact of class imbalance on the performance of neural networks for segmentation tasks and propose several improvements to mitigate the overfitting problem.
The proposed improvements include data augmentation techniques, loss function modifications, and network architecture adjustments.
The effectiveness of these improvements is evaluated through experiments on various datasets.
The results demonstrate that the proposed techniques effectively reduce overfitting and improve the segmentation performance in the presence of class imbalance.
The findings of this study provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners working on image segmentation tasks with imbalanced classes.
This paper presents a novel approach to improve the segmentation of 3D cardiovascular magnetic resonance (MR) images using neural style transfer.
The segmentation of cardiovascular MR images is a challenging task due to the inconsistent data quality and variability in image appearance.
Traditional segmentation methods often struggle to accurately segment the complex structures in these images.
In this study, we propose a method that leverages the power of neural style transfer to improve the segmentation accuracy.
We train a deep neural network to learn the style of high-quality segmented images and transfer this style to the inconsistent data.
Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms traditional segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
This approach has the potential to significantly improve the clinical utility of cardiovascular MR image segmentation.
This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using a multi-threshold technique by histogram sampling.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional thresholding techniques by utilizing multiple thresholds and sampling the image histogram.
The algorithm first samples the image histogram to obtain an initial set of thresholds.
Then, it iteratively refines these thresholds by considering the local histogram characteristics.
Experimental results on various images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional thresholding techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method can be applied to a wide range of image segmentation tasks and has the potential to improve the performance of various computer vision applications.
This paper investigates the feasibility of training deep learning models for medical image segmentation using a single manually delineated scan.
The authors propose a novel approach called Extreme Augmentation, which leverages data augmentation techniques to generate a large number of synthetic training samples from the single annotated scan.
The performance of the trained models is evaluated on a dataset of medical images, and compared to models trained using traditional methods with a larger number of annotated scans.

The results show that the Extreme Augmentation approach achieves comparable performance to the traditional methods, suggesting that deep learning based medical image segmentation can be effectively trained using a single manually delineated scan.
This has significant implications for reducing the time and cost associated with annotating large datasets for training deep learning models in the medical domain.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
In this paper, we propose a novel mixed-supervised dual-network framework for medical image segmentation.
The framework combines the strengths of both supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to improve segmentation accuracy.
The supervised network is trained using labeled data, while the unsupervised network leverages unlabeled data to learn the underlying structure of the images.
The two networks are then combined to generate the final segmentation results.
Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed framework outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed framework has the potential to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation algorithms and improve clinical decision-making.
This paper presents a method for computing the spatial probability of inclusion inside partial contours for computer vision applications.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of geometric and statistical techniques to estimate the probability of a point being inside a partial contour.
The method is based on the assumption that the probability of inclusion is proportional to the length of the contour segment that contains the point.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in various computer vision tasks, such as object recognition and image segmentation.
The proposed method provides a valuable tool for improving the accuracy and reliability of computer vision algorithms that rely on partial contour information.
The paper presents a novel deep learning layer called Deep Differentiable Simplex Layer (DDSL) for learning geometric signals.
The DDSL is designed to handle geometric data, such as point clouds and meshes, and enables end-to-end learning of geometric tasks.
The layer is based on the simplex representation, which allows for efficient computation and differentiability.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of DDSL on various geometric tasks, including shape classification and segmentation, and show that it outperforms existing methods.
The proposed DDSL provides a promising approach for learning geometric signals in deep learning models.

SkrGAN: Sketching-rendering Unconditional Generative Adversarial Networks for Medical Image Synthesis

Abstract:
Medical image synthesis plays a crucial role in various applications, such as data augmentation, disease diagnosis, and surgical planning.
However, generating realistic medical images is challenging due to the limited availability of labeled data and the complexity of medical imaging modalities.
In this paper, we propose SkrGAN, a novel unconditional generative adversarial network (GAN) framework for medical image synthesis.
SkrGAN combines the advantages of sketching and rendering techniques to generate high-quality medical images from random noise.
The sketching module generates a rough outline of the desired medical image, while the rendering module refines the sketch by adding detailed textures and structures.
We train SkrGAN on a large dataset of labeled medical images and evaluate its performance on various medical imaging tasks, including MRI, CT, and ultrasound image synthesis.
Our experimental results demonstrate that SkrGAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of image quality, diversity, and realism.
Moreover, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the contributions of different components in SkrGAN and provide insights into its working mechanism.
Overall, SkrGAN shows great potential for medical image synthesis and can be a valuable tool for medical professionals in their daily practice.
Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining large amounts of annotated medical images for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a multi-task attention-based semi-supervised learning framework for medical image segmentation.
Our approach leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation performance.
Specifically, we introduce a multi-task learning strategy that jointly optimizes the segmentation task and an auxiliary task of predicting the presence of anatomical structures.
Additionally, we incorporate an attention mechanism to focus the model's attention on relevant regions of the image.

Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning approaches for medical image segmentation.
The proposed framework shows promise for improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, even with limited labeled data.
DeepAtlas is a novel approach for joint semi-supervised learning of image registration and segmentation.
The paper proposes a deep learning framework that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to simultaneously learn the tasks of image registration and segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a dual-branch network architecture, where one branch is responsible for image registration and the other for segmentation.
The two branches are trained jointly using a combination of supervised and unsupervised loss functions.
Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both registration accuracy and segmentation performance.
The paper also provides insights into the benefits of using unlabeled data for improving the performance of both tasks.
Overall, DeepAtlas presents a promising approach for joint learning of image registration and segmentation, with potential applications in medical imaging and other domains.
This paper presents a novel approach for brain segmentation from k-space using an end-to-end recurrent attention network.
The proposed method leverages the temporal information in the k-space data to improve the accuracy of the segmentation.
The recurrent attention network is designed to selectively focus on relevant regions in the k-space data, allowing for more accurate segmentation of the brain.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of brain segmentation in clinical applications.
Camera pose estimation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves determining the position and orientation of a camera in a 3D scene.
Traditional methods for camera pose estimation rely on feature matching and geometric constraints, which can be computationally expensive and sensitive to noise.
In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown promising results in various computer vision tasks, including camera pose estimation.
This paper provides an introduction to camera pose estimation with deep learning, discussing the challenges and advantages of using deep learning for this task.
We review the existing literature on deep learning-based camera pose estimation methods, including both supervised and unsupervised approaches.
We also discuss the datasets and evaluation metrics commonly used in this field.
Finally, we highlight some of the current limitations and future directions for research in camera pose estimation with deep learning.
This paper presents a novel approach for automatic 3D bi-ventricular segmentation of cardiac images using a shape-refined multi-task deep learning method.
The proposed method combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a shape refinement module to accurately segment the left and right ventricles in cardiac images.
The CNN is trained on a large dataset of annotated cardiac images to learn the spatial and contextual information necessary for accurate segmentation.
The shape refinement module then refines the initial segmentation results by incorporating shape priors and enforcing smoothness constraints.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment planning of cardiac diseases by providing accurate and reliable segmentation of the ventricles in cardiac images.
This paper presents a self-supervised learning approach for cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation by predicting the anatomical position of the heart.
The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial information in cardiac MR images to learn meaningful representations without the need for manual annotations.

The authors introduce a novel network architecture that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to predict the anatomical position of the heart from a given image patch.
The network is trained using a self-supervised learning framework, where the predicted anatomical position is used as a surrogate task to guide the learning of the segmentation task.

Experimental results on a large dataset of cardiac MR images demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in cardiac MR image segmentation, outperforming existing supervised and unsupervised methods.

The authors also provide a detailed analysis of the learned representations and show that the network learns to capture anatomical structures and spatial relationships between different cardiac regions.
Overall, this work presents a promising approach for cardiac MR image segmentation that can potentially improve the accuracy and efficiency of clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in this field, but they often suffer from overfitting due to the large number of parameters.
In this paper, we propose a regularized CNN architecture for semantic image segmentation.
Our approach incorporates a regularization term into the loss function to prevent overfitting and improve generalization.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art approaches.
The experimental results demonstrate that our regularized CNN achieves competitive performance while reducing overfitting.
Overall, our work contributes to the development of more robust and accurate models for semantic image segmentation.
This paper proposes a novel approach for cross-modality domain adaptation in medical image segmentation.

The proposed method, called Synergistic Image and Feature Adaptation (SIFA), aims to address the challenge of adapting segmentation models trained on one modality to another modality with limited labeled data.
SIFA leverages both image-level and feature-level adaptation techniques to effectively transfer knowledge from the source modality to the target modality.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving superior segmentation performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
The findings of this study highlight the potential of SIFA for improving the generalization and applicability of medical image segmentation models across different modalities.
This paper proposes a novel approach for blurry boundary delineation using semantic-guided encoder feature learning.
Blurry boundary delineation is a challenging task in computer vision, as it requires accurately identifying and segmenting object boundaries in images with low resolution or blurriness.
The proposed approach leverages the power of deep learning and semantic information to improve the accuracy of blurry boundary delineation.
Specifically, a semantic-guided encoder is trained to learn discriminative features that capture both low-level image details and high-level semantic information.
These features are then used to generate precise boundary maps for blurry images.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of boundary accuracy and robustness to blur.
The findings of this study have implications for various applications in computer vision, such as image segmentation and object recognition.
This paper presents a budget-aware approach for semi-supervised semantic and instance segmentation.
The proposed method aims to optimize the allocation of annotation budget by adaptively selecting the most informative samples for annotation.
The approach combines a budget-aware active learning strategy with a semi-supervised learning framework.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods while requiring fewer annotations.
The findings suggest that the budget-aware approach can effectively improve the efficiency and effectiveness of annotation in semantic and instance segmentation tasks.
This paper proposes a method for weakly supervised semantic segmentation using information extracted from image captions.
The authors leverage the fact that captions often describe the objects present in an image, and use this information to generate pseudo-labels for training a segmentation model.
They introduce a novel caption-based attention mechanism that focuses on relevant regions in the image, and use this attention to guide the segmentation process.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving competitive performance compared to fully supervised approaches.
The approach presented in this paper provides a promising direction for weakly supervised semantic segmentation using readily available caption data.
This paper presents a method for extracting 3D city models from historical image data using a technique called Nostalgin.
The proposed method utilizes deep learning algorithms to analyze historical images and extract relevant information such as building footprints and heights.
The extracted data is then used to generate accurate 3D models of the city at different time periods.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the Nostalgin method by applying it to a dataset of historical images from a specific city and comparing the generated 3D models with ground truth data.
The results show that the Nostalgin method is able to accurately reconstruct the city's 3D models from historical image data, providing a valuable tool for urban planning and historical preservation.
Skin cancer is a prevalent and potentially deadly disease that requires early detection for effective treatment.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for skin cancer segmentation and classification using a combination of NABLA-N and Inception Recurrent Residual Convolutional Networks (IRRCNs).
Our method leverages the strengths of both networks to accurately segment and classify skin cancer images.
We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of skin cancer images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation and classification accuracy.
Our findings suggest that the combination of NABLA-N and IRRCNs can be a promising approach for skin cancer diagnosis and treatment.
This paper presents a study on the application of super resolution convolutional neural network (SRCNN) models for enhancing the resolution of rock micro-CT images.
The authors propose and evaluate different SRCNN architectures for this task, comparing their performance in terms of image quality and computational efficiency.

The experiments are conducted on a dataset of rock micro-CT images, and the results show that the SRCNN models are able to significantly improve the resolution of these images, leading to enhanced details and better visualization of rock structures.
The findings of this study have implications for the field of rock characterization and can contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable analysis techniques for rock samples.
This paper proposes a novel approach for referring image segmentation using a cross-modal self-attention network.
Referring image segmentation is the task of segmenting objects in an image based on natural language expressions.
The proposed network leverages both visual and textual information to improve the accuracy of segmentation.
The network consists of a visual encoder, a textual encoder, and a cross-modal self-attention module.
The visual encoder extracts visual features from the input image, while the textual encoder encodes the referring expression.
The cross-modal self-attention module attends to both visual and textual features to capture their interactions.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed network provides a promising solution for referring image segmentation tasks in various applications such as image understanding and scene understanding.
The paper presents CLEVR-Ref+, a dataset designed to diagnose the visual reasoning capabilities of models using referring expressions.
Referring expressions are natural language instructions that refer to specific objects in an image.
The dataset extends the existing CLEVR dataset by including referring expressions that require complex reasoning and understanding of spatial relationships.
The authors evaluate several state-of-the-art models on CLEVR-Ref+ and find that they struggle with the challenging reasoning tasks.
They also propose a new model, Ref-Net, which achieves better performance on CLEVR-Ref+.
The dataset and evaluation results provide insights into the limitations of current visual reasoning models and highlight the need for further research in this area.
This paper explores the use of geometry in active learning for binary and multi-class image segmentation.
Active learning is a machine learning technique that aims to reduce the amount of labeled data required for training by selecting the most informative samples for annotation.
In image segmentation, the goal is to partition an image into meaningful regions.
The authors propose a novel active learning framework that incorporates geometric information to guide the selection of informative samples.
They demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on various datasets and compare it to existing active learning methods.

The results show that incorporating geometry improves the performance of active learning for image segmentation tasks, reducing the amount of labeled data required for training while maintaining high accuracy.
This research contributes to the field of active learning and provides insights into the role of geometry in improving the efficiency of image segmentation algorithms.
This paper presents a novel approach for classifying cardiac pathologies on cine MRI images using semi-supervised learning of apparent flow.
The proposed method leverages the motion characteristics of the heart to improve the interpretability and explainability of the classification results.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on a dataset of cardiac MRI images, achieving high accuracy and providing insights into the underlying pathology.
The results suggest that the proposed method has the potential to assist clinicians in diagnosing and understanding cardiac diseases.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning disentangled representations of satellite image time series.
The proposed method utilizes a variational autoencoder framework to learn a latent space representation that separates the underlying factors of variation in the data.
Specifically, the model is trained to disentangle the spatial and temporal components of the satellite images.
The spatial component captures the static features of the scene, while the temporal component captures the dynamic changes over time.
Experimental results on a large-scale satellite image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning disentangled representations.
The learned representations can be used for various downstream tasks, such as anomaly detection and change detection in satellite imagery.
This paper proposes a novel approach for multi-source domain adaptation under target shift using optimal transport.
The goal is to learn a target classifier that performs well on a target domain with a different distribution from the source domains.
The proposed method leverages the optimal transport theory to align the source and target domains by minimizing the discrepancy between their distributions.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to existing methods.
The findings suggest that optimal transport can be a powerful tool for addressing the challenges of multi-source domain adaptation under target shift.
This paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture called CE-Net for 2D medical image segmentation.
The CE-Net consists of an encoder-decoder structure with a context encoder module.
The context encoder module captures global contextual information by aggregating features from different scales.
The proposed CE-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on various medical image segmentation tasks, including liver and lung segmentation.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed CE-Net for 2D medical image segmentation.
FickleNet is a novel approach for weakly and semi-supervised semantic image segmentation that utilizes stochastic inference.
The proposed method leverages weak annotations and limited labeled data to improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation.
FickleNet incorporates a stochastic inference module that generates multiple segmentation masks for each image, allowing for uncertainty estimation and better handling of ambiguous regions.
The method is evaluated on benchmark datasets and achieves state-of-the-art results in weakly and semi-supervised semantic image segmentation tasks.
The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FickleNet in various scenarios, highlighting its potential for practical applications in computer vision.
This paper presents a novel approach to class-independent sequential full image segmentation using a convolutional neural network (CNN).
The proposed method focuses on finding a segment within an attention region, given a pointer pixel within this segment.
The CNN is trained to predict the location of the pointer pixel within the attention region, and then uses this information to segment the image.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The class-independent nature of the approach makes it applicable to a wide range of image segmentation tasks, without the need for class-specific training or prior knowledge.
Fast-SCNN is a fast and efficient semantic segmentation network designed for real-time applications.
The paper proposes a novel architecture that combines the advantages of both fully convolutional networks and spatial pyramid pooling.
The network achieves state-of-the-art performance on various benchmark datasets while maintaining a high inference speed.
The authors also introduce a lightweight module called the context aggregation module, which effectively captures contextual information while minimizing computational complexity.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed Fast-SCNN architecture, making it a promising solution for real-time semantic segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for learning to segment objects in images using only image-level supervision.
Traditional methods for image segmentation require pixel-level annotations, which are expensive and time-consuming to obtain.
In this work, we propose a framework that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn to segment objects using only image-level labels.
Our approach involves training a CNN to predict object presence in an image, and then using this information to generate pseudo pixel-level annotations.
These pseudo annotations are then used to fine-tune the CNN, resulting in improved segmentation performance.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods that rely on pixel-level annotations.
Our approach has the potential to significantly reduce the annotation effort required for training image segmentation models, making it more accessible and practical for a wide range of applications.
Automated quality control (QC) is crucial in image segmentation to ensure accurate and reliable results.
In this paper, we propose a novel automated QC framework for image segmentation, specifically applied to the UK Biobank Cardiac MR Imaging Study.
Our framework utilizes machine learning algorithms to detect and correct segmentation errors, improving the overall quality of the segmentation results.
We evaluate the performance of our framework on a large dataset of cardiac MR images and compare it to manual QC.
The results demonstrate that our automated QC framework achieves comparable or even better performance than manual QC, while significantly reducing the time and effort required.
This automated QC framework has the potential to greatly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of image segmentation in large-scale studies, such as the UK Biobank Cardiac MR Imaging Study.
This paper presents UltraCompression, a framework for high density compression of ultrasound volumes using physics modeling deep neural networks.
Ultrasound imaging is widely used in medical diagnostics, but the large size of ultrasound volumes poses challenges for storage and transmission.
Existing compression methods often result in loss of important diagnostic information.
The proposed framework leverages physics modeling to capture the underlying physical properties of ultrasound volumes and combines it with deep neural networks for efficient compression.

Experimental results demonstrate that UltraCompression achieves high compression ratios while preserving diagnostic information, making it a promising solution for high density compression of ultrasound volumes.
This paper presents a novel approach to optimal decision-making in mixed-agent partially observable stochastic environments using reinforcement learning.
The authors propose a framework that combines deep reinforcement learning with a multi-agent setting, where agents have limited observability of the environment.
The proposed method utilizes a centralized critic and decentralized actors to enable efficient learning and decision-making.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various benchmark problems, showing significant improvements in performance compared to existing methods.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of reinforcement learning by providing a solution for optimal decision-making in complex, mixed-agent environments with limited observability.
This paper investigates the plasticity of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) through the use of random pruning.
The authors propose a novel method for randomly pruning connections in a CNN and analyze the effects on the network's performance.
They conduct experiments on various benchmark datasets and compare the performance of pruned networks with their unpruned counterparts.
The results show that random pruning can lead to significant improvements in network performance, suggesting that CNNs have a high degree of plasticity and can adapt to changes in their connectivity.
The findings of this study have implications for the design and optimization of CNN architectures.
This paper presents a fast and accurate method for 3D medical image segmentation using a data-swapping approach.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning techniques and incorporates a novel data-swapping strategy to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The method is evaluated on a large dataset of medical images and compared with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior segmentation accuracy and significantly reduces the computational time compared to existing methods.
The findings of this study have important implications for improving the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation, which is crucial for various clinical applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for highly imbalanced medical image segmentation, specifically for the detection of multiple sclerosis (MS) lesions.
The authors introduce asymmetric loss functions and deep densely connected networks (DDCNs) to address the challenges posed by imbalanced datasets in medical image analysis.
The proposed method is evaluated on a large dataset of brain MRI scans from MS patients, achieving superior performance compared to existing methods.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the asymmetric loss functions and DDCNs in improving the accuracy and robustness of MS lesion detection, highlighting their potential for clinical applications in the diagnosis and monitoring of MS.
This paper presents a new ensemble learning framework for 3D biomedical image segmentation.
The proposed framework combines multiple base segmentation models to improve the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation results.
The ensemble learning framework consists of three main components: base segmentation models, diversity generation, and fusion.
The base segmentation models are trained independently using different algorithms or architectures.
The diversity generation component introduces diversity among the base models by applying various data augmentation techniques.
The fusion component combines the outputs of the base models to generate the final segmentation result.

Experimental results on a dataset of 3D biomedical images demonstrate that the proposed ensemble learning framework outperforms individual base models and achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed framework has the potential to enhance the accuracy and reliability of 3D biomedical image segmentation, which is crucial for various medical applications.
This paper presents a novel deep learning architecture called MDU-Net for biomedical image segmentation.
The proposed MDU-Net combines the U-Net architecture with dense connections and multi-scale feature fusion.
The dense connections enable information flow between different layers, enhancing the gradient flow and alleviating the vanishing gradient problem.
The multi-scale feature fusion module integrates features from different scales, allowing the network to capture both local and global contextual information.

Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that MDU-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in biomedical image segmentation tasks, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed MDU-Net has the potential to contribute to the field of biomedical image analysis and facilitate various medical applications.
DSCnet is a novel deep learning framework proposed for replicating lidar point clouds.
Lidar point clouds are widely used in various applications such as autonomous driving and robotics.
However, collecting large-scale lidar datasets is expensive and time-consuming.
To address this issue, DSCnet leverages a deep sensor cloning approach to generate synthetic lidar point clouds that closely resemble real-world data.
The framework consists of a generator network that learns to generate lidar point clouds from input images, and a discriminator network that distinguishes between real and synthetic point clouds.

Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DSCnet achieves high fidelity and accuracy in replicating lidar point clouds, making it a promising tool for data augmentation and simulation in lidar-based applications.
This paper proposes a novel approach for learning to steer a vehicle by mimicking features from heterogeneous auxiliary networks.
The authors argue that existing methods for autonomous driving often rely on a single auxiliary network, which may not capture all relevant information for steering.
To address this limitation, the authors propose a framework that combines multiple auxiliary networks, each trained on a different task related to driving.
The proposed framework leverages a feature mimicking module to transfer knowledge from the auxiliary networks to the steering network.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of steering accuracy and generalization to unseen scenarios.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of more robust and reliable autonomous driving systems.
Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, but it often requires a large amount of labeled data for training.
This paper proposes a cost-effective region-based active learning approach for semantic segmentation, called CEREALS.
The proposed method aims to reduce the annotation cost by selecting informative regions for labeling.
CEREALS utilizes a region proposal network to generate candidate regions and then selects the most informative ones based on uncertainty and diversity measures.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CEREALS achieves competitive performance with significantly fewer labeled samples compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to reduce the annotation cost and improve the efficiency of semantic segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel extension to fuzzy connectivity for body composition analysis, specifically focusing on thigh, brain, and whole body tissue segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes fuzzy connectivity to accurately segment different tissues in these regions, providing valuable information for medical diagnosis and treatment planning.
The extension to fuzzy connectivity incorporates additional features such as intensity, texture, and shape information to improve the segmentation accuracy.

Experimental results on a dataset of thigh, brain, and whole body MRI scans demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of medical imaging and can potentially enhance the understanding and treatment of various diseases and conditions.
This paper presents a novel approach for adapting semantic image segmentation models from daytime to nighttime conditions.

The proposed method, called Dark Model Adaptation, leverages a combination of domain adaptation techniques and image enhancement algorithms to effectively transfer knowledge from daytime images to nighttime images.

The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach through extensive experiments on various datasets and show that the adapted models achieve comparable performance to models trained directly on nighttime data.
The results suggest that Dark Model Adaptation can be a valuable tool for improving the performance of semantic image segmentation models in low-light conditions.
This paper presents a deep learning approach for estimating the recurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) using an end-to-end framework.
AF is a common cardiac arrhythmia that can lead to serious health complications.
Accurate estimation of AF recurrence is crucial for guiding treatment decisions and monitoring patient outcomes.
The proposed approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model temporal dependencies.
The model is trained on a large dataset of ECG recordings from patients with known AF recurrence outcomes.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning approach achieves high accuracy in estimating AF recurrence, outperforming traditional machine learning methods.
The findings suggest that deep learning techniques can provide valuable insights for predicting AF recurrence and improving patient care in clinical settings.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.

While deep learning models have achieved impressive results in this field, there is still a lack of understanding of how these models make predictions and what factors contribute to their performance.
In this paper, we propose a diagnostic framework for semantic segmentation models that aims to provide insights into their decision-making process.
We introduce several diagnostic tasks, including object localization, boundary detection, and occlusion reasoning, and evaluate their effectiveness on a state-of-the-art semantic segmentation model.
Our results show that these diagnostic tasks can help identify the strengths and weaknesses of the model, and provide valuable insights for improving its performance.
We believe that our diagnostic framework can contribute to the development of more interpretable and robust semantic segmentation models.
This paper presents a new image annotation tool called Mask Editor, which is designed specifically for image segmentation tasks.
The tool allows users to easily create pixel-level masks for objects of interest in images.
It provides a user-friendly interface with various features such as brush and eraser tools, zooming and panning capabilities, and the ability to save and load annotations.
The tool also supports multiple annotation formats, making it compatible with different segmentation algorithms.
The effectiveness and usability of Mask Editor are demonstrated through experiments and user studies, showing its potential as a valuable tool for image segmentation tasks.
This paper presents a novel approach for interactive binary image segmentation with edge preservation.
The proposed method combines user interaction and edge preservation techniques to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The user interacts with the system by providing initial seed points, which are used to guide the segmentation process.
The edge preservation technique is employed to preserve the boundaries of the objects in the image, ensuring that the segmentation results are visually appealing and semantically meaningful.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving high-quality segmentation results while requiring minimal user interaction.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various applications, such as medical image analysis and object recognition.
YouTube-VOS is a sequence-to-sequence video object segmentation method that leverages the large-scale YouTube-VOS dataset.
The method utilizes a convolutional LSTM network to model the temporal dependencies in video sequences and generate accurate object masks.
The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the YouTube-VOS dataset, outperforming previous methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The paper presents detailed experimental results and analysis, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method for video object segmentation tasks.
TreeSegNet is a novel approach for subdecimeter aerial image segmentation using adaptive tree convolutional neural networks (CNNs).
The proposed method addresses the challenges of accurately segmenting tree objects in high-resolution aerial images by leveraging the hierarchical structure of trees.
TreeSegNet consists of two main components: a tree detection module and a tree segmentation module.
The tree detection module uses a region proposal network to identify potential tree regions, while the tree segmentation module employs an adaptive tree CNN to refine the segmentation results.

Experimental results on a large-scale dataset demonstrate that TreeSegNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising solution for tree segmentation in aerial imagery applications.
This paper presents a weakly-supervised learning-based approach for feature localization in confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) glioma images.
CLE is a powerful imaging technique that allows for real-time visualization of cellular structures in vivo.
However, accurately localizing features of interest in CLE images is challenging due to the presence of noise and artifacts.

To address this issue, we propose a weakly-supervised learning framework that leverages the power of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically learn discriminative features for glioma localization.
Our approach utilizes a combination of weak supervision and self-supervised learning to train the CNN model.

Experimental results on a large dataset of CLE glioma images demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in accurately localizing glioma features, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of glioma diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.
This paper presents a novel approach for left atrial segmentation in 3D gadolinium enhanced-MRI using dilated convolutions in neural networks.
Left atrial segmentation is an important task in the diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation.
Traditional methods for left atrial segmentation rely on manual annotation, which is time-consuming and subjective.
In this study, we propose a deep learning model that utilizes dilated convolutions to capture both local and global information in the MRI images.
We evaluate our model on a dataset of 100 patients and compare its performance with other state-of-the-art methods.
Our results show that the proposed model achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
This suggests that dilated convolutions can be a promising technique for left atrial segmentation in 3D gadolinium enhanced-MRI.
Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown great success in semantic segmentation, but they often suffer from high computational costs and memory requirements.
In this paper, we propose a novel architecture for semantic segmentation that combines the efficiency of shallow networks with the representational power of deep networks.
Our approach involves using a series of dilated convolutions to capture multi-scale contextual information, followed by a global pooling layer to reduce the spatial dimensions.
We also introduce a novel loss function that encourages the network to focus on the most informative regions of the image.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while being significantly more efficient than existing methods.

Semantically-consistent image-to-image translation is a challenging task in computer vision, as it requires generating images that not only capture the style of a given input image but also maintain the semantic content.
In this paper, we propose a novel framework called Sem-GAN that addresses this problem.
Sem-GAN consists of two main components: a semantic segmentation network and a generative adversarial network (GAN).
The semantic segmentation network is used to extract the semantic information from the input image, which is then used to guide the image translation process.
The GAN is responsible for generating the translated image, while the semantic information is used as a constraint to ensure the semantic consistency between the input and output images.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that Sem-GAN achieves superior performance in terms of both visual quality and semantic consistency.

Medical image synthesis is an important task in the field of medical imaging, as it allows for the generation of realistic images that can be used for various purposes such as training deep learning models or augmenting limited datasets.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called SynNet, which is a structure-preserving fully convolutional network for medical image synthesis.
Our method leverages the power of fully convolutional networks to generate high-quality synthetic images while preserving the structural information present in the input images.
We evaluate our approach on two different medical imaging tasks: brain tumor segmentation and retinal vessel segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and quantitative metrics.
Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components of our proposed method.
Overall, our work presents a promising solution for medical image synthesis that can benefit various applications in the field of medical imaging.
This paper proposes a method for accurately quantifying the uncertainty in neural network predictions of biomarkers, with the goal of improving the safety of deep learning models.

The authors argue that current deep learning models often lack the ability to provide reliable uncertainty estimates, which can lead to incorrect or misleading predictions in critical applications such as medical diagnosis.
The proposed method combines Bayesian neural networks with Monte Carlo dropout to estimate the predictive uncertainty of biomarker predictions.
The authors evaluate the method on a dataset of medical images and demonstrate that it provides more accurate uncertainty estimates compared to existing approaches.
They also show that incorporating these uncertainty estimates into decision-making processes can improve the safety and reliability of deep learning models in medical applications.
Overall, this paper contributes to the growing field of safe deep learning by addressing the important issue of uncertainty quantification in neural network predictions.
This paper presents a novel approach called CompNet for brain MRI extraction.
The proposed method utilizes a complementary segmentation network that combines both deep learning and traditional image processing techniques.

The network consists of two branches: a deep learning branch that uses a U-Net architecture for initial segmentation, and a traditional image processing branch that refines the segmentation using morphological operations and region growing.
Experimental results on a publicly available brain MRI dataset demonstrate that CompNet achieves superior performance compared to existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of brain MRI extraction, which is crucial for various medical applications.
This paper presents a language-based image editing approach using recurrent attentive models.
The proposed method leverages the power of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and attention mechanisms to generate image edits based on natural language descriptions.
The RNN is trained to encode the input text into a latent representation, which is then used by the attention mechanism to selectively focus on relevant image regions.
The attention maps are combined with the original image to create the final edited image.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in generating accurate and visually appealing image edits based on textual descriptions.
The language-based image editing framework has potential applications in various domains, including image manipulation, content creation, and visual storytelling.
This paper presents a performance evaluation of deep learning networks for semantic segmentation of traffic stereo-pair images.
The authors compare the performance of three popular deep learning architectures, namely U-Net, SegNet, and DeepLab, on a dataset of traffic stereo-pair images.
The evaluation is based on various metrics such as pixel accuracy, mean intersection over union (IoU), and F1 score.
The results show that DeepLab outperforms U-Net and SegNet in terms of all the evaluated metrics.
The authors also analyze the impact of different hyperparameters on the performance of the networks.
Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the performance of deep learning networks for semantic segmentation of traffic stereo-pair images and can guide future research in this area.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical image analysis, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis and treatment planning.
In recent years, deep learning techniques, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown promising results in medical image segmentation.
However, CNNs often suffer from the loss of spatial information due to the downsampling operations.
To address this issue, we propose a novel architecture called Recurrent Residual Convolutional Neural Network based on U-Net (R2U-Net) for medical image segmentation.
The R2U-Net incorporates recurrent connections and residual learning into the U-Net architecture to preserve spatial information and enhance feature representation.

Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that the proposed R2U-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The R2U-Net shows great potential for various medical image segmentation tasks and can contribute to improving clinical decision-making and patient care.
Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in various clinical applications.
In this paper, we propose a consensus-based approach for medical image segmentation using semi-supervised learning and graph cuts.
We first generate multiple initial segmentations using different algorithms and then use a semi-supervised learning framework to refine these segmentations.
The refined segmentations are then combined using a graph cuts algorithm to obtain the final segmentation.
Experimental results on a dataset of brain MRI images demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves higher segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, which can benefit various clinical applications.
This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting facades in real-world images, referred to as "facade segmentation in the wild".
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture that is trained on a large dataset of annotated facade images.
The network is designed to learn the complex patterns and structures present in facades, enabling it to accurately segment facades in diverse and challenging real-world images.
The authors evaluate the performance of the proposed method on several benchmark datasets and compare it to existing facade segmentation approaches.

The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and robustness, making it a valuable tool for various applications such as urban planning, architectural design, and augmented reality.
